concerning the effect as FDA requests.

requirements.topic: evaluating and reporting an unanticipated adverse device effect
requirements.complies: The text says the sponsor evaluated an unanticipated adverse device effect and reported the results to FDA, all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators within 10 working days of first receiving notice, and sent further reports as FDA requested.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the sponsor received notice of an unanticipated adverse device effect but reported the evaluation results late, only to some parties, or not at all, or ignored FDA requests for additional reports.
requirements.hint: State that the evaluation results went to FDA, all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators within 10 working days of first notice, with additional reports as FDA asks.

requirements.title: IRB approval withdrawal notice
requirements.need: A sponsor must notify FDA and all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators of any withdrawal of approval of an investigation or part of an investigation by a reviewing IRB within 5 working days after receipt of the withdrawal.

quote.text:
Withdrawal of IRB approval. A
sponsor shall notify FDA and all re-
viewing IRB’s and participating inves-
tigators of any withdrawal of approval
of an investigation or a part of an in-
vestigation by a reviewing IRB within
5 working days after receipt of the
withdrawal of approval.

requirements.topic: a reviewing IRB withdrawing approval of a device investigation
requirements.complies: The text says a reviewing IRB withdrew approval of the investigation or part of it and the sponsor notified FDA, all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators within 5 working days of receiving the withdrawal.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the sponsor received an IRB withdrawal of approval but did not notify FDA or the other parties, or notified them later than 5 working days, or told only the IRB.
requirements.hint: Say the sponsor notified FDA, all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators within 5 working days after receiving the withdrawal of approval.

requirements.title: FDA approval withdrawal notice
requirements.need: A sponsor must notify all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators of any withdrawal of FDA approval of the investigation within 5 working days after receipt of notice of the withdrawal.

quote.text:
Withdrawal of FDA approval. A
sponsor shall notify all reviewing IRB’s
and participating investigators of any
withdrawal of FDA approval of the in-
vestigation, and shall do so within 5
working days after receipt of notice of
the withdrawal of approval.

requirements.topic: withdrawal of FDA approval of an investigation and telling the study sites about it
requirements.complies: The sponsor states that when it receives notice that FDA approval of the investigation is withdrawn, it notifies all reviewing IRBs and all participating investigators within 5 working days of receiving that notice.
requirements.conflicts: The sponsor says it will inform IRBs and investigators of an FDA approval withdrawal only at the next scheduled meeting, or says it will notify FDA but not the IRBs and investigators, or gives no time limit or a limit longer than 5 working days.
requirements.hint: State that every reviewing IRB and every participating investigator is told of an FDA approval withdrawal within 5 working days after the sponsor receives the notice.

requirements.title: Current investigator list
requirements.need: A sponsor must submit to FDA, at 6-month intervals, a current list of the names and addresses of all investigators participating in the investigation, with the first list submitted 6 months after FDA approval.

quote.text:
Current investigator list. A sponsor
shall submit to FDA, at 6-month inter-
vals, a current list of the names and
addresses of all investigators partici-
pating in the investigation. The spon-
sor shall submit the first such list 6
months after FDA approval.

requirements.topic: periodic reporting to FDA of who is conducting the investigation
requirements.complies: The sponsor states it sends FDA a current list of the names and addresses of all participating investigators every 6 months, with the first list sent 6 months after FDA approval.
requirements.conflicts: The sponsor says it will send the investigator list only once, or only when investigators change, or at intervals other than 6 months, or says it will keep the list internally without sending it to FDA.
requirements.hint: State that a current list of all investigators' names and addresses goes to FDA every 6 months, starting 6 months after FDA approval.

requirements.title: Progress reports
requirements.need: A sponsor must submit progress reports to all reviewing IRBs at regular intervals and at least yearly, to FDA as well for a significant risk device, and semi-annual progress reports to all reviewing IRBs and FDA for a treatment IDE.

quote.text:
Progress reports. At regular inter-
vals, and at least yearly, a sponsor
shall submit progress reports to all re-
viewing IRB’s. In the case of a signifi-
cant risk device, a sponsor shall also
submit progress reports to FDA. A
sponsor of a treatment IDE shall sub-
mit semi-annual progress reports to all
reviewing IRB’s and FDA in accordance
with § 812.36(f) and annual reports in ac-
cordance with this section.

requirements.topic: progress reporting on an investigation to IRBs and FDA
requirements.complies: The sponsor states it submits progress reports to all reviewing IRBs at regular intervals and at least yearly, also to FDA for a significant risk device, and semi-annual progress reports to all reviewing IRBs and FDA for a treatment IDE.
requirements.conflicts: The sponsor says progress reports go only to FDA, or only to IRBs, or are sent less often than yearly, or says a treatment IDE needs no semi-annual reports to IRBs and FDA.
requirements.hint: State the reporting schedule by device type: at least yearly to all reviewing IRBs, plus FDA for significant risk devices, and semi-annual to IRBs and FDA for a treatment IDE.

requirements.title: Recall and device disposition notice
requirements.need: A sponsor must notify FDA and all reviewing IRBs of any request that an investigator return, repair, or otherwise dispose of any units of a device within 30 working days after the request is made, stating why the request was made.

quote.text:
Recall and device disposition. A
sponsor shall notify FDA and all re-
viewing IRB’s of any request that an
investigator return, repair, or other-
wise dispose of any units of a device.
Such notice shall occur within 30 work-
ing days after the request is made and
shall state why the request was made.

requirements.topic: asking an investigator to return, repair or dispose of device units and telling FDA and IRBs about it
requirements.complies: The sponsor states that when it asks an investigator to return, repair or otherwise dispose of device units, it notifies FDA and all reviewing IRBs within 30 working days of the request and states why the request was made.
requirements.conflicts: The sponsor says it will handle device returns internally without telling FDA or the IRBs, or notifies them later than 30 working days, or omits any statement of the reason for the request.
requirements.hint: State that any request to return, repair or dispose of device units is reported to FDA and all reviewing IRBs within 30 working days, with the reason included.

requirements.title: Final report
requirements.need: For a significant risk device, the sponsor must notify FDA within 30 working days of completion or termination of the investigation and submit a final report to FDA and all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators within 6 months; for a non-significant risk device, submit a final report to all reviewing IRBs within 6 months after termination or completion.

quote.text:
Final report. In the case of a sig-
nificant risk device, the sponsor shall
notify FDA within 30 working days of
the completion or termination of the
investigation and shall submit a final
report to FDA and all reviewing the
IRB’s and participating investigators
within 6 months after completion or
termination. In the case of a device
that is not a significant risk device,
the sponsor shall submit a final report
to all reviewing IRB’s within 6 months
after termination or completion.

requirements.topic: closing out an investigation and reporting its completion or termination
requirements.complies: The sponsor states that for a significant risk device it notifies FDA within 30 working days of completion or termination and submits a final report to FDA, all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators within 6 months, and for a non-significant risk device it submits a final report to all reviewing IRBs within 6 months.
requirements.conflicts: The sponsor says no final report is needed, or sends the final report only to FDA, or misses the 30 working day FDA notice for a significant risk device, or sets a deadline longer than 6 months.
requirements.hint: State the two paths: significant risk means FDA notice within 30 working days and a final report to FDA, IRBs and investigators within 6 months; non-significant risk means a final report to IRBs within 6 months.

requirements.title: Uninformed consent use report
requirements.need: A sponsor must submit to FDA a copy of any investigator report of use of a device without obtaining informed consent within 5 working days of receipt of notice of such use.

quote.text:
Informed consent. A sponsor shall
submit to FDA a copy of any report by
an investigator under paragraph (a)(5)
of this section of use of a device with-
out obtaining informed consent, within
5 working days of receipt of notice of
such use.

requirements.topic: use of a device without informed consent and reporting it to FDA
requirements.complies: The sponsor states it submits a copy of any investigator report of device use without informed consent to FDA within 5 working days of receiving notice of that use.
requirements.conflicts: The sponsor says such reports stay with the investigator or IRB and are not sent to FDA, or are sent later than 5 working days after the sponsor learns of the use.
requirements.hint: State that a copy of any investigator report of device use without informed consent goes to FDA within 5 working days of the sponsor receiving notice.

requirements.title: Significant risk determination report
requirements.need: If an IRB determines that a device is a significant risk device and the sponsor had proposed that the IRB consider it not significant risk, the sponsor must submit a report of the IRB's determination to FDA within 5 working days after first learning of it.

quote.text:
Significant risk device determina-
tions. If an IRB determines that a de-
vice is a significant risk device, and
the sponsor had proposed that the IRB
consider the device not to be a signifi-
cant risk device, the sponsor shall sub-
mit to FDA a report of the IRB’s deter-
mination within 5 working days after
the sponsor first learns of the IRB’s de-
termination.

requirements.topic: IRB significant risk determinations for investigational device studies and reporting them to FDA
requirements.complies: The sponsor states that when an IRB deemed the device significant risk after the sponsor had proposed it be considered not significant risk, the sponsor submitted a report of that determination to FDA within 5 working days of first learning of it.
requirements.conflicts: The sponsor says it learned of the IRB's significant risk determination but did not report it to FDA, or waited longer than 5 working days, or decided no report was needed because it disagreed with the IRB.
requirements.hint: Describe submitting a report of the IRB's significant risk determination to FDA within 5 working days after the sponsor first learns of it, when the sponsor had proposed non-significant risk.

requirements.title: Information on request
requirements.need: A sponsor must, upon request by a reviewing IRB or FDA, provide accurate, complete, and current information about any aspect of the investigation.

quote.text:
Other. A sponsor shall, upon re-
quest by a reviewing IRB or FDA, pro-
vide accurate, complete, and current
information about any aspect of the in-
vestigation.

requirements.topic: sponsors giving information about an investigational device study to an IRB or FDA
requirements.complies: The sponsor states that on request from a reviewing IRB or FDA it provides accurate, complete and current information about any aspect of the investigation.
requirements.conflicts: The sponsor says it withholds information from an IRB or FDA, provides outdated or partial records, or answers only some questions about the investigation.
requirements.hint: State that the sponsor will give accurate, complete and current information on any aspect of the investigation whenever a reviewing IRB or FDA asks.

requirements.title: Importer as agent and sponsor
requirements.need: A person who imports or offers for importation an investigational device must be the agent of the foreign exporter and act as the sponsor of the clinical investigation, or ensure that another person does so.

quote.text:
(a) Imports. In addition to complying
with other requirements of this part, a
person who imports or offers for impor-
tation an investigational device sub-
ject to this part shall be the agent of
the foreign exporter with respect to in-
vestigations of the device and shall act
as the sponsor of the clinical investiga-
tion, or ensure that another person
acts as the agent of the foreign ex-
porter and the sponsor of the investiga-
tion.

requirements.topic: importing an investigational device from a foreign exporter for a clinical investigation
requirements.complies: The importer states it is the agent of the foreign exporter for investigations of the device and acts as the sponsor of the clinical investigation, or that another named person fills both roles.
requirements.conflicts: The importer describes itself only as a shipping or distribution channel, names no agent of the foreign exporter, and assigns no sponsor role for the clinical investigation.
requirements.hint: Say who is the foreign exporter's agent and who acts as sponsor of the investigation, and confirm the importer is one of them or has ensured another person is.

requirements.title: Export prior approval
requirements.need: A person exporting an investigational device subject to this part must obtain FDA's prior approval as required by section 801(e) of the act or comply with section 802 of the act.

quote.text:
(b) Exports. A person exporting an in-
vestigational device subject to this
part shall obtain FDA’s prior approval,
as required by section 801(e) of the act
or comply with section 802 of the act.

requirements.topic: exporting an investigational device subject to the device rules
requirements.complies: The exporter states it obtained FDA prior approval as required by section 801(e) of the act, or that it complies with section 802 of the act, before exporting the device.
requirements.conflicts: The exporter says it ships the investigational device to other countries without FDA prior approval and without following section 802 of the act.
requirements.hint: State that before export the person obtains FDA prior approval under section 801(e) or complies with section 802 of the act.

requirements.title: Devices requiring PMA
requirements.need: This part applies to any class III medical device, unless exempt under section 520(g) of the act, that was not on the market before May 28, 1976 and is not substantially equivalent to a pre-1976 device or a device classified into class I or II, that is required to have an approved PMA or declared completed PDP, or that was regulated as a new drug or antibiotic drug before May 28, 1976.

quote.text:
This part applies to any class III
medical device, unless exempt under
section 520(g) of the act, that:
(1) Was not on the market (intro-
duced or delivered for introduction into
commerce for commercial distribution)
before May 28, 1976, and is not substan-
tially equivalent to a device on the
market before May 28, 1976, or to a de-
vice first marketed on, or after that
date, which has been classified into
class I or class II; or
(2) Is required to have an approved
premarket approval application (PMA)
or a declared completed product devel-
opment protocol under a regulation
issued under section 515(b) of the act;
or
(3) Was regulated by FDA as a new
drug or antibiotic drug before May 28,
1976, and therefore is governed by sec-
tion 520(1) of the act.

requirements.topic: which class III medical devices fall under the premarket approval rules
requirements.complies: The text states the part applies to a class III device that was not on the market before May 28, 1976 and is not substantially equivalent to a pre-1976 device or a class I or II device, or that needs an approved PMA or declared completed PDP, or that was regulated as a new drug or antibiotic drug before May 28, 1976, unless exempt under section 520(g).
requirements.conflicts: The text says the part covers every class III device without exception, or excludes devices that need an approved PMA, or ignores the May 28, 1976 marketing and new drug history criteria.
requirements.hint: List the three device categories in the rule and note the section 520(g) exemption when describing which class III devices the part applies to.

requirements.title: Conditions to approval
requirements.need: This part amends the conditions to approval for any PMA approved before its effective date; any condition inconsistent with this part is revoked and any consistent condition remains in effect.

quote.text:
This part amends the conditions
to approval for any PMA approved be-
fore the effective date of this part. Any
condition to approval for an approved
PMA that is inconsistent with this part
is revoked. Any condition to approval
for an approved PMA that is consistent
with this part remains in effect.

requirements.topic: conditions to approval of premarket approval applications approved before the part's effective date
requirements.complies: The text states the part amends conditions to approval for PMAs approved before its effective date, that inconsistent conditions are revoked, and that consistent conditions remain in effect.
requirements.conflicts: The text says all earlier approval conditions stay unchanged, or that the part leaves inconsistent conditions in force, or that it revokes conditions that match the part.
requirements.hint: Say the part amends earlier PMA approval conditions, revoking those inconsistent with it and keeping those consistent with it.

requirements.title: Statement of material fact
requirements.need: A statement of material fact is a representation tending to show that safety or effectiveness is more probable than it would be otherwise, and a false affirmation, silence, or omission leading a reasonable person to a particular conclusion about safety or effectiveness may be a false statement of material fact even if unintended.

quote.text:
Statement of material fact means a
representation that tends to show that
the safety or effectiveness of a device
is more probable than it would be in
the absence of such a representation. A
false affirmation or silence or an omis-
sion that would lead a reasonable per-
son to draw a particular conclusion as
to the safety or effectiveness of a de-
vice also may be a false statement of
material fact, even if the statement
was not intended by the person making
it to be misleading or to have any pro-
bative effect.

requirements.topic: claims and statements about a medical device's safety or effectiveness
requirements.complies: The text states plainly what the device is shown to do, gives the evidence behind each claim, and discloses limitations and negative findings so a reader is not led to a conclusion about safety or effectiveness that the data do not support.
requirements.conflicts: The text implies the device is safer or more effective than the evidence shows, or leaves out unfavorable results or stays silent on a known risk in a way that leads a reasonable reader to assume safety or effectiveness.
requirements.hint: Describe only what the data support, and include any omission or silence that could lead a reader to a safety or effectiveness conclusion you cannot back up.

requirements.title: Foreign data compliance
requirements.need: If data from clinical investigations conducted outside the United States are submitted to support a PMA, the applicant must comply with the provisions in § 812.28 of this chapter, as applicable.

quote.text:
Data to support PMA. If data from
clinical investigations conducted out-
side the United States are submitted to
support a PMA, the applicant shall
comply with the provisions in § 812.28 of
this chapter, as applicable.

requirements.topic: clinical investigation data from outside the United States submitted to support a PMA
requirements.complies: The text states that foreign clinical investigation data submitted in the PMA were conducted in compliance with the provisions of 21 CFR 812.28, as applicable.
requirements.conflicts: The text submits or relies on clinical investigation data from outside the United States without stating compliance with 21 CFR 812.28, or says those provisions were not followed.
requirements.hint: State that any foreign clinical investigation data in the PMA comply with 21 CFR 812.28, as applicable.

requirements.title: Foreign data sole basis
requirements.need: A PMA based solely on foreign clinical data and otherwise meeting the approval criteria may be approved if the foreign data are applicable to the U.S. population and medical practice, the studies were performed by clinical investigators of recognized competence, and the data may be considered valid without an on-site inspection or FDA can validate the data through an inspection or other appropriate means.

quote.text:
As sole basis for marketing approval.

A PMA based solely on foreign clinical
data and otherwise meeting the cri-
teria for approval under this part may
be approved if:
(1) The foreign data are applicable to
the U.S. population and U.S. medical
practice;
(2) The studies have been performed
by clinical investigators of recognized
competence; and
(3) The data may be considered valid
without the need for an on-site inspec-
tion by FDA or, if FDA considers such
an inspection to be necessary, FDA can
validate the data through an on-site in-
spection or other appropriate means.

requirements.topic: a PMA whose only clinical data come from outside the United States
requirements.complies: The text states that the foreign data apply to the U.S. population and U.S. medical practice, that the studies were done by clinical investigators of recognized competence, and that the data are valid without an on-site FDA inspection or can be validated by FDA through an inspection or other means.
requirements.conflicts: The text relies solely on foreign data but does not address applicability to the U.S. population and medical practice, investigator competence, or data validity and FDA inspection, or admits the data cannot be validated.
requirements.hint: Address all three conditions: U.S. applicability, recognized investigator competence, and validity without inspection or FDA validation.

requirements.title: Completed PDP equals PMA
requirements.need: A class III device for which a product development protocol has been declared completed by FDA under this chapter will be considered to have an approved PMA.

quote.text:
A class III device for which a product
development protocol has been de-
clared completed by FDA under this
chapter will be considered to have an
approved PMA.

requirements.topic: a class III device with a product development protocol declared completed by FDA
requirements.complies: The text states that the device's product development protocol has been declared completed by FDA and that the device is therefore considered to have an approved PMA.
requirements.conflicts: The text says a device with a completed product development protocol still needs a separate PMA approval, or claims PMA status for a device whose protocol FDA has not declared completed.
requirements.hint: State that FDA has declared the product development protocol completed and that this is treated as an approved PMA.

requirements.title: PMA signature requirement
requirements.need: The applicant or an authorized representative must sign the PMA, and if the applicant does not reside or have a place of business in the United States, the PMA must be countersigned by an authorized representative residing or maintaining a place of business in the United States and identify the representative's name and address.

quote.text:
The applicant or an authorized
representative shall sign the PMA. If
the applicant does not reside or have a
place of business within the United
States, the PMA shall be countersigned
by an authorized representative resid-
ing or maintaining a place of business
in the United States and shall identify
the representative’s name and address.

requirements.topic: signing and countersigning of a PMA application
requirements.complies: The text shows the PMA signed by the applicant or an authorized representative, and, where the applicant has no U.S. residence or place of business, countersigned by a U.S.-based authorized representative with that person's name and address identified.
requirements.conflicts: The text presents an unsigned PMA, or a foreign applicant's PMA with no U.S.-based countersignature or without the representative's name and address.
requirements.hint: Have the applicant or authorized representative sign, and if the applicant is outside the United States add a U.S.-based countersignature with name and address.

requirements.title: Applicant name and address
requirements.need: Unless an omission is justified under paragraph (d), a PMA must include in electronic format the name and address of the applicant.

quote.text:
Unless the applicant justifies an
omission in accordance with paragraph
(d) of this section, a PMA shall include
in electronic format:
(1) The name and address of the ap-
plicant.

requirements.topic: the applicant's name and address in a PMA submission
requirements.complies: The PMA includes, in electronic format, the name and address of the applicant, or states a justification for omitting it under paragraph (d).
requirements.conflicts: The PMA leaves out the applicant's name or address in electronic format without any justification under paragraph (d).
requirements.hint: Include the applicant's name and address in electronic format, or justify the omission under paragraph (d).

requirements.title: Table of contents and sections
requirements.need: A PMA must include a table of contents specifying volume and page number for each item, separate sections on nonclinical laboratory studies and clinical investigations involving human subjects, be submitted as a single version, and identify information believed to be trade secret or confidential commercial or financial information.

quote.text:
A table of contents that specifies
the volume and page number for each
item referred to in the table. A PMA
shall include separate sections on non-
clinical laboratory studies and on clin-
ical investigations involving human
subjects. A PMA shall be submitted as
a single version. The applicant shall in-
clude information that it believes to be
trade secret or confidential commer-
cial or financial information in the
PMA and identify the information that
it believes to be trade secret or con-
fidential commercial or financial infor-
mation.

requirements.topic: the contents and organization of a premarket approval application submitted to FDA
requirements.complies: The document opens with a table of contents that lists each item with its volume and page number, has separate sections for nonclinical laboratory studies and for clinical investigations involving human subjects, is submitted as one single version, and marks the information the applicant considers trade secret or confidential commercial or financial information.
requirements.conflicts: The document has no table of contents or one without volume and page numbers, mixes nonclinical laboratory studies and clinical investigations into one section, is submitted as multiple versions, or includes trade secret or confidential commercial or financial information without identifying it as such.
requirements.hint: Include a table of contents giving volume and page number for every item, keep nonclinical laboratory studies and clinical investigations in separate sections, submit one single version, and flag any trade secret or confidential commercial or financial information.

requirements.title: Summary content
requirements.need: A PMA must include a summary in sufficient detail for a general understanding of the data and information, containing indications for use, device description, alternative practices and procedures, marketing history, summary of studies, and conclusions drawn from the studies.

quote.text:
A summary in sufficient detail
that the reader may gain a general un-
derstanding of the data and informa-
tion in the application. The summary
shall contain the following informa-
tion:
(i) Indications for use. A general de-
scription of the disease or condition
the device will diagnose, treat, prevent,
cure, or mitigate, including a descrip-
tion of the patient population for
which the device is intended.

requirements.topic: the summary section of a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: The summary gives the indications for use, a description of the device, alternative practices and procedures, marketing history, a summary of the studies, and the conclusions drawn from the studies, in enough detail that a reader gains a general understanding of the data and information in the application.
requirements.conflicts: The summary omits the indications for use, device description, alternative practices and procedures, marketing history, study summaries, or conclusions, or is so thin that a reader cannot gain a general understanding of the data and information.
requirements.hint: Write a summary covering indications for use, device description, alternative practices and procedures, marketing history, study summaries, and conclusions, detailed enough for a general understanding of the data.

requirements.title: Conclusions on safety and effectiveness
requirements.need: The PMA summary must include a discussion demonstrating that the data constitute valid scientific evidence within the meaning of § 860.7 and provide reasonable assurance that the device is safe and effective for its intended use, presenting benefit and risk considerations including adverse effects and any proposed additional studies or surveillance.

quote.text:
Conclusions drawn from the stud-
ies. A discussion demonstrating that
the data and information in the appli-
cation constitute valid scientific evi-
dence within the meaning of § 860.7 and
provide reasonable assurance that the
device is safe and effective for its in-
tended use. A concluding discussion
shall present benefit and risk consider-
ations related to the device including a
discussion of any adverse effects of the
device on health and any proposed ad-
ditional studies or surveillance the ap-
plicant intends to conduct following
approval of the PMA.

requirements.topic: the conclusions on safety and effectiveness in a premarket approval application summary
requirements.complies: The conclusions discuss how the data constitute valid scientific evidence under § 860.7 and give reasonable assurance the device is safe and effective for its intended use, and present benefit and risk considerations including adverse effects on health and any proposed additional studies or surveillance after approval.
requirements.conflicts: The conclusions assert safety and effectiveness without showing the data are valid scientific evidence under § 860.7, or omit benefit and risk considerations, adverse effects on health, or proposed post-approval studies or surveillance.
requirements.hint: In the conclusions, show the data meet § 860.7 valid scientific evidence and give reasonable assurance of safety and effectiveness, and discuss benefits, risks, adverse effects, and any proposed post-approval studies or surveillance.

requirements.title: Device description
requirements.need: A PMA must include a complete description of the device including pictorial representations, each functional component or ingredient, properties relevant to diagnosis, treatment, prevention, cure, or mitigation, principles of operation, and the methods and facilities and controls used for manufacture, processing, packing, storage, and installation in sufficient detail for a knowledgeable quality control judgment.

quote.text:
A complete description of:
(i) The device, including pictorial
representations;
(ii) Each of the functional compo-
nents or ingredients of the device if the
device consists of more than one phys-
ical component or ingredient;
(iii) The properties of the device rel-
evant to the diagnosis, treatment, pre-
vention, cure, or mitigation of a dis-
ease or condition;
(iv) The principles of operation of the
device; and
(v) The methods used in, and the fa-
cilities and controls used for, the man-
ufacture, processing, packing, storage,
and, where appropriate, installation of
the device, in sufficient detail so that a
person generally familiar with current
good manufacturing practice can make
a knowledgeable judgment about the
quality control used in the manufac-
ture of the device.

requirements.topic: the device description section of a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: The description covers the device with pictorial representations, each functional component or ingredient, the properties relevant to diagnosis, treatment, prevention, cure, or mitigation, the principles of operation, and the manufacturing methods, facilities, and controls for manufacture, processing, packing, storage, and installation, detailed enough for a person familiar with current good manufacturing practice to judge the quality control.
requirements.conflicts: The description lacks pictorial representations, omits functional components or ingredients, properties relevant to the intended medical use, or principles of operation, or gives manufacturing methods, facilities, and controls too thinly for a person familiar with current good manufacturing practice to judge quality control.
requirements.hint: Describe the device with pictures, every component or ingredient, properties relevant to its medical use, principles of operation, and manufacturing methods, facilities, and controls in enough detail for a good manufacturing practice expert to judge quality control.

requirements.title: Standards reference and deviations
requirements.need: A PMA must reference any performance standard under section 514 or section 534 in effect or proposed at submission and any relevant voluntary standard known or that should reasonably be known, provide adequate information demonstrating how the device meets or justifies deviation from a performance standard, and explain any deviation from a voluntary standard.

quote.text:
Reference to any performance
standard under section 514 of the Fed-
eral Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act or
under section 534 of Subchapter C—
Electronic Product Radiation Control
of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cos-
metic Act (formerly the Radiation
Control for Health and Safety Act of
1968) in effect or proposed at the time
of the submission and to any voluntary
standard that is relevant to any aspect
of the safety or effectiveness of the de-
vice and that is known to or that
should reasonably be known to the ap-
plicant.

requirements.topic: references to performance and voluntary standards in a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: The application cites each section 514 or section 534 performance standard in effect or proposed at submission and each relevant voluntary standard known or that should reasonably be known, shows how the device meets each performance standard or justifies any deviation, and explains any deviation from a voluntary standard.
requirements.conflicts: The application cites no performance standards or voluntary standards, ignores a relevant standard the applicant knew or should have known, or claims conformity without showing how the device meets the standard or justifying a deviation.
requirements.hint: List every applicable section 514 or 534 performance standard and relevant voluntary standard, show how the device meets each one or justify any deviation, and explain deviations from voluntary standards.

requirements.title: Nonclinical study results
requirements.need: A PMA must include a technical section with results of nonclinical laboratory studies including microbiological, toxicological, immunological, biocompatibility, stress, wear, shelf life, and other tests, with a statement that each study was conducted in compliance with part 58 or a brief statement of the reason for noncompliance.

quote.text:
A section containing results of the
nonclinical laboratory studies with the
device including microbiological, toxi-
cological, immunological, biocompat-
ibility, stress, wear, shelf life, and
other laboratory or animal tests as ap-
propriate. Information on nonclinical
laboratory studies shall include a
statement that each such study was
conducted in compliance with part 58,
or, if the study was not conducted in
compliance with such regulations, a
brief statement of the reason for the
noncompliance.

requirements.topic: nonclinical laboratory study results in a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: The technical section reports results of nonclinical laboratory studies such as microbiological, toxicological, immunological, biocompatibility, stress, wear, and shelf life tests, and states for each study that it was conducted in compliance with part 58 or gives a brief reason for noncompliance.
requirements.conflicts: The technical section omits nonclinical laboratory study results, or reports studies without stating part 58 compliance or giving a reason for noncompliance.
requirements.hint: Report the nonclinical laboratory study results and, for each study, state that it complied with part 58 or briefly give the reason it did not.

requirements.title: Clinical investigation results
requirements.need: A PMA must include a technical section with results of clinical investigations involving human subjects including protocols, investigator and subject numbers, selection and exclusion criteria, study population and period, safety and effectiveness data, adverse reactions, discontinuations, complaints, device failures and replacements, tabulations of data, and statistical analyses, identifying any investigation conducted under an IDE.

quote.text:
A section containing results of
the clinical investigations involving
human subjects with the device includ-
ing clinical protocols, number of inves-
tigators and subjects per investigator,
subject selection and exclusion cri-
teria, study population, study period,
safety and effectiveness data, adverse
reactions and complications, patient
discontinuation, patient complaints,
device failures and replacements, tab-
ulations of data from all individual
subject report forms and copies of such
forms for each subject who died during
a clinical investigation or who did not
complete the investigation, results of

[Page 8]
153

Food and Drug Administration, HHS § 814.20

statistical analyses of the clinical in-
vestigations, device failures and re-
placements, contraindications and pre-
cautions for use of the device, and any
other appropriate information from the
clinical investigations.

requirements.topic: clinical investigation results included in a premarket approval application for a medical device
requirements.complies: The technical section reports each clinical protocol, the number of investigators and subjects per investigator, subject selection and exclusion criteria, the study population and study period, safety and effectiveness data, adverse reactions and complications, patient discontinuations, patient complaints, device failures and replacements, tabulations of data from all individual subject report forms, results of statistical analyses, contraindications and precautions, and identifies any investigation conducted under an IDE.
requirements.conflicts: The section gives only a summary of overall outcomes and omits protocols, subject counts, selection and exclusion criteria, adverse reactions, discontinuations, complaints, device failures, data tabulations or statistical analyses, or fails to say whether an investigation was conducted under an IDE.
requirements.hint: Include every listed element for each clinical investigation and state which investigations were conducted under an IDE.

requirements.title: IRB and consent compliance statement
requirements.need: For clinical investigations conducted in the United States, the PMA must include a statement for each investigation that it was conducted in compliance with the institutional review board regulations in part 56 or was not subject to those regulations under § 56.104 or § 56.105, and that it was conducted in compliance with the informed consent regulations in part 50, or a brief statement of the reason for noncompliance.

quote.text:
For clinical investigations con-
ducted in the United States, a state-
ment with respect to each investiga-
tion that it either was conducted in
compliance with the institutional re-
view board regulations in part 56 of
this chapter, or was not subject to the
regulations under § 56.104 or § 56.105, and
that it was conducted in compliance
with the informed consent regulations
in part 50 of this chapter; or if the in-
vestigation was not conducted in com-
pliance with those regulations, a brief
statement of the reason for the non-
compliance.

requirements.topic: statements about institutional review board and informed consent compliance for clinical investigations conducted in the United States
requirements.complies: For each United States investigation the application states that it was conducted in compliance with the part 56 institutional review board regulations or was not subject to them under § 56.104 or § 56.105, and that it was conducted in compliance with the part 50 informed consent regulations, or gives a brief reason for any noncompliance.
requirements.conflicts: The application covers United States investigations without any statement on institutional review board or informed consent compliance, or says an investigation was not compliant without giving a brief reason.
requirements.hint: Add a per-investigation statement naming part 56 (or the § 56.104 or § 56.105 exemption) and part 50 compliance, or a brief reason for noncompliance.

requirements.title: IDE sponsor compliance statement
requirements.need: For clinical investigations conducted in the United States, the PMA must include a statement that each investigation was conducted in compliance with part 812 concerning sponsors of clinical investigations and clinical investigators, or a brief statement of the reason for noncompliance.

quote.text:
For clinical investigations con-
ducted in the United States, a state-
ment that each investigation was con-
ducted in compliance with part 812 of
this chapter concerning sponsors of
clinical investigations and clinical in-
vestigators, or if the investigation was
not conducted in compliance with
those regulations, a brief statement of
the reason for the noncompliance.

requirements.topic: statements about part 812 sponsor and clinical investigator compliance for clinical investigations conducted in the United States
requirements.complies: For each United States investigation the application states that it was conducted in compliance with part 812 concerning sponsors of clinical investigations and clinical investigators, or gives a brief statement of the reason for noncompliance.
requirements.conflicts: The application describes United States investigations but never addresses part 812 compliance, or notes noncompliance without stating the reason.
requirements.hint: Add a statement for each United States investigation that it complied with part 812, or a brief reason why it did not.

requirements.title: Foreign GCP compliance
requirements.need: For clinical investigations conducted outside the United States intended to support the PMA, the requirements under § 812.28 apply, and if any investigation was not conducted in accordance with good clinical practice, the PMA must include a waiver request under § 812.28(c) or a brief statement of the reason and a description of steps taken to ensure credible and accurate data and protection of subjects.

quote.text:
For clinical investigations con-
ducted outside the United States that
are intended to support the PMA, the
requirements under § 812.28 of this
chapter apply. If any such investiga-
tion was not conducted in accordance
with good clinical practice (GCP) as de-
scribed in § 812.28(a), include either a
waiver request in accordance with
§ 812.28(c) or a brief statement of the
reason for not conducting the inves-
tigation in accordance with GCP and a
description of steps taken to ensure
that the data and results are credible
and accurate and that the rights, safe-
ty, and well-being of subjects have been
adequately protected.

requirements.topic: clinical investigations conducted outside the United States that are intended to support a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: The application states that the requirements of § 812.28 apply to each foreign investigation and, where an investigation was not conducted in accordance with good clinical practice, includes a waiver request under § 812.28(c) or a brief reason plus a description of steps taken to ensure the data and results are credible and accurate and that subjects' rights, safety and well-being were protected.
requirements.conflicts: The application relies on foreign investigations without addressing § 812.28 or good clinical practice, or says an investigation was not conducted under good clinical practice without a waiver request, a reason, or any description of steps to protect data credibility and subjects.
requirements.hint: For each foreign investigation state that § 812.28 applies and, if good clinical practice was not followed, add a § 812.28(c) waiver request or a reason plus the steps taken to protect data accuracy and subjects.

requirements.title: Single investigation justification
requirements.need: For a PMA supported solely by data from one investigation, the applicant must include a justification showing that data and other information from a single investigator are sufficient to demonstrate safety and effectiveness and to ensure reproducibility of test results.

quote.text:
For a PMA supported solely by
data from one investigation, a jus-
tification showing that data and other
information from a single investigator
are sufficient to demonstrate the safe-
ty and effectiveness of the device and
to ensure reproducibility of test re-
sults.

requirements.topic: a premarket approval application supported solely by data from one investigation
requirements.complies: The application includes a justification explaining that data and other information from a single investigator are sufficient to demonstrate the device's safety and effectiveness and to ensure reproducibility of test results.
requirements.conflicts: The application rests on a single investigation but gives no justification, or only asserts that the data are sufficient without addressing reproducibility of test results.
requirements.hint: When only one investigation supports the application, add a justification covering both safety and effectiveness and reproducibility of test results.

requirements.title: Bibliography and other data
requirements.need: A PMA must include a bibliography of all published reports known or that should reasonably be known concerning safety or effectiveness, an identification, discussion, and analysis of any other relevant data or reports from any source, and copies of published reports or unpublished information if an FDA advisory committee or FDA requests.

quote.text:
A bibliography of all published
reports not submitted under paragraph
(b)(6) of this section, whether adverse
or supportive, known to or that should
reasonably be known to the applicant
and that concern the safety or effec-
tiveness of the device.

requirements.topic: bibliography and other data on device safety or effectiveness in a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: The application includes a bibliography of all published reports known or that should reasonably be known to the applicant concerning the safety or effectiveness of the device, whether adverse or supportive, and identifies, discusses and analyzes other relevant data or reports from any source.
requirements.conflicts: The application lists only supportive publications, omits adverse reports the applicant knew or should have known, or presents other relevant data without identification, discussion or analysis.
requirements.hint: List all known published reports on safety or effectiveness, adverse and supportive, and identify, discuss and analyze any other relevant data.

requirements.title: Device samples
requirements.need: A PMA must include one or more samples of the device and its components if requested by FDA, or if impractical, name the location at which FDA may examine and test one or more devices.

quote.text:
One or more samples of the device
and its components, if requested by
FDA. If it is impractical to submit a
requested sample of the device, the ap-
plicant shall name the location at
which FDA may examine and test one
or more devices.

requirements.topic: submitting device samples or naming a place where FDA can examine and test the device in a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: The application states that one or more samples of the device and its components are included, or, where submitting a sample is impractical, names a specific location where FDA may examine and test one or more devices.
requirements.conflicts: The application neither includes any device sample nor names any location where FDA could examine and test the device, or it says samples will never be made available and gives no alternative location.
requirements.hint: Include device and component samples if FDA requests them, or name a specific location where FDA can examine and test the device.

requirements.title: Proposed labeling copies
requirements.need: A PMA must include copies of all proposed labeling for the device, which may include instructions for installation and any information, literature, or advertising that constitutes labeling under section 201(m) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.

quote.text:
Copies of all proposed labeling
for the device. Such labeling may in-
clude, e.g., instructions for installation
and any information, literature, or ad-
vertising that constitutes labeling
under section 201(m) of the Federal
Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.

requirements.topic: proposed labeling for a medical device in a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: The application contains copies of all proposed labeling, including installation instructions and any information, literature, or advertising that counts as labeling under section 201(m).
requirements.conflicts: The application omits proposed labeling, includes only partial labeling, or leaves out advertising or promotional literature that constitutes labeling under section 201(m).
requirements.hint: Attach copies of every proposed label, installation instruction, and piece of information, literature, or advertising that counts as labeling under section 201(m).

requirements.title: Environmental assessment
requirements.need: A PMA must include an environmental assessment under § 25.20(n) prepared in the format in § 25.40 unless the action qualifies for exclusion under § 25.30 or § 25.34, and if the applicant believes exclusion applies, the PMA must provide information establishing that the action is within the excluded category and meets the exclusion criteria.

quote.text:
An environmental assessment
under § 25.20(n) prepared in the applica-
ble format in § 25.40, unless the action
qualifies for exclusion under § 25.30 or
§ 25.34. If the applicant believes that
the action qualifies for exclusion, the
PMA shall under § 25.15(a) and (d) pro-
vide information that establishes to

21 CFR Ch. I (4–1–25 Edition)§ 814.20

FDA’s satisfaction that the action re-
quested is included within the excluded
category and meets the criteria for the
applicable exclusion.

requirements.topic: environmental assessment or exclusion claim in a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: The application includes an environmental assessment under § 25.20(n) in the § 25.40 format, or, if claiming exclusion, provides information establishing that the action falls within the excluded category and meets the exclusion criteria.
requirements.conflicts: The application has no environmental assessment and no exclusion claim, or it asserts an exclusion without any information showing the action is in the excluded category and meets the criteria.
requirements.hint: Provide an environmental assessment in the § 25.40 format, or supply information establishing that the action qualifies for an exclusion under § 25.30 or § 25.34.

requirements.title: Financial certification or disclosure
requirements.need: A PMA must include a financial certification or disclosure statement or both as required by part 54 of this chapter.

quote.text:
A financial certification or dis-
closure statement or both as required
by part 54 of this chapter.

requirements.topic: financial certification or disclosure for clinical investigators in a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: The application includes a financial certification, a financial disclosure statement, or both as required by part 54.
requirements.conflicts: The application contains no financial certification and no financial disclosure statement, or it states that part 54 financial information was not prepared.
requirements.hint: Include a financial certification, a disclosure statement, or both as required by part 54.

requirements.title: Pediatric use information
requirements.need: A PMA must include, if readily available, a description of any pediatric subpopulations that suffer from the disease or condition the device is intended to treat, diagnose, or cure and the number of affected pediatric patients.

quote.text:
Information concerning uses in pe-
diatric patients. The application must
include the following information, if
readily available:
(i) A description of any pediatric sub-
populations (neonates, infants, chil-
dren, adolescents) that suffer from the
disease or condition that the device is
intended to treat, diagnose, or cure;
and
(ii) The number of affected pediatric
patients.

requirements.topic: pediatric use information for the disease or condition a device treats, diagnoses, or cures
requirements.complies: The application describes, where readily available, the pediatric subpopulations (neonates, infants, children, adolescents) affected by the disease or condition and gives the number of affected pediatric patients.
requirements.conflicts: The application omits any description of affected pediatric subpopulations and any count of affected pediatric patients, or states that pediatric use was not considered at all.
requirements.hint: If readily available, describe the pediatric subpopulations affected by the disease or condition and give the number of affected pediatric patients.

requirements.title: Other requested information
requirements.need: A PMA must include such other information as FDA may request, and FDA will obtain the concurrence of the appropriate FDA advisory committee before requesting additional information if necessary.

quote.text:
Such other information as FDA
may request. If necessary, FDA will ob-
tain the concurrence of the appropriate
FDA advisory committee before re-
questing additional information.

requirements.topic: additional information requested by FDA during review of a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: The application includes the other information FDA requested, and any request for additional information was made with concurrence of the appropriate FDA advisory committee where necessary.
requirements.conflicts: The application omits information FDA requested, or additional information was demanded without obtaining concurrence of the appropriate FDA advisory committee where necessary.
requirements.hint: Include any other information FDA requests, and note that FDA obtains advisory committee concurrence before requesting additional information if necessary.

requirements.title: Incorporation by reference
requirements.need: Pertinent information in FDA files specifically referred to by an applicant may be incorporated into a PMA by reference, but information in a master file or other information submitted by a person other than the applicant will not be considered part of a PMA unless the reference is authorized in a record submitted to FDA by that person, and a master file not referenced within 5 years will be returned.

quote.text:
Pertinent information in FDA
files specifically referred to by an ap-
plicant may be incorporated into a
PMA by reference. Information in a
master file or other information sub-
mitted to FDA by a person other than
the applicant will not be considered
part of a PMA unless such reference is
authorized in a record submitted to
FDA by the person who submitted the
information or the master file. If a
master file is not referenced within 5
years after the date that it is sub-
mitted to FDA, FDA will return the
master file to the person who sub-
mitted it.

requirements.topic: referencing FDA files, master files or other people's submitted information in a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: The applicant cites specific FDA file information by reference in the PMA, and any master file or third-party information is included only with a written authorization record from the person who submitted it to FDA.
requirements.conflicts: The PMA relies on a master file or another person's submitted information without any authorization record from that person, or treats such material as part of the PMA regardless of consent.
requirements.hint: Name each referenced FDA file, and for any master file or third-party information attach the submitter's written authorization to FDA.

requirements.title: Omission justification statement
requirements.need: If the applicant believes certain required information is not applicable and omits it, the applicant must submit a statement identifying the omitted information and justifying the omission as a separate section identified in the table of contents, and FDA will notify the applicant if the justification is not accepted.

quote.text:
If the applicant believes that cer-
tain information required under para-
graph (b) of this section to be in a PMA
is not applicable to the device that is
the subject of the PMA, and omits any
such information from its PMA, the ap-
plicant shall submit a statement that
identifies the omitted information and
justifies the omission. The statement
shall be submitted as a separate sec-
tion in the PMA and identified in the
table of contents. If the justification
for the omission is not accepted by the
agency, FDA will so notify the appli-
cant.

requirements.topic: omitting required information from a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: A separate section listed in the table of contents identifies each omitted item of required information and states why it does not apply to the device.
requirements.conflicts: Required information is left out with no statement, or the justification appears only as an unlabeled remark not identified in the table of contents.
requirements.hint: Put every omission in its own section, list it in the table of contents, and give the reason each item is not applicable to the device.

requirements.title: Pending application updates
requirements.need: The applicant must periodically update its pending application with new safety and effectiveness information learned from ongoing or completed studies that may reasonably affect an evaluation of safety or effectiveness or the contraindications, warnings, precautions, and adverse reactions in draft labeling, submitting updates in electronic format with the FDA-assigned PMA number 3 months after the filing date, following receipt of an approvable letter, and at other times as FDA requests.

quote.text:
The applicant shall periodically
update its pending application with
new safety and effectiveness informa-
tion learned about the device from on-
going or completed studies that may
reasonably affect an evaluation of the
safety or effectiveness of the device or
that may reasonably affect the state-
ment of contraindications, warnings,
precautions, and adverse reactions in
the draft labeling. The update report
shall be consistent with the data re-
porting provisions of the protocol. The
applicant shall submit any update re-
port in electronic format and shall in-
clude in the report the number as-
signed by FDA to the PMA.

requirements.topic: updating a pending premarket approval application with new safety and effectiveness information
requirements.complies: The applicant sends electronic update reports carrying the FDA-assigned PMA number, covering new study findings that could affect the safety or effectiveness evaluation or the draft labeling's contraindications, warnings, precautions and adverse reactions, at 3 months after filing, after an approvable letter, and when FDA asks.
requirements.conflicts: New study findings that could affect safety, effectiveness or draft labeling are never reported, or updates are sent on paper without the PMA number and outside the required times.
requirements.hint: Submit electronic update reports with the PMA number at 3 months after filing, after any approvable letter, and whenever FDA requests, describing new study findings and any labeling changes.

requirements.title: Color additive information
requirements.need: If a color additive subject to section 721 is used in or on the device and has not previously been listed for such use, the applicant may submit the part 71 information as part of the PMA in electronic format, and the PMA will not be approved until the color additive is listed for use in or on the device.

quote.text:
If a color additive subject to sec-
tion 721 of the Federal Food, Drug, and
Cosmetic Act is used in or on the de-
vice and has not previously been listed
for such use, then, in lieu of submitting
a color additive petition under part 71
of this chapter, at the option of the ap-
plicant, the information required to be
submitted under part 71 may be sub-
mitted as part of the PMA. When sub-
mitted as part of the PMA, the infor-
mation shall be submitted in electronic
format. A PMA for a device that con-
tains a color additive that is subject to
section 721 of the Federal Food, Drug,
and Cosmetic Act will not be approved
until the color additive is listed for use
in or on the device.

requirements.topic: using a color additive in or on a device in a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: The applicant states the color additive has not been listed for this use and submits the part 71 information electronically within the PMA, acknowledging approval waits until the additive is listed for the device.
requirements.conflicts: The PMA uses an unlisted color additive with no part 71 information, or claims the device can be approved before the additive is listed for that use.
requirements.hint: If the color additive is not yet listed for this use, include the part 71 information electronically in the PMA and note that approval waits for listing.

requirements.title: Filing determination notice
requirements.need: The filing of an application means FDA has made a threshold determination that the application is sufficiently complete to permit substantive review, and within 45 days after a PMA is received FDA will notify the applicant whether the application has been filed.

quote.text:
The filing of an application means
that FDA has made a threshold deter-
mination that the application is suffi-
ciently complete to permit a sub-
stantive review. Within 45 days after a
PMA is received by FDA, the agency
will notify the applicant whether the
application has been filed.

requirements.topic: FDA filing decisions on premarket approval applications
requirements.complies: The text explains that filing means FDA judged the application complete enough for substantive review and that FDA notifies the applicant within 45 days of receipt whether it has been filed.
requirements.conflicts: The text says filing means the device is approved, or states FDA has no deadline for telling the applicant whether the application was filed.
requirements.hint: Describe filing as a completeness threshold and state that FDA notifies the applicant within 45 days of receiving the PMA.

requirements.title: Filing notice content
requirements.need: If none of the reasons for refusing to file applies, FDA will file the PMA and notify the applicant in writing of the filing, including the PMA reference number and the date FDA filed the PMA, and the 180-day review period starts on the date of filing.

quote.text:
If FDA does not find that any of
the reasons in paragraph (e) of this sec-
tion for refusing to file the PMA ap-
plies, the agency will file the PMA and
will notify the applicant in writing of
the filing. The notice will include the
PMA reference number and the date
FDA filed the PMA. The date of filing
is the date that a PMA accepted for fil-
ing was received by the agency. The
180-day period for review of a PMA
starts on the date of filing.

requirements.topic: FDA written filing notices and review timing for premarket approval applications
requirements.complies: The text says FDA files the PMA when no refusal reason applies, sends a written notice giving the PMA reference number and the filing date, and counts the 180-day review period from that filing date.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the 180-day review starts on the date the application was received rather than filed, or that the filing notice need not include the PMA reference number or filing date.
requirements.hint: State that the written filing notice includes the PMA reference number and filing date, and that the 180-day review runs from the date of filing.

requirements.title: Refusal to file notice
requirements.need: If FDA refuses to file a PMA, the agency will notify the applicant of the reasons for the refusal, identifying the deficiencies that prevent filing and including the PMA reference number.

quote.text:
If FDA refuses to file a PMA, the
agency will notify the applicant of the
reasons for the refusal. This notice will
identify the deficiencies in the applica-
tion that prevent filing and will in-
clude the PMA reference number.

requirements.topic: FDA refusing to file a premarket approval application (PMA) and notifying the applicant
requirements.complies: The notice states the reasons FDA refused to file the PMA, lists the specific deficiencies in the application that prevent filing, and includes the PMA reference number.
requirements.conflicts: The notice refuses to file the PMA without giving any reasons, does not identify which deficiencies prevented filing, or omits the PMA reference number.
requirements.hint: When describing a refusal-to-file notice, say it gives the reasons, names the deficiencies that prevent filing, and cites the PMA reference number.

requirements.title: Options after refusal
requirements.need: If FDA refuses to file the PMA, the applicant may resubmit with additional information necessary to comply with section 515(c)(1)(A)-(G) and § 814.20 including the original PMA reference number, or request in writing within 10 working days an informal conference with the Director of the associated Office of Health Technology, with FDA holding the conference within 10 working days and rendering its decision within 5 working days.

quote.text:
If FDA refuses to file the PMA,
the applicant may:
(1) Resubmit the PMA with addi-
tional information necessary to comply
with the requirements of section
515(c)(1) (A)–(G) of the act and § 814.20.
A resubmitted PMA shall include the
PMA reference number of the original
submission. If the resubmitted PMA is
accepted for filing, the date of filing is
the date FDA receives the resubmis-
sion;
(2) Request in writing within 10
working days of the date of receipt of
the notice refusing to file the PMA, an
informal conference with the Director
of the associated Office of Health Tech-
nology to review FDA’s decision not to
file the PMA.

requirements.topic: what an applicant can do after FDA refuses to file a PMA
requirements.complies: The applicant either resubmits the PMA with the additional information needed to meet section 515(c)(1)(A)-(G) and § 814.20, including the original PMA reference number, or requests in writing within 10 working days an informal conference with the Director of the associated Office of Health Technology.
requirements.conflicts: The applicant is described as having no option after refusal, or as resubmitting without the original PMA reference number, or as requesting a conference later than 10 working days after receiving the refusal notice or not in writing.
requirements.hint: List the two options: resubmission with the needed information and the original PMA reference number, or a written informal conference request within 10 working days.

requirements.title: Grounds to refuse filing
requirements.need: FDA may refuse to file a PMA if the application is incomplete because it does not on its face contain all information required under section 515(c)(1)(A)-(G), does not contain each item required under § 814.20 and any omission justification is inadequate, the applicant has a pending 510(k) for the same device and FDA has not determined whether the device falls within § 814.1(c), the PMA contains a false statement of material fact, or the PMA is not accompanied by a part 54 certification or disclosure statement.

quote.text:
FDA may refuse to file a PMA if
any of the following applies:
(1) The application is incomplete be-
cause it does not on its face contain all
the information required under section
515(c)(1) (A)–(G) of the act;
(2) The PMA does not contain each of
the items required under § 814.20 and
justification for omission of any item
is inadequate;
(3) The applicant has a pending pre-
market notification under section
510(k) of the act with respect to the
same device, and FDA has not deter-
mined whether the device falls within
the scope of § 814.1(c).
(4) The PMA contains a false state-
ment of material fact.
(5) The PMA is not accompanied by a
statement of either certification or dis-
closure as required by part 54 of this
chapter.

requirements.topic: grounds on which FDA may refuse to file a PMA
requirements.complies: The text states FDA may refuse to file when the application on its face lacks information required under section 515(c)(1)(A)-(G), when a required § 814.20 item is missing and its omission justification is inadequate, when a 510(k) for the same device is pending and scope under § 814.1(c) is undetermined, when the PMA contains a false statement of material fact, or when the part 54 certification or disclosure statement is missing.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA must file every PMA regardless of missing required information, missing § 814.20 items, a pending 510(k) for the same device, a false statement of material fact, or a missing part 54 certification or disclosure statement.
requirements.hint: Describe the five listed grounds for refusing to file, including missing required information, inadequate omission justification, a pending 510(k) for the same device, a false material statement, and a missing part 54 statement.

requirements.title: Substantive review and panel referral
requirements.need: FDA will begin substantive review of a PMA after it is accepted for filing, may refer the PMA to a panel on its own initiative and will do so upon request of an applicant unless the application substantially duplicates information previously reviewed by a panel, and FDA will maintain a record of all communications with the applicant and the panel.

cant, unless FDA determines that the
application substantially duplicates in-
formation previously reviewed by a
panel. If FDA refers an application to a
panel, FDA will forward the PMA, or
relevant portions thereof, to each
member of the appropriate FDA panel
for review. During the review process,
