requirements.topic: FDA substantive review of a filed PMA and referral to an advisory panel
requirements.complies: The text says FDA begins substantive review after the PMA is accepted for filing, may refer it to a panel on its own initiative and will do so at the applicant's request unless it substantially duplicates information a panel already reviewed, and keeps a record of all communications with the applicant and the panel.
requirements.conflicts: The text says review starts before the PMA is accepted for filing, that FDA will never refer a PMA to a panel even when the applicant requests it, or that no record of communications with the applicant or panel is kept.
requirements.hint: State that substantive review follows acceptance for filing, that panel referral happens on FDA's initiative or the applicant's request unless the application substantially duplicates prior panel review, and that communications are recorded.

requirements.title: Advisory committee report
requirements.need: The advisory committee must submit a report to FDA including its recommendation and the basis for it on the PMA, and before submission the committee must hold a public meeting to review the PMA in accordance with part 14, which may be held by telephone conference.

quote.text:
The advisory committee shall
submit a report to FDA which includes
the committee’s recommendation and
the basis for such recommendation on
the PMA. Before submission of this re-
port, the committee shall hold a public
meeting to review the PMA in accord-
ance with part 14. This meeting may be
held by a telephone conference under
§ 14.22(g). The advisory committee re-
port and recommendation may be in
the form of a meeting transcript signed
by the chairperson of the committee.

requirements.topic: advisory committee review of a PMA and its report to FDA
requirements.complies: The advisory committee holds a public meeting under part 14 to review the PMA, which may be a telephone conference under § 14.22(g), and then submits a report giving its recommendation and the basis for it, possibly as a meeting transcript signed by the chairperson.
requirements.conflicts: The advisory committee submits a report with no recommendation or no basis for it, or issues its report without first holding a public meeting to review the PMA.
requirements.hint: Say the committee holds a public meeting (which may be by telephone conference) before sending FDA a report with its recommendation and the reasons for it.

requirements.title: Review completion and action
requirements.need: FDA will complete its review of the PMA and the advisory committee report and recommendation and, within the later of 180 days from the date of filing or the number of days determined under § 814.37(c), issue an approval order, an approvable letter, a not approvable letter, or an order denying approval.

quote.text:
FDA will complete its review of
the PMA and the advisory committee
report and recommendation and, with-
in the later of 180 days from the date of
filing of the PMA under § 814.42 or the
number of days after the date of filing
as determined under § 814.37(c), issue an
approval order under paragraph (d) of
this section, an approvable letter under
paragraph (e) of this section, a not ap-
provable letter under paragraph (f) of
this section, or an order denying ap-
proval of the application under
§ 814.45(a).

requirements.topic: FDA completing review of a PMA and issuing a decision
requirements.complies: The text says FDA completes review of the PMA and the advisory committee report and recommendation and, within the later of 180 days from filing or the period set under § 814.37(c), issues an approval order, an approvable letter, a not approvable letter, or an order denying approval.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA issues no decision, or issues a decision on a different timeline than the later of 180 days from filing or the § 814.37(c) period, or issues some other outcome not among the four listed actions.
requirements.hint: State that FDA finishes review of the PMA and the advisory committee report and issues one of the four listed actions within the later of 180 days from filing or the § 814.37(c) period.

requirements.title: Amending pending PMA
requirements.need: An applicant may amend a pending PMA or PMA supplement to revise existing information or provide additional information.

quote.text:
An applicant may amend a pend-
ing PMA or PMA supplement to revise
existing information or provide addi-
tional information.

requirements.topic: amending a pending premarket approval application or its supplement
requirements.complies: The text states that an applicant may amend a pending PMA or PMA supplement to revise existing information or to provide additional information.
requirements.conflicts: The text states that a pending PMA or PMA supplement cannot be amended, or that changes to existing information or added information are not allowed before FDA decides the application.
requirements.hint: Say that an applicant may amend a pending PMA or PMA supplement, either to revise existing information or to add new information.

requirements.title: FDA-requested amendments
requirements.need: FDA may request the applicant to amend a PMA or PMA supplement with any information regarding the device necessary for FDA or the appropriate advisory committee to complete review, and with information concerning pediatric uses as required under §§ 814.20(b)(13) and 814.39(c)(2).

quote.text:
FDA may request the applicant
to amend a PMA or PMA supplement
with any information regarding the de-
vice that is necessary for FDA or the
appropriate advisory committee to
complete the review of the PMA or
PMA supplement.
(2) FDA may request the applicant to
amend a PMA or PMA supplement with
information concerning pediatric uses
as required under §§ 814.20(b)(13) and
814.39(c)(2).

requirements.topic: FDA requests for more information on a pending premarket approval application or supplement
requirements.complies: The text states that FDA may ask the applicant to amend a PMA or PMA supplement with any device information needed for FDA or the advisory committee to finish review, and with pediatric use information required under §§ 814.20(b)(13) and 814.39(c)(2).
requirements.conflicts: The text states that FDA cannot ask applicants for additional device information during review, or that pediatric use information under §§ 814.20(b)(13) and 814.39(c)(2) need not be provided on request.
requirements.hint: State that FDA may request an amendment with any device information needed to complete review and with the pediatric use information required by §§ 814.20(b)(13) and 814.39(c)(2).

requirements.title: Amendment content and review extension
requirements.need: A PMA amendment must include the PMA or PMA supplement number assigned to the original submission and, if submitted on the applicant's own initiative, the reason for submitting it, and FDA may extend the review period up to 180 days for a major amendment or for the number of days elapsing when an applicant declines to submit a requested major amendment.

quote.text:
A PMA amendment submitted to
FDA shall include the PMA or PMA
supplement number assigned to the
original submission and, if submitted
on the applicant’s own initiative, the
reason for submitting the amendment.
FDA may extend the time required for
its review of the PMA, or PMA supple-
ment, as follows:
(1) If the applicant on its own initia-
tive or at FDA’s request submits a
major PMA amendment (e.g., an
amendment that contains significant
new data from a previously unreported
study, significant updated data from a
previously reported study, detailed new
analyses of previously submitted data,
or significant required information
previously omitted), the review period
may be extended up to 180 days.

requirements.topic: contents of a premarket approval amendment and extension of the review period
requirements.complies: The text states that an amendment must include the PMA or PMA supplement number from the original submission and, if the applicant submits it on its own initiative, the reason for submitting it, and that FDA may extend review by up to 180 days for a major amendment or by the number of days lost when the applicant declines to submit a requested major amendment.
requirements.conflicts: The text states that an amendment needs no PMA or PMA supplement number or reason for submission, or that FDA cannot extend its review period for a major amendment or for a declined requested major amendment.
requirements.hint: Require the original PMA or PMA supplement number and, for applicant-initiated amendments, the reason, and note FDA's power to extend review up to 180 days for a major amendment or for days lost when a requested major amendment is declined.

requirements.title: Withdrawal of PMA
requirements.need: An applicant may on its own initiative withdraw a PMA or PMA supplement, and if FDA requests a PMA amendment and no written response is received within 180 days of the request, FDA will consider the pending PMA or PMA supplement voluntarily withdrawn by the applicant.

quote.text:
An applicant may on its own ini-
tiative withdraw a PMA or PMA sup-
plement. If FDA requests an applicant
to submit a PMA amendment and a
written response to FDA’s request is
not received within 180 days of the date
of the request, FDA will consider the
pending PMA or PMA supplement to be
withdrawn voluntarily by the appli-
cant.

requirements.topic: withdrawing a premarket approval application or supplement
requirements.complies: The text states that an applicant may withdraw a PMA or PMA supplement on its own initiative, and that if no written response to an FDA request for an amendment arrives within 180 days of the request, FDA will treat the pending PMA or PMA supplement as voluntarily withdrawn.
requirements.conflicts: The text states that applicants cannot withdraw a PMA or PMA supplement themselves, or that a pending application stays active indefinitely when the applicant never answers an FDA amendment request in writing.
requirements.hint: State that applicants may withdraw on their own initiative and that no written response to an FDA amendment request within 180 days means FDA treats the submission as voluntarily withdrawn.

requirements.title: Resubmission requirements
requirements.need: An applicant may resubmit a PMA or PMA supplement after withdrawal, after it is considered withdrawn, after FDA refuses to accept it for filing, or after denial of approval, and the resubmission must comply with § 814.20 or § 814.39 and include the PMA number assigned to the original submission and the applicant's reasons for resubmission.

quote.text:
An applicant may resubmit a
PMA or PMA supplement after with-
drawing it or after it is considered
withdrawn under paragraph (d) of this
section, or after FDA has refused to ac-
cept it for filing, or has denied ap-
proval of the PMA or PMA supplement.
A resubmitted PMA or PMA supple-
ment shall comply with the require-
ments of § 814.20 or § 814.39, respec-
tively, and shall include the PMA num-
ber assigned to the original submission
and the applicant’s reasons for resub-
mission of the PMA or PMA supple-
ment.

requirements.topic: resubmitting a premarket approval application or supplement after withdrawal, refusal to file or denial
requirements.complies: The text states that an applicant may resubmit after withdrawing, after the submission is considered withdrawn, after FDA refuses to accept it for filing, or after FDA denies approval, and that the resubmission must meet § 814.20 or § 814.39 and include the original PMA number and the applicant's reasons for resubmitting.
requirements.conflicts: The text states that a withdrawn, refused or denied PMA or PMA supplement can never be resubmitted, or that a resubmission need not follow § 814.20 or § 814.39 or include the original PMA number and reasons for resubmission.
requirements.hint: Say resubmission is allowed after withdrawal, deemed withdrawal, refusal to file or denial, and that it must follow § 814.20 or § 814.39 and carry the original PMA number and the reasons for resubmitting.

requirements.title: Supplement before safety change
requirements.need: After FDA approval of a PMA, an applicant must submit a PMA supplement for review and approval before making a change affecting the safety or effectiveness of the device, unless FDA has advised that an alternate submission is permitted or the change does not require a supplement, including new indications, labeling changes, different manufacturing facility, sterilization or packaging changes, performance or design changes, and expiration date extensions based on unapproved testing protocols.

quote.text:
After FDA’s approval of a PMA,
an applicant shall submit a PMA sup-
plement for review and approval by
FDA before making a change affecting
the safety or effectiveness of the device
for which the applicant has an ap-
proved PMA, unless the change is of a
type for which FDA, under paragraph
(e) of this section, has advised that an
alternate submission is permitted or is
of a type which, under section
515(d)(6)(A) of the act and paragraph (f)
of this section, does not require a PMA
supplement under this paragraph.

requirements.topic: submitting a supplement before changing an approved device in ways that affect safety or effectiveness
requirements.complies: The text states that after PMA approval the applicant must submit a PMA supplement and get FDA review and approval before making a change affecting safety or effectiveness, unless FDA has advised that an alternate submission is permitted or the change does not require a supplement.
requirements.conflicts: The text states that an applicant may make changes affecting safety or effectiveness, such as new indications, labeling changes, a different manufacturing facility, sterilization or packaging changes, performance or design changes, or expiration date extensions based on unapproved testing protocols, without first submitting and getting approval of a PMA supplement.
requirements.hint: State that changes affecting safety or effectiveness need a PMA supplement reviewed and approved before the change, unless FDA has allowed an alternate submission or the change needs no supplement.

requirements.title: Changes without supplement
requirements.need: An applicant may make a change after PMA approval without submitting a PMA supplement if the change does not affect safety or effectiveness and is reported in post approval periodic reports required as a condition to approval, or if the change is consistent with an approved predetermined change control plan.

quote.text:
An applicant may make a change
in a device after FDA’s approval of a
PMA for the device without submitting
a PMA supplement if the change does
not affect the device’s safety or effec-
tiveness and the change is reported to
FDA in post approval periodic reports
required as a condition to approval of
the device, e.g., an editorial change in
labeling which does not affect the safe-
ty or effectiveness of the device, or if
the change is consistent with a pre-
determined change control plan (PCCP)
approved under section 515C of the act.

requirements.topic: changing an approved medical device after PMA approval and whether a PMA supplement must be filed
requirements.complies: The text says the change does not affect the device's safety or effectiveness and is reported to FDA in post approval periodic reports required as a condition of approval, or that the change follows an approved predetermined change control plan (PCCP). It gives an example such as an editorial labeling change that does not affect safety or effectiveness.
requirements.conflicts: The text says a change that affects safety or effectiveness was made without submitting a PMA supplement and without reporting it in post approval periodic reports, or says a change was made outside any approved predetermined change control plan.
requirements.hint: State that the change does not affect safety or effectiveness and is reported in post approval periodic reports, or that it is consistent with an approved PCCP.

requirements.title: Supplement content
requirements.need: All procedures and actions that apply to an application under § 814.20 also apply to PMA supplements except that the information required is limited to that needed to support the change, a summary is required only for certain supplements, the supplement must be submitted in electronic format with a separate section identifying each change and the reason, and must include pediatric use information or reference a previous submission.

quote.text:
All procedures and actions that
apply to an application under § 814.20
also apply to PMA supplements except
that the information required in a sup-
plement is limited to that needed to
support the change. A summary under
§ 814.20(b)(3) is required for only a sup-
plement submitted for new indications
for use of the device, significant
changes in the performance or design
specifications, circuits, components,
ingredients, principles of operation, or
physical layout of the device, or when
otherwise required by FDA.

requirements.topic: the content and format of a PMA supplement submission
requirements.complies: The text says the supplement contains only the information needed to support the change, includes a summary only for new indications, significant changes in performance or design specifications, circuits, components, ingredients, principles of operation or physical layout, or when FDA requires one, is submitted electronically with a separate section identifying each change and its reason, and includes pediatric use information or references a previous submission.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the supplement repeats the full original application content, omits the separate section identifying each change and its reason, is filed on paper, or leaves out pediatric use information without referencing a prior submission.
requirements.hint: Describe the supplement as limited to information supporting the change, electronic, with a separate section listing each change and its reason, and with pediatric use information or a reference to a prior submission.

requirements.title: Changes being effected
requirements.need: After PMA approval, certain changes reflecting newly acquired information that enhances device safety may be placed into effect before receipt of a written FDA order approving the supplement if the supplement and mailing cover are marked "Special PMA Supplement—Changes Being Effected," provide a full explanation of the basis, the applicant has received FDA acknowledgement of receipt, and the supplement identifies the date the changes are being effected.

quote.text:
After FDA approves a PMA,
any change described in paragraph
(d)(2) of this section to reflect newly
acquired information that enhances
the safety of the device or the safety in
the use of the device may be placed
into effect by the applicant prior to the
receipt under § 814.17 of a written FDA
order approving the PMA supplement
provided that:
(i) The PMA supplement and its mail-
ing cover are plainly marked ‘‘Special
PMA Supplement—Changes Being Ef-
fected’’;
(ii) The PMA supplement provides a
full explanation of the basis for the
changes;
(iii) The applicant has received ac-
knowledgement from FDA of receipt of
the supplement; and
(iv) The PMA supplement specifically
identifies the date that such changes
are being effected.

requirements.topic: putting a safety-enhancing device change into effect before FDA approves the PMA supplement
requirements.complies: The text says the change reflects newly acquired information that enhances device safety or safety in use, the supplement and mailing cover are marked "Special PMA Supplement—Changes Being Effected," it gives a full explanation of the basis, FDA has acknowledged receipt, and it identifies the date the changes are being effected.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the change was made before FDA approval without the special marking, without a full explanation of the basis, before FDA acknowledged receipt, or without stating the date the changes are being effected.
requirements.hint: List all four conditions: the special marking, the full explanation of the basis, FDA acknowledgement of receipt, and the date the changes are being effected.

requirements.title: Reporting identified changes
requirements.need: FDA will identify a change for which a PMA supplement is not required and require it to be reported in a periodic report under § 814.84 or a 30-day PMA supplement, and a change reported in a 30-day PMA supplement may be made 30 days after FDA files the supplement unless FDA requires additional information, informs the holder the supplement is not approvable, or disapproves it.

quote.text:
FDA will identify a change to a
device for which an applicant has an
approved PMA and for which a PMA
supplement under paragraph (a) is not
required. FDA will identify such a
change in an advisory opinion under
§ 10.85, if the change applies to a ge-
neric type of device, or in correspond-
ence to the applicant, if the change ap-
plies only to the applicant’s device.
FDA will require that a change for
which a PMA supplement under para-
graph (a) is not required be reported to
FDA in:
(i) A periodic report under § 814.84 or
(ii) A 30-day PMA supplement under
this paragraph.

requirements.topic: reporting device changes that FDA says do not need a PMA supplement
requirements.complies: The text says FDA identified the change in an advisory opinion or in correspondence to the applicant and required it to be reported in a periodic report under § 814.84 or in a 30-day PMA supplement, and that a change in a 30-day supplement was made 30 days after FDA filed it because FDA did not request more information, did not say it was not approvable, and did not disapprove it.
requirements.conflicts: The text says a change FDA identified as not needing a supplement was never reported, or that a 30-day supplement change was made before 30 days or after FDA requested additional information, said the supplement was not approvable, or disapproved it.
requirements.hint: Say how FDA identified the change and that it was reported in a periodic report or a 30-day supplement, and note the 30-day timing conditions.

requirements.title: 30-day notice for manufacturing
requirements.need: Modifications to manufacturing procedures or methods of manufacture that affect safety and effectiveness of a device subject to an approved PMA do not require a PMA supplement and are eligible for a 30-day notice describing the change in detail, summarizing supporting data, and stating compliance with part 820, and the manufacturer may distribute the device 30 days after FDA receives the notice unless FDA notifies the applicant the notice is not adequate.

quote.text:
Under section 515(d) of the act,
modifications to manufacturing proce-
dures or methods of manufacture that
affect the safety and effectiveness of a
device subject to an approved PMA do
not require submission of a PMA sup-
plement under paragraph (a) of this
section and are eligible to be the sub-
ject of a 30-day notice. A 30-day notice
shall describe in detail the change,
summarize the data or information
supporting the change, and state that
the change has been made in accord-
ance with the requirements of part 820
of this chapter. The manufacturer may
distribute the device 30 days after the
date on which FDA receives the 30-day
notice, unless FDA notifies the appli-
cant within 30 days from receipt of the
notice that the notice is not adequate.

requirements.topic: manufacturing changes to an approved device reported through a 30-day notice
requirements.complies: The text says the manufacturing procedure or method change affects safety and effectiveness, a 30-day notice describes the change in detail, summarizes the supporting data or information, and states the change was made in accordance with part 820, and the device is distributed 30 days after FDA receives the notice unless FDA says the notice is not adequate.
requirements.conflicts: The text says a manufacturing change affecting safety and effectiveness was made with no 30-day notice, or the notice lacks a detailed description, supporting data summary, or part 820 compliance statement, or the device was distributed before 30 days or after FDA said the notice was not adequate.
requirements.hint: Describe the 30-day notice contents (detailed change, supporting data summary, part 820 compliance statement) and the 30-day distribution timing with the FDA adequacy exception.

requirements.title: Exception or alternative request
requirements.need: The submission and grant of a written request for an exception or alternative under § 801.128 or § 809.11 satisfies the requirement to submit a PMA supplement before making a change affecting safety or effectiveness.

quote.text:
The submission and grant of a
written request for an exception or al-
ternative under § 801.128 or § 809.11 of
this chapter satisfies the requirement
in paragraph (a) of this section.

requirements.topic: using an exception or alternative request in place of a PMA supplement for a device change
requirements.complies: The text says a written request for an exception or alternative under § 801.128 or § 809.11 was submitted and granted, and that this satisfies the requirement to submit a PMA supplement before making the change.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the change affecting safety or effectiveness was made relying on an exception or alternative request that was never submitted or never granted, or claims such a request is not needed.
requirements.hint: State that the written exception or alternative request under § 801.128 or § 809.11 was both submitted and granted before the change was made.

requirements.title: 180-day review time frame
requirements.need: Within 180 days after receipt of an application accepted for filing and to which the applicant does not submit a major amendment, FDA will review the PMA and, after receiving the advisory committee report and recommendation, send an approval order, approvable letter, not approvable letter, or order denying approval, and the approvable and not approvable letters provide an opportunity to amend or withdraw or to consider the letter a denial and request administrative review.

quote.text:
Within 180 days after receipt of an
application that is accepted for filing
and to which the applicant does not
submit a major amendment, FDA will
review the PMA and, after receiving
the report and recommendation of the
appropriate FDA advisory committee,
send the applicant an approval order
under § 814.44(d), an approvable letter
under § 814.44(e), a not approvable letter
under § 814.44(f), or an order denying ap-
proval under § 814.45.

requirements.topic: FDA review timeline and decision letters for premarket approval applications
requirements.complies: The text states that FDA will review the PMA and, within 180 days of receiving an application accepted for filing with no major amendment submitted, send an approval order, approvable letter, not approvable letter, or order denying approval after receiving the advisory committee report and recommendation, and that the letters allow amendment, withdrawal, or a request for administrative review.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA has no deadline for acting on a PMA, or that review continues indefinitely regardless of the 180-day period, or that no decision letter or opportunity to amend, withdraw, or seek review is provided.
requirements.hint: Describe the 180-day review clock, the four possible decision documents, and the applicant's options after an approvable or not approvable letter.

requirements.title: Approval order and labeling condition
requirements.need: FDA will issue an order approving a PMA if none of the reasons for denial applies, and may approve on the basis of draft final labeling if the only deficiencies are editorial or similar minor labeling deficiencies, conditioned upon the applicant incorporating the specified labeling changes exactly as directed and submitting a copy of the final printed labeling before marketing.

quote.text:
FDA will issue to the applicant
an order approving a PMA if none of
the reasons in § 814.45 for denying ap-
proval of the application applies. FDA
will approve an application on the
basis of draft final labeling if the only
deficiencies in the application concern
editorial or similar minor deficiencies
in the draft final labeling. Such ap-
proval will be conditioned upon the ap-
plicant incorporating the specified la-
beling changes exactly as directed and
upon the applicant submitting to FDA
a copy of the final printed labeling be-
fore marketing.

requirements.topic: FDA approval orders for premarket approval applications and labeling deficiencies
requirements.complies: The text states that FDA issues an approval order when none of the denial reasons applies, and may approve based on draft final labeling when the only problems are editorial or similar minor labeling deficiencies, conditioned on the applicant making the specified labeling changes exactly as directed and submitting the final printed labeling before marketing.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA approves a PMA even though denial reasons apply, or that approval based on draft labeling carries no condition, or that the applicant may change the labeling as it sees fit and market before submitting final printed labeling.
requirements.hint: State that approval issues when no denial reason applies, and that draft-labeling approval is conditioned on exact incorporation of specified changes and submission of final printed labeling before marketing.

requirements.title: Approvable letter conditions
requirements.need: FDA will send an approvable letter if the application substantially meets the requirements and FDA believes it can approve if specific additional information is submitted or conditions are agreed to, describing the required information or conditions such as final labeling, pediatric use information, an FDA inspection finding compliance with part 820, restrictions imposed on the device, and postapproval requirements.

quote.text:
FDA will send the applicant an
approvable letter if the application
substantially meets the requirements
of this part and the agency believes it
can approve the application if specific
additional information is submitted or
specific conditions are agreed to by the
applicant.
(1) The approvable letter will de-
scribe the information FDA requires to
be provided by the applicant or the
conditions the applicant is required to
meet to obtain approval.

requirements.topic: FDA approvable letters for premarket approval applications
requirements.complies: The text states that FDA sends an approvable letter when the application substantially meets the requirements and FDA believes it can approve if specific additional information is submitted or specific conditions are agreed to, and that the letter describes the required information or conditions, such as final labeling, pediatric use information, an inspection finding compliance with part 820, device restrictions, and postapproval requirements.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA sends an approvable letter without stating what information or conditions are needed, or claims approval is guaranteed with no further submissions or agreements.
requirements.hint: Explain that an approvable letter lists the specific additional information or conditions the applicant must provide or agree to before approval.

requirements.title: Not approvable letter response
requirements.need: An applicant responding to a not approvable letter may amend the PMA as requested (a major amendment), treat the letter as a denial and request administrative review by petition for reconsideration, or withdraw the PMA.

quote.text:
In response to a not approvable
letter, the applicant may:
(1) Amend the PMA as requested in
the not approvable letter (such an
amendment will be considered a major
amendment under § 814.37(c)(1)); or
(2) Consider the not approvable letter
to be a denial of approval of the PMA
under § 814.45 and request administra-
tive review under section 515(d)(4) of
the act by filing a petition in the form
of a petition for reconsideration under
§ 10.33; or
(3) Withdraw the PMA.

requirements.topic: applicant responses to a not approvable letter on a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: The text states that in response to a not approvable letter the applicant may amend the PMA as requested, which counts as a major amendment, treat the letter as a denial and request administrative review by filing a petition for reconsideration, or withdraw the PMA.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the applicant has no way to respond to a not approvable letter, or lists responses other than amending, seeking administrative review, or withdrawing.
requirements.hint: List the three permitted responses: amend as requested, treat as denial and petition for reconsideration, or withdraw.

requirements.title: Voluntary withdrawal of PMA
requirements.need: A PMA is considered voluntarily withdrawn if the applicant fails to respond in writing to a written request for an amendment or to an approvable or not approvable letter within 180 days, or submits written notice of withdrawal.

quote.text:
FDA will consider a PMA to have
been withdrawn voluntarily if:
(1) The applicant fails to respond in
writing to a written request for an
amendment within 180 days after the
date FDA issues such request;
(2) The applicant fails to respond in
writing to an approvable or not approv-
able letter within 180 days after the
date FDA issues such letter; or
(3) The applicant submits a written
notice to FDA that the PMA has been
withdrawn.

requirements.topic: voluntary withdrawal of a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: The text states that a PMA is considered voluntarily withdrawn if the applicant fails to respond in writing within 180 days to a written request for an amendment or to an approvable or not approvable letter, or if the applicant submits written notice that the PMA is withdrawn.
requirements.conflicts: The text says a PMA stays active no matter how long the applicant fails to respond, or that withdrawal requires something other than the 180-day nonresponse or a written notice.
requirements.hint: State the 180-day written-response deadlines and the written notice option as the triggers for voluntary withdrawal.

requirements.title: Consistency with approval conditions
requirements.need: A device may not be manufactured, packaged, stored, labeled, distributed, or advertised in a manner inconsistent with any conditions to approval specified in the PMA approval order.

quote.text:
A device may not be manufactured,
packaged, stored, labeled, distributed,
or advertised in a manner that is in-
consistent with any conditions to ap-
proval specified in the PMA approval
order for the device.

requirements.topic: manufacturing, labeling, distribution and advertising of a device approved under a PMA
requirements.complies: The text states that the device is manufactured, packaged, stored, labeled, distributed, and advertised only in ways consistent with the conditions to approval in the PMA approval order.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the company may manufacture, label, distribute, or advertise the device in ways that differ from the conditions in the PMA approval order.
requirements.hint: Say that all manufacturing, packaging, storage, labeling, distribution, and advertising must match the conditions in the PMA approval order.

requirements.title: Imposed postapproval requirements
requirements.need: FDA may impose postapproval requirements in a PMA approval order or by regulation, including sale or use restrictions, continuing evaluation and periodic reporting, labeling warnings, identification codes, record maintenance, periodic reports, and batch testing.

quote.text:
FDA may impose postapproval re-
quirements in a PMA approval order or
by regulation at the time of approval
of the PMA or by regulation subse-
quent to approval. Postapproval re-
quirements may include as a condition
to approval of the device:
(1) Restriction of the sale, distribu-
tion, or use of the device as provided by
section 515(d)(1)(B)(ii) or 520(e) of the
act.

requirements.topic: conditions FDA places on a device after it approves a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: The text states that FDA can attach conditions to a PMA approval or add them later by regulation, and lists examples such as restricting sale, distribution or use, continuing evaluation, periodic reporting, labeling warnings, identification codes, record keeping and batch testing.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA cannot add any conditions once a PMA is approved, or that approval is unconditional and the sponsor has no ongoing obligations.
requirements.hint: Describe the postapproval conditions FDA may impose at or after PMA approval, naming the listed examples such as sale or use restrictions and periodic reporting.

requirements.title: Patient tracing records
requirements.need: The applicant must maintain records enabling submission of information needed to trace patients if necessary to protect the public health, with patient identity disclosed only to the extent required for medical welfare, safety or effectiveness determination, or record verification.

quote.text:
Maintenance of records that will
enable the applicant to submit to FDA
information needed to trace patients if
such information is necessary to pro-
tect the public health. Under section
519(a)(4) of the act, FDA will require
that the identity of any patient be dis-
closed in records maintained under this
paragraph only to the extent required
for the medical welfare of the indi-
vidual, to determine the safety or ef-
fectiveness of the device, or to verify a
record, report, or information sub-
mitted to the agency.

requirements.topic: record keeping that lets a device maker trace patients
requirements.complies: The text says the applicant keeps records that let it give FDA the information needed to trace patients when required to protect public health, and that patient identity is disclosed only as far as needed for the patient's medical welfare, to judge safety or effectiveness, or to verify a record or report.
requirements.conflicts: The text says no patient tracing records are kept, or that full patient identities are shared freely with FDA or others without limiting disclosure to medical welfare, safety or effectiveness, or record verification.
requirements.hint: State that patient tracing records are maintained and that patient identity is disclosed only for medical welfare, safety or effectiveness determination, or record verification.

requirements.title: FDA access to records
requirements.need: An applicant must grant FDA access to records and reports required under this part, permit authorized employees to copy and verify them, and permit inspection of manufacturing facilities to verify approved conditions.

quote.text:
An applicant shall grant to FDA
access to any records and reports re-
quired under the provisions of this
part, and shall permit authorized FDA
employees to copy and verify such
records and reports and to inspect at a
reasonable time and in a reasonable
manner all manufacturing facilities to
verify that the device is being manu-
factured, stored, labeled, and shipped
under approved conditions.

requirements.topic: FDA access to a device maker's records and manufacturing facilities
requirements.complies: The text says the applicant gives FDA access to required records and reports, lets authorized FDA employees copy and verify them, and allows inspection of manufacturing facilities at reasonable times and in a reasonable manner to confirm the device is made, stored, labeled and shipped under approved conditions.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA is refused access to records or facilities, that records may not be copied or verified, or that inspections are blocked or only allowed on the company's terms.
requirements.hint: State that FDA gets access to required records and reports, may copy and verify them, and may inspect facilities at reasonable times to confirm approved manufacturing, storage, labeling and shipping conditions.

requirements.title: Noncompliance ground for withdrawal
requirements.need: Failure to comply with any postapproval requirement constitutes a ground for withdrawal of approval of a PMA.

quote.text:
Failure to comply with any post-
approval requirement constitutes a
ground for withdrawal of approval of a
PMA.

requirements.topic: consequences of failing to meet conditions placed on an approved device
requirements.complies: The text states that failing to comply with any postapproval requirement is a ground for FDA to withdraw approval of the PMA.
requirements.conflicts: The text says missing a postapproval requirement has no consequence, or that approval can never be withdrawn for noncompliance.
requirements.hint: State plainly that failure to comply with any postapproval requirement is a ground for withdrawal of PMA approval.

requirements.title: Compliance with reporting rules
requirements.need: The holder of an approved PMA must comply with part 803 and any other requirements applicable to the device by other regulations or by the order approving the device.

quote.text:
The holder of an approved PMA
shall comply with the requirements of
part 803 and with any other require-
ments applicable to the device by other
regulations in this subchapter or by
order approving the device.

requirements.topic: ongoing reporting duties of the holder of an approved device application
requirements.complies: The text says the holder of an approved PMA complies with part 803 and with any other requirements that apply to the device under other regulations or under the order approving the device.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the holder is exempt from part 803 or from other applicable requirements, or that only the original application matters after approval.
requirements.hint: State that the PMA holder complies with part 803 and with all other requirements applicable to the device from other regulations or the approval order.

requirements.title: Periodic report content
requirements.need: Unless FDA specifies otherwise, a periodic report must identify changes under § 814.39(a) and (b), summarize unpublished and published reports and literature, identify exception or alternative changes, and identify each device identifier in use or discontinued.

quote.text:
Unless FDA specifies otherwise,
any periodic report shall:
(1) Identify changes described in
§ 814.39(a) and changes required to be
reported to FDA under § 814.39(b).
(2) Contain a summary and bibliog-
raphy of the following information not
previously submitted as part of the
PMA:

requirements.topic: contents of periodic reports submitted for an approved device
requirements.complies: The text says the periodic report identifies changes under § 814.39(a) and changes reportable under § 814.39(b), gives a summary and bibliography of previously unsubmitted information, identifies exception or alternative changes, and identifies each device identifier in use or discontinued.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the periodic report omits change identification, leaves out the summary and bibliography, or does not list device identifiers in use or discontinued.
requirements.hint: List each required periodic report element: changes under § 814.39(a) and (b), a summary and bibliography of new information, exception or alternative changes, and every device identifier in use or discontinued.

requirements.title: Grounds for denying PMA
requirements.need: FDA may deny approval of a PMA if the applicant fails to follow this part or any statutory ground applies, including a false statement of material fact, noncompliant labeling, refusal to permit inspection, noncompliant nonclinical studies, or noncompliant clinical investigations.

quote.text:
FDA may issue an order denying
approval of a PMA if the applicant fails
to follow the requirements of this part
or if, upon the basis of the information
submitted in the PMA or any other in-
formation before the agency, FDA de-
termines that any of the grounds for
denying approval of a PMA specified in
section 515(d)(2) (A)–(E) of the act ap-
plies.

requirements.topic: FDA decisions on premarket approval applications for medical devices
requirements.complies: The text states that FDA may deny approval of a PMA when the applicant fails to follow the applicable requirements or when a statutory ground for denial applies, such as a false statement of material fact, noncompliant labeling, refusal to permit inspection, or noncompliant nonclinical or clinical studies.
requirements.conflicts: The text claims FDA cannot deny a PMA for any reason once it is submitted, or that false statements of material fact, noncompliant labeling, refusal to permit inspection, or noncompliant studies are not grounds for denial.
requirements.hint: Describe the grounds on which FDA may deny PMA approval, including failure to follow the requirements and the statutory grounds such as false statements, labeling, inspection refusal, and study noncompliance.

requirements.title: Inspection access required
requirements.need: An applicant must permit an authorized FDA employee to inspect facilities and controls at a reasonable time and manner and to access, copy, and verify all records pertinent to the application.

quote.text:
The applicant does not permit an
authorized FDA employee an oppor-
tunity to inspect at a reasonable time
and in a reasonable manner the facili-
ties, controls, and to have access to
and to copy and verify all records per-
tinent to the application;

requirements.topic: FDA inspection of facilities, controls and records during PMA review
requirements.complies: The text states that the applicant permits an authorized FDA employee to inspect facilities and controls at a reasonable time and in a reasonable manner and to access, copy and verify all records pertinent to the application.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the applicant refuses or restricts FDA inspection of facilities and controls, or denies FDA access to copy and verify records pertinent to the application.
requirements.hint: State that the applicant allows authorized FDA employees to inspect facilities and controls at reasonable times and to access, copy and verify all pertinent records.

requirements.title: Good laboratory practice compliance
requirements.need: A nonclinical laboratory study essential to safety that is described in the PMA must have been conducted in compliance with the good laboratory practice regulations in part 58, or the noncompliance must be explained and not undermine the study's validity.

quote.text:
A nonclinical laboratory study
that is described in the PMA and that
is essential to show that the device is
safe for use under the conditions pre-
scribed, recommended, or suggested in
its proposed labeling, was not con-
ducted in compliance with the good
laboratory practice regulations in part
58 and no reason for the noncompliance
is provided or, if it is, the differences
between the practices used in con-
ducting the study and the good labora-
tory practice regulations do not sup-
port the validity of the study;

requirements.topic: conduct of nonclinical laboratory studies supporting a PMA
requirements.complies: The text states that each nonclinical laboratory study essential to showing safety was conducted in compliance with the good laboratory practice regulations in part 58, or explains any noncompliance and shows the differences do not undermine the study's validity.
requirements.conflicts: The text says an essential nonclinical study was not conducted under good laboratory practice regulations, gives no reason for the noncompliance, or admits the differences from part 58 mean the study's validity is not supported.
requirements.hint: State that essential nonclinical studies followed part 58 good laboratory practice rules, or explain any deviation and why the study remains valid.

requirements.title: Clinical investigation compliance
requirements.need: Any clinical investigation involving human subjects described in the PMA must have been conducted in compliance with the IRB, informed consent, and GCP requirements so that subject rights and safety were protected and data are reliable.

quote.text:
Any clinical investigation involv-
ing human subjects described in the
PMA, subject to the institutional re-
view board regulations in part 56 of
this chapter or informed consent regu-
lations in part 50 of this chapter or
GCP referenced in § 814.15(a) and de-
scribed in § 812.28(a) of this chapter,
was not conducted in compliance with
those regulations such that the rights
or safety of human subjects were not
adequately protected or the supporting
data were determined to be otherwise
unreliable.

requirements.topic: conduct of clinical investigations involving human subjects in a PMA
requirements.complies: The text states that each clinical investigation involving human subjects was conducted in compliance with the IRB regulations in part 56, the informed consent regulations in part 50, and the GCP requirements, so subject rights and safety were protected and the data are reliable.
requirements.conflicts: The text says a clinical investigation was not conducted in compliance with IRB, informed consent or GCP requirements, that subject rights or safety were not protected, or that the supporting data are unreliable.
requirements.hint: State that human-subject clinical investigations followed part 56, part 50 and the GCP requirements, protecting subject rights and safety and yielding reliable data.

requirements.title: Denial order content
requirements.need: FDA issues any order denying approval in accordance with § 814.17, stating the deficiencies and applicable grounds and identifying measures to place the PMA in approvable form, with notice of review opportunity.

quote.text:
FDA will issue any order denying
approval of the PMA in accordance
with § 814.17. The order will inform the
applicant of the deficiencies in the
PMA, including each applicable ground
for denial under section 515(d)(2) of the
act and the regulations under this part,
and, where practical, will identify
measures required to place the PMA in
approvable form.

requirements.topic: content of an FDA order denying approval of a PMA
requirements.complies: The text states that FDA issues any denial order in accordance with § 814.17, informs the applicant of the deficiencies and each applicable ground for denial, and where practical identifies measures needed to place the PMA in approvable form.
requirements.conflicts: The text says a denial order is issued without following § 814.17, does not state the deficiencies or applicable grounds, or does not identify measures to make the PMA approvable.
requirements.hint: Describe the denial order as issued under § 814.17, listing the deficiencies, each applicable ground, and where practical the measures to reach approvable form.

requirements.title: Public notice of denial
requirements.need: FDA gives public notice of a denial order on its website stating that a safety and effectiveness summary is available, and PMA file data become publicly disclosable under § 814.9.

quote.text:
FDA will give the public notice
of an order denying approval of the
PMA. The notice will be placed on the
FDA’s home page on the Internet
(http://www.fda.gov), and it will state
that a detailed summary of informa-
tion respecting the safety and effec-
tiveness of the device, including infor-
mation about any adverse effects of the
device on health, is available on the
Internet and has been placed on public
display and that copies are available
upon request.

requirements.topic: public notice of an FDA order denying approval of a PMA
requirements.complies: The text states that FDA gives public notice of the denial order on its website, stating that a detailed summary of safety and effectiveness information, including adverse effects, is available on the Internet, on public display, and by request.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA keeps the denial order confidential, gives no public notice, or does not state that the safety and effectiveness summary is available on the Internet, on public display, and by request.
requirements.hint: State that FDA posts public notice of the denial on its website and says the safety and effectiveness summary, including adverse effects, is available online, on public display and by request.

requirements.title: Denial after letters
requirements.need: FDA issues a denial order after an approvable or not approvable letter when a requested amendment still leaves a ground for denial, the applicant declines to amend, or the applicant petitions for review.

quote.text:
FDA will issue an order denying
approval of a PMA after an approvable
or not approvable letter has been sent
and the applicant:
(1) Submits a requested amendment
but any ground for denying approval of
the application under section 515(d)(2)
of the act still applies; or
(2) Notifies FDA in writing that the
requested amendment will not be sub-
mitted; or
(3) Petitions for review under section
515(d)(4) of the act by filing a petition
in the form of a petition for reconsider-
ation under § 10.33.

requirements.topic: FDA decisions on premarket approval applications after an approvable or not approvable letter
requirements.complies: FDA sends an approvable or not approvable letter, and after the applicant submits a requested amendment that still leaves a ground for denial, notifies FDA in writing that it will not submit the amendment, or petitions for review, FDA issues an order denying approval of the PMA.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA must approve the PMA once the applicant submits any amendment, or that FDA cannot deny approval after an approvable or not approvable letter has been sent, or that a petition for review blocks a denial order.
requirements.hint: Describe the denial order as coming after the letter and after one of the three applicant actions, and tie it to a remaining ground for denial under section 515(d)(2).

requirements.title: Grounds for withdrawing PMA
requirements.need: FDA may withdraw approval of a PMA if a statutory ground applies, any postapproval requirement imposed by the approval order or regulation has not been met, or nonclinical or clinical studies were not conducted in compliance with applicable regulations.

quote.text:
FDA may issue an order with-
drawing approval of a PMA if, from any
information available to the agency,
FDA determines that:
(1) Any of the grounds under section
515(e)(1) (A)–(G) of the act applies.
(2) Any postapproval requirement im-
posed by the PMA approval order or by
regulation has not been met.

requirements.topic: withdrawal of approval of a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: FDA issues an order withdrawing approval of a PMA after determining that a ground under section 515(e)(1)(A)-(G) applies, that a postapproval requirement imposed by the approval order or by regulation has not been met, or that nonclinical or clinical studies were not conducted in compliance with applicable regulations.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA cannot withdraw PMA approval for failure to meet postapproval requirements, or that approval is permanent once granted, or that only a statutory ground under section 515(e)(1) can support withdrawal.
requirements.hint: List the grounds for withdrawal as including unmet postapproval requirements from the approval order or regulations and noncompliant nonclinical or clinical studies.

requirements.title: Hearing before withdrawal
requirements.need: Before issuing an order withdrawing approval of a PMA, FDA issues the holder a notice of opportunity for an informal hearing under part 16.

quote.text:
Before issuing an order with-
drawing approval of a PMA, FDA will
issue the holder of the approved appli-
cation a notice of opportunity for an
informal hearing under part 16.

requirements.topic: procedure before FDA withdraws approval of a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: Before issuing an order withdrawing approval of a PMA, FDA sends the holder of the approved application a notice of opportunity for an informal hearing under part 16.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA withdraws PMA approval immediately without notifying the holder, or that the holder gets no chance to request an informal hearing under part 16 before the withdrawal order.
requirements.hint: State that the notice of opportunity for an informal hearing under part 16 comes before the withdrawal order is issued.

requirements.title: Withdrawal order content
requirements.need: If no hearing is requested or the agency proceeds after a hearing, FDA issues an order withdrawing approval stating each ground and including notice of administrative review opportunity.

quote.text:
If the applicant does not request a
hearing or if after the part 16 hearing
is held the agency decides to proceed
with the withdrawal, FDA will issue to
the holder of the approved application
an order withdrawing approval of the
application. The order will be issued
under § 814.17, will state each ground
for withdrawing approval, and will in-
clude a notice of an opportunity for ad-
ministrative review under section
515(e)(2) of the act.

requirements.topic: content and issuance of an FDA order withdrawing approval of a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: When no hearing is requested or the agency decides to proceed after a part 16 hearing, FDA issues an order under § 814.17 withdrawing approval that states each ground for withdrawal and includes notice of an opportunity for administrative review under section 515(e)(2).
requirements.conflicts: The text says the withdrawal order need not state the grounds, or that it omits notice of administrative review, or that FDA issues the order without regard to whether a hearing was requested or held.
requirements.hint: Say the withdrawal order is issued under § 814.17, states each ground, and includes notice of administrative review under section 515(e)(2).

requirements.title: Public notice of withdrawal
requirements.need: FDA publishes notice of a withdrawal order in the Federal Register stating that a safety and effectiveness summary is on public display, and PMA file data become publicly disclosable under § 814.9.

quote.text:
FDA will give the public notice of
an order withdrawing approval of a
PMA. The notice will be published in
the FEDERAL REGISTER and will state

[Page 17]
