that a detailed summary of informa-
tion respecting the safety and effec-
tiveness of the device, including infor-
mation about any adverse effects of the
device on health, has been placed on
public display and that copies are
available upon request.

requirements.topic: public notice of FDA withdrawal of approval of a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: FDA publishes notice of the withdrawal order in the Federal Register stating that a detailed summary of safety and effectiveness information, including adverse effects on health, has been placed on public display and that copies are available on request, and PMA file data become publicly disclosable under § 814.9.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the withdrawal is kept confidential, or that no Federal Register notice is published, or that the safety and effectiveness summary is not made available to the public.
requirements.hint: Describe the Federal Register notice and the public display of the safety and effectiveness summary, including adverse effects and availability of copies on request.

requirements.title: Temporary suspension grounds
requirements.need: FDA issues an order temporarily suspending approval of a PMA, including any supplement, if it determines there is a reasonable probability that continued distribution would cause serious adverse health consequences or death.

quote.text:
FDA will issue an order tempo-
rarily suspending approval of a PMA if
FDA determines that there is a reason-
able probability that continued dis-
tribution of the device would cause se-
rious, adverse health consequences or
death.

requirements.topic: temporary suspension of approval of a premarket approval application
requirements.complies: FDA issues an order temporarily suspending approval of a PMA, including any supplement, after determining there is a reasonable probability that continued distribution of the device would cause serious adverse health consequences or death.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA cannot suspend a PMA approval, or that distribution may continue despite a reasonable probability of serious adverse health consequences or death, or that supplements are exempt from suspension.
requirements.hint: State that the temporary suspension order, covering any supplement, follows a determination of a reasonable probability of serious adverse health consequences or death from continued distribution.

requirements.title: Suspension hearing
requirements.need: FDA may initiate a part 16 regulatory hearing to determine whether to suspend approval, may waive or modify part 16 procedures for immediate action, and deems failure to request a hearing within the specified timeframe a waiver.

quote.text:
Any regulatory hearing to deter-
mine whether to issue an order tempo-
rarily suspending approval of a PMA
shall be initiated and conducted by
FDA pursuant to part 16 of this chap-
ter. If FDA believes that immediate ac-
tion to remove a dangerous device from
the market is necessary to protect the
public health, the agency may, in ac-
cordance with § 16.60(h) of this chapter,
waive, suspend, or modify any part 16
procedure pursuant to § 10.19 of this
chapter.

requirements.topic: FDA hearings on temporarily suspending approval of a premarket approval application for a medical device
requirements.complies: FDA starts and runs the hearing under part 16, and if immediate action to remove a dangerous device from the market is needed to protect public health, FDA states that it is waiving, suspending or modifying part 16 procedures under § 16.60(h) and § 10.19.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA suspends approval without offering any part 16 regulatory hearing, or says FDA may ignore part 16 procedures for immediate action without citing the waiver provisions, or treats a late hearing request as still valid.
requirements.hint: Describe the part 16 hearing FDA initiates and note that part 16 procedures may be waived, suspended or modified under § 16.60(h) and § 10.19 when immediate action is needed.

requirements.title: Suspension order
requirements.need: If no hearing is requested or after the hearing FDA finds a reasonable probability of serious adverse health consequences or death, FDA issues an order temporarily suspending approval of the PMA.

quote.text:
If the
PMA holder does not request a regu-
latory hearing or if, after the hearing,
and after consideration of the adminis-
trative record of the hearing, FDA de-
termines that there is a reasonable
probability that the continued dis-
tribution of a device under an approved
PMA would cause serious, adverse
health consequences or death, the
agency shall, under the authority of
section 515(e)(3) of the act, issue an
order to the PMA holder temporarily
suspending approval of the PMA.

requirements.topic: FDA orders temporarily suspending approval of a premarket approval application for a medical device
requirements.complies: The text states that FDA issues an order temporarily suspending approval when the PMA holder does not request a hearing, or when after the hearing and review of the administrative record FDA finds a reasonable probability that continued distribution would cause serious adverse health consequences or death.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA suspends approval without any hearing request or finding, or says suspension follows automatically without a determination of a reasonable probability of serious adverse health consequences or death.
requirements.hint: State the two triggers for the suspension order: no hearing request, or a post-hearing finding of a reasonable probability of serious adverse health consequences or death.

requirements.title: Hearing after suspension
requirements.need: After issuing a temporary suspension order, FDA proceeds expeditiously, within 60 days, to hold a hearing on whether to permanently withdraw approval under section 515(e)(1) and § 814.46.

quote.text:
If FDA issues an order tem-
porarily suspending approval of a PMA,
the agency shall proceed expeditiously,
but within 60 days, to hold a hearing on
whether to permanently withdraw ap-
proval of the PMA in accordance with
section 515(e)(1) of the act and the pro-
cedures set out in § 814.46.

requirements.topic: FDA hearings on permanently withdrawing approval of a premarket approval application after a temporary suspension
requirements.complies: The text says that after issuing a temporary suspension order FDA proceeds expeditiously, within 60 days, to hold a hearing on whether to permanently withdraw approval under section 515(e)(1) and § 814.46.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA may delay the withdrawal hearing beyond 60 days, or that no hearing on permanent withdrawal is held after a temporary suspension order.
requirements.hint: State that FDA moves expeditiously and holds the permanent withdrawal hearing within 60 days under section 515(e)(1) and § 814.46.

requirements.title: PMA file existence confidential
requirements.need: The existence of a PMA file may not be disclosed by FDA before an approval order is issued to the applicant unless it has previously been publicly disclosed or acknowledged.

quote.text:
The existence of a PMA file may
not be disclosed by FDA before an ap-
proval order is issued to the applicant
unless it previously has been publicly
disclosed or acknowledged.

requirements.topic: disclosure of the existence of a premarket approval application file
requirements.complies: The text states that FDA may not disclose the existence of a PMA file before an approval order issues to the applicant, unless the existence was previously publicly disclosed or acknowledged.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA may confirm or reveal that a PMA file exists before approval even when it has never been publicly disclosed or acknowledged.
requirements.hint: Say FDA keeps the existence of a PMA file confidential until approval unless it was already publicly disclosed or acknowledged.

requirements.title: Undisclosed PMA data protected
requirements.need: If the existence of a PMA file has not been publicly disclosed or acknowledged, data or information in the PMA file are not available for public disclosure.

quote.text:
If the existence of a PMA file has
not been publicly disclosed or acknowl-
edged, data or information in the PMA
file are not available for public disclo-
sure.

requirements.topic: public access to data and information in an undisclosed premarket approval application file
requirements.complies: The text states that when the existence of a PMA file has not been publicly disclosed or acknowledged, the data and information in the file are not available for public disclosure.
requirements.conflicts: The text says data or information in a PMA file whose existence has never been publicly disclosed or acknowledged can be released to the public.
requirements.hint: State that data and information in a PMA file stay unavailable for public disclosure while the file's existence is undisclosed.

requirements.title: Pre-order disclosure limits
requirements.need: If the existence of a PMA file has been publicly disclosed or acknowledged before an approval or denial order issues, data or information in the file are not available for public disclosure before the order issues, though FDA may disclose a summary of portions of safety and effectiveness data if relevant to public consideration of a specific pending issue.

quote.text:
If the existence of a PMA file
has been publicly disclosed or acknowl-
edged before an order approving, or an
order denying approval of the PMA is
issued, data or information contained
in the file are not available for public
disclosure before such order issues.
FDA may, however, disclose a sum-
mary of portions of the safety and ef-
fectiveness data before an approval
order or an order denying approval of
the PMA issues if disclosure is relevant
to public consideration of a specific
pending issue.

requirements.topic: public disclosure of data in a premarket approval application file before an approval or denial order
requirements.complies: The text states that when the PMA file's existence was publicly disclosed or acknowledged before an approval or denial order issues, the data and information in the file are not available for public disclosure before that order, though FDA may disclose a summary of portions of safety and effectiveness data if relevant to public consideration of a specific pending issue.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA may release the full data or information in the PMA file before the approval or denial order issues, or says no summary of safety and effectiveness data may ever be released before the order.
requirements.hint: State that before the order issues only a summary of portions of safety and effectiveness data may be disclosed, and only when relevant to a specific pending issue.

requirements.title: Public summary on order
requirements.need: Upon issuance of an order approving or denying approval of any PMA, FDA will make available to the public the fact of the PMA's existence and a detailed summary of the safety and effectiveness information that is the basis for the order.

quote.text:
Upon issuance of an order approv-
ing, or an order denying approval of
any PMA, FDA will make available to
the public the fact of the existence of
the PMA and a detailed summary of in-
formation submitted to FDA respect-
ing the safety and effectiveness of the
device that is the subject of the PMA
and that is the basis for the order.

requirements.topic: FDA decisions on premarket approval applications for medical devices and what the public is told about them
requirements.complies: The text says that when FDA issues an order approving or denying a PMA, FDA makes public the fact that the PMA exists and a detailed summary of the safety and effectiveness information submitted to FDA that formed the basis for the order.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA keeps the existence of an approved or denied PMA secret, or that no summary of the safety and effectiveness information behind the order is ever released to the public.
requirements.hint: State that on the date of an approval or denial order, FDA publicly releases both the fact of the PMA's existence and a detailed summary of the supporting safety and effectiveness information.

requirements.title: Data public after order
requirements.need: After FDA issues an order approving or denying approval of any PMA, specified data and information in the PMA file are immediately available for public disclosure, including previously disclosed safety and effectiveness data, protocols unless trade secret, adverse reaction reports with deletions, disclosed component lists, assay methods, and correspondence.

quote.text:
After FDA issues an order approv-
ing, or an order denying approval of
any PMA, the following data and infor-
mation in the PMA file are imme-
diately available for public disclosure:
(1) All safety and effectiveness data
and information previously disclosed to
the public, as such disclosure is defined
in § 20.81.

requirements.topic: public access to data and information in a premarket approval file after FDA rules on the application
requirements.complies: The text says that immediately after FDA issues an approval or denial order on a PMA, safety and effectiveness data and information already disclosed to the public under § 20.81 become available for public disclosure.
requirements.conflicts: The text says that after an approval or denial order the PMA file stays closed, or that safety and effectiveness data already disclosed to the public are withheld from disclosure.
requirements.hint: Say that once FDA issues the approval or denial order, previously disclosed safety and effectiveness data in the PMA file are immediately available to the public.

requirements.title: Disclosure on abandonment
requirements.need: All safety and effectiveness data and other information not previously disclosed are available for public disclosure if the PMA is abandoned, an order denying approval issues and appeals are exhausted, an order withdrawing approval issues and appeals are exhausted, the device is reclassified, the device is found substantially equivalent to a class I or II device, or the PMA is considered voluntarily withdrawn, provided the data are not trade secret or confidential commercial or financial information.

quote.text:
All safety and effectiveness data
and other information not previously
disclosed to the public are available for
public disclosure if any one of the fol-
lowing events occurs and the data and
information do not constitute trade se-
cret or confidential commercial or fi-
nancial information under § 20.61:
(1) The PMA has been abandoned.

requirements.topic: public release of previously undisclosed safety and effectiveness data from a premarket approval file after events such as abandonment, denial, withdrawal, reclassification or voluntary withdrawal
requirements.complies: The text says that previously undisclosed safety and effectiveness data and other information become publicly available when an event such as PMA abandonment, a denial order with appeals exhausted, a withdrawal order with appeals exhausted, reclassification, a finding of substantial equivalence to a class I or II device, or voluntary withdrawal occurs, as long as the data are not trade secret or confidential commercial or financial information under § 20.61.
requirements.conflicts: The text says such data stay secret after these events even when they are not trade secrets or confidential commercial or financial information, or says the data are released regardless of trade secret or confidentiality status.
requirements.hint: List the triggering events and state that previously undisclosed data become public then, except where they are trade secret or confidential commercial or financial information under § 20.61.

requirements.title: PMA abandonment criteria
requirements.need: FDA will consider a PMA abandoned if the applicant fails to respond to a request for additional information within 180 days after the request issues or other circumstances indicate further work is not being undertaken, and the applicant fails to communicate with FDA within 7 days after FDA notifies the applicant that the PMA appears abandoned.

quote.text:
The PMA has been abandoned.
FDA will consider a PMA abandoned if:
(i)(A) The applicant fails to respond
to a request for additional information
within 180 days after the date FDA
issues the request or
(B) Other circumstances indicate
that further work is not being under-
taken with respect to it, and
(ii) The applicant fails to commu-
nicate with FDA within 7 days after
the date on which FDA notifies the ap-
plicant that the PMA appears to have
been abandoned.

requirements.topic: when FDA treats a premarket approval application as abandoned because the applicant stops responding
requirements.complies: The text says FDA considers a PMA abandoned when the applicant does not respond to a request for additional information within 180 days of the request or other circumstances show work is not continuing, and the applicant does not communicate with FDA within 7 days after FDA notifies it that the PMA appears abandoned.
requirements.conflicts: The text says a PMA is never treated as abandoned for missed responses, or sets different time limits such as no 180 day response window or no 7 day window after FDA's notice.
requirements.hint: Describe both conditions: failure to respond within 180 days (or other signs work has stopped) and failure to contact FDA within 7 days of its notice that the PMA appears abandoned.

requirements.title: Trade secret data protected
requirements.need: Manufacturing methods or processes including quality control procedures, production, sales, distribution and similar data, and quantitative or semiquantitative formulas in a PMA file are not available for public disclosure unless previously disclosed or relating to an abandoned PMA and no longer trade secret or confidential commercial or financial information.

quote.text:
The following data and informa-
tion in a PMA file are not available for
public disclosure unless they have been
previously disclosed to the public, as
such disclosure is defined in § 20.81, or
they relate to a device for which a
PMA has been abandoned and they no
longer represent a trade secret or con-
fidential commercial or financial infor-
mation as defined in § 20.61:
(1) Manufacturing methods or proc-
esses, including quality control proce-
dures.

requirements.topic: confidential manufacturing, quality control, production, sales, distribution and formula information in a premarket approval file
requirements.complies: The text says manufacturing methods and processes including quality control procedures, production, sales, distribution and similar data, and quantitative or semiquantitative formulas in a PMA file are not publicly disclosed unless previously disclosed under § 20.81 or tied to an abandoned PMA where they are no longer trade secret or confidential commercial or financial information under § 20.61.
requirements.conflicts: The text says such manufacturing, quality control, production, sales, distribution or formula information is released to the public freely, or is released even though it remains a trade secret or confidential commercial or financial information.
requirements.hint: State that these categories stay out of public disclosure except when already disclosed or when they relate to an abandoned PMA and no longer qualify as trade secret or confidential commercial or financial information.

requirements.title: HUD periodic reports
requirements.need: A person granted an exemption under section 520(m) of the act must submit periodic reports as described in § 814.126(b).

quote.text:
A person granted an exemption
under section 520(m) of the act shall
submit periodic reports as described in
§ 814.126(b).

requirements.topic: periodic reporting duties of a person granted a humanitarian device exemption under section 520(m)
requirements.complies: The text says a person granted an exemption under section 520(m) of the act must submit periodic reports as described in § 814.126(b).
requirements.conflicts: The text says a person granted a section 520(m) exemption has no duty to file periodic reports, or that reports are filed under some other provision instead of § 814.126(b).
requirements.hint: State plainly that holders of a section 520(m) exemption submit periodic reports following § 814.126(b).

requirements.title: HDE suspension or withdrawal
requirements.need: FDA may suspend or withdraw approval of an HDE after providing notice and an opportunity for an informal hearing.

quote.text:
FDA may suspend or withdraw ap-
proval of an HDE after providing notice
and an opportunity for an informal
hearing.

requirements.topic: suspending or withdrawing FDA approval of a humanitarian device exemption (HDE)
requirements.complies: The text states that FDA may suspend or withdraw HDE approval only after giving the applicant notice and an opportunity for an informal hearing.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA can suspend or withdraw HDE approval immediately without notice or without any chance for an informal hearing.
requirements.hint: State that any suspension or withdrawal of HDE approval comes after notice and an opportunity for an informal hearing.

requirements.title: HUD designation request
requirements.need: Before submitting an HDE, the applicant must submit a request for HUD designation to FDA's Office of Orphan Products Development containing the required statement, contact information, disease description, device description and rationale, and prevalence documentation.

quote.text:
Prior to
submitting an HDE application, the ap-
plicant shall submit a request for HUD
designation to FDA’s Office of Orphan
Products Development. The request
shall contain the following:
(1) A statement that the applicant re-
quests HUD designation for a rare dis-
ease or condition or a valid subset of a
disease or condition which shall be
identified with specificity;

requirements.topic: requesting humanitarian use device (HUD) designation from FDA before applying for an HDE
requirements.complies: The text says the applicant submits a HUD designation request to FDA's Office of Orphan Products Development before the HDE, and the request identifies the rare disease or condition with specificity and includes the required statement and contact information.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the applicant files the HDE first and seeks HUD designation later, or sends the designation request somewhere other than the Office of Orphan Products Development, or omits the statement that designation is requested for a rare disease or condition.
requirements.hint: Describe submitting the HUD designation request to FDA's Office of Orphan Products Development before the HDE, with the required statement naming the rare disease or condition specifically.

requirements.title: Prevalence documentation
requirements.need: The request must include documentation with authoritative references demonstrating the device treats or diagnoses a disease or condition affecting not more than 8,000 people in the United States per year, or for diagnostics that not more than 8,000 patients per year would be diagnosed.

quote.text:
Documentation, with appended
authoritative references, to dem-
onstrate that the device is designed to
treat or diagnose a disease or condition
that affects or is manifested in not
more than 8,000 people in the United
States per year. If the device is for di-
agnostic purposes, the documentation
must demonstrate that not more than
8,000 patients per year would be sub-
jected to diagnosis by the device in the
United States.

requirements.topic: documenting how many people in the United States the device's target disease or condition affects
requirements.complies: The text says the request includes documentation with appended authoritative references showing the device treats or diagnoses a disease or condition affecting not more than 8,000 people in the United States per year, or for diagnostics that not more than 8,000 patients per year would be diagnosed.
requirements.conflicts: The text claims the disease or condition affects more than 8,000 people per year in the United States, or gives no authoritative references, or for a diagnostic device does not show that not more than 8,000 patients per year would be diagnosed.
requirements.hint: Include documentation with authoritative references showing the yearly U.S. patient count is not more than 8,000, using the diagnosed-patient count for diagnostic devices.

requirements.title: FDA action on designation
requirements.need: Within 45 days of receipt FDA approves, returns pending additional information, or disapproves the HUD designation request, and the review period may be extended up to 45 days upon receipt of additional information.

quote.text:
Within 45 days of re-
ceipt of a request for HUD designation,
FDA will take one of the following ac-
tions:
(1) Approve the request and notify
the applicant that the device has been
designated as a HUD based on the in-
formation submitted;
(2) Return the request to the appli-
cant pending further review upon sub-
mission of additional information.

requirements.topic: FDA's handling of a HUD designation request within its review timeframe
requirements.complies: The text says FDA within 45 days of receiving the request approves it, returns it pending additional information, or disapproves it, and that the review period may be extended up to 45 days when additional information is received.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA has no deadline, or takes longer than 45 days without any extension, or never returns or disapproves a request.
requirements.hint: State the 45-day FDA action window and the possible extension of up to 45 days when additional information is submitted.

requirements.title: Revocation of designation
requirements.need: FDA may revoke a HUD designation if the request contained an untrue statement of material fact or omitted material information, or if the device is not eligible for HUD designation based on available evidence.

quote.text:
FDA
may revoke a HUD designation if the
agency finds that:
(1) The request for designation con-
tained an untrue statement of material
fact or omitted material information;
or
(2) Based on the evidence available,
the device is not eligible for HUD des-
ignation.

requirements.topic: revoking a humanitarian use device (HUD) designation
requirements.complies: The text says FDA may revoke a HUD designation if the request contained an untrue statement of material fact or omitted material information, or if available evidence shows the device is not eligible for HUD designation.
requirements.conflicts: The text says a HUD designation can never be revoked, or that FDA revokes it for reasons other than an untrue statement of material fact, omitted material information, or ineligibility shown by available evidence.
requirements.hint: State that FDA may revoke the designation for an untrue statement of material fact, omitted material information, or evidence that the device is not eligible.

requirements.title: HDE signature requirements
requirements.need: The applicant or an authorized representative must sign the HDE, and a foreign applicant must have the HDE countersigned by an authorized U.S. representative whose name and address are identified.

quote.text:
The applicant or an authorized
representative shall sign the HDE. If
the applicant does not reside or have a
place of business within the United
States, the HDE shall be countersigned
by an authorized representative resid-
ing or maintaining a place of business
in the United States and shall identify
the representative’s name and address.

requirements.topic: signing a humanitarian device exemption (HDE) application
requirements.complies: The text says the applicant or an authorized representative signs the HDE, and a foreign applicant has the HDE countersigned by an authorized U.S. representative whose name and address are identified.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the HDE needs no signature, or a foreign applicant signs without a U.S. representative countersigning, or the U.S. representative's name and address are not identified.
requirements.hint: Have the applicant or authorized representative sign, and for foreign applicants name and address an authorized U.S. representative who countersigns.

requirements.title: HDE required contents
requirements.need: Unless an omission is justified, an HDE must include the HUD determination, an explanation why the device would not otherwise be available and no comparable device exists, a risk-benefit explanation, the § 814.20(b) information, the amount charged with cost attestation if over $250, and pediatric use information.

quote.text:
Unless the applicant jus-
tifies an omission in accordance with
paragraph (d) of this section, an HDE
shall include:
(1) A copy of or reference to the de-
termination made by FDA’s Office of
Orphan Products Development (in ac-
cordance with § 814.102) that the device
qualifies as a HUD;

requirements.topic: contents of a Humanitarian Device Exemption (HDE) application to FDA
requirements.complies: The application includes a copy of or reference to FDA's Office of Orphan Products Development determination that the device qualifies as a HUD, or states a justified omission of that item.
requirements.conflicts: The application leaves out the HUD determination without any justification, or claims the device qualifies as a HUD without citing or attaching the Office of Orphan Products Development determination.
requirements.hint: Include the HUD determination (or a reference to it) in the HDE, and if you leave it out, justify the omission under paragraph (d).

requirements.title: HUD labeling statement
requirements.need: In addition to the proposed labeling requirement in § 814.20(b)(10), the labeling must bear the statement that it is a Humanitarian Device authorized by Federal law for the specified use and that effectiveness has not been demonstrated.

quote.text:
In addition to the proposed label-
ing requirement set forth in
§ 814.20(b)(10), the labeling shall bear
the following statement: Humanitarian
Device. Authorized by Federal law for
use in the [treatment or diagnosis] of
[specify disease or condition]. The ef-
fectiveness of this device for this use
has not been demonstrated;

requirements.topic: labeling of a Humanitarian Device
requirements.complies: The labeling bears the statement that it is a Humanitarian Device authorized by Federal law for the named treatment or diagnosis of a specified disease or condition, and that effectiveness for that use has not been demonstrated.
requirements.conflicts: The labeling omits the Humanitarian Device statement, or claims the device's effectiveness for the use has been demonstrated.
requirements.hint: Add the exact Humanitarian Device statement to the labeling, naming the treatment or diagnosis and the specific disease or condition, and stating effectiveness has not been demonstrated.

requirements.title: Amount charged and attestation
requirements.need: The HDE must state the amount charged for the device and, if more than $250, include an independent CPA report or responsible individual attestation verifying the amount does not exceed research, development, fabrication, and distribution costs.

quote.text:
The amount to be charged for the
device and, if the amount is more than
$250, a report by an independent cer-
tified public accountant, made in ac-
cordance with the Statement on Stand-
ards for Attestation established by the
American Institute of Certified Public
Accountants, or in lieu of such a re-
port, an attestation by a responsible
individual of the organization,
verifying that the amount charged does
not exceed the costs of the device’s re-
search, development, fabrication, and
distribution.

requirements.topic: the price charged for a Humanitarian Device and supporting cost documentation
requirements.complies: The HDE states the amount to be charged, and if that amount is more than $250 it includes an independent CPA report or a responsible individual's attestation that the amount does not exceed research, development, fabrication, and distribution costs.
requirements.conflicts: The HDE states a charge above $250 with no CPA report or attestation, or asserts the charge exceeds the device's research, development, fabrication, and distribution costs.
requirements.hint: State the amount charged, and if it is over $250 attach a CPA report or a responsible individual attestation that the charge does not exceed those four cost categories.

requirements.title: Justifying omitted information
requirements.need: If the applicant omits required information believing it is not applicable, the applicant must submit a separate statement identifying and justifying the omission in the table of contents.

quote.text:
If the ap-
plicant believes that certain informa-
tion required under paragraph (b) of
this section is not applicable to the de-
vice that is the subject of the HDE, and
omits any such information from its
HDE, the applicant shall submit a
statement that identifies and justifies
the omission. The statement shall be
submitted as a separate section in the
HDE and identified in the table of con-
tents.

requirements.topic: omitted information in a Humanitarian Device Exemption application
requirements.complies: A separate section identifies each required item left out as not applicable and gives the justification, and that section is listed in the table of contents.
requirements.conflicts: Required information is left out with no statement identifying or justifying the omission, or the justification is buried in the application and not listed in the table of contents.
requirements.hint: Put any omission justification in its own separate section and name that section in the table of contents.

requirements.title: HDE amendments and withdrawal
requirements.need: An HDE or HDE supplement may be amended or resubmitted as prescribed for PMAs in § 814.37, and FDA will consider a pending HDE voluntarily withdrawn if a written response to an FDA amendment request is not received within 75 days.

quote.text:
An HDE or HDE supplement may be
amended or resubmitted upon an appli-
cant’s own initiative, or at the request
of FDA, for the same reasons and in
the same manner as prescribed for
PMA’s in § 814.37, except that the time-
frames set forth in § 814.37(c)(1) and (d)
do not apply. If FDA requests an HDE
applicant to submit an HDE amend-
ment, and a written response to FDA’s
request is not received within 75 days
of the date of the request, FDA will
consider the pending HDE or HDE sup-
plement to be withdrawn voluntarily
by the applicant.

requirements.topic: amending a Humanitarian Device Exemption or responding to an FDA amendment request
requirements.complies: The applicant amends or resubmits the HDE on its own initiative or at FDA's request following the PMA amendment procedures, and sends a written response to an FDA amendment request within 75 days.
requirements.conflicts: The applicant ignores an FDA request for an HDE amendment past 75 days, or states that the 75 day response deadline does not apply.
requirements.hint: Track the date of any FDA amendment request and send a written response within 75 days, or FDA will treat the HDE as voluntarily withdrawn.

requirements.title: Supplemental HDE applications
requirements.need: After approval of an original HDE, an applicant must submit supplements in accordance with the PMA requirements under § 814.39, except that a request for a new indication must comply with § 814.110.

quote.text:
After FDA approval of an original
HDE, an applicant shall submit supple-
ments in accordance with the require-
ments for PMA’s under § 814.39, except
that a request for a new indication for
use of a HUD shall comply with re-
quirements set forth in § 814.110.

requirements.topic: supplements to an approved Humanitarian Device Exemption
requirements.complies: After original HDE approval, the applicant submits supplements following the PMA supplement requirements of § 814.39, and any request for a new indication follows § 814.110.
requirements.conflicts: The applicant changes an approved HDE without submitting a supplement, or files a new indication request under § 814.39 instead of § 814.110.
requirements.hint: Submit post-approval changes as supplements under § 814.39, and route any new indication request through § 814.110.

requirements.title: New indication designation
requirements.need: An applicant seeking a new indication for use of an approved HUD must obtain a new HUD designation under § 814.102 and submit an original HDE under § 814.104.

quote.text:
An applicant seeking a new indi-
cation for use of a HUD approved under
this subpart H shall obtain a new des-
ignation of HUD status in accordance
with § 814.102 and shall submit an origi-
nal HDE in accordance with § 814.104.

requirements.topic: seeking approval to market a previously approved medical device for a new intended use
requirements.complies: The applicant states it will obtain a new designation of humanitarian use device status under § 814.102 and will submit an original humanitarian device exemption application under § 814.104 for the new indication.
requirements.conflicts: The applicant says it can begin marketing the approved device for the new indication by relying on the existing approval, or that it will file only a supplement or amendment rather than a new designation and original application.
requirements.hint: Say that a new indication requires both a new HUD designation under § 814.102 and an original HDE under § 814.104.

requirements.title: HDE filing decision
requirements.need: Within 30 days of receipt FDA notifies the applicant whether the HDE has been filed, and may refuse to file if the application is incomplete, a comparable device is available, it contains an untrue statement or omits material information, or lacks the part 54 certification or disclosure statement.

quote.text:
Within 30 days from the date an HDE is
received by FDA, the agency will no-
tify the applicant whether the applica-
tion has been filed. FDA may refuse to
file an HDE if any of the following ap-
plies:
(1) The application is incomplete be-
cause it does not on its face contain all
the information required under
§ 814.104(b);

requirements.topic: FDA's decision on whether to accept a humanitarian device exemption application for filing
requirements.complies: The applicant states that FDA will notify it within 30 days of receipt whether the application has been filed, and that FDA may refuse to file if the application is incomplete, a comparable device is available, it contains an untrue statement or omits material information, or the part 54 certification or disclosure statement is missing.
requirements.conflicts: The applicant claims FDA has no time limit for the filing decision, or that FDA must file every application regardless of completeness, comparable device availability, untrue statements, omitted material information, or missing part 54 certification or disclosure statement.
requirements.hint: Describe the 30 day filing notice and list the grounds on which FDA may refuse to file, including the part 54 certification or disclosure statement.

requirements.title: HDE review timeframe
requirements.need: Within 75 days after receipt of an HDE accepted for filing and without a major amendment, FDA must send the applicant an approval order, approvable letter, not approvable letter, or order denying approval.

quote.text:
Within 75 days after receipt of an
HDE that is accepted for filing and to
which the applicant does not submit a
major amendment, FDA shall send the
applicant an approval order, an approv-
able letter, a not approvable letter
(under § 814.116), or an order denying
approval (under § 814.118).

requirements.topic: how long FDA takes to act on a filed humanitarian device exemption application
requirements.complies: The applicant states that within 75 days after receipt of an HDE accepted for filing, and with no major amendment submitted, FDA will send an approval order, an approvable letter, a not approvable letter, or an order denying approval.
requirements.conflicts: The applicant claims FDA has no deadline for acting on a filed HDE, or that FDA will issue a final decision only after a longer period even when no major amendment is submitted.
requirements.hint: State the 75 day deadline from receipt of a filed HDE with no major amendment and name the four possible FDA responses.

requirements.title: HDE approval order
requirements.need: FDA issues an approval order if no ground for denial applies, may approve on draft final labeling conditioned on incorporating specified changes and submitting final printed labeling before marketing, and the approval notice is posted publicly.

quote.text:
FDA will issue to
the applicant an order approving an
HDE if none of the reasons in § 814.118
for denying approval of the application

applies. FDA will approve an applica-
tion on the basis of draft final labeling
if the only deficiencies in the applica-
tion concern editorial or similar minor
deficiencies in the draft final labeling.
Such approval will be conditioned upon
the applicant incorporating the speci-
fied labeling changes exactly as di-
rected and upon the applicant submit-
ting to FDA a copy of the final printed
labeling before marketing.

requirements.topic: FDA issuing an approval order for a humanitarian device exemption application
requirements.complies: The applicant states that FDA will issue an approval order if none of the § 814.118 denial reasons applies, and that approval based on draft final labeling is conditioned on incorporating the specified changes exactly and submitting final printed labeling before marketing.
requirements.conflicts: The applicant claims FDA will approve even when a § 814.118 denial reason applies, or that labeling changes can be made loosely and final printed labeling need not be submitted before marketing.
requirements.hint: Say approval comes when no § 814.118 denial reason applies, and that draft labeling approval requires exact changes plus final printed labeling before marketing.

requirements.title: HDE approvable letter
requirements.need: FDA sends an approvable letter describing the information or conditions required for approval, which may include final labeling, pediatric use information, use restrictions, postapproval requirements, and a compliant FDA inspection.

quote.text:
FDA will send
the applicant an approvable letter if
the application substantially meets the
requirements of this subpart and the
agency believes it can approve the ap-
plication if specific additional informa-
tion is submitted or specific conditions
are agreed to by the applicant. The ap-
provable letter will describe the infor-
mation FDA requires to be provided by
the applicant or the conditions the ap-
plicant is required to meet to obtain
approval.

requirements.topic: FDA sending an approvable letter for a humanitarian device exemption application
requirements.complies: The applicant states that FDA will send an approvable letter when the application substantially meets the subpart requirements and FDA believes it can approve once specific additional information is submitted or specific conditions are agreed to, and that the letter describes that information or those conditions.
requirements.conflicts: The applicant claims FDA will approve outright without any additional information or conditions, or that an approvable letter does not state what the applicant must provide or agree to.
requirements.hint: Describe the approvable letter as listing the specific information to submit or conditions to agree to before approval.

requirements.title: Voluntary HDE withdrawal
requirements.need: FDA considers an HDE voluntarily withdrawn if the applicant fails to respond in writing to an amendment request or to an approvable or not approvable letter within 75 days, or submits written notice of withdrawal.

quote.text:
FDA will consider an HDE to have
been withdrawn voluntarily if:
(1) The applicant fails to respond in
writing to a written request for an
amendment within 75 days after the
date FDA issues such request;
(2) The applicant fails to respond in
writing to an approvable or not approv-
able letter within 75 days after the date
FDA issues such letter; or
(3) The applicant submits a written
notice to FDA that the HDE has been
withdrawn.

requirements.topic: an applicant's failure to respond to FDA requests or letters on a humanitarian device exemption application
requirements.complies: The applicant states that the HDE will be considered voluntarily withdrawn if it does not respond in writing within 75 days to a written amendment request or to an approvable or not approvable letter, or if it submits written notice of withdrawal.
requirements.conflicts: The applicant claims it can let an FDA amendment request or approvable or not approvable letter go unanswered indefinitely without the application being treated as withdrawn, or that withdrawal requires something other than written notice.
requirements.hint: State the 75 day written response deadline for amendment requests and approvable or not approvable letters, and that written notice also counts as withdrawal.

requirements.title: Grounds for HDE denial
requirements.need: FDA may deny or withdraw approval of an HDE if the applicant fails to meet statutory or regulatory requirements or conditions of approval, or if there is no reasonable assurance of safety, the device is ineffective, benefit does not outweigh risk, there is an untrue statement or omission, labeling is noncompliant, studies were noncompliant, inspection is refused, or the HUD designation should be revoked.

quote.text:
FDA may deny approval or with-
draw approval of an application if the
applicant fails to meet the require-
ments of section 520(m) of the act or of
this part, or of any condition of ap-
proval imposed by an IRB or by FDA,
or any postapproval requirements im-
posed under § 814.126.

requirements.topic: FDA approval of a humanitarian device exemption (HDE) application and the grounds for denying or withdrawing that approval
requirements.complies: The text states that FDA may deny or withdraw HDE approval when the applicant fails to meet section 520(m) or part 814 requirements, fails conditions of approval set by an IRB or FDA, or fails postapproval requirements under § 814.126, and it lists grounds such as no reasonable assurance of safety, ineffectiveness, benefits not outweighing risks, untrue statements or omissions, noncompliant labeling, noncompliant studies, refused inspection, or a revoked HUD designation.
requirements.conflicts: The text claims FDA has no basis to deny or withdraw an HDE approval even when the applicant misses statutory or regulatory requirements, breaks IRB or FDA conditions of approval, skips postapproval requirements, submits untrue statements, uses noncompliant labeling or studies, refuses inspection, or no longer holds a valid HUD designation.
requirements.hint: Describe the specific failures and conditions that let FDA deny or withdraw an HDE approval, tying each to section 520(m), part 814, IRB or FDA conditions, or § 814.126 postapproval requirements.

requirements.title: HDE withdrawal hearing
requirements.need: Before issuing an order withdrawing approval of an HDE, FDA provides the applicant notice and an opportunity for a hearing as required for PMAs under § 814.46(c) and (d), and public notice under § 814.46(e).

quote.text:
Before issuing an order with-
drawing approval of an HDE, FDA will
provide the applicant with notice and
an opportunity for a hearing as re-
quired for PMA’s under § 814.46(c) and
(d), and will provide the public with no-
tice in accordance with § 814.46(e), as
applicable.

requirements.topic: FDA procedure for withdrawing approval of a humanitarian device exemption (HDE)
requirements.complies: The text states that before FDA issues an order withdrawing HDE approval, FDA gives the applicant notice and an opportunity for a hearing as required for PMAs under § 814.46(c) and (d), and gives the public notice under § 814.46(e) as applicable.
requirements.conflicts: The text says FDA can withdraw HDE approval by order without first giving the applicant notice or a chance for a hearing, or without giving the public the notice required under § 814.46(e).
requirements.hint: State that an HDE withdrawal order comes only after applicant notice and a hearing opportunity under § 814.46(c) and (d), plus public notice under § 814.46(e).

requirements.title: HDE temporary suspension
requirements.need: An HDE or HDE supplement may be temporarily suspended for the same reasons and in the same manner as prescribed for PMAs in § 814.47.

quote.text:
An HDE or HDE supplement may be
temporarily suspended for the same
reasons and in the same manner as pre-
scribed for PMA’s in § 814.47.

requirements.topic: temporary suspension of a humanitarian device exemption (HDE) or HDE supplement
requirements.complies: The text states that an HDE or HDE supplement may be temporarily suspended for the same reasons and in the same manner as prescribed for PMAs in § 814.47.
requirements.conflicts: The text says an HDE or HDE supplement cannot be temporarily suspended, or that suspension follows different reasons or procedures than those set for PMAs in § 814.47.
requirements.hint: Say that HDE and HDE supplement temporary suspension uses the same reasons and manner as PMA suspension under § 814.47.

requirements.title: HDE file disclosure
requirements.need: The HDE file, including all data and information submitted with or referenced in the HDE, any incorporated IDE, amendments, supplements, reports, and master files, is available for public disclosure in accordance with this section and part 20.

quote.text:
The
‘‘HDE file’’ includes all data and infor-
mation submitted with or referenced in
the HDE, any IDE incorporated into
the HDE, any HDE amendment or sup-
plement, any report submitted under
§ 814.126, any master file, or any other
related submission. Any record in the
HDE file will be available for public
disclosure in accordance with the pro-
visions of this section and part 20 of
this chapter.

requirements.topic: public disclosure of the contents of a humanitarian device exemption (HDE) file
requirements.complies: The text states that the HDE file includes all data and information submitted with or referenced in the HDE, any incorporated IDE, amendments, supplements, reports under § 814.126, master files, and other related submissions, and that any record in the HDE file is available for public disclosure under this section and part 20.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the HDE file and its contents, such as submitted data, incorporated IDEs, amendments, supplements, § 814.126 reports, or master files, are kept confidential and are not available for public disclosure under part 20.
requirements.hint: List what the HDE file contains and state that any record in it is available for public disclosure under this section and part 20.

requirements.title: IRB approval for HUD use
requirements.need: The HDE holder must ensure a HUD is administered only in facilities with IRB oversight and only with IRB approval, except in an emergency where the physician must notify the IRB chairman in writing within 5 days identifying the patient, date, and reason for use.

quote.text:
The HDE holder is
responsible for ensuring that a HUD
approved under this subpart is adminis-
tered only in facilities having over-
sight by an Institutional Review Board
(IRB) constituted and acting pursuant
to part 56 of this chapter, including
continuing review of use of the device.

In addition, a HUD may be adminis-
tered only if such use has been ap-
proved by an IRB.

requirements.topic: IRB oversight and approval for administering a humanitarian use device (HUD)
requirements.complies: The text states that the HDE holder ensures a HUD is administered only in facilities with oversight by an IRB constituted and acting under part 56, including continuing review, and only when that use has been approved by an IRB; in an emergency the physician notifies the IRB chairman in writing within 5 days identifying the patient, the date, and the reason for use.
requirements.conflicts: The text says a HUD may be given in facilities without IRB oversight, or without IRB approval of the use, or that emergency use needs no written notice to the IRB chairman within 5 days identifying the patient, date, and reason.
requirements.hint: State that the HDE holder limits HUD use to IRB-overseen facilities with IRB approval and continuing review, and describe the 5 day written emergency notice to the IRB chairman with patient, date, and reason.

requirements.title: Notice of IRB withdrawal
requirements.need: A holder of an approved HDE must notify FDA of any withdrawal of IRB approval for use of a HUD within 5 working days after being notified of the withdrawal.

quote.text:
A
holder of an approved HDE shall notify
FDA of any withdrawal of approval for
the use of a HUD by a reviewing IRB
within 5 working days after being noti-
fied of the withdrawal of approval.

requirements.topic: reporting withdrawal of IRB approval for use of a humanitarian use device (HUD) to FDA
requirements.complies: The text states that a holder of an approved HDE notifies FDA of any withdrawal of IRB approval for HUD use within 5 working days after being notified of the withdrawal.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the HDE holder need not tell FDA when a reviewing IRB withdraws approval for HUD use, or may wait longer than 5 working days after being notified to report it.
requirements.hint: State that the approved HDE holder reports any IRB withdrawal of HUD use approval to FDA within 5 working days of being notified.

requirements.title: HDE postapproval requirements
requirements.need: An approved HDE is subject to the postapproval requirements and reports under subpart E except § 814.82(a)(7), and medical device reports submitted to FDA under part 803 must also be submitted to the IRB of record.

quote.text:
An HDE approved under this sub-
part H shall be subject to the post-
approval requirements and reports set
forth under subpart E of this part, as
applicable, with the exception of
§ 814.82(a)(7). In addition, medical de-
vice reports submitted to FDA in com-
pliance with the requirements of part
803 of this chapter shall also be sub-
mitted to the IRB of record.

requirements.topic: postapproval reporting duties of a holder of an approved humanitarian device exemption (HDE)
requirements.complies: The text says the approved HDE is subject to the postapproval requirements and reports under subpart E except § 814.82(a)(7), and that every medical device report sent to FDA under part 803 is also sent to the IRB of record.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the HDE holder is exempt from subpart E postapproval reports, or that part 803 medical device reports go only to FDA and not to the IRB of record.
requirements.hint: State that subpart E postapproval requirements and reports apply except § 814.82(a)(7), and that part 803 reports to FDA are also submitted to the IRB of record.

requirements.title: HDE periodic report content
requirements.need: The holder of an approved HDE must prepare and submit complete, accurate, and timely periodic reports including updates of designation and application information, the number of devices shipped or sold with explanation if over 8,000, clinical experience and safety information, and a summary of device changes.

quote.text:
In addition to the reports identi-
fied in paragraph (a) of this section,
the holder of an approved HDE shall
prepare and submit the following com-
plete, accurate, and timely reports:
(1) Periodic reports. An HDE applicant

ance with the approval order.

requirements.topic: periodic reports filed by the holder of an approved humanitarian device exemption (HDE)
requirements.complies: The text says the HDE holder prepares and submits complete, accurate and timely periodic reports as required by the approval order, covering updates of designation and application information, the number of devices shipped or sold with an explanation if over 8,000, clinical experience and safety information, and a summary of device changes.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the HDE holder files no periodic reports, files them late or incomplete, or omits the device shipment count, clinical experience and safety information, or the summary of device changes.
requirements.hint: Describe the periodic reports the approval order requires, listing each item the holder must include and stating they are complete, accurate and timely.

requirements.title: HDE recordkeeping
requirements.need: An HDE holder must maintain records of the names and addresses of facilities to which the HUD has been shipped, correspondence with reviewing IRBs, and any other information requested by an IRB or FDA, in accordance with the HDE approval order.

quote.text:
An HDE holder shall main-
tain records of the names and addresses
of the facilities to which the HUD has
been shipped, correspondence with re-
viewing IRB’s, as well as any other in-
formation requested by a reviewing
IRB or FDA. Such records shall be
maintained in accordance with the
HDE approval order.

requirements.topic: recordkeeping by the holder of an approved humanitarian device exemption (HDE)
requirements.complies: The text says the HDE holder keeps records of the names and addresses of facilities that received the HUD, correspondence with reviewing IRBs, and any other information a reviewing IRB or FDA requests, maintained per the HDE approval order.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the HDE holder keeps no records of where the HUD was shipped, does not keep IRB correspondence, or refuses information requested by an IRB or FDA.
requirements.hint: List the records kept (facility names and addresses, IRB correspondence, other requested information) and state they are maintained per the HDE approval order.

requirements.title: Entities subject to rule
requirements.need: The standards, requirements and implementation specifications apply to health plans, health care clearinghouses, health care providers transmitting health information electronically for a covered transaction, and, where provided, business associates.

quote.text:
(a) Except as otherwise provided, the
standards, requirements, and imple-
mentation specifications adopted under
this part apply to the following enti-
ties:
(1) A health plan.
(2) A health care clearinghouse.
(3) A health care provider who trans-
mits any health information in elec-
tronic form in connection with a trans-
action covered by this subchapter.

requirements.topic: entities covered by the health information privacy standards
requirements.complies: The text says the standards, requirements and implementation specifications apply to health plans, health care clearinghouses, and health care providers who transmit health information electronically for a covered transaction.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the standards do not apply to health plans, clearinghouses or electronic-transmitting providers, or limits them to some other group of entities.
requirements.hint: Name the covered entities: health plans, health care clearinghouses, and health care providers who transmit health information electronically for a covered transaction.

requirements.title: Hybrid entity safeguards
requirements.need: A covered entity that is a hybrid entity must ensure its health care component does not disclose protected health information to another component where subpart E would prohibit it, protects electronic protected health information to the same extent as separate entities, and that shared workforce members do not misuse protected health information.

quote.text:
The cov-
ered entity that is a hybrid entity
must ensure that a health care compo-
nent of the entity complies with the
applicable requirements of this part. In
particular, and without limiting this
requirement, such covered entity must
ensure that:
(A) Its health care component does
not disclose protected health informa-
tion to another component of the cov-
ered entity in circumstances in which
subpart E of this part would prohibit
such disclosure if the health care com-
ponent and the other component were
separate and distinct legal entities;

requirements.topic: safeguards a hybrid covered entity applies to its health care component
requirements.complies: The text says the hybrid entity ensures its health care component does not disclose protected health information to another component where subpart E would prohibit the disclosure if they were separate legal entities, protects electronic protected health information to the same extent as separate entities, and prevents shared workforce members from misusing protected health information.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the health care component freely shares protected health information with other components, applies weaker protection to electronic protected health information than separate entities would, or lets shared workforce members use protected health information without restriction.
requirements.hint: State that the health care component follows subpart E as if it were a separate entity, protects electronic protected health information to that same extent, and restricts shared workforce members' use of protected health information.

requirements.title: Designating health care components
requirements.need: A hybrid covered entity must designate its health care components and document the designation, including any component that would be a covered entity or business associate if separate.

The covered entity is responsible
for designating the components that

components of the covered entity and
documenting the designation in ac-
cordance with paragraph (c) of this sec-
tion, provided that, if the covered enti-
ty designates one or more health care
components, it must include any com-
ponent that would meet the definition
of a covered entity or business asso-
ciate if it were a separate legal entity.

requirements.topic: designation of health care components by a hybrid covered entity
requirements.complies: The text says the hybrid covered entity designates which components form its health care components, documents the designation as required by paragraph (c), and includes any component that would be a covered entity or business associate if it were a separate legal entity.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the hybrid entity has not designated its health care components, keeps no documentation of the designation, or leaves out a component that would be a covered entity or business associate if separate.
requirements.hint: State that the hybrid entity designates and documents its health care components, including every component that would be a covered entity or business associate if it were a separate legal entity.

requirements.title: Designation record retention
requirements.need: A covered entity must maintain a written or electronic record of any designation under this section and retain it for 6 years from creation or last effective date, whichever is later.

paragraph (c)(1) of this section for 6

whichever is later.

requirements.topic: keeping records of designations made under the HIPAA administrative simplification rules
requirements.complies: The entity keeps a written or electronic record of each designation and holds it for 6 years from the date it was created or the date it last was in effect, whichever is later.
requirements.conflicts: The entity keeps no record of its designations, or destroys the record before 6 years have passed since creation or last effective date.
requirements.hint: State that each designation is recorded in writing or electronically and kept for 6 years from creation or last effective date, whichever is later.

requirements.title: Compliance with parts 160 and 162
requirements.need: Covered entities and, where provided, business associates must comply with the applicable provisions of parts 160 and 162 when complying with this part.

quote.text:
In complying with the requirements
of this part, covered entities and,
where provided, business associates,
are required to comply with the appli-
cable provisions of parts 160 and 162 of
this subchapter.

requirements.topic: following the HIPAA administrative simplification rules in parts 160 and 162
requirements.complies: The entity states that in carrying out the requirements of this part it also follows the applicable provisions of parts 160 and 162.
requirements.conflicts: The entity says it follows this part but ignores or claims exemption from the applicable provisions of parts 160 and 162.
requirements.hint: Say that covered entities and business associates, where provided, comply with the applicable provisions of parts 160 and 162 when meeting this part.

requirements.title: Privacy rules apply to covered entities

and implementation specifications of
this subpart apply to covered entities

mation.

requirements.topic: application of the HIPAA privacy standards to covered entities and protected health information

requirements.conflicts: The text says covered entities are not bound by the Subpart E privacy standards for protected health information, or limits them to other parties.
requirements.hint: State that the Subpart E privacy standards apply to covered entities with respect to protected health information, except as otherwise provided.

requirements.title: Clearinghouse as business associate

requirements.conflicts: The text says a clearinghouse acting outside a business associate role is exempt from some Subpart E standards, requirements or implementation specifications.
requirements.hint: State that a clearinghouse handling protected health information other than as a business associate complies with all Subpart E standards, requirements and implementation specifications.

requirements.title: Business associate obligations
requirements.need: The standards, requirements and implementation specifications of Subpart E apply to a business associate with respect to the protected health information of a covered entity.

quirements, and implementation speci-

apply to a business associate with re-
spect to the protected health informa-

requirements.title: Required business associate contract terms

requirements.topic: contracts or other arrangements between governmental covered entities and governmental business associates about protected health information

requirements.title: Other contract requirements
requirements.need: A contract may permit a business associate to use protected health information for its proper management and administration or legal responsibilities, and to disclose it if required by law or if the recipient gives reasonable assurances of confidentiality and notifies of breaches.
