requirements.complies: The text says a workforce member or business associate who in good faith believes the entity acted unlawfully or endangered patients, workers or the public may disclose protected health information to the authorized recipients without the entity being in violation.
requirements.conflicts: The text says such a good faith report to an authorized recipient is a violation, or that workforce members and business associates may never disclose protected health information in these situations.
requirements.hint: Describe the good faith belief and the authorized recipients, and say the covered entity is not considered in violation for such a disclosure.

requirements.title: Treatment, payment, operations uses
requirements.need: A covered entity may use or disclose protected health information for treatment, payment or health care operations as set forth in paragraph (c), provided the use or disclosure is consistent with other applicable requirements of the subpart.

quote.text:
Except with respect to uses or
disclosures that require an authoriza-
tion under § 164.508(a)(2) through (4) or
that are prohibited under
§ 164.502(a)(5)(i), a covered entity may
use or disclose protected health infor-
mation for treatment, payment, or
health care operations as set forth in
paragraph (c) of this section, provided
that such use or disclosure is con-
sistent with other applicable require-
ments of this subpart.

requirements.topic: use or disclosure of protected health information for treatment, payment or health care operations
requirements.complies: The text says the covered entity may use or disclose protected health information for treatment, payment or health care operations as set out in paragraph (c), while still meeting the other applicable requirements of the subpart.
requirements.conflicts: The text says treatment, payment or health care operations uses are allowed without regard to the other subpart requirements, or that they are barred even where paragraph (c) and the other requirements are met.
requirements.hint: State that treatment, payment and health care operations uses are permitted under paragraph (c) and remain subject to the other applicable subpart requirements.

requirements.title: Consent not a substitute for authorization
requirements.need: A covered entity may obtain consent for treatment, payment or health care operations uses, but consent is not effective when an authorization is required or another condition must be met.

quote.text:
A covered entity
may obtain consent of the individual to
use or disclose protected health infor-
mation to carry out treatment, pay-
ment, or health care operations.
(2) Consent, under paragraph (b) of
this section, shall not be effective to
permit a use or disclosure of protected
health information when an authoriza-
tion, under § 164.508, is required or when
another condition must be met for such
use or disclosure to be permissible
under this subpart.

requirements.topic: obtaining a patient's consent for use or disclosure of protected health information for treatment, payment or health care operations
requirements.complies: The text says the covered entity may obtain consent for treatment, payment or health care operations uses, and that consent does not permit a use or disclosure when an authorization is required or another condition must be met.
requirements.conflicts: The text says consent alone is enough even where an authorization is required or another condition must be met, or that consent can never be obtained for treatment, payment or health care operations.
requirements.hint: Say consent may be obtained for treatment, payment and health care operations but does not replace an authorization or satisfy another required condition.

requirements.title: Treatment, payment, operations specifications
requirements.need: A covered entity may use or disclose protected health information for its own treatment, payment or health care operations, for treatment activities of a health care provider, and to another covered entity or provider for payment activities.

quote.text:
A covered entity may use or
disclose protected health information
for its own treatment, payment, or
health care operations.
(2) A covered entity may disclose pro-
tected health information for treat-
ment activities of a health care pro-
vider.

requirements.topic: using or sharing patients' health information for treatment, payment or health care operations
requirements.complies: The text says the organization may use or share protected health information for its own treatment, payment or health care operations, may share it for another provider's treatment activities, and may share it with another covered entity or provider for payment activities.
requirements.conflicts: The text says health information may never be used or shared for treatment, payment or health care operations, or claims such sharing is allowed for purposes beyond treatment, payment, health care operations, another provider's treatment, or payment activities.
requirements.hint: State that use and disclosure of protected health information is limited to treatment, payment and health care operations, another provider's treatment, and payment activities.

requirements.title: Authorization required
requirements.need: A covered entity may not use or disclose protected health information without a valid authorization, and any use or disclosure must be consistent with the authorization obtained.

quote.text:
Except as other-
wise permitted or required by this sub-
chapter, a covered entity may not use
or disclose protected health informa-
tion without an authorization that is
valid under this section. When a cov-
ered entity obtains or receives a valid
authorization for its use or disclosure
of protected health information, such
use or disclosure must be consistent
with such authorization.

requirements.topic: using or disclosing patients' health information without the patient's authorization
requirements.complies: The text says the organization will not use or disclose protected health information without a valid authorization, and that any use or disclosure stays within what that authorization allows.
requirements.conflicts: The text says health information can be used or shared without any authorization, or says the organization may use or share information beyond what the signed authorization permits.
requirements.hint: Say that a valid authorization is required before any use or disclosure not otherwise permitted, and that the use or disclosure will match the authorization.

requirements.title: Authorization for psychotherapy notes
requirements.need: A covered entity must obtain an authorization for any use or disclosure of psychotherapy notes, except for the listed treatment, payment, health care operations and legally required purposes.

quote.text:
Notwithstanding any
provision of this subpart, other than
the transition provisions in § 164.532, a
covered entity must obtain an author-
ization for any use or disclosure of psy-
chotherapy notes, except:
(i) To carry out the following treat-
ment, payment, or health care oper-
ations:
(A) Use by the originator of the psy-
chotherapy notes for treatment;

requirements.topic: use or disclosure of psychotherapy notes
requirements.complies: The text says an authorization is obtained before any use or disclosure of psychotherapy notes, except when the originator uses them for treatment or for the other listed treatment, payment, health care operations and legally required purposes.
requirements.conflicts: The text says psychotherapy notes can be used or shared freely without an authorization, or lists exceptions other than the treatment, payment, health care operations and legally required purposes.
requirements.hint: State that psychotherapy notes require an authorization except for the listed treatment, payment, health care operations and legally required purposes.

requirements.title: Authorization for marketing
requirements.need: A covered entity must obtain an authorization for any use or disclosure of protected health information for marketing, except face-to-face communications and nominal value promotional gifts, and must state third party financial remuneration.

quote.text:
Notwithstanding any provision of
this subpart, other than the transition
provisions in § 164.532, a covered entity
must obtain an authorization for any
use or disclosure of protected health
information for marketing, except if
the communication is in the form of:
(A) A face-to-face communication
made by a covered entity to an indi-
vidual; or
(B) A promotional gift of nominal
value provided by the covered entity.

requirements.topic: use or disclosure of patients' health information for marketing
requirements.complies: The text says an authorization is obtained before any use or disclosure of protected health information for marketing, except face-to-face communications and promotional gifts of nominal value, and that the authorization states any third party financial remuneration.
requirements.conflicts: The text says health information may be used for marketing without an authorization, or treats mailings, emails or other non-face-to-face marketing as exempt, or omits any mention of third party payment.
requirements.hint: Say marketing uses need an authorization except face-to-face talks and nominal value gifts, and that the authorization discloses third party payment.

requirements.title: Authorization for sale of PHI
requirements.need: A covered entity must obtain an authorization for any disclosure of protected health information that is a sale of protected health information, and the authorization must state that remuneration will result.

quote.text:
Notwith-
standing any provision of this subpart,
other than the transition provisions in
§ 164.532, a covered entity must obtain
an authorization for any disclosure of
protected health information which is
a sale of protected health information,
as defined in § 164.501 of this subpart.
(ii) Such authorization must state that
the disclosure will result in remunera-
tion to the covered entity.

requirements.topic: sale of patients' health information
requirements.complies: The text says an authorization is obtained before any disclosure of protected health information that is a sale, and that the authorization states the disclosure will result in remuneration to the organization.
requirements.conflicts: The text says health information may be sold or exchanged for payment without an authorization, or uses an authorization that does not mention that remuneration will result.
requirements.hint: State that any sale of protected health information needs an authorization that says remuneration will result.

requirements.title: Valid authorization defined
requirements.need: A valid authorization must meet the applicable requirements of paragraphs (a)(3)(ii), (a)(4)(ii), (c)(1) and (c)(2), and may contain additional elements only if they are not inconsistent.

quote.text:
A valid authorization is a doc-
ument that meets the requirements in
paragraphs (a)(3)(ii), (a)(4)(ii), (c)(1),
and (c)(2) of this section, as applicable.
(ii) A valid authorization may con-
tain elements or information in addi-
tion to the elements required by this
section, provided that such additional
elements or information are not incon-
sistent with the elements required by
this section.

requirements.topic: what makes a patient authorization form valid
requirements.complies: The text says an authorization is valid only if it contains the required elements under paragraphs (a)(3)(ii), (a)(4)(ii), (c)(1) and (c)(2), and that extra elements are allowed only if they do not conflict with the required ones.
requirements.conflicts: The text says an authorization is valid without the required elements, or adds extra terms that contradict the required elements, such as a different expiration or a waiver of the right to revoke.
requirements.hint: List the required authorization elements and say any added elements must not conflict with them.

requirements.title: Defective authorizations
requirements.need: An authorization is not valid if the expiration date has passed, it is incomplete, revoked, violates the compound or conditioning rules, or contains known false material information.

quote.text:
An au-
thorization is not valid, if the docu-
ment submitted has any of the fol-
lowing defects:
(i) The expiration date has passed or
the expiration event is known by the
covered entity to have occurred;
(ii) The authorization has not been
filled out completely, with respect to
an element described by paragraph (c)
of this section, if applicable;

requirements.topic: submitting and accepting authorizations for use or disclosure of health information
requirements.complies: The text states that an authorization is rejected as invalid when its expiration date has passed, when the expiration event is known to have occurred, or when it is not completely filled out for a required element.
requirements.conflicts: The text says an authorization is still accepted after its expiration date has passed, or that a partially filled out authorization is treated as valid.
requirements.hint: State that an authorization is invalid if expired, incomplete, revoked, improperly combined or conditioned, or contains known false information.

requirements.title: Compound authorizations
requirements.need: An authorization may not be combined with another document into a compound authorization except for the research, psychotherapy notes and other authorization combinations described in this paragraph.

quote.text:
An au-
thorization for use or disclosure of pro-
tected health information may not be
combined with any other document to
create a compound authorization, ex-
cept as follows:
(i) An authorization for the use or
disclosure of protected health informa-
tion for a research study may be com-
bined with any other type of written
permission for the same or another re-
search study.

requirements.topic: combining an authorization with other documents into one form
requirements.complies: The text says an authorization may not be combined with another document into a compound authorization, except for research study permissions, psychotherapy notes, and the other combinations the paragraph allows.
requirements.conflicts: The text says an authorization can be merged with any other document into a single form without restriction, or presents a combined form as allowed in situations outside the listed exceptions.
requirements.hint: Say that combining an authorization with another document is barred unless it falls within the listed exceptions such as research study permissions.

requirements.title: No conditioning of authorizations
requirements.need: A covered entity may not condition treatment, payment, enrollment or eligibility for benefits on an authorization, except for research-related treatment, pre-enrollment health plan authorizations and health care solely to create PHI for disclosure.

quote.text:
A covered entity may not
condition the provision to an indi-
vidual of treatment, payment, enroll-
ment in the health plan, or eligibility
for benefits on the provision of an au-
thorization, except:
(i) A covered health care provider
may condition the provision of re-
search-related treatment on provision
of an authorization for the use or dis-
closure of protected health information
for such research under this section;

requirements.topic: making treatment, payment, enrollment or benefits depend on signing an authorization
requirements.complies: The text says the covered entity will not condition treatment, payment, enrollment or eligibility for benefits on an authorization, except for research-related treatment, pre-enrollment health plan authorizations, and health care solely to create PHI for disclosure.
requirements.conflicts: The text says a patient must sign an authorization to receive treatment, payment, plan enrollment or benefits, with no mention of the permitted exceptions.
requirements.hint: State that treatment, payment, enrollment and benefits are not conditioned on an authorization except in the listed situations.

requirements.title: Retain signed authorizations
requirements.need: A covered entity must document and retain any signed authorization as required by § 164.530(j).

quote.text:
A covered entity
must document and retain any signed
authorization under this section as re-
quired by § 164.530(j).

requirements.topic: keeping records of signed authorizations
requirements.complies: The text says the covered entity documents and retains every signed authorization as required by § 164.530(j).
requirements.conflicts: The text says signed authorizations are not kept, are discarded after use, or that no record of them is maintained.
requirements.hint: State that signed authorizations are documented and retained per § 164.530(j).

requirements.title: Authorization core elements
requirements.need: A valid authorization must contain at least the core elements: description of information, persons authorized to disclose and receive, purpose, expiration date or event, and signature and date.

quote.text:
A valid authorization under this
section must contain at least the fol-
lowing elements:
(i) A description of the information
to be used or disclosed that identifies
the information in a specific and mean-
ingful fashion.
(ii) The name or other specific identi-
fication of the person(s), or class of
persons, authorized to make the re-
quested use or disclosure.

requirements.topic: contents of a valid authorization form
requirements.complies: The text lists the required elements: a specific and meaningful description of the information, the persons or class of persons authorized to disclose and to receive it, the purpose, the expiration date or event, and the individual's signature and date.
requirements.conflicts: The text presents an authorization missing one or more core elements, such as no expiration date, no named recipients, or a vague description of the information.
requirements.hint: List all core elements: information description, disclosing and receiving persons, purpose, expiration date or event, and signature and date.

requirements.title: Authorization required statements
requirements.need: An authorization must contain statements notifying the individual of the right to revoke, the ability or inability to condition treatment or benefits, and the potential for redisclosure.

quote.text:
In addition to
the core elements, the authorization
must contain statements adequate to
place the individual on notice of all of
the following:
(i) The individual’s right to revoke
the authorization in writing, and ei-
ther:
(A) The exceptions to the right to re-
voke and a description of how the indi-
vidual may revoke the authorization;
or
(B) To the extent that the informa-
tion in paragraph (c)(2)(i)(A) of this
section is included in the notice re-
quired by § 164.520, a reference to the
covered entity’s notice.

requirements.topic: notices and statements included in an authorization form
requirements.complies: The text includes statements telling the individual of the right to revoke in writing, how to revoke or a reference to the notice under § 164.520, whether treatment or benefits can be conditioned, and the potential for redisclosure.
requirements.conflicts: The text omits the revocation statement, does not say whether treatment or benefits are conditioned, or fails to mention that redisclosed information may no longer be protected.
requirements.hint: Include statements on the right to revoke, conditioning of treatment or benefits, and potential redisclosure.

requirements.title: Plain language authorization
requirements.need: The authorization must be written in plain language.

quote.text:
The
authorization must be written in plain
language.

requirements.topic: written permission form asking a person to allow use or sharing of their health information
requirements.complies: The authorization is written in short, everyday sentences with common words, organized under simple headings, and explains each item in terms a lay reader can follow.
requirements.conflicts: The authorization is filled with legal jargon, dense run-on sentences, unexplained abbreviations, and technical terms the reader cannot follow.
requirements.hint: Write the authorization in short, simple sentences and everyday words, and explain any term the reader may not know.

requirements.title: Copy of authorization
requirements.need: A covered entity that seeks an authorization must provide the individual with a copy of the signed authorization.

quote.text:
If a covered
entity seeks an authorization from an
individual for a use or disclosure of
protected health information, the cov-
ered entity must provide the individual
with a copy of the signed authoriza-
tion.

requirements.topic: giving a person a copy of the permission form they signed for use or sharing of their health information
requirements.complies: The text states that after the individual signs the authorization, the covered entity gives the individual a copy of the signed authorization.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the signed authorization is kept only in the entity's files and no copy is given to the individual, or that a copy is provided only on request or for a fee.
requirements.hint: State that the individual receives a copy of the signed authorization after signing.

requirements.title: Valid attestation defined
requirements.need: A valid attestation must meet the content requirements, verify the use or disclosure is not prohibited by § 164.502(a)(5)(iii), and may be electronic.

quote.text:
A valid attestation is a document
that meets the requirements of para-
graph (c)(1) of this section.
(ii) A valid attestation verifies that
the use or disclosure is not otherwise
prohibited by § 164.502(a)(5)(iii).
(iii) A valid attestation may be elec-
tronic, provided that it meets the re-
quirements in paragraph (c)(1) of this
section, as applicable.

requirements.topic: written attestation about whether a requested use or disclosure of health information is prohibited
requirements.complies: The attestation contains the content required by paragraph (c)(1), states that the use or disclosure is not prohibited by § 164.502(a)(5)(iii), and may be submitted electronically.
requirements.conflicts: The attestation omits the required content, does not state that the use or disclosure is not prohibited by § 164.502(a)(5)(iii), or the text says an electronic attestation is never accepted.
requirements.hint: Include the paragraph (c)(1) content and a statement that the use or disclosure is not prohibited by § 164.502(a)(5)(iii), and note that an electronic version is allowed.

requirements.title: Defective attestations
requirements.need: An attestation is not valid if it lacks a required element, contains an element not required, violates the compound attestation rule, or is known or reasonably believed to be false.

quote.text:
An attesta-
tion is not valid if the document sub-
mitted has any of the following defects:
(i) The attestation lacks an element
or statement required by paragraph (c)
of this section.
(ii) The attestation contains an ele-
ment or statement not required by
paragraph (c) of this section

requirements.topic: checking whether a submitted attestation about a use or disclosure of health information is valid
requirements.complies: The text lists the defects that make an attestation invalid: a missing required element or statement, an extra element or statement not required by paragraph (c), a violation of the compound attestation rule, or being known or reasonably believed to be false.
requirements.conflicts: The text treats an attestation as valid even though it lacks a required element, adds an element not required, is combined with another document, or is known or reasonably believed to be false.
requirements.hint: List each defect that makes an attestation invalid, matching the four defects in the rule.

requirements.title: Compound attestation
requirements.need: An attestation may not be combined with any other document except one needed to satisfy the content requirements or § 164.502(a)(5)(iii)(C).

quote.text:
An attesta-
tion may not be combined with any
other document except where such
other document is needed to satisfy the
requirements at paragraph (c)(iv) of
this section or at § 164.502(a)(5)(iii)(C),
as applicable.

requirements.topic: combining an attestation about a use or disclosure of health information with other documents
requirements.complies: The text states that the attestation stands alone and is not combined with any other document, except a document needed to meet the paragraph (c)(iv) requirements or § 164.502(a)(5)(iii)(C).
requirements.conflicts: The text says the attestation is attached to or bundled with unrelated forms, contracts, or other documents beyond the ones the rule allows.
requirements.hint: State that the attestation is not combined with other documents except the one needed for paragraph (c)(iv) or § 164.502(a)(5)(iii)(C).

requirements.title: Attestation required elements
requirements.need: A valid attestation must contain the required elements, including a specific description of the information, the persons involved, a statement the use is not prohibited, the criminal penalties statement, and signature and date.

quote.text:
A valid attesta-
tion under this section must contain
the following elements:
(i) A description of the information
requested that identifies the informa-
tion in a specific fashion, including one
of the following:
(A) The name of any individual(s)
whose protected health information is
sought, if practicable.

requirements.topic: contents of an attestation about a requested use or disclosure of health information
requirements.complies: The attestation names the individuals whose information is sought where practicable, describes the information specifically, identifies the persons involved, states the use or disclosure is not prohibited, includes the criminal penalties statement, and is signed and dated.
requirements.conflicts: The attestation gives only a vague description of the information, omits the individuals' names where practicable, leaves out the statement that the use is not prohibited or the criminal penalties statement, or is unsigned or undated.
requirements.hint: Include each required element: a specific description naming the individuals where practicable, the persons involved, the not-prohibited statement, the criminal penalties statement, and a signature with date.

requirements.title: Plain language attestation
requirements.need: The attestation must be written in plain language.

quote.text:
The at-
testation must be written in plain lan-
guage.

requirements.topic: writing an attestation document
requirements.complies: The attestation is written in short sentences and everyday words that an ordinary reader can follow on a first reading.
requirements.conflicts: The attestation is written in dense legal jargon, long nested clauses and technical abbreviations that an ordinary reader cannot follow.
requirements.hint: Write the attestation in short sentences and everyday words so an ordinary reader understands it on the first reading.

requirements.title: Facility directory uses
requirements.need: A covered health care provider may use or disclose limited directory information only if the individual is informed in advance and given the opportunity to restrict or prohibit it, including in emergency circumstances.

quote.text:
A covered
health care provider must inform an
individual of the protected health in-
formation that it may include in a di-
rectory and the persons to whom it
may disclose such information (includ-
ing disclosures to clergy of information
regarding religious affiliation) and pro-
vide the individual with the oppor-
tunity to restrict or prohibit some or
all of the uses or disclosures permitted
by paragraph (a)(1) of this section.

requirements.topic: putting a patient's information in a facility directory
requirements.complies: The provider tells the individual in advance what directory information may be included and to whom it may be disclosed, including clergy for religious affiliation, and gives the individual the chance to restrict or prohibit some or all of those uses or disclosures.
requirements.conflicts: The provider lists the individual's directory information, including religious affiliation to clergy, without telling the individual in advance and without offering any chance to restrict or prohibit it.
requirements.hint: Before placing information in the directory, tell the individual what will be included and to whom, and offer the chance to restrict or prohibit it.

requirements.title: Disclosures to family and others
requirements.need: A covered entity may disclose PHI to family, relatives, friends or others involved in care only in accordance with the agreement, opportunity to object, professional judgment, disaster relief and decedent provisions of this paragraph.

quote.text:
A covered entity
may, in accordance with paragraphs
(b)(2), (b)(3), or (b)(5) of this section,
disclose to a family member, other rel-
ative, or a close personal friend of the
individual, or any other person identi-
fied by the individual, the protected
health information directly relevant to
such person’s involvement with the in-
dividual’s health care or payment re-
lated to the individual’s health care.

requirements.topic: disclosing a patient's health information to family, relatives, friends or others involved in care
requirements.complies: The covered entity discloses only PHI directly relevant to that person's involvement in the individual's health care or payment, and does so under the agreement, opportunity to object, professional judgment, disaster relief or decedent provisions of the paragraph.
requirements.conflicts: The covered entity gives a family member or friend the individual's full health record, including information unrelated to that person's involvement in care, without following the agreement, opportunity to object, professional judgment, disaster relief or decedent provisions.
requirements.hint: Limit what you share with family, relatives, friends or others to PHI directly relevant to their involvement in the individual's care or payment, and follow the paragraph's agreement, opportunity to object, professional judgment, disaster relief or decedent provisions.

requirements.title: Uses required by law
requirements.need: A covered entity may use or disclose PHI to the extent required by law and limited to the relevant requirements of that law, and must meet the requirements of paragraph (c), (e) or (f) as applicable.

quote.text:
A covered entity may
use or disclose protected health infor-
mation to the extent that such use or
disclosure is required by law and the
use or disclosure complies with and is
limited to the relevant requirements of
such law.
(2) A covered entity must meet the
requirements described in paragraph
(c), (e), or (f) of this section for uses or
disclosures required by law.

requirements.topic: using or disclosing health information because a law requires it
requirements.complies: The covered entity discloses only the PHI that the law requires and only as much as the relevant requirements of that law demand, and it meets the applicable paragraph (c), (e) or (f) requirements.
requirements.conflicts: The covered entity discloses more PHI than the law requires or discloses PHI for a purpose the law does not mandate, and does not meet the applicable paragraph (c), (e) or (f) requirements.
requirements.hint: Disclose only the PHI the law requires, limited to that law's relevant requirements, and meet the applicable paragraph (c), (e) or (f) requirements.

requirements.title: Abuse and neglect reports
requirements.need: A covered entity may disclose PHI about a suspected victim of abuse, neglect or domestic violence only as required by law, with agreement, or as expressly authorized, and must promptly inform the individual except in the stated circumstances.

quote.text:
A covered
entity that makes a disclosure per-
mitted by paragraph (c)(1) of this sec-
tion must promptly inform the indi-
vidual that such a report has been or
will be made, except if:
(i) The covered entity, in the exercise
of professional judgment, believes in-
forming the individual would place the
individual at risk of serious harm; or

requirements.topic: reporting suspected abuse, neglect or domestic violence involving a patient
requirements.complies: The covered entity makes the report only as required by law, with the individual's agreement, or as expressly authorized, and promptly informs the individual that the report has been or will be made.
requirements.conflicts: The covered entity reports the suspected abuse, neglect or domestic violence without a legal requirement, agreement or express authorization, or fails to inform the individual that the report has been or will be made when none of the stated exceptions applies.
requirements.hint: Report only as required by law, with agreement or as expressly authorized, and promptly tell the individual about the report unless doing so would place them at risk of serious harm.

requirements.title: Health oversight disclosures
requirements.need: A covered entity may disclose PHI to a health oversight agency for authorized oversight activities, but an investigation of the individual is not a health oversight activity unless it arises out of health care or public benefits related to health.

quote.text:
A covered entity may dis-
close protected health information to a
health oversight agency for oversight
activities authorized by law, including
audits; civil, administrative, or crimi-
nal investigations; inspections; licen-
sure or disciplinary actions; civil, ad-
ministrative, or criminal proceedings
or actions; or other activities nec-
essary for appropriate oversight of:
(i) The health care system;

requirements.topic: disclosing health information to a health oversight agency for oversight activities
requirements.complies: The covered entity discloses PHI to a health oversight agency for oversight activities authorized by law, such as audits, investigations, inspections, licensure or disciplinary actions, or proceedings necessary for oversight of the health care system.
requirements.conflicts: The covered entity discloses PHI to a health oversight agency for an investigation of the individual that does not arise out of health care or public benefits related to health, or for an activity not authorized by law as oversight.
requirements.hint: Disclose PHI to a health oversight agency only for oversight activities authorized by law, and do not treat an investigation of the individual as oversight unless it arises out of health care or health-related public benefits.

requirements.title: Judicial and administrative disclosures
requirements.need: A covered entity may disclose PHI in judicial or administrative proceedings only in response to a court order limited to what is authorized, or to lawful process with satisfactory assurance of notice or a qualified protective order.

quote.text:
A covered entity may
disclose protected health information
in the course of any judicial or admin-
istrative proceeding:
(i) In response to an order of a court
or administrative tribunal, provided
that the covered entity discloses only
the protected health information ex-
pressly authorized by such order; or
(ii) In response to a subpoena, dis-
covery request, or other lawful process,
that is not accompanied by an order of
a court or administrative tribunal, if:

requirements.topic: disclosing patients' health information in lawsuits, court cases and administrative proceedings
requirements.complies: The text says health information is released only when a court or administrative tribunal order expressly authorizes it, and only the information named in that order, or when a subpoena or discovery request comes with documented assurance that the patient was notified or with a qualified protective order.
requirements.conflicts: The text says records are sent to whoever asks in a lawsuit, that entire files go out under a subpoena with no notice to the patient and no protective order, or that more information than the court order names is disclosed.
requirements.hint: State that disclosure happens only under a court order limited to the information it authorizes, or under lawful process with documented notice or a qualified protective order.

requirements.title: Law enforcement disclosures
requirements.need: A covered entity may disclose PHI for law enforcement purposes only if the applicable conditions are met, and for identification or location purposes may disclose only the listed limited information, never DNA, dental records or body fluid analyses.

quote.text:
A covered entity
may disclose protected health informa-
tion for a law enforcement purpose to a
law enforcement official if the condi-
tions in paragraphs (f)(1) through (f)(6)
of this section are met, as applicable.
(1) Permitted disclosures: Pursuant to
process and as otherwise required by law.

requirements.topic: giving patients' health information to police or other law enforcement officials
requirements.complies: The text says health information goes to law enforcement only when the specific legal conditions are met, and for identifying or locating a suspect, fugitive, witness or missing person only the listed limited details are shared, with DNA, dental records and body fluid analyses excluded.
requirements.conflicts: The text says staff hand over full medical records or DNA, dental records or body fluid test results to police on request, or release information for law enforcement purposes without meeting any of the required conditions.
requirements.hint: Describe law enforcement disclosures as allowed only when the rule's conditions are met, and list the limited identifying details permitted, explicitly excluding DNA, dental records and body fluid analyses.

requirements.title: Disclosures about decedents
requirements.need: A covered entity may disclose PHI to coroners, medical examiners and funeral directors for their authorized duties, including in reasonable anticipation of death when necessary for funeral directors.

quote.text:
A covered entity may
disclose protected health information

the purpose of identifying a deceased

or other duties as authorized by law. A
covered entity that also performs the
duties of a coroner or medical exam-
iner may use protected health informa-
tion for the purposes described in this
paragraph.

requirements.topic: sharing patients' health information with coroners, medical examiners and funeral directors after a death
requirements.complies: The text says health information is given to a coroner or medical examiner to identify a deceased person, determine cause of death or carry out other duties authorized by law, and to funeral directors as needed, including in reasonable anticipation of death.
requirements.conflicts: The text says staff refuse all requests from coroners, medical examiners or funeral directors, or release deceased patients' records to them for purposes beyond their authorized duties.
requirements.hint: State that disclosures to coroners, medical examiners and funeral directors are limited to their authorized duties, including identification, cause of death and funeral arrangements.

requirements.title: Cadaveric donation disclosures
requirements.need: A covered entity may use or disclose PHI to organ procurement organizations or similar entities to facilitate cadaveric organ, eye or tissue donation and transplantation.

quote.text:
A covered entity may use or
disclose protected health information
to organ procurement organizations or
other entities engaged in the procure-
ment, banking, or transplantation of
cadaveric organs, eyes, or tissue for the
purpose of facilitating organ, eye or
tissue donation and transplantation.

requirements.topic: sharing patients' health information with organ, eye and tissue procurement or transplant organizations
requirements.complies: The text says health information is used or disclosed to organ procurement organizations and similar entities to facilitate cadaveric organ, eye or tissue donation and transplantation.
requirements.conflicts: The text says donation organizations are denied the information they need, or that records are shared with procurement entities for purposes unrelated to donation and transplantation.
requirements.hint: State that information goes to organ procurement organizations and similar entities only to facilitate cadaveric organ, eye or tissue donation and transplantation.

requirements.title: Research uses and disclosures
requirements.need: A covered entity may use or disclose PHI for research only with documented IRB or privacy board waiver of authorization, researcher representations for preparatory review, or representations and documentation for decedent research.

quote.text:
A covered entity may use or
disclose protected health information
for research, regardless of the source of
funding of the research, provided that:
(i) Board approval of a waiver of au-

proved by either:

requirements.topic: using or disclosing patients' health information for research
requirements.complies: The text says health information is used or disclosed for research only when there is documented IRB or privacy board approval of a waiver or alteration of authorization, or when the researcher has made the required representations for preparatory review or for decedent research.
requirements.conflicts: The text says researchers get patient records for a study without any IRB or privacy board waiver documentation, or that authorization requirements are skipped because the research is unfunded or informal.
requirements.hint: State that research use or disclosure requires documented IRB or privacy board waiver or alteration approval, or the specific researcher representations the rule allows.

requirements.title: Waiver approval documentation
requirements.need: Documentation of an IRB or privacy board alteration or waiver must identify the board and date, state the waiver criteria, describe the PHI needed, state the review procedure used, and be signed by the chair or designee.

quote.text:
For a use or disclosure to be permitted

requirements.topic: the paperwork documenting an IRB or privacy board waiver or alteration of research authorization
requirements.complies: The text says the documentation identifies the IRB or privacy board and the date the waiver or alteration was approved, states the waiver criteria, describes the health information needed, states the review procedure used, and is signed by the board chair or designee.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the waiver paperwork lacks the board's name or approval date, omits the criteria, the description of information needed or the review procedure, or is unsigned or signed by someone other than the chair or designee.
requirements.hint: List every required element of the waiver documentation: board identity and date, waiver criteria, description of the information needed, review procedure, and signature of the chair or designee.

requirements.title: Serious threat disclosures
requirements.need: A covered entity may use or disclose PHI in good faith to prevent or lessen a serious and imminent threat or to help law enforcement identify or apprehend an individual, but not when the information was learned in treatment or counseling, and the disclosure is limited.

quote.text:
A covered enti-
ty may, consistent with applicable law
and standards of ethical conduct, use
or disclose protected health informa-
tion, if the covered entity, in good
faith, believes the use or disclosure:
(i)(A) Is necessary to prevent or less-
en a serious and imminent threat to
the health or safety of a person or the
public; and
(B) Is to a person or persons reason-
ably able to prevent or lessen the
threat, including the target of the
threat;

requirements.topic: sharing a patient's health information to prevent a serious and imminent threat or to help law enforcement identify or apprehend someone
requirements.complies: The text says the covered entity may disclose limited protected health information in good faith when it believes the disclosure is necessary to prevent or lessen a serious and imminent threat to a person or the public, and the disclosure goes only to people reasonably able to prevent or lessen the threat, including the target.
requirements.conflicts: The text says health information learned in treatment or counseling may be shared to stop a threat, or describes disclosures that are not limited, or shares threat-related information with people who cannot act on the threat.
requirements.hint: State that the disclosure is made in good faith, is limited, goes only to persons able to prevent or lessen the threat, and excludes information learned in treatment or counseling.

requirements.title: Specialized government functions
requirements.need: A covered entity may use and disclose PHI of Armed Forces personnel for activities deemed necessary by appropriate military command authorities to assure proper execution of the military mission, if the authority has published the required notice in the Federal Register.

quote.text:
A covered enti-
ty may use and disclose the protected
health information of individuals who
are Armed Forces personnel for activi-
ties deemed necessary by appropriate
military command authorities to as-
sure the proper execution of the mili-

(A) Appropriate military command
authorities; and

requirements.topic: sharing health information of Armed Forces personnel for military mission activities
requirements.complies: The text says the covered entity may use and disclose the protected health information of Armed Forces personnel for activities that appropriate military command authorities deem necessary to assure proper execution of the military mission, and notes that the required notice was published in the Federal Register.
requirements.conflicts: The text says military health information is shared for mission activities without any Federal Register notice having been published, or shares it for purposes military command authorities have not deemed necessary.
requirements.hint: Say the use or disclosure is for activities deemed necessary by appropriate military command authorities and that the required Federal Register notice has been published.

requirements.title: Military separation disclosures
requirements.need: A covered entity that is a component of the Departments of Defense or Homeland Security may disclose protected health information to the Department of Veterans Affairs upon an individual's separation or discharge from military service for DVA benefit eligibility determinations.

quote.text:
A covered entity that is a
component of the Departments of De-
fense or Homeland Security may dis-
close to the Department of Veterans
Affairs (DVA) the protected health in-
formation of an individual who is a
member of the Armed Forces upon the
separation or discharge of the indi-
vidual from military service for the
purpose of a determination by DVA of
the individual’s eligibility for or enti-
tlement to benefits under laws admin-
istered by the Secretary of Veterans
Affairs.

requirements.topic: sharing health information of service members leaving the military with the Department of Veterans Affairs for benefits decisions
requirements.complies: The text says a covered entity that is a component of the Department of Defense or the Department of Homeland Security may disclose the protected health information of a member of the Armed Forces to the Department of Veterans Affairs upon separation or discharge, for a DVA determination of eligibility for or entitlement to veterans benefits.
requirements.conflicts: The text says any hospital or clinic may send service members' health information to the Department of Veterans Affairs, or shares it for purposes other than a DVA benefits eligibility determination, or shares it before separation or discharge.
requirements.hint: Limit the disclosure to a covered entity that is a component of the Departments of Defense or Homeland Security, made upon separation or discharge, for a DVA benefits eligibility determination.

requirements.title: Veterans benefits disclosures
requirements.need: A covered entity that is a component of the Department of Veterans Affairs may use and disclose protected health information to Department components that determine eligibility for or provide benefits under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs.

quote.text:
A covered entity that is
a component of the Department of Vet-
erans Affairs may use and disclose pro-
tected health information to compo-
nents of the Department that deter-
mine eligibility for or entitlement to,
or that provide, benefits under the laws
administered by the Secretary of Vet-
erans Affairs.

requirements.topic: sharing health information within the Department of Veterans Affairs for veterans benefits
requirements.complies: The text says a covered entity that is a component of the Department of Veterans Affairs may use and disclose protected health information to Department components that determine eligibility for or entitlement to, or that provide, benefits under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs.
requirements.conflicts: The text says a private provider or a non-VA entity may send health information to VA benefits components, or says VA components share health information for purposes unrelated to veterans benefits.
requirements.hint: State that the covered entity is a component of the Department of Veterans Affairs and that the recipient component determines eligibility for, or provides, benefits under laws administered by the Secretary of Veterans Affairs.

requirements.title: Foreign military personnel
requirements.need: A covered entity may use and disclose protected health information of foreign military personnel to their appropriate foreign military authority for the same purposes permitted for Armed Forces personnel under the Federal Register notice.

quote.text:
A cov-
ered entity may use and disclose the
protected health information of indi-
viduals who are foreign military per-

military authority for the same pur-
poses for which uses and disclosures

sonnel under the notice published in

paragraph (k)(1)(i) of this section.

requirements.topic: sharing health information of foreign military personnel with their foreign military authority
requirements.complies: The text says the covered entity may use and disclose the protected health information of foreign military personnel to their appropriate foreign military authority for the same purposes permitted for Armed Forces personnel under the Federal Register notice.
requirements.conflicts: The text says foreign military personnel's health information is shared with their foreign military authority for purposes beyond those permitted for Armed Forces personnel under the Federal Register notice, or is shared with a foreign authority that is not their appropriate military authority.
requirements.hint: Say the recipient is the individual's appropriate foreign military authority and that the purpose matches those permitted for Armed Forces personnel under the Federal Register notice.

requirements.title: National security disclosures
requirements.need: A covered entity may disclose protected health information to authorized federal officials for lawful intelligence, counter-intelligence, and other national security activities authorized by the National Security Act and implementing authority.

quote.text:
A covered entity may disclose
protected health information to au-
thorized federal officials for the con-
duct of lawful intelligence, counter-in-
telligence, and other national security
activities authorized by the National
Security Act (50 U.S.C. 401, et seq.) and
implementing authority (e.g., Execu-
tive Order 12333).

requirements.topic: sharing health information with federal officials for intelligence and national security activities
requirements.complies: The text says the covered entity may disclose protected health information to authorized federal officials for lawful intelligence, counter-intelligence, and other national security activities authorized by the National Security Act and its implementing authority.
requirements.conflicts: The text says health information is given to federal officials for national security work that is not lawful or not authorized by the National Security Act, or is given to officials who are not authorized federal officials.
requirements.hint: State that the recipients are authorized federal officials and that the activity is lawful intelligence, counter-intelligence or other national security activity authorized by the National Security Act and its implementing authority.

requirements.title: Protective services disclosures
requirements.need: A covered entity may disclose protected health information to authorized Federal officials for protective services to the President or other authorized persons, or for investigations authorized by 18 U.S.C. 871 and 879.

quote.text:
A covered entity may dis-
close protected health information to
authorized Federal officials for the pro-
vision of protective services to the
President or other persons authorized
by 18 U.S.C. 3056 or to foreign heads of
state or other persons authorized by 22
U.S.C. 2709(a)(3), or for the conduct of
investigations authorized by 18 U.S.C.

requirements.topic: sharing patients' health information with federal officials for protecting the President, foreign heads of state and other protected persons, or for investigations under federal threat statutes
requirements.complies: The text says health information may be given to authorized federal officials only for protective services to the President, foreign heads of state or other protected persons, or for investigations authorized by 18 U.S.C. 871 and 879.
requirements.conflicts: The text says health information is handed to any federal official for any purpose, or to officials for protective services or threat investigations without the officials being authorized.
requirements.hint: State that disclosure goes only to authorized federal officials and only for protective services or the investigations named in 18 U.S.C. 871 and 879.

requirements.title: Medical suitability determinations
requirements.need: A covered entity that is a component of the Department of State may use protected health information to make medical suitability determinations and disclose suitability to State Department officials who need access for security clearances, worldwide availability determinations, or family accompaniment abroad.

requirements.topic: State Department use of health information to decide whether someone is medically suitable for overseas assignment and security clearance
requirements.complies: The text says a State Department health component may use health information to make medical suitability determinations and may tell State Department officials who need it whether the person was found medically suitable, for security clearances, worldwide availability or family accompaniment abroad.
requirements.conflicts: The text says suitability findings are shared with officials outside the State Department, with anyone who asks, or for purposes other than security clearances, worldwide availability or family accompaniment abroad.
requirements.hint: Limit the use to medical suitability determinations and the disclosure to State Department officials who need it for security clearances, worldwide availability or family accompaniment abroad.

requirements.title: Correctional institution disclosures
requirements.need: A covered entity may disclose protected health information about an inmate to a correctional institution or law enforcement official with lawful custody if the institution or official represents the information is necessary for health care, health and safety, law enforcement on the premises, or administration of safety, security, and good order.

A covered entity
may disclose to a correctional institu-

ing lawful custody of an inmate or
other individual protected health infor-
mation about such inmate or indi-
vidual, if the correctional institution
or such law enforcement official rep-
resents that such protected health in-
formation is necessary for:

requirements.topic: giving health information about inmates to correctional institutions or law enforcement officials who have custody of them
requirements.complies: The text says health information about an inmate may be disclosed to a correctional institution or a law enforcement official with lawful custody when that institution or official states the information is needed for the inmate's health care, health and safety, law enforcement on the premises, or safety, security and good order.
requirements.conflicts: The text says inmate health information is released to correctional or law enforcement staff without any statement that it is needed, or for purposes outside health care, health and safety, on-site law enforcement, or safety, security and good order.
requirements.hint: Require lawful custody and a representation from the institution or official that the information is necessary for one of the listed purposes.

requirements.title: Correctional institution uses
requirements.need: A covered entity that is a correctional institution may use protected health information of inmates for any purpose for which such information may be disclosed.

quote.text:
A covered entity
that is a correctional institution may
use protected health information of in-
dividuals who are inmates for any pur-
pose for which such protected health
information may be disclosed.

requirements.topic: correctional institutions using inmates' health information internally
requirements.complies: The text says a correctional institution that is a covered entity may use an inmate's health information for any purpose for which that information could be disclosed.
requirements.conflicts: The text says a correctional institution may use inmate health information for purposes beyond those for which disclosure is allowed, such as any internal purpose without limit tied to the disclosure rules.
requirements.hint: Tie internal uses by the correctional institution to the same purposes for which the information may be disclosed.

requirements.title: Inmate status after release
requirements.need: An individual is no longer an inmate when released on parole, probation, supervised release, or otherwise no longer in lawful custody.

quote.text:
For
the purposes of this provision, an indi-
vidual is no longer an inmate when re-
leased on parole, probation, supervised
release, or otherwise is no longer in
lawful custody.

requirements.topic: when a person stops counting as an inmate because of release or parole
requirements.complies: The text says a person is no longer an inmate once released on parole, probation or supervised release, or when otherwise no longer in lawful custody.
requirements.conflicts: The text says a person released on parole, probation or supervised release still counts as an inmate, or treats custody as continuing after release.
requirements.hint: State that parole, probation, supervised release or any end of lawful custody means the person is no longer an inmate.

requirements.title: Public benefits eligibility sharing
requirements.need: A health plan that is a government program providing public benefits may disclose protected health information relating to eligibility or enrollment to another agency administering a government program providing public benefits if the sharing is required or expressly authorized by statute or regulation.

thorized by statute or regulation.

requirements.topic: government public benefits health plans sharing eligibility or enrollment information with other public benefits agencies
requirements.complies: The text says a government health plan providing public benefits may share eligibility or enrollment information with another agency running a public benefits program when a statute or regulation requires or expressly authorizes the sharing or a shared data system.
requirements.conflicts: The text says eligibility or enrollment information is shared with other agencies without any statute or regulation requiring or expressly authorizing it, or is shared with agencies outside public benefits programs.
requirements.hint: Name the statute or regulation that requires or expressly authorizes the sharing of eligibility or enrollment information between the public benefits agencies.

requirements.title: Public benefits program coordination
requirements.need: A covered entity that is a government agency administering a government program providing public benefits may disclose protected health information to another covered entity that is a government agency administering a government program providing public benefits if the programs serve the same or similar populations and the disclosure is necessary to coordinate covered functions or improve administration.

tions of such programs or to improve

ing to the covered functions of such

requirements.topic: sharing health information between government agencies that run public benefits programs
requirements.complies: The text says the disclosing agency runs a public benefits program and the receiving agency runs a public benefits program, that the two programs serve the same or similar populations, and that the disclosure is needed to coordinate covered functions or improve administration of those programs.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the two programs serve different populations, or that the disclosure is made for a purpose unrelated to coordinating or administering the programs, or that one of the parties is not a government agency administering a public benefits program.
requirements.hint: State that both agencies are government bodies running public benefits programs for the same or similar populations and that the disclosure is needed to coordinate or improve administration of those programs.

requirements.title: NICS firearm reporting
requirements.need: A covered entity may use or disclose protected health information to report to the National Instant Criminal Background Check System the identity of an individual prohibited from possessing a firearm, but only if it is a designated State entity or lawful authority and discloses only to NICS or a designated State entity, limited to demographic information needed and not diagnostic or clinical information.

an individual who is prohibited from
possessing a firearm under 18 U.S.C.
922(g)(4), provided the covered entity:

requirements.topic: reporting a person's identity to the National Instant Criminal Background Check System because a firearm prohibition applies
requirements.complies: The text says the covered entity is a designated State entity or lawful authority, reports only to NICS or a designated State entity, and sends only the demographic information needed to identify the individual, with no diagnostic or clinical details.
requirements.conflicts: The text says a non-designated party reports to NICS, or that the report includes diagnostic or clinical information, or that information is sent to recipients other than NICS or a designated State entity.
requirements.hint: Name the reporting entity as a designated State entity or lawful authority, name NICS or a designated State entity as the only recipient, and limit the data to demographic identifiers.

requirements.title: Workers compensation disclosures
requirements.need: A covered entity may disclose protected health information as authorized by and to the extent necessary to comply with laws relating to workers' compensation or similar programs providing benefits for work-related injuries or illness without regard to fault.

quote.text:
A covered entity may
disclose protected health information
as authorized by and to the extent nec-
essary to comply with laws relating to
workers’ compensation or other similar
programs, established by law, that pro-
vide benefits for work-related injuries
or illness without regard to fault.

requirements.topic: disclosing health information for workers compensation or similar work injury benefit programs
requirements.complies: The text says the disclosure is authorized by workers' compensation or similar no-fault work injury benefit law and is limited to the amount of information that law requires.
requirements.conflicts: The text says health information is shared for workers' compensation purposes beyond what the law authorizes, or for purposes unrelated to a work injury benefit program.
requirements.hint: Tie the disclosure to a specific workers' compensation or similar no-fault work injury law and say only the information that law requires is shared.

requirements.title: De-identification standard
requirements.need: Health information that does not identify an individual and for which there is no reasonable basis to believe it can be used to identify an individual is not individually identifiable health information.

quote.text:
Health infor-
mation that does not identify an indi-
vidual and with respect to which there
is no reasonable basis to believe that
the information can be used to identify
an individual is not individually identi-
fiable health information.

requirements.topic: deciding whether health information is individually identifiable
requirements.complies: The text says the information does not identify an individual and that there is no reasonable basis to believe it could be used to identify an individual, so it is not individually identifiable health information.
requirements.conflicts: The text treats information as de-identified even though it identifies a person or there is a reasonable basis to believe it could be used to identify someone.
requirements.hint: State both that the information does not identify anyone and that there is no reasonable basis to believe it could be used to identify an individual.

requirements.title: Safe harbor identifier removal
requirements.need: A covered entity may determine health information is not individually identifiable only if the specified identifiers of the individual or relatives, employers, or household members are removed and the covered entity has no actual knowledge the information could be used to identify an individual.

quote.text:
The following identifiers of the
individual or of relatives, employers,
or household members of the indi-
vidual, are removed:
(A) Names;

smaller than a State, including street

requirements.topic: removing identifiers from health information under the safe harbor method
requirements.complies: The text lists the identifiers being removed, including names and all geographic subdivisions smaller than a State such as street address, city, county, precinct and full zip code, and states the covered entity has no actual knowledge the remaining information could identify an individual.
requirements.conflicts: The text leaves names or address-level geography such as street address, city, county or full zip code in the data, or admits the covered entity knows the remaining information could still identify someone.
requirements.hint: List each removed identifier category including names and sub-State geography, and state the covered entity has no actual knowledge the information could identify an individual.

requirements.title: Re-identification code rules
requirements.need: A covered entity may assign a code or other means of record identification to allow de-identified information to be re-identified only if the code is not derived from or related to information about the individual and the covered entity does not use or disclose the code for any other purpose or disclose the re-identification mechanism.

requirements.topic: assigning re-identification codes to de-identified health information
requirements.complies: The text says the code is not derived from or related to information about the individual and cannot be translated to identify the individual, and that the code is used only for re-identification and the re-identification mechanism is not disclosed.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the code is built from the individual's data such as initials, birth date or record number, or that the code or the re-identification key is shared or used for other purposes.
requirements.hint: Describe a code unrelated to the individual's data, used only for re-identification, with the re-identification mechanism kept undisclosed.

requirements.title: Minimum necessary standard
requirements.need: A covered entity must meet the minimum necessary requirements with respect to a request for, or the use and disclosure of, protected health information.

paragraphs (d)(2) through (d)(5) of this

requirements.topic: requests for, uses of and disclosures of patients' protected health information
requirements.complies: The text states that every request for, use of and disclosure of protected health information is checked against the minimum necessary requirements in paragraphs (d)(2) through (d)(5) before it proceeds.
requirements.conflicts: The text says protected health information is requested, used or disclosed without applying the minimum necessary requirements, or claims those requirements do not apply to such requests, uses or disclosures.
requirements.hint: State that each request, use and disclosure of protected health information is measured against the minimum necessary requirements in paragraphs (d)(2) through (d)(5).

requirements.title: Minimum necessary uses
requirements.need: A covered entity must identify workforce persons or classes who need access to protected health information and the categories of information needed, and must make reasonable efforts to limit access consistent with those identifications.

A covered entity must

and

protected health information to which
