propriate to such access.

requirements.topic: workforce access to patients' protected health information
requirements.complies: The text says the organization lists the persons or job classes in its workforce who need protected health information to do their duties, lists for each the categories of information needed and any conditions on access, and makes reasonable efforts to limit access to match those lists.
requirements.conflicts: The text says staff can look up any patient information they want, that no list of who needs which information exists, or that access is not limited to the identified persons, categories and conditions.
requirements.hint: Describe a written list of workforce persons or classes, the information categories each needs and any access conditions, plus efforts to keep access within that list.

requirements.title: Minimum necessary disclosures
requirements.need: A covered entity must implement policies and procedures limiting routine disclosures to the amount reasonably necessary, and for other disclosures must develop criteria and review requests individually, and may rely on a requested disclosure as minimum necessary only in specified circumstances.

quote.text:
For any type of
disclosure that it makes on a routine
and recurring basis, a covered entity
must implement policies and proce-
dures (which may be standard proto-
cols) that limit the protected health
information disclosed to the amount
reasonably necessary to achieve the
purpose of the disclosure.

requirements.topic: disclosures of patients' protected health information
requirements.complies: The text says written policies and procedures limit routine and recurring disclosures to the amount reasonably necessary for the purpose, and that other disclosures are judged against set criteria and reviewed one request at a time.
requirements.conflicts: The text says routine disclosures send the full record or more than the purpose needs, that no policies limit routine disclosures, or that non-routine disclosures are released without criteria or individual review.
requirements.hint: State that policies limit routine disclosures to what the purpose reasonably needs and that other disclosures get criteria plus individual review.

requirements.title: Minimum necessary requests
requirements.need: A covered entity must limit any request for protected health information from other covered entities to what is reasonably necessary, implement policies for routine requests, and develop criteria and review other requests individually.

quote.text:
A covered entity
must limit any request for protected
health information to that which is
reasonably necessary to accomplish the
purpose for which the request is made,
when requesting such information from
other covered entities.

requirements.topic: requests to other covered entities for patients' protected health information
requirements.complies: The text says requests to other covered entities are limited to what is reasonably necessary for the stated purpose, with policies for routine requests and criteria plus individual review for other requests.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the organization asks other covered entities for more information than the purpose needs, or sends blanket requests without policies or individual review.
requirements.hint: Describe limiting each request to other covered entities to what the purpose reasonably needs, with policies for routine requests and individual review for the rest.

requirements.title: Entire medical record limit
requirements.need: A covered entity may not use, disclose, or request an entire medical record unless the entire record is specifically justified as reasonably necessary to accomplish the purpose.

quote.text:
For all uses, disclo-
sures, or requests to which the require-
ments in paragraph (d) of this section
apply, a covered entity may not use,
disclose or request an entire medical
record, except when the entire medical
record is specifically justified as the
amount that is reasonably necessary to
accomplish the purpose of the use, dis-
closure, or request.

requirements.topic: use, disclosure or request of an entire medical record
requirements.complies: The text says an entire medical record is used, disclosed or requested only when a written justification states that the whole record is reasonably necessary for the purpose.
requirements.conflicts: The text says whole medical records are routinely sent or requested, or that the full record is released without any specific justification that it is reasonably necessary.
requirements.hint: State that the entire record is used, disclosed or requested only with a specific written justification that the whole record is reasonably necessary.

requirements.title: Limited data set use
requirements.need: A covered entity may use or disclose a limited data set meeting the requirements only if it enters into a data use agreement with the limited data set recipient.

quote.text:
A
covered entity may use or disclose a
limited data set that meets the re-
quirements of paragraphs (e)(2) and
(e)(3) of this section, if the covered en-
tity enters into a data use agreement
with the limited data set recipient, in
accordance with paragraph (e)(4) of this
section.

requirements.topic: use or disclosure of a limited data set of patient information
requirements.complies: The text says a limited data set is used or disclosed only after a data use agreement is signed with the recipient, in line with paragraph (e)(4).
requirements.conflicts: The text says a limited data set is shared with a recipient with no data use agreement, or that the agreement is skipped or signed after the data is handed over.
requirements.hint: State that a limited data set is shared only after a data use agreement with the recipient is in place under paragraph (e)(4).

requirements.title: Limited data set identifiers
requirements.need: A limited data set is protected health information that excludes the specified direct identifiers of the individual or of relatives, employers, or household members.
requirements.topic: limited data sets of patient health information shared with outside parties
requirements.complies: The passage says the data set leaves out names, street addresses beyond town, city, state and zip code, phone and fax numbers, email addresses, social security numbers, medical record numbers, health plan beneficiary numbers, account numbers, certificate and license numbers, and vehicle and device identifiers and serial numbers, including for relatives, employers and household members.
requirements.conflicts: The passage says the data set includes names, street or full postal addresses, phone or fax numbers, email addresses, social security numbers, medical record numbers, account or beneficiary numbers, license or device serial numbers, or such identifiers of relatives, employers or household members.
requirements.hint: List every direct identifier the rule names and state that each one is removed from the data set, including identifiers of relatives, employers and household members.

requirements.title: Limited data set purposes
requirements.need: A covered entity may use or disclose a limited data set only for research, public health, or health care operations, and may use protected health information to create a limited data set or disclose it to a business associate for that purpose.

quote.text:
A covered entity may use or disclose
a limited data set under paragraph
(e)(1) of this section only for the pur-
poses of research, public health, or
health care operations.

requirements.topic: uses and disclosures of a limited data set of health information
requirements.complies: The passage states the limited data set is used or disclosed only for research, public health or health care operations, and that protected health information may be used to create it or disclosed to a business associate for that purpose.
requirements.conflicts: The passage states the limited data set is used or disclosed for marketing, fundraising, sale, employment decisions, or any purpose other than research, public health or health care operations.
requirements.hint: Name the purpose as research, public health or health care operations and say no other purpose is allowed.

requirements.title: Data use agreement
requirements.need: A covered entity may use or disclose a limited data set only if it obtains a data use agreement that establishes permitted uses and disclosures, who may use or receive the data, and that the recipient will not use or further disclose the information except as permitted, will use appropriate safeguards, will report non-permitted uses or disclosures, will ensure agents agree to the same restrictions, and will not identify the information or contact the individuals.

quote.text:
A
covered entity may use or disclose a
limited data set under paragraph (e)(1)
of this section only if the covered enti-
ty obtains satisfactory assurance, in
the form of a data use agreement that
meets the requirements of this section,
that the limited data set recipient will
only use or disclose the protected
health information for limited pur-
poses.

requirements.topic: data use agreements for recipients of a limited data set
requirements.complies: The passage says a data use agreement is obtained before any use or disclosure, and it sets out permitted uses and disclosures, who may use or receive the data, a promise not to use or further disclose except as permitted, safeguards, reporting of non-permitted uses or disclosures, binding of agents to the same restrictions, and a ban on identifying the information or contacting the individuals.
requirements.conflicts: The passage says the limited data set is shared without a data use agreement, or the agreement omits permitted uses, who may receive the data, safeguards, breach reporting, agent restrictions, or the ban on re-identification and contacting individuals.
requirements.hint: State that a signed data use agreement covering all six required terms is in place before any limited data set is shared.

requirements.title: Data use agreement compliance
requirements.need: A covered entity is not in compliance if it knew of a pattern of activity or practice of the limited data set recipient constituting a material breach or violation of the data use agreement unless it took reasonable steps to cure the breach or end the violation and, if unsuccessful, discontinued disclosure and reported the problem to the Secretary; a limited data set recipient that violates a data use agreement is in noncompliance.

quote.text:
A covered entity
is not in compliance with the standards
in paragraph (e) of this section if the
covered entity knew of a pattern of ac-
tivity or practice of the limited data
set recipient that constituted a mate-
rial breach or violation of the data use
agreement, unless the covered entity
took reasonable steps to cure the
breach or end the violation, as applica-
ble, and, if such steps were unsuccess-
ful:
(1) Discontinued disclosure of pro-
tected health information to the re-
cipient; and
(2) Reported the problem to the Sec-
retary.

requirements.topic: handling of a limited data set recipient who breaches the data use agreement
requirements.complies: The passage says that on learning of a pattern of material breach by the recipient, the covered entity took reasonable steps to cure it or end it, and if that failed stopped disclosing protected health information to the recipient and reported the problem to the Secretary.
requirements.conflicts: The passage says the covered entity knew of a pattern of material breach by the recipient and kept disclosing data without curing or ending the violation, without stopping disclosure, or without reporting it to the Secretary.
requirements.hint: Describe the steps taken to cure or end a known pattern of breach and, if they fail, stopping disclosure and reporting to the Secretary.

requirements.title: Fundraising use of PHI
requirements.need: Subject to the conditions of paragraph (f)(2), a covered entity may use or disclose to a business associate or institutionally related foundation specified protected health information for fundraising without an authorization.

quote.text:
Subject to the conditions of
paragraph (f)(2) of this section, a cov-
ered entity may use, or disclose to a
business associate or to an institution-
ally related foundation, the following
protected health information for the
purpose of raising funds for its own
benefit, without an authorization
meeting the requirements of § 164.508:

requirements.topic: use or disclosure of patient health information for fundraising
requirements.complies: The passage says the covered entity uses or discloses the specified protected health information for its own fundraising, to a business associate or to an institutionally related foundation, without an authorization and subject to the conditions in paragraph (f)(2).
requirements.conflicts: The passage says fundraising uses or disclosures of protected health information are made without an authorization and without meeting the paragraph (f)(2) conditions, or are made to parties other than a business associate or institutionally related foundation.
requirements.hint: State that the fundraising use is for the entity's own benefit, goes only to a business associate or institutionally related foundation, and meets the paragraph (f)(2) conditions.

requirements.title: Fundraising requirements
requirements.need: A covered entity may not use or disclose protected health information for fundraising unless the required statement is in its notice of privacy practices, must provide a clear and conspicuous opportunity to opt out with each communication, may not condition treatment or payment on the choice, may not make communications to individuals who opted out, and may provide a method to opt back in.

quote.text:
A covered
entity may not use or disclose pro-
tected health information for fund-
raising purposes as otherwise per-
mitted by paragraph (f)(1) of this sec-
tion unless a statement required by
§ 164.520(b)(1)(iii)(A) is included in the
covered entity’s notice of privacy prac-
tices.

requirements.topic: fundraising communications and opt-out rights for patients
requirements.complies: The passage says the notice of privacy practices contains the required fundraising statement, each fundraising communication gives a clear and conspicuous chance to opt out, treatment or payment is never conditioned on the choice, no communication goes to anyone who opted out, and a way to opt back in is offered.
requirements.conflicts: The passage says fundraising proceeds without the required notice statement, opt-out is hard to find or absent, treatment or payment depends on not opting out, people who opted out still receive communications, or there is no way to opt back in.
requirements.hint: Cover the notice statement, an easy opt-out in every communication, no conditioning of treatment or payment, honoring opt-outs, and an opt-back-in method.

requirements.title: Underwriting use limits
requirements.need: A health plan that receives protected health information for underwriting, premium rating, or related activities and does not place the insurance or benefits may only use or disclose the information for that purpose or as required by law, subject to the genetic information prohibition.

quote.text:
If a
health plan receives protected health
information for the purpose of under-
writing, premium rating, or other ac-
tivities relating to the creation, re-
newal, or replacement of a contract of
health insurance or health benefits,
and if such health insurance or health
benefits are not placed with the health
plan, such health plan may only use or
disclose such protected health informa-
tion for such purpose or as may be re-
quired by law, subject to the prohibi-
tion at § 164.502(a)(5)(i) with respect to
genetic information included in the
protected health information.

requirements.topic: health plan handling of protected health information received for underwriting, premium rating or creating, renewing or replacing a health insurance or health benefits contract that is not placed with the plan
requirements.complies: The health plan states that information received for underwriting or premium rating on a contract not placed with the plan is used only for that underwriting or rating purpose or when the law requires disclosure, and that genetic information in it is not used or disclosed in ways barred by the genetic information prohibition.
requirements.conflicts: The health plan says it reuses or shares the underwriting information for marketing, for other lines of business, or for any purpose it chooses, or it treats genetic information in that information as freely usable.
requirements.hint: State that information received for underwriting or rating on a contract not placed with the plan is used or disclosed only for that purpose or as required by law, and note the genetic information limit.

requirements.title: Verification before disclosure
requirements.need: Prior to any disclosure permitted by this subpart, a covered entity must verify the identity and authority of a person requesting protected health information if not known, and obtain any documentation, statements, or representations that are a condition of the disclosure.

quote.text:
Prior to any disclosure per-
mitted by this subpart, a covered enti-
ty must:
(i) Except with respect to disclosures
under § 164.510, verify the identity of a
person requesting protected health in-
formation and the authority of any
such person to have access to protected
health information under this subpart,
if the identity or any such authority of
such person is not known to the cov-
ered entity; and
(ii) Obtain any documentation, state-
ments, or representations, whether
oral or written, from the person re-
questing the protected health informa-
tion when such documentation, state-
ment, or representation is a condition
of the disclosure under this subpart.

requirements.topic: a covered entity disclosing protected health information to a person who requests it
requirements.complies: Before disclosing, the covered entity checks the requester's identity and authority to receive the information when these are not already known, and collects any documentation, statements or representations that the disclosure requires.
requirements.conflicts: The covered entity releases protected health information to a requester without checking who the person is or whether the person has authority, and without collecting required documentation or statements.
requirements.hint: Describe verifying the requester's identity and authority when unknown and obtaining any documentation or statements the disclosure depends on before releasing information.

requirements.title: Verification reliance rules
requirements.need: A covered entity may rely, if reasonable under the circumstances, on documentation, statements, or representations that on their face meet applicable requirements, on specified proof to verify identity of public officials, on specified statements to verify authority of public officials, and on professional judgment or good faith belief for certain disclosures.

quote.text:
If a disclosure is conditioned by
this subpart on particular documenta-
tion, statements, or representations
from the person requesting the pro-
tected health information, a covered
entity may rely, if such reliance is rea-
sonable under the circumstances, on
documentation, statements, or rep-
resentations that, on their face, meet
the applicable requirements.

requirements.topic: a covered entity relying on documentation, statements or representations when disclosing protected health information
requirements.complies: The covered entity relies on documents, statements or representations that on their face meet the requirements, and does so only when that reliance is reasonable under the circumstances.
requirements.conflicts: The covered entity relies on paperwork or statements that plainly fail the requirements, or relies on them in circumstances where doing so is not reasonable.
requirements.hint: Say reliance is allowed only when reasonable under the circumstances and the documentation, statements or representations on their face meet the requirements.

requirements.title: Right to notice
requirements.need: Except as provided in paragraphs (a)(3) or (4), an individual has a right to adequate notice of the uses and disclosures of protected health information that may be made by the covered entity, and of the individual's rights and the covered entity's legal duties.

quote.text:
Except as pro-
vided by paragraph (a)(3) or (4) of this
section, an individual has a right to
adequate notice of the uses and disclo-
sures of protected health information
that may be made by the covered enti-
ty, and of the individual’s rights and
the covered entity’s legal duties with
respect to protected health informa-
tion.

requirements.topic: notice to individuals of how a covered entity uses and discloses protected health information and of their rights and the entity's duties
requirements.complies: The covered entity gives individuals a notice describing the uses and disclosures of protected health information it may make, the individuals' rights, and the entity's legal duties, except where the exceptions in paragraphs (a)(3) or (4) apply.
requirements.conflicts: The covered entity gives individuals no notice, or a notice that omits the uses and disclosures it may make, the individuals' rights, or the entity's legal duties.
requirements.hint: Describe giving individuals a notice covering the uses and disclosures the entity may make, their rights, and the entity's duties, noting the (a)(3) and (a)(4) exceptions.

requirements.title: Part 2 records notice
requirements.need: An individual who is the subject of records protected under 42 CFR part 2 has a right to adequate notice of the uses and disclosures of such records and of the individual's rights and the covered entity's legal duties.

quote.text:
As provided in
42 CFR 2.22, an individual who is the
subject of records protected under 42
CFR part 2 has a right to adequate no-
tice of the uses and disclosures of such
records, and of the individual’s rights
and the covered entity’s legal duties
with respect to such records.

requirements.topic: notice to individuals whose records are protected under 42 CFR part 2 of uses and disclosures of those records and of their rights and the entity's duties
requirements.complies: The covered entity gives individuals who are the subject of 42 CFR part 2 records a notice describing the uses and disclosures of those records, the individuals' rights, and the entity's legal duties, as 42 CFR 2.22 provides.
requirements.conflicts: The covered entity gives no notice to individuals whose records are protected under 42 CFR part 2, or a notice that leaves out the uses and disclosures of those records, their rights, or the entity's duties.
requirements.hint: Describe giving individuals subject to 42 CFR part 2 records a notice of uses and disclosures of those records, their rights, and the entity's duties, as 42 CFR 2.22 provides.

requirements.title: Group health plan notice
requirements.need: An individual enrolled in a group health plan has a right to notice from the plan or from the health insurance issuer or HMO as specified, and a group health plan that creates or receives protected health information beyond summary health information must maintain a notice and provide it upon request, while a plan that does not create or receive such information is not required to maintain or provide a notice.

quote.text:
A group health plan that provides
health benefits solely through an in-
surance contract with a health insur-
ance issuer or HMO, and that creates
or receives protected health informa-
tion in addition to summary health in-
formation as defined in § 164.504(a) or
information on whether the individual
is participating in the group health
plan, or is enrolled in or has
disenrolled from a health insurance
issuer or HMO offered by the plan,
must:
(A) Maintain a notice under this sec-
tion; and
(B) Provide such notice upon request
to any person.

requirements.topic: notice obligations of a group health plan that provides benefits through an insurance contract with a health insurance issuer or HMO
requirements.complies: The group health plan that creates or receives protected health information beyond summary health information and enrollment or participation data maintains a notice and provides it on request to any person, and individuals enrolled in the plan are told of their right to notice from the plan or from the issuer or HMO as specified.
requirements.conflicts: The group health plan that creates or receives protected health information beyond summary health information keeps no notice and refuses requests for one, or the text says a plan in that position has no notice duties.
requirements.hint: State that a group health plan creating or receiving protected health information beyond summary health information and enrollment data must maintain a notice and give it on request, and that a plan that does not create or receive such information need not maintain or provide one.

requirements.title: Inmate notice exception
requirements.need: An inmate does not have a right to notice under this section, and the requirements of this section do not apply to a correctional institution that is a covered entity.

quote.text:
An inmate
does not have a right to notice under
this section, and the requirements of
this section do not apply to a correc-
tional institution that is a covered en-
tity.

requirements.topic: giving privacy notice to inmates of a correctional institution
requirements.complies: The text states that inmates do not have a right to notice under this section and that the notice requirements do not apply to a correctional institution that is a covered entity.
requirements.conflicts: The text says inmates must receive the privacy notice or that a correctional institution must issue notices to inmates under this section.
requirements.hint: State plainly that inmates have no right to notice under this section and that the requirements do not apply to a correctional institution that is a covered entity.

requirements.title: Separate statements in notice
requirements.need: If the covered entity intends to engage in specified activities such as fundraising, disclosure to a plan sponsor, underwriting, or use of part 2 records, the notice must include a separate statement informing the individual of such activities.

quote.text:
If the covered entity
intends to engage in any of the fol-
lowing activities, the description re-
quired by paragraph (b)(1)(ii)(A) or (B)
of this section must include a separate
statement informing the individual of
such activities, as applicable:

requirements.topic: privacy notice statements about fundraising, plan sponsor disclosures, underwriting and part 2 records
requirements.complies: The notice includes a separate statement for each intended activity such as fundraising, disclosure to a plan sponsor, underwriting, or use of part 2 records, telling the individual about that activity.
requirements.conflicts: The notice mentions fundraising, plan sponsor disclosures, underwriting or part 2 records only inside general text with no separate statement, or omits them while the entity intends to do them.
requirements.hint: For each intended activity on the list, add its own separate statement in the notice describing that activity.

requirements.title: Optional notice elements
requirements.need: A covered entity may describe more limited uses or disclosures in its notice, but may not include a limitation affecting its right to make a use or disclosure required by law or permitted by § 164.512(j)(1)(i), and must include the required statements to apply changes to information created or received before a revised notice.

quote.text:
In addition to
the information required by paragraph
(b)(1) of this section, if a covered entity
elects to limit the uses or disclosures
that it is permitted to make under this
subpart, the covered entity may de-
scribe its more limited uses or disclo-
sures in its notice, provided that the
covered entity may not include in its
notice a limitation affecting its right
to make a use or disclosure that is re-
quired by law or permitted by
§ 164.512(j)(1)(i).

requirements.topic: voluntary limits a covered entity places on its own uses and disclosures in its privacy notice
requirements.complies: The notice describes the entity's more limited uses or disclosures and does not limit any use or disclosure required by law or permitted by § 164.512(j)(1)(i), and it includes the required statements for applying changes to information created or received before a revised notice.
requirements.conflicts: The notice claims a limit that would block a use or disclosure required by law or permitted by § 164.512(j)(1)(i), or applies changes to earlier information without the required statements.
requirements.hint: If you describe narrower uses or disclosures, keep out any limit on uses required by law or permitted by § 164.512(j)(1)(i) and include the required statements for changes to earlier information.

requirements.title: Health plan notice provision
requirements.need: A health plan must provide the notice no later than the compliance date to then-covered individuals and at enrollment to new enrollees, notify individuals at least once every three years of the notice's availability, and follow specified rules for material changes including web posting and annual mailing or provision within 60 days.

quote.text:
A health plan must provide
the notice:
(A) No later than the compliance
date for the health plan, to individuals
then covered by the plan;
(B) Thereafter, at the time of enroll-
ment, to individuals who are new en-
rollees.

requirements.topic: health plan delivery of the privacy notice to enrollees
requirements.complies: The plan gives the notice by the compliance date to people then covered, gives it at enrollment to new enrollees, tells individuals at least once every three years that the notice is available, and for material changes posts the notice on its website and mails it or provides it within 60 days.
requirements.conflicts: The plan gives no notice at enrollment, never tells individuals every three years that the notice is available, or makes material changes without web posting and mailing or providing the revised notice within 60 days.
requirements.hint: Cover the timing: compliance date for current members, enrollment for new enrollees, a reminder at least every three years, and web posting plus mailing or 60 day provision for material changes.

requirements.title: Provider notice provision
requirements.need: A covered health care provider with a direct treatment relationship must provide the notice no later than the first service delivery or as soon as reasonably practicable after emergency treatment, make a good faith effort to obtain written acknowledgment and document efforts if not obtained, have the notice available and posted at physical sites, and make revised notices available upon request.

quote.text:
A covered
health care provider that has a direct
treatment relationship with an indi-
vidual must:
(i) Provide the notice:
(A) No later than the date of the first
service delivery, including service de-
livered electronically, to such indi-
vidual after the compliance date for
the covered health care provider; or
(B) In an emergency treatment situa-
tion, as soon as reasonably practicable
after the emergency treatment situa-
tion.

requirements.topic: health care provider delivery of the privacy notice to patients in a direct treatment relationship
requirements.complies: The provider gives the notice no later than the first service delivery, including electronic delivery, or as soon as reasonably practicable after emergency treatment, makes a good faith effort to get written acknowledgment and documents the effort if none is obtained, keeps the notice available and posted at its sites, and gives revised notices on request.
requirements.conflicts: The provider hands out the notice only after several visits, skips the written acknowledgment effort or any record of it, has no notice posted at its sites, or refuses to give revised notices on request.
requirements.hint: Describe giving the notice at first service delivery or soon after emergency treatment, the documented good faith effort for written acknowledgment, posted copies at sites, and revised notices on request.

requirements.title: Electronic notice rules
requirements.need: A covered entity that maintains a website about customer services or benefits must prominently post its notice and make it available electronically, may provide notice by e-mail if the individual agrees and the agreement is not withdrawn, must provide a paper copy if e-mail transmission fails, must provide electronic notice automatically for first electronic service delivery, and the individual retains the right to a paper copy.

quote.text:
A covered entity that main-
tains a web site that provides informa-
tion about the covered entity’s cus-
tomer services or benefits must promi-
nently post its notice on the web site
and make the notice available elec-
tronically through the web site.

requirements.topic: electronic delivery of the privacy notice through websites and e-mail
requirements.complies: The entity prominently posts the notice on its customer services or benefits website and makes it available there, sends it by e-mail only when the individual agrees and has not withdrawn, provides a paper copy if e-mail fails, gives electronic notice automatically at first electronic service delivery, and keeps the right to a paper copy.
requirements.conflicts: The website has no posted notice or hides it, e-mail notice is sent without the individual's agreement, no paper copy is offered when e-mail fails, or the text says individuals lose the right to a paper copy.
requirements.hint: Cover prominent web posting, e-mail only with unwithdrawn agreement, a paper copy if e-mail fails, automatic electronic notice at first electronic service, and the continuing right to a paper copy.

requirements.title: Joint notice requirements
requirements.need: Covered entities participating in organized health care arrangements may comply by a joint notice if they agree to abide by its terms, the notice meets content specifications and describes the covered entities and service delivery sites, and provision by one covered entity satisfies the requirement for all, without removing obligations for part 2 records.

quote.text:
Cov-
ered entities that participate in orga-
nized health care arrangements may
comply with this section by a joint no-
tice, provided that:
(1) The covered entities participating
in the organized health care arrange-
ment agree to abide by the terms of the
notice with respect to protected health
information created or received by the
covered entity as part of its participa-
tion in the organized health care ar-
rangement;

requirements.topic: joint privacy notices issued by covered entities in organized health care arrangements
requirements.complies: The covered entities in the arrangement state that they agree to abide by the terms of the joint notice for information created or received through their participation, the notice describes the covered entities and service delivery sites and meets content requirements, and one entity providing the notice is described as satisfying the requirement for all while part 2 records obligations remain.
requirements.conflicts: The text says entities in the arrangement never agreed to the joint notice's terms, or the notice omits which covered entities and service delivery sites it covers, or it claims a joint notice removes obligations for part 2 records.
requirements.hint: Describe the joint notice as agreed to by all participating entities, covering the named entities and sites, meeting content rules, and not lifting part 2 record duties.

requirements.title: Notice documentation
requirements.need: A covered entity must document compliance with the notice requirements by retaining copies of the notices issued and, if applicable, any written acknowledgments of receipt or documentation of good faith efforts to obtain acknowledgment.

quote.text:
A covered entity must docu-
ment compliance with the notice re-
quirements, as required by § 164.530(j),
by retaining copies of the notices
issued by the covered entity and, if ap-
plicable, any written acknowledgments
of receipt of the notice or documenta-
tion of good faith efforts to obtain such
written acknowledgment, in accord-
ance with paragraph (c)(2)(ii) of this
section.

requirements.topic: recordkeeping of privacy notices and acknowledgments of receipt
requirements.complies: The text states that the covered entity keeps copies of every notice it issued and, where applicable, written acknowledgments of receipt or records of good faith efforts to obtain acknowledgment.
requirements.conflicts: The text says notices are not retained, or that acknowledgments of receipt and records of good faith efforts are discarded or never kept.
requirements.hint: Say the entity retains copies of issued notices plus any written acknowledgments or documentation of good faith efforts to get them.

requirements.title: Right to request restrictions
requirements.need: A covered entity must permit an individual to request restrictions on uses or disclosures for treatment, payment, or health care operations and on disclosures under § 164.510(b), is not required to agree except for a restriction on disclosure to a health plan where the individual paid in full, and may not use or disclose information in violation of an agreed restriction except for emergency treatment.

quote.text:
A covered entity must permit
an individual to request that the cov-
ered entity restrict:
(A) Uses or disclosures of protected
health information about the indi-
vidual to carry out treatment, pay-
ment, or health care operations; and
(B) Disclosures permitted under
§ 164.510(b).

requirements.topic: patients asking to restrict use or disclosure of their health information
requirements.complies: The text says individuals may request restrictions on uses and disclosures for treatment, payment, or health care operations and on disclosures under § 164.510(b), that the entity need not agree except when the individual paid in full and asks to restrict disclosure to a health plan, and that agreed restrictions are honored except for emergency treatment.
requirements.conflicts: The text says individuals are not allowed to ask for restrictions, or that the entity ignores an agreed restriction, or that it discloses to a health plan despite a paid-in-full restriction outside an emergency.
requirements.hint: State that requests are accepted, agreement is optional except for paid-in-full health plan restrictions, and agreed limits are followed except in emergencies.

requirements.title: Terminating restrictions
requirements.need: A covered entity may terminate a restriction if the individual agrees or requests termination in writing, if the individual orally agrees and the agreement is documented, or if the covered entity informs the individual of termination, but termination is not effective for restrictions under paragraph (a)(1)(vi) and is only effective for information created or received after notice.

quote.text:
A covered entity
may terminate a restriction, if:
(i) The individual agrees to or re-
quests the termination in writing;
(ii) The individual orally agrees to
the termination and the oral agree-
ment is documented; or
(iii) The covered entity informs the
individual that it is terminating its
agreement to a restriction, except that
such termination is:
(A) Not effective for protected health
information restricted under paragraph
(a)(1)(vi) of this section; and
(B) Only effective with respect to
protected health information created
or received after it has so informed the
individual.

requirements.topic: ending an agreed restriction on use or disclosure of health information
requirements.complies: The text says a restriction may end when the individual agrees or requests in writing, when the individual agrees orally and that agreement is documented, or when the entity informs the individual of termination, with termination not applying to paragraph (a)(1)(vi) restrictions and only covering information created or received after the notice.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the entity can end a restriction without telling the individual or without any written or documented oral agreement, or that termination applies to already existing information or to paragraph (a)(1)(vi) restrictions.
requirements.hint: List the three termination routes and state that termination never touches (a)(1)(vi) restrictions and only affects information created or received afterward.

requirements.title: Restriction documentation
requirements.need: A covered entity must document a restriction in accordance with § 160.530(j) of this subchapter.

quote.text:
A covered entity must docu-
ment a restriction in accordance with
§ 160.530(j) of this subchapter.

requirements.topic: written records of restrictions on use or disclosure of health information
requirements.complies: The text states that each restriction is documented as required by § 160.530(j).
requirements.conflicts: The text says restrictions are handled informally with no written record kept.
requirements.hint: Say the entity documents each restriction in line with § 160.530(j).

requirements.title: Confidential communications
requirements.need: A covered health care provider must permit and accommodate reasonable requests to receive communications by alternative means or at alternative locations, and a health plan must do so if the individual clearly states that disclosure could endanger the individual.

quote.text:
A covered
health care provider must permit indi-
viduals to request and must accommo-

to receive communications of pro-
tected health information from the
covered health care provider by alter-
native means or at alternative loca-
tions.

requirements.topic: receiving health information by alternative means or at alternative locations
requirements.complies: The text says the provider lets individuals ask to receive communications by other means or at other locations and accommodates reasonable requests, and the health plan does so when the individual clearly states that disclosure could endanger them.
requirements.conflicts: The text says requests for alternative means or locations are refused, or that a plan ignores a request where the individual clearly states disclosure could endanger them.
requirements.hint: State that reasonable requests for other means or locations are accepted and accommodated, with plans acting when the individual says disclosure could endanger them.

requirements.title: Confidential communication conditions
requirements.need: A covered entity may require a written request and may condition accommodation on payment information and specification of an alternative address or contact method, but a covered health care provider may not require an explanation for the request, and a health plan may require a statement that disclosure could endanger the individual.

quote.text:
A covered entity may re-
quire the individual to make a request
for a confidential communication de-
scribed in paragraph (b)(1) of this sec-
tion in writing.

requirements.topic: requesting confidential communications of health information by an alternative address or contact method
requirements.complies: The provider accepts a written request for confidential communication and may ask for payment information and an alternative address or contact method, and does not ask the individual to explain why. A health plan may ask for a statement that disclosure could endanger the individual.
requirements.conflicts: The provider demands a written explanation of why the individual wants confidential communication, or refuses the request unless the individual justifies it.
requirements.hint: State that a written request may be required and that payment details and an alternative address or contact method may be requested, but no explanation of the reason.

requirements.title: Right of access
requirements.need: Except as otherwise provided, an individual has a right of access to inspect and obtain a copy of protected health information about the individual in a designated record set, except for psychotherapy notes and information compiled in anticipation of or for use in a civil, criminal, or administrative action or proceeding.

quote.text:
Except
as otherwise provided in paragraph
(a)(2) or (a)(3) of this section, an indi-
vidual has a right of access to inspect
and obtain a copy of protected health
information about the individual in a
designated record set, for as long as the
protected health information is main-
tained in the designated record set, ex-
cept for:
(i) Psychotherapy notes; and
(ii) Information compiled in reason-
able anticipation of, or for use in, a
civil, criminal, or administrative ac-
tion or proceeding.

requirements.topic: individuals inspecting and obtaining copies of their own health information held in a designated record set
requirements.complies: The individual is allowed to inspect and receive a copy of protected health information about them in the designated record set, while psychotherapy notes and information compiled for a civil, criminal or administrative action are excluded.
requirements.conflicts: The individual is refused a copy of their own record in the designated record set for reasons other than the listed exceptions, or psychotherapy notes or litigation-prepared information are handed over as part of the right of access.
requirements.hint: Describe the right to inspect and copy records in the designated record set and name the two exceptions: psychotherapy notes and information compiled for legal or administrative proceedings.

requirements.title: Unreviewable access denials
requirements.need: A covered entity may deny access without opportunity for review when the information is excepted from the right of access, when a correctional institution or provider acting under its direction determines a copy would jeopardize health, safety, security, custody, or rehabilitation, when research access was agreed to be suspended, when Privacy Act denial requirements are met, or when the information was obtained under a promise of confidentiality and access would likely reveal the source.

A

access without providing the individual
an opportunity for review, in the fol-
lowing circumstances.
(i) The protected health information
is excepted from the right of access by
paragraph (a)(1) of this section.

requirements.topic: denying an individual access to their health information without any chance to have the denial reviewed
requirements.complies: Access is denied with no review when the information falls under the right-of-access exceptions, when a correctional institution or its provider finds a copy would jeopardize health, safety, security, custody or rehabilitation, when agreed research access is suspended, when Privacy Act denial rules are met, or when information given under a promise of confidentiality would likely reveal its source.
requirements.conflicts: Access is denied with no review for a reason outside the listed grounds, or a denial on one of these grounds is described as reviewable.
requirements.hint: List the specific situations where access can be denied with no review, and keep every other denial out of that list.

requirements.title: Reviewable access denials
requirements.need: A covered entity may deny access with a right to review when a licensed health care professional determines access is reasonably likely to endanger life or physical safety, when the information references another person and access is reasonably likely to cause substantial harm to that person, or when a personal representative's access is reasonably likely to cause substantial harm.

quote.text:
A
covered entity may deny an individual
access, provided that the individual is
given a right to have such denials re-
viewed, as required by paragraph (a)(4)
of this section, in the following cir-
cumstances:
(i) A licensed health care professional
has determined, in the exercise of pro-
fessional judgment, that the access re-
quested is reasonably likely to endan-
ger the life or physical safety of the in-
dividual or another person;

requirements.topic: denying an individual access to their health information with a right to have the denial reviewed
requirements.complies: Access is denied with a right to review because a licensed health care professional judged access reasonably likely to endanger life or physical safety, because the information references another person and access is reasonably likely to cause that person substantial harm, or because a personal representative's access is reasonably likely to cause substantial harm.
requirements.conflicts: Access is denied with a right to review for reasons other than danger to life or physical safety or substantial harm to another person, or a denial on these grounds is described as final with no review.
requirements.hint: Name the three reviewable grounds and state that the individual is told of the right to have the denial reviewed.

requirements.title: Review of access denial
requirements.need: If access is denied on a reviewable ground, the individual has the right to have the denial reviewed by a licensed health care professional designated as a reviewing official who did not participate in the original decision, and the covered entity must provide or deny access in accordance with the reviewing official's determination.

quote.text:
If ac-
cess is denied on a ground permitted
under paragraph (a)(3) of this section,
the individual has the right to have the
denial reviewed by a licensed health
care professional who is designated by
the covered entity to act as a review-
ing official and who did not participate
in the original decision to deny. The
covered entity must provide or deny
access in accordance with the deter-
mination of the reviewing official
under paragraph (d)(4) of this section.

requirements.topic: review of a denial of an individual's access to their health information
requirements.complies: The individual can have a reviewable denial reviewed by a licensed health care professional designated as reviewing official who did not make the original decision, and the entity provides or denies access according to that official's determination.
requirements.conflicts: The same person who denied access also reviews the denial, no reviewing official is designated, or the entity ignores the reviewing official's determination.
requirements.hint: State that a different licensed health care professional designated as reviewing official decides the review and that the entity follows that decision.

requirements.title: Access request handling
requirements.need: The covered entity must permit an individual to request access to protected health information.

quote.text:
The cov-
ered entity must permit an individual

requirements.topic: individuals asking for access to their health information
requirements.complies: The covered entity lets the individual submit a request for access to protected health information.
requirements.conflicts: The covered entity refuses to accept or allow any request for access to protected health information.
requirements.hint: State plainly that the entity permits individuals to request access to their protected health information.

requirements.title: Access request process
requirements.need: A covered entity must permit individuals to request access to inspect or obtain a copy of their protected health information in a designated record set, and may require written requests only if it informs individuals of that requirement.

quote.text:
The covered entity may require indi-
viduals to make requests for access in
writing, provided that it informs indi-
viduals of such a requirement.

requirements.topic: patients asking to see or get a copy of their health records
requirements.complies: The text says individuals can ask to inspect or get a copy of their health information, and that a written request is required only when the patient is told in advance that requests must be in writing.
requirements.conflicts: The text says patients cannot ask for their records at all, or that a written request is demanded without ever telling patients that writing is required.
requirements.hint: State that patients may request access to their records and, if you require it in writing, say that patients are told of the written-request requirement.

requirements.title: 30-day action on access
requirements.need: A covered entity must act on a request for access no later than 30 days after receipt, either informing the individual of acceptance and providing the access or giving a written denial.

quote.text:
Except as provided in paragraph

tity must act on a request for access no

requirements.topic: how fast a health care provider responds to a patient's request for their records
requirements.complies: The text says the provider acts on the request within 30 days of receiving it, either telling the patient the request is accepted and giving the access or sending a written denial.
requirements.conflicts: The text says responses take 60 or 90 days, or that the provider can ignore a request or answer it without any deadline.
requirements.hint: Say the provider responds within 30 days of getting the request, by providing the access or sending a written denial.

requirements.title: One 30-day extension
requirements.need: If unable to act within the initial period, a covered entity may extend the time by no more than 30 days, only once, and must within the original time limit give the individual a written statement of the reasons for the delay and the completion date.

requirements.topic: extending the deadline for responding to a patient's records request

requirements.conflicts: The text says the provider can extend the deadline more than once or for more than 30 days, or can delay without sending the patient a written reason and completion date within the original 30 days.
requirements.hint: Describe a single 30-day extension, with a written notice of the reason and completion date sent inside the original 30 days.

requirements.title: Provide requested access
requirements.need: A covered entity must provide the access requested, including inspection, a copy, or both, of the protected health information in designated record sets, and need produce the information only once even if it is held in multiple record sets or locations.

requirements.topic: giving patients the health records they asked for
requirements.complies: The text says the provider gives the patient the access requested, whether inspection, a copy, or both, and produces the same information only once even if it sits in several record sets or locations.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the provider refuses to hand over the requested records, or insists on producing duplicates from every record set or location before responding.
requirements.hint: State that the requested access (inspection, copy, or both) is provided and that duplicate copies from multiple locations are not required.

requirements.title: Form and format
requirements.need: A covered entity must provide access in the form and format requested if readily producible, or otherwise in a readable hard copy form or another form and format agreed with the individual.

The

copy form or such other form and for-
mat as agreed to by the covered entity
and the individual.

requirements.topic: the form and format in which patients receive copies of their health records
requirements.complies: The text says the provider supplies the records in the form and format the patient asked for when that is readily producible, and otherwise in a readable hard copy or another form and format the provider and patient agree on.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the provider picks whatever format it likes regardless of the request, or hands over an unreadable or unusable format without agreeing on an alternative with the patient.
requirements.hint: Say the requested form and format is used when readily producible, otherwise a readable hard copy or a format agreed with the patient.

requirements.title: Electronic copy on request
requirements.need: When the information is maintained electronically and the individual requests an electronic copy, a covered entity must provide it in the requested electronic form and format if readily producible, or otherwise in a readable electronic form and format agreed with the individual.

ducible in such form and format; or, if

requirements.complies: The text says that when records are kept electronically and the patient asks for an electronic copy, the provider gives it in the requested electronic form and format if readily producible, otherwise in a readable electronic form and format agreed with the patient.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the provider refuses electronic copies, or gives only paper, or supplies an unreadable electronic format without agreeing on an alternative with the patient.
requirements.hint: State that electronic records are provided as an electronic copy in the requested format when readily producible, otherwise in a readable electronic format agreed with the patient.

requirements.title: Summary instead of access
requirements.need: A covered entity may give a summary or explanation instead of access only if the individual agrees in advance to the summary or explanation and to any fees imposed for it.

requirements.topic: giving a patient a summary or explanation of their health information instead of the actual records
requirements.complies: The patient agreed in advance to receive a summary or explanation instead of the records, and also agreed in advance to any fee charged for preparing it.
requirements.conflicts: The provider hands the patient a summary or explanation instead of the records without the patient agreeing beforehand, or charges a fee for the summary that the patient never agreed to in advance.
requirements.hint: State that the patient agreed in advance both to the summary or explanation and to any fee for it before it is provided.

requirements.title: Timely and convenient access
requirements.need: A covered entity must provide access in a timely manner as required by the 30-day rule, arranging a convenient time and place or mailing the copy at the individual's request.

The

requirements.topic: how and when a patient gets access to their health information
requirements.complies: The provider gives access within the 30-day timeframe, works out a convenient time and place with the patient, or mails the copy when the patient asks for mailing.
requirements.conflicts: The provider makes the patient wait beyond the 30-day timeframe, or refuses to arrange a convenient time and place and refuses to mail the copy even though the patient asked.
requirements.hint: Say the access is provided within the 30-day timeframe and that a convenient time and place is arranged or the copy is mailed at the patient's request.

requirements.title: Direct transmission to third party
requirements.need: If the individual's written, signed request clearly identifies a designated person and where to send the copy, the covered entity must transmit the copy directly to that person.

If an individual’s request for ac-

requirements.topic: sending a patient's health information copy directly to another person the patient names

requirements.hint: State that the patient's written, signed request names the designated person and the address, and that the copy is sent directly to that person.

requirements.title: Cost-based fees only

requirements.topic: fees charged to a patient for copies or summaries of their health information
requirements.complies: The fee is reasonable and cost-based and covers only labor for copying, supplies, postage when mailing was requested, and preparing an agreed summary or explanation.
requirements.conflicts: The fee includes charges beyond labor for copying, supplies, postage, and preparing an agreed summary or explanation, such as a flat records fee or a charge for searching or reviewing the records.
requirements.hint: List the fee components and show they are limited to copying labor, supplies, postage, and preparing an agreed summary or explanation.

requirements.title: Access to other information
requirements.need: When denying access in part, a covered entity must to the extent possible give the individual access to any other requested protected health information after excluding the information it has grounds to deny.

deny access.

requirements.topic: denying a patient access to part of their health information
requirements.complies: The provider denies only the specific information it has grounds to deny and, as far as possible, still gives the patient access to the rest of the requested information.
requirements.conflicts: The provider denies the entire request and withholds all the requested information even though only part of it is covered by a ground for denial.
requirements.hint: State that only the information with a ground for denial is excluded and the patient still receives the remaining requested information.

requirements.title: Content of denial

requirements.topic: telling a patient that access to their health information is denied

requirements.conflicts: The denial is given only by phone or is late, or it omits the basis for denial, the review rights and how to use them, or the complaint instructions and contact name or title and telephone number.
requirements.hint: Include in the written denial the basis, the review rights and how to exercise them, and the complaint steps with a contact name or title and telephone number.

requirements.title: Redirect if not maintained

requirements.topic: responding to a person's request to see their health information held by a health care provider

requirements.conflicts: The text says the provider simply refuses the request or tells the person the information cannot be found, without saying where the information is kept or where to direct the request.

requirements.title: Independent review of denial
requirements.need: On a request for review of a denial, the covered entity must promptly refer it to a designated licensed health care professional not involved in the denial, who must decide within a reasonable time, and the covered entity must promptly give written notice of the determination and carry it out.

requirements.topic: reviewing a decision to deny a person access to their health information
requirements.complies: The text says a review request is sent promptly to a designated licensed health care professional who was not involved in the denial, that this reviewer decides within a reasonable time, and that the provider promptly gives written notice of the decision and carries it out.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the same person who denied access also reviews the denial, or that no licensed professional is designated, or that the decision is never put in writing or never acted on.
requirements.hint: Describe prompt referral to a designated licensed health care professional who was not involved in the denial, a decision within a reasonable time, and prompt written notice that is carried out.

requirements.title: Access documentation
requirements.need: A covered entity must document the designated record sets subject to access and the titles of the persons or offices responsible for receiving and processing access requests, and retain the documentation as required by § 164.530(j).

essing requests for access by individ-

requirements.topic: recordkeeping about how a health care provider handles requests to see health information
requirements.complies: The text says the provider keeps documentation listing the designated record sets subject to access and the titles of the persons or offices that receive and process access requests, and retains it as required by § 164.530(j).
requirements.conflicts: The text says no list of designated record sets or responsible titles is kept, or that such documentation is discarded without regard to the retention requirements of § 164.530(j).

requirements.title: Right to amend
requirements.need: An individual has the right to have a covered entity amend protected health information or a record about the individual in a designated record set for as long as it is maintained there.

An individual has the right
to have a covered entity amend pro-
tected health information or a record

health information is maintained in
the designated record set.

requirements.topic: a person's request to correct or amend their health information
requirements.complies: The text says an individual has the right to have the provider amend protected health information or a record about them in a designated record set for as long as the information is maintained there.
requirements.conflicts: The text says individuals have no right to amend their records, or that the right ends before the information is removed from the designated record set.
requirements.hint: State that individuals may have their information amended in a designated record set for as long as it is maintained there.

requirements.need: A covered entity may deny an amendment request only if the information was not created by it (unless the originator is no longer available), is not part of the designated record set, would not be available for inspection under § 164.524, or is accurate and complete.

(ii) Is not part of the designated
record set;
(iii) Would not be available for in-
spection under § 164.524; or
(iv) Is accurate and complete.

requirements.topic: deciding whether to deny a person's request to amend their health information
requirements.complies: The text says a request may be denied only when the information was not created by the provider (unless the originator is no longer available), is not part of the designated record set, would not be available for inspection under § 164.524, or is accurate and complete.
requirements.conflicts: The text says requests may be denied for other reasons, such as inconvenience or cost, or denies a request without tying it to one of the listed grounds.
requirements.hint: List only the four permitted grounds for denial and note the exception when the originator is no longer available.

requirements.title: Amendment request process
requirements.need: A covered entity must permit individuals to request amendment of protected health information in the designated record set, and may require written requests and a supporting reason only if it informs individuals in advance.

quote.text:
The covered entity must permit an in-
dividual to request that the covered en-
tity amend the protected health infor-
mation maintained in the designated
record set. The covered entity may re-
quire individuals to make requests for
amendment in writing and to provide a
reason to support a requested amend-
ment, provided that it informs individ-
uals in advance of such requirements.

requirements.topic: how a health care provider accepts requests to amend health information
requirements.complies: The text says the provider lets individuals request amendments to information in the designated record set, and if it requires written requests or a supporting reason, it tells individuals about those requirements in advance.
requirements.conflicts: The text says the provider refuses to accept amendment requests, or imposes written-request or reason requirements without informing individuals in advance.
requirements.hint: State that amendment requests are permitted and that any written-request or reason requirement is communicated to individuals in advance.

requirements.title: 60-day action on amendment
requirements.need: A covered entity must act on an amendment request no later than 60 days after receipt, granting it with the required actions or providing a written denial, and may extend by no more than 30 days only once with a written statement of reasons and completion date.

quote.text:
The covered entity must act on the
individual’s request for an amendment
no later than 60 days after receipt of
such a request, as follows.
(A) If the covered entity grants the
requested amendment, in whole or in
part, it must take the actions required
by paragraphs (c)(1) and (2) of this sec-
tion.
(B) If the covered entity denies the
requested amendment, in whole or in
part, it must provide the individual
with a written denial, in accordance
with paragraph (d)(1) of this section.

requirements.topic: handling a patient's request to amend their health records
requirements.complies: The passage says the request is decided within 60 days of receipt, either by granting it and carrying out the required follow-up steps or by sending a written denial, and that any single extension is at most 30 days and is documented in writing with reasons and a completion date.
requirements.conflicts: The passage says requests are handled whenever staff get to them, that a decision can take several months, or that an extension is granted without a written statement of reasons and completion date, or extended more than once.
requirements.hint: State the 60-day decision deadline, the two outcomes (grant with required actions or written denial), and the one-time 30-day extension with written reasons and a completion date.

requirements.title: Making the amendment
requirements.need: When accepting an amendment, a covered entity must at a minimum identify the affected records in the designated record set and append or otherwise link the amendment to them.

quote.text:
The cov-
ered entity must make the appropriate
amendment to the protected health in-
formation or record that is the subject
of the request for amendment by, at a
minimum, identifying the records in
the designated record set that are af-
fected by the amendment and append-
ing or otherwise providing a link to the
location of the amendment.

requirements.topic: carrying out an accepted amendment to a patient's health records
requirements.complies: The passage says the affected records in the designated record set are identified and the amendment is appended or linked to their location.
requirements.conflicts: The passage says the amendment is accepted but no record is identified or updated, or that the amendment is filed separately with no link to the records it affects.
requirements.hint: Describe identifying the affected records in the designated record set and appending or linking the amendment to them.

requirements.title: Informing of acceptance
requirements.need: A covered entity must timely inform the individual that the amendment is accepted and obtain the individual's identification of and agreement to notify relevant persons with whom the amendment must be shared.

quote.text:
In accord-
ance with paragraph (b) of this section,
the covered entity must timely inform
the individual that the amendment is
accepted and obtain the individual’s
identification of and agreement to
have the covered entity notify the rel-
evant persons with which the amend-
ment needs to be shared in accordance
with paragraph (c)(3) of this section.

requirements.topic: telling a patient their amendment request was accepted
requirements.complies: The passage says the individual is informed promptly that the amendment is accepted and is asked to name the persons who should be notified and to agree to that notification.
requirements.conflicts: The passage says the individual is never told the amendment was accepted, or that the entity decides on its own who to notify without getting the individual's identification and agreement.
requirements.hint: Say the individual is informed promptly of acceptance and that their identification of and agreement to notify relevant persons is obtained.

requirements.title: Notifying others of amendment
requirements.need: A covered entity must make reasonable efforts to inform and provide the amendment within a reasonable time to persons identified by the individual and to persons, including business associates, known to hold the information and that may rely on it to the individual's detriment.

quote.text:
The covered enti-
ty must make reasonable efforts to in-
form and provide the amendment with-
in a reasonable time to:
(i) Persons identified by the indi-
vidual as having received protected
health information about the indi-
vidual and needing the amendment;
and
(ii) Persons, including business asso-
ciates, that the covered entity knows
have the protected health information
that is the subject of the amendment
and that may have relied, or could
foreseeably rely, on such information
to the detriment of the individual.

requirements.topic: notifying other parties that a patient's health record was amended
requirements.complies: The passage says reasonable efforts are made to inform and provide the amendment within a reasonable time to persons the individual named and to persons, including business associates, known to hold the information and that may rely on it to the individual's detriment.
requirements.conflicts: The passage says no one outside the entity is told of the amendment, or that notification is skipped for business associates and others known to hold and rely on the old information.
requirements.hint: Describe reasonable efforts to inform and send the amendment within a reasonable time to the persons the individual named and to known holders, including business associates, who may rely on the old information.

requirements.title: Content of amendment denial
requirements.need: A denial of amendment must be timely, written, in plain language, and state the basis, the right to submit a written statement of disagreement and how to file it, the option to have the request and denial included in future disclosures, and how to complain including the contact name or title and telephone number.

quote.text:
The covered entity must
provide the individual with a timely,
written denial, in accordance with
paragraph (b)(2) of this section. The de-
nial must use plain language and con-
tain:
(i) The basis for the denial, in accord-
ance with paragraph (a)(2) of this sec-
tion;
(ii) The individual’s right to submit a
written statement disagreeing with the
denial and how the individual may file
such a statement;
(iii) A statement that, if the indi-
vidual does not submit a statement of
disagreement, the individual may re-
quest that the covered entity provide
the individual’s request for amendment
and the denial with any future disclo-

(iv) A description of how the indi-
vidual may complain to the covered en-
