dures established in § 164.530(d) or to
the Secretary pursuant to the proce-
dures established in § 160.306.

requirements.topic: denying a patient's request to amend their health records
requirements.complies: The passage says the denial is sent on time, in writing and in plain language, and states the basis, the right to file a written statement of disagreement and how to do so, the option to have the request and denial included in future disclosures, and how to complain with a contact name or title and telephone number.
requirements.conflicts: The passage says denials are given verbally or late, or the written denial omits the basis, the disagreement right and filing steps, the future-disclosure option, or complaint instructions and contact details.
requirements.hint: List every required element of the written denial: plain language, basis, disagreement right and how to file, future-disclosure option, and complaint route with contact name or title and phone number.

requirements.title: Statement of disagreement
requirements.need: A covered entity must permit an individual to submit a written statement disagreeing with the denial of all or part of a requested amendment and the basis of the disagreement, though it may reasonably limit the statement's length.

quote.text:
The cov-
ered entity must permit the individual
to submit to the covered entity a writ-
ten statement disagreeing with the de-
nial of all or part of a requested
amendment and the basis of such dis-
agreement. The covered entity may
reasonably limit the length of a state-
ment of disagreement.

requirements.topic: a patient disagreeing in writing with a denied amendment
requirements.complies: The passage says the individual is allowed to submit a written statement disagreeing with the denial of all or part of the amendment and giving the basis of the disagreement, with length limits that are reasonable.
requirements.conflicts: The passage says statements of disagreement are refused or ignored, or that the entity rejects any statement that goes beyond a length limit it never disclosed or that is unreasonably short.
requirements.hint: State that a written statement of disagreement with its basis is permitted and that any length limit applied is reasonable.

requirements.title: Copy of rebuttal
requirements.need: If a covered entity prepares a written rebuttal to a statement of disagreement, it must provide a copy to the individual who submitted the statement.

quote.text:
The covered en-
tity may prepare a written rebuttal to
the individual’s statement of disagree-
ment. Whenever such a rebuttal is pre-
pared, the covered entity must provide
a copy to the individual who submitted
the statement of disagreement.

requirements.topic: written rebuttals to patients' statements of disagreement about amendment requests
requirements.complies: The covered entity prepared a written rebuttal to the individual's statement of disagreement and sent a copy of that rebuttal to the individual who submitted the statement.
requirements.conflicts: The covered entity prepared a written rebuttal to the statement of disagreement but kept it internal and did not give the individual a copy, or says the individual has no right to see the rebuttal.
requirements.hint: State that whenever a written rebuttal is prepared, a copy is provided to the individual who submitted the statement of disagreement.

requirements.title: Recordkeeping for disputes
requirements.need: A covered entity must identify the disputed record or information in the designated record set and append or link the amendment request, its denial, any statement of disagreement, and any rebuttal to the designated record set.

quote.text:
The covered entity
must, as appropriate, identify the
record or protected health information
in the designated record set that is the
subject of the disputed amendment and
append or otherwise link the individ-
ual’s request for an amendment, the
covered entity’s denial of the request,
the individual’s statement of disagree-
ment, if any, and the covered entity’s
rebuttal, if any, to the designated
record set.

requirements.topic: recordkeeping for disputed amendment requests in the designated record set
requirements.complies: The disputed record or information is identified in the designated record set, and the amendment request, the denial, any statement of disagreement and any rebuttal are appended or linked to the designated record set.
requirements.conflicts: The dispute paperwork is filed only in a separate correspondence folder, or the record is left unmarked with no link to the request, denial, statement of disagreement or rebuttal.
requirements.hint: Describe identifying the disputed record and appending or linking the request, denial, statement of disagreement and rebuttal to the designated record set.

requirements.title: Disclosures after dispute
requirements.need: A covered entity must include the appended dispute material or an accurate summary with subsequent disclosures of the information when a statement of disagreement was submitted, and include the request and denial only if the individual asked for that; if a standard transaction cannot carry the material, it may be transmitted separately.

quote.text:
If a state-
ment of disagreement has been sub-
mitted by the individual, the covered
entity must include the material ap-

(d)(4) of this section, or, at the election

requirements.topic: including dispute material when disclosing health information after a statement of disagreement
requirements.complies: When a statement of disagreement was submitted, subsequent disclosures of the disputed information include the appended material or an accurate summary of it; the request and denial are included only if the individual asked, and material that a standard transaction cannot carry is sent separately.
requirements.conflicts: Subsequent disclosures of the disputed information go out with no statement of disagreement or summary attached, or the entity always attaches the request and denial even when the individual did not ask.
requirements.hint: Say that later disclosures of disputed information carry the appended material or an accurate summary, with the request and denial only on the individual's request.

requirements.title: Acting on notices of amendment
requirements.need: A covered entity informed by another covered entity of an amendment to an individual's protected health information must amend the information in its designated record sets as provided in § 164.526(c)(1).

quote.text:
A covered
entity that is informed by another cov-
ered entity of an amendment to an in-
dividual’s protected health informa-
tion, in accordance with paragraph
(c)(3) of this section, must amend the
protected health information in des-
ignated record sets as provided by
paragraph (c)(1) of this section.

requirements.topic: amending health information after being notified of another covered entity's amendment
requirements.complies: The covered entity was informed by another covered entity of an amendment and amended the protected health information in its designated record sets as provided in § 164.526(c)(1).
requirements.conflicts: The covered entity was notified of another covered entity's amendment but left its own records unchanged, or says it has no duty to act on such notices.
requirements.hint: State that a notice of amendment from another covered entity is acted on by amending the information in the designated record sets under § 164.526(c)(1).

requirements.title: Amendment documentation
requirements.need: A covered entity must document the titles of the persons or offices responsible for receiving and processing amendment requests and retain the documentation as required by § 164.530(j).

A covered entity must docu-
ment the titles of the persons or offices
responsible for receiving and proc-
essing requests for amendments by in-
dividuals and retain the documentation
as required by § 164.530(j).

requirements.topic: documenting the people and offices that handle amendment requests
requirements.complies: The covered entity documented the titles of the persons or offices responsible for receiving and processing amendment requests and retained that documentation as required by § 164.530(j).
requirements.conflicts: No record exists of which titles receive and process amendment requests, or the list of responsible titles was discarded rather than retained.
requirements.hint: Name the documented titles of the persons or offices that receive and process amendment requests and say the documentation is retained under § 164.530(j).

requirements.title: Right to accounting
requirements.need: An individual has a right to an accounting of disclosures of protected health information made in the six years before the request, except for the listed categories such as treatment, payment and health care operations, disclosures to the individual, incidental disclosures, authorized disclosures, facility directory and notification disclosures, national security, correctional and law enforcement disclosures, limited data set disclosures, and disclosures before the compliance date.

ceive an accounting of disclosures of
protected health information made by

to the date on which the accounting is

and health care operations as provided
in § 164.506;
(ii) To individuals of protected health
information about them as provided in
§ 164.502;
(iii) Incident to a use or disclosure
otherwise permitted or required by this

(vi) For national security or intel-

(vii) To correctional institutions or
law enforcement officials as provided
in § 164.512(k)(5);
(viii) As part of a limited data set in
accordance with § 164.514(e); or
(ix) That occurred prior to the com-
pliance date for the covered entity.

requirements.topic: patients' right to an accounting of disclosures of their health information
requirements.complies: The individual can request an accounting covering disclosures made in the six years before the request, and the entity excludes the listed categories such as treatment, payment and health care operations, disclosures to the individual, authorized disclosures, facility directory and notification, national security, correctional and law enforcement, limited data set, and pre compliance date disclosures.
requirements.conflicts: The entity tells individuals they cannot get an accounting, or counts treatment, payment and health care operations disclosures, authorized disclosures or other listed categories in the accounting.
requirements.hint: Describe the six year accounting right and list the excluded disclosure categories, including treatment, payment and health care operations and authorized disclosures.

requirements.title: Suspension for oversight or law enforcement
requirements.need: A covered entity must temporarily suspend the right to an accounting when a health oversight agency or law enforcement official provides a written statement that the accounting would likely impede its activities and specifies the time; for an oral statement it must document the statement, suspend the right, and limit the suspension to no longer than 30 days unless a written statement follows.

and specifying the time for which such

requirements.topic: responding to a patient's request for a list of who their health information was shared with, when police or a health oversight agency ask to delay it
requirements.complies: The covered entity holds back the accounting for the time stated in a written statement from the oversight agency or law enforcement official saying the accounting would likely impede its activities; if the request came orally, it writes down the statement, suspends the accounting, and keeps the suspension to 30 days or less unless a written statement arrives.
requirements.conflicts: The covered entity gives the full accounting right away despite a written statement from law enforcement asking for delay, or suspends the accounting indefinitely on the basis of a phone call with no written record and no 30-day limit.
requirements.hint: Describe suspending the accounting only when the agency or official gives a written statement with a time period, and for oral statements record it and cap the suspension at 30 days.

requirements.title: Shorter accounting period
requirements.need: An individual may request an accounting of disclosures for a period of time less than six years from the date of the request.

quote.text:
An individual may request an ac-
counting of disclosures for a period of
time less than six years from the date
of the request.

requirements.topic: the time period a patient asks to cover in a request for a list of disclosures of their health information
requirements.complies: The covered entity accepts and honors a request to list disclosures for a period shorter than six years before the date of the request, such as the past three months.
requirements.conflicts: The covered entity refuses a request for a shorter period and insists the individual take the full six years, or tells the individual they may only request exactly six years.
requirements.hint: State that an individual can ask for any period shorter than six years back from the request date and that the request will be honored.

requirements.title: Scope of accounting
requirements.need: The written accounting must include disclosures of protected health information that occurred during the six years, or shorter requested period, before the request, including disclosures to or by business associates.

Except as otherwise provided by
paragraph (a) of this section, the ac-

protected health information that oc-
curred during the six years (or such
shorter time period at the request of
the individual as provided in paragraph
(a)(3) of this section) prior to the date
of the request for an accounting, in-
cluding disclosures to or by business
associates of the covered entity.

requirements.topic: the contents of a written list of disclosures of a patient's health information
requirements.complies: The written accounting lists disclosures of protected health information made in the six years before the request, or the shorter period the individual asked for, and includes disclosures to and by business associates.
requirements.conflicts: The accounting covers only the past year, or leaves out disclosures made by or to business associates, or ignores the shorter period the individual requested.
requirements.hint: Say the accounting covers the six years before the request or the shorter period requested, and that disclosures to and by business associates are included.

requirements.title: Content per disclosure
requirements.need: For each disclosure the accounting must include the date, the name and if known the address of the recipient, a brief description of the information disclosed, and a brief statement of the purpose or a copy of the written request for disclosure.

Except as otherwise provided by
paragraphs (b)(3) or (b)(4) of this sec-
tion, the accounting must include for

(ii) The name of the entity or person

requirements.topic: what each entry in a list of disclosures of a patient's health information must contain
requirements.complies: Each entry gives the date of the disclosure, the name and, if known, the address of the recipient, a brief description of the information disclosed, and a brief statement of the purpose or a copy of the written request for the disclosure.
requirements.conflicts: Entries list only a recipient name with no date, no description of the information, and no purpose or copy of the request.
requirements.hint: For every disclosure include the date, recipient name and known address, a short description of the information, and the purpose or a copy of the written request.

requirements.title: Research disclosures accounting
requirements.need: For research disclosures under § 164.512(i) involving 50 or more individuals, the accounting may give the protocol name, a plain-language description including purpose and record selection criteria, the type of information disclosed, the date or period of disclosures, the sponsor and researcher contact details, and a statement that the individual's information may or may not have been disclosed; on request the covered entity must assist in contacting the sponsor and researcher if disclosure was reasonably likely.

requirements.topic: listing research disclosures of a patient's health information involving 50 or more individuals
requirements.complies: For research disclosures involving 50 or more individuals, the accounting gives the protocol name, a plain-language description with the research purpose and record selection criteria, the type of information disclosed, the date or period of disclosures including the last one, the sponsor's and researcher's name, address and phone number, and a statement that the individual's information may or may not have been disclosed; the covered entity helps the individual contact the sponsor and researcher on request when disclosure was reasonably likely.
requirements.conflicts: For large research disclosures the accounting gives only a vague mention of research with no protocol name, no purpose or record criteria, no sponsor or researcher contact details, and no statement about whether the individual's information may have been included.
requirements.hint: For research disclosures of 50 or more individuals, list the protocol name, plain-language purpose and record criteria, information type, dates, sponsor and researcher contacts, and the may-or-may-not statement.

requirements.title: 60-day action on accounting
requirements.need: A covered entity must act on an accounting request no later than 60 days after receipt by providing the accounting, and may extend by no more than 30 days only once with a written statement of reasons and the date the accounting will be provided.

The covered

as follows.

requirements.topic: timing of a covered entity's response to a patient's request for a list of disclosures
requirements.complies: The covered entity provides the accounting within 60 days of receiving the request, or, if it needs more time, sends a written statement of the reasons and the date the accounting will come within those 60 days and takes no more than one 30-day extension.
requirements.conflicts: The covered entity takes 90 days with no notice, or grants itself two or more extensions, or sends a delay notice after the 60 days have already passed.
requirements.hint: Commit to providing the accounting within 60 days, with at most one 30-day extension announced in writing with reasons and a delivery date before the 60 days run out.

requirements.title: First accounting free
requirements.need: A covered entity must provide the first accounting in any 12-month period without charge, and may charge a reasonable, cost-based fee for later requests in the same period only if it informs the individual in advance and offers a chance to withdraw or modify the request.

The covered entity must provide
the first accounting to an individual in
any 12 month period without charge.

sonable, cost-based fee for each subse-
quent request for an accounting by the

requirements.topic: charging individuals for copies or accountings of their health information disclosures
requirements.complies: The first accounting request in a 12 month period is provided at no charge, and any later request in that period is billed only after the individual is told the fee in advance and given the chance to withdraw or narrow the request.
requirements.conflicts: A fee is charged for the first accounting in a 12 month period, or a later request is billed without telling the individual the amount beforehand or without letting them withdraw or modify the request to avoid the fee.
requirements.hint: State that the first accounting in each 12 month period is free and that later requests are billed only after advance notice of the fee plus an option to withdraw or modify.

requirements.title: Accounting documentation
requirements.need: A covered entity must document the information required to be included in an accounting, the written accounting provided to the individual, and the titles of the persons or offices responsible for receiving and processing accounting requests, and retain it as required by § 164.530(j).

ment the following and retain the doc-

cluded in an accounting under para-

requirements.topic: recordkeeping for requests and accountings of health information disclosures
requirements.complies: The entity keeps records of the disclosure information that belongs in an accounting, copies of the written accountings given to individuals, and the titles of the persons or offices that receive and process accounting requests, retained per § 164.530(j).
requirements.conflicts: No records are kept of what was included in accountings, of the written accountings sent out, or of who handles accounting requests, or such records are discarded before the § 164.530(j) retention period ends.

requirements.title: Security subpart applicability
requirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must comply with the applicable standards, implementation specifications and requirements of the security subpart for electronic protected health information of a covered entity.

A covered entity or business asso-
ciate must comply with the applicable
standards, implementation specifica-
tions, and requirements of this subpart
with respect to electronic protected
health information of a covered entity.

requirements.topic: application of the HIPAA security standards to electronic health information
requirements.complies: The entity states that it applies the security subpart's standards, implementation specifications and requirements to all electronic protected health information it handles as a covered entity or business associate.
requirements.conflicts: The entity says the security subpart does not apply to its electronic protected health information, or applies only some of its standards and implementation specifications.
requirements.hint: Say plainly that the security subpart's standards, implementation specifications and requirements apply to the electronic protected health information involved.

requirements.title: General security requirements
requirements.need: Covered entities and business associates must ensure confidentiality, integrity and availability of electronic protected health information, protect against anticipated threats and impermissible uses or disclosures, and ensure workforce compliance.
