baseRequirements.title: IDE exempts device requirements
baseRequirements.need: An approved IDE permits a device that would otherwise need a performance standard or premarket approval to be shipped lawfully for investigation and exempts it from specified act requirements, except GMP requirements in § 820.30 if applicable unless the sponsor states an intention to comply.

quote.text:
An approved
investigational device exemption (IDE)
permits a device that otherwise would
be required to comply with a perform-
ance standard or to have premarket ap-
proval to be shipped lawfully for the
purpose of conducting investigations of
that device. An IDE approved under
§ 812.30 or considered approved under
§ 812.2(b) exempts a device from the re-
quirements of the following sections of
the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic
Act (the act) and regulations issued
thereunder: Misbranding under section
502 of the act, registration, listing, and
premarket notification under section
510, performance standards under sec-
tion 514, premarket approval under sec-
tion 515, a banned device regulation
under section 516, records and reports
under section 519, restricted device re-
quirements under section 520(e), good
manufacturing practice requirements
under section 520(f) except for the re-
quirements found in § 820.30, if applica-
ble (unless the sponsor states an inten-
tion to comply with these require-
ments under § 812.20(b)(3) or
§ 812.140(b)(4)(v)) and color additive re-
quirements under section 721.

baseRequirements.topic: shipping and investigating a medical device under an approved investigational device exemption (IDE)
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that an approved IDE lets a device that would otherwise need a performance standard or premarket approval be shipped lawfully for investigation, and that it exempts the device from the listed act requirements, including good manufacturing practice requirements under section 520(f) except for § 820.30 if applicable unless the sponsor states an intention to comply.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text claims an IDE removes all good manufacturing practice requirements including § 820.30 without any sponsor statement of intention to comply, or says a device needing premarket approval may be shipped for investigation without an approved IDE.
baseRequirements.hint: Say that an approved IDE permits lawful shipment for investigation and exempts the device from the listed requirements, keeping § 820.30 applicable unless the sponsor states an intention to comply.

baseRequirements.title: Abbreviated IDE requirements
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor of a non-significant risk device investigation considered to have an approved IDE must label the device per § 812.5, obtain and maintain IRB approval, ensure informed consent, comply with monitoring, maintain records and reports, and comply with promotion prohibitions.

quote.text:
(1) An investigation of a device other
than a significant risk device, if the de-
vice is not a banned device and the
sponsor:
(i) Labels the device in accordance
with § 812.5;
(ii) Obtains IRB approval of the in-
vestigation after presenting the re-
viewing IRB with a brief explanation of
why the device is not a significant risk
device, and maintains such approval;
(iii) Ensures that each investigator
participating in an investigation of the
device obtains from each subject under
the investigator’s care, informed con-
sent in accordance with part 50 of this
chapter.

baseRequirements.topic: sponsor duties in a non-significant risk device investigation treated as having an approved IDE
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the sponsor labels the device per § 812.5, obtains and keeps IRB approval after giving the IRB a brief explanation of why the device is not significant risk, ensures each investigator gets informed consent under part 50, and complies with monitoring, records and reports, and the promotion prohibitions.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the sponsor skips IRB approval, does not label the device per § 812.5, leaves informed consent to chance, or ignores monitoring, recordkeeping or the promotion prohibitions.
baseRequirements.hint: List each duty: § 812.5 labeling, IRB approval with a brief non-significant-risk explanation kept current, informed consent under part 50, monitoring, records and reports, and no promotion.

baseRequirements.title: Exempted investigations
baseRequirements.need: This part, except § 812.119, does not apply to investigations of devices in commercial distribution before May 28, 1976, substantially equivalent devices, certain noninvasive diagnostic devices, consumer preference testing, veterinary devices, laboratory animal research devices, and custom devices.

quote.text:
(c) Exempted investigations. This part,
with the exception of § 812.119, does not
apply to investigations of the following
categories of devices:
(1) A device, other than a transi-
tional device, in commercial distribu-
tion immediately before May 28, 1976,
when used or investigated in accord-
ance with the indications in labeling in
effect at that time.

baseRequirements.topic: investigations of device categories exempt from the IDE part
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that this part, except § 812.119, does not apply to investigations of devices in commercial distribution immediately before May 28, 1976 when used per the labeling then in effect, and to the other listed categories such as substantially equivalent devices, certain noninvasive diagnostic devices, consumer preference testing, veterinary devices, laboratory animal research devices and custom devices.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the full part applies to a device in commercial distribution before May 28, 1976 used per its then-current labeling, or to another listed exempt category, without noting the § 812.119 exception.
baseRequirements.hint: Name the exempt categories and state that this part, except § 812.119, does not apply to investigations of them.

baseRequirements.title: Limit on exemptions
baseRequirements.need: For class II or class III devices described in § 812.2(c)(1) or (2), this part applies beginning on the date stipulated in an FDA regulation or order calling for premarket approval submissions or establishing a performance standard.

quote.text:
(d) Limit on certain exemptions. In the
case of class II or class III device de-
scribed in paragraph (c)(1) or (2) of this
section, this part applies beginning on
the date stipulated in an FDA regula-
tion or order that calls for the submis-
sion of premarket approval applica-
tions for an unapproved class III de-
vice, or establishes a performance
standard for a class II device.

baseRequirements.topic: when the IDE part starts to apply to certain class II or class III devices previously exempt
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that for a class II or class III device described in § 812.2(c)(1) or (2), this part applies beginning on the date set in an FDA regulation or order calling for premarket approval submissions for an unapproved class III device or establishing a performance standard for a class II device.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says such a class II or class III device stays exempt from this part after FDA has issued a regulation or order calling for premarket approval or setting a performance standard.
baseRequirements.hint: State that the exemption ends on the date FDA's regulation or order requires premarket approval submissions or sets a performance standard.

baseRequirements.title: Investigations subject to INDs
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor with an effective IND for a device investigation on July 16, 1980 must continue complying with part 312 until 90 days after that date, and to continue must comply with § 812.2(b)(1) or obtain FDA approval under § 812.30.

quote.text:
(e) Investigations subject to IND’s. A
sponsor that, on July 16, 1980, has an
effective investigational new drug ap-
plication (IND) for an investigation of
a device shall continue to comply with
the requirements of part 312 until 90
days after that date. To continue the
investigation after that date, a sponsor
shall comply with paragraph (b)(1) of
this section, if the device is not a sig-
nificant risk device, or shall have ob-
tained FDA approval under § 812.30 of
an IDE application for the investiga-
tion of the device.

baseRequirements.topic: device investigations covered by an investigational new drug application effective on July 16, 1980
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that a sponsor with an effective IND for a device investigation on July 16, 1980 continues to comply with part 312 until 90 days after that date, and to continue afterward complies with § 812.2(b)(1) for a non-significant risk device or obtains FDA approval under § 812.30.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says a sponsor with such an IND may stop following part 312 immediately or continue the investigation after the 90 days without meeting § 812.2(b)(1) or getting § 812.30 approval.
baseRequirements.hint: State the part 312 duty through 90 days after July 16, 1980, then either § 812.2(b)(1) compliance for non-significant risk devices or § 812.30 approval.

baseRequirements.title: Waiver request
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor may request FDA to waive any requirement of this part by submitting a waiver request with supporting documentation separately or as part of an application to the address in § 812.19.

quote.text:
(a) Request. A sponsor may request
FDA to waive any requirement of this
part. A waiver request, with supporting
documentation, may be submitted sep-
arately or as part of an application to
the address in § 812.19.

baseRequirements.topic: requesting FDA to waive a requirement of the IDE part
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that a sponsor may ask FDA to waive any requirement of this part by sending a waiver request with supporting documentation, either separately or as part of an application, to the address in § 812.19.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says a sponsor may waive a requirement on its own authority, or may send a waiver request without supporting documentation or to an address other than the one in § 812.19.
baseRequirements.hint: Say the sponsor may request a waiver from FDA, with supporting documentation, submitted separately or within an application to the § 812.19 address.

baseRequirements.title: Waiver effect
baseRequirements.need: Any requirement continues to apply unless and until FDA waives it.

quote.text:
(c) Effect of request. Any requirement
shall continue to apply unless and
until FDA waives it.

baseRequirements.topic: FDA requirements and waivers for investigational device exemption submissions
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that a requirement stays in force until FDA waives it, and that a waiver request does not by itself remove the requirement.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text claims a requirement no longer applies once a waiver request is sent, or that a sponsor may stop following a requirement before FDA waives it.
baseRequirements.hint: Say that each requirement keeps applying unless and until FDA grants a waiver.

baseRequirements.title: Submission addresses
baseRequirements.need: A person sending an application, supplemental application, report, waiver request, import or export approval request, or other correspondence must send the submission to the appropriate FDA center address specified in § 812.19(a).

quote.text:
(a) If you are sending an application,
supplemental application, report, re-
quest for waiver, request for import or
export approval, or other correspond-
ence relating to matters covered by
this part, you must send the submis-
sion to the appropriate address as fol-
lows:

baseRequirements.topic: sending applications, reports, waiver requests and other correspondence to FDA about investigational device exemptions
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the submission is sent to the appropriate FDA center address listed in § 812.19(a).
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the submission may be sent to any address, to a random office, or to no specified FDA address.
baseRequirements.hint: Name the appropriate FDA center address from § 812.19(a) as where the submission is sent.

baseRequirements.title: Wrapper identification
baseRequirements.need: A person must state on the outside wrapper of each submission what the submission is, for example an ''IDE application,'' a ''supplemental IDE application,'' or a ''correspondence concerning an IDE.''

quote.text:
(b) You must state on the outside
wrapper of each submission what the
submission is, for example, an ‘‘IDE ap-
plication,’’ a ‘‘supplemental IDE appli-
cation,’’ or a ‘‘correspondence con-
cerning an IDE (or an IDE applica-
tion).’’

baseRequirements.topic: marking the outside of submissions sent to FDA about investigational device exemptions
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the outside wrapper of each submission is labeled with what it is, such as "IDE application," "supplemental IDE application," or "correspondence concerning an IDE."
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the outside wrapper is left blank or unlabeled, or that the submission type is only stated inside the package.
baseRequirements.hint: State on the outside wrapper what the submission is, using a label like "IDE application" or "correspondence concerning an IDE."

baseRequirements.title: When to submit IDE
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must submit an IDE application to FDA if the sponsor intends to use a significant risk device, intends to conduct an investigation with an exception from informed consent under § 50.24, or if FDA notifies the sponsor that an application is required.

quote.text:
(a) Submission. (1) A sponsor shall
submit an application to FDA if the
sponsor intends to use a significant
risk device in an investigation, intends
to conduct an investigation that in-
volves an exception from informed con-
sent under § 50.24 of this chapter, or if
FDA notifies the sponsor that an appli-
cation is required for an investigation.

baseRequirements.topic: deciding whether to submit an IDE application to FDA for a device investigation
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the sponsor submits an IDE application when the device is significant risk, when the study uses an exception from informed consent under § 50.24, or when FDA says an application is required.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the sponsor skips an IDE application despite using a significant risk device, using an exception from informed consent under § 50.24, or being told by FDA that an application is required.
baseRequirements.hint: List each trigger (significant risk device, § 50.24 exception from informed consent, FDA notice) and say an IDE application is submitted when any applies.

baseRequirements.title: No start before approval
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must not begin an investigation for which FDA's approval of an application is required until FDA has approved the application.

quote.text:
(2) A sponsor shall not begin an in-
vestigation for which FDA’s approval
of an application is required until FDA
has approved the application.

baseRequirements.topic: starting an investigation that needs FDA approval of an IDE application
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the investigation does not begin until FDA has approved the application.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the sponsor starts the investigation before FDA approves the application, or begins while approval is still pending.
baseRequirements.hint: State that the investigation starts only after FDA approves the application.

baseRequirements.title: Signed IDE submission
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must submit a signed ''Application for an Investigational Device Exemption'' with accompanying materials in electronic format to an address in § 812.19, and subsequent correspondence must also be submitted in electronic format.

quote.text:
(3) A sponsor shall submit a signed
‘‘Application for an Investigational De-
vice Exemption’’ (IDE application), to-
gether with accompanying materials in
electronic format, to one of the ad-
dresses in § 812.19, and if eCopy by reg-
istered mail or by hand. Subsequent
correspondence concerning an applica-
tion or a supplemental application
shall be submitted in electronic format
and if eCopy by registered mail or by
hand.

baseRequirements.topic: submitting a signed IDE application and later correspondence to FDA in electronic format
baseRequirements.complies: The text says a signed "Application for an Investigational Device Exemption" with accompanying materials is sent in electronic format to an address in § 812.19, and later correspondence is also sent in electronic format.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the application is unsigned, sent only on paper, or sent to an address not listed in § 812.19, or that later correspondence is not in electronic format.
baseRequirements.hint: Say the IDE application is signed, sent in electronic format to a § 812.19 address, and that later correspondence is also electronic.

baseRequirements.title: Exception from informed consent IDE
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must submit a separate IDE for any clinical investigation involving an exception from informed consent under § 50.24, which may not proceed without prior written FDA authorization, and must prominently identify on the cover sheet that the investigation is subject to § 50.24.

quote.text:

baseRequirements.topic: submitting an investigational device exemption (IDE) for a clinical investigation that uses an exception from informed consent
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor states that a separate IDE was submitted for the investigation, that the investigation will not begin until FDA gives prior written authorization, and the cover sheet prominently says the investigation is subject to the requirements in § 50.24.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the investigation proceeds under an exception from informed consent without a separate IDE or before FDA written authorization, or the cover sheet does not mention § 50.24.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe a separate IDE submission for the § 50.24 exception, waiting for FDA written authorization before starting, and a cover sheet that prominently names § 50.24.

baseRequirements.title: IDE application contents
baseRequirements.need: An IDE application must include, in order, the sponsor's name and address, a complete report of prior investigations and summary of the investigational plan, manufacturing methods and controls, investigator agreements and list, IRB information, institution names, sale amount explanation, environmental claim, labeling, consent materials, and any other requested information.

quote.text:
(b) Contents. An IDE application shall
include, in the following order:
(1) The name and address of the spon-
sor.
(2) A complete report of prior inves-
tigations of the device and an accurate
summary of those sections of the inves-
tigational plan described in § 812.25(a)
through (e) or, in lieu of the summary,
the complete plan.

baseRequirements.topic: the contents and ordering of an IDE application
baseRequirements.complies: The application lists, in order, the sponsor's name and address, a complete report of prior investigations and an accurate summary of the investigational plan sections (or the complete plan), manufacturing methods and controls, investigator agreements and list, IRB information, institution names, sale amount explanation, environmental claim, labeling, consent materials, and other requested information.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The application omits required items such as the report of prior investigations, manufacturing controls, investigator list or IRB information, or presents the required contents out of the stated order.
baseRequirements.hint: Present every required item and keep them in the order listed in § 812.20(b).

baseRequirements.title: Complete plan when required
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must submit to FDA a complete investigational plan and a complete report of prior investigations if no IRB has reviewed them, if FDA has found an IRB's review inadequate, or if FDA requests them.

quote.text:
The sponsor shall
submit to FDA a complete investiga-
tional plan and a complete report of
prior investigations of the device if no
IRB has reviewed them, if FDA has
found an IRB’s review inadequate, or if
FDA requests them.

baseRequirements.topic: submitting a complete investigational plan and complete report of prior investigations to FDA
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor states that a complete investigational plan and a complete report of prior investigations are being submitted to FDA because no IRB reviewed them, FDA found an IRB's review inadequate, or FDA requested them.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says only a summary is sent to FDA even though no IRB reviewed the plan, FDA found the IRB review inadequate, or FDA asked for the complete documents.
baseRequirements.hint: State that the complete plan and complete prior-investigation report go to FDA whenever one of the three triggers applies.

baseRequirements.title: Investigator agreement certification
baseRequirements.need: An IDE application must include a certification that all investigators have signed the agreement, that the list includes all investigators, and that no investigators will be added until they have signed the agreement.

quote.text:
(5) A certification that all investiga-
tors who will participate in the inves-
tigation have signed the agreement,
that the list of investigators includes
all the investigators participating in
the investigation, and that no inves-
tigators will be added to the investiga-
tion until they have signed the agree-
ment.

baseRequirements.topic: certifying investigator agreements and the investigator list in an IDE application
baseRequirements.complies: The application includes a certification that all participating investigators signed the agreement, that the investigator list includes every participating investigator, and that no investigator will be added until they have signed the agreement.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says investigators may join before signing the agreement, or that the investigator list is incomplete or the signed agreements are missing.
baseRequirements.hint: Include a certification covering signed agreements for all investigators, a complete investigator list, and no additions before signing.

baseRequirements.title: Additional information requests
baseRequirements.need: FDA may request additional information or revision in the investigational plan, and the sponsor may treat such a request as a disapproval for purposes of requesting a hearing under part 16.

quote.text:
(c) Additional information. FDA may
request additional information con-
cerning an investigation or revision in
the investigational plan. The sponsor
may treat such a request as a dis-
approval of the application for pur-
poses of requesting a hearing under
part 16.

baseRequirements.topic: FDA requests for additional information or plan revisions during IDE review
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that FDA may request additional information or a revision of the investigational plan, and that the sponsor may treat such a request as a disapproval for purposes of requesting a hearing under part 16.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says FDA cannot ask for more information or plan revisions, or that the sponsor has no option to treat such a request as a disapproval when seeking a part 16 hearing.
baseRequirements.hint: Note that FDA may request more information or plan revisions and that the sponsor may treat the request as a disapproval for a part 16 hearing.

baseRequirements.title: Incorporation by reference
baseRequirements.need: Information previously submitted to the applicable FDA center in accordance with this chapter ordinarily need not be resubmitted but may be incorporated by reference.

quote.text:
(d) Information previously submitted.

Information previously submitted to
the Center for Devices and Radio-
logical Health, the Center for Biologics
Evaluation and Research, or the Center
for Drug Evaluation and Research, as
applicable, in accordance with this
chapter ordinarily need not be resub-
mitted, but may be incorporated by
reference.

baseRequirements.topic: reusing information already submitted to an FDA center in an IDE application
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that information previously submitted to the applicable FDA center in accordance with this chapter ordinarily need not be resubmitted and may be incorporated by reference.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says all previously submitted information must be sent again in full, or that incorporation by reference of prior submissions is not allowed.
baseRequirements.hint: Say that previously submitted information ordinarily need not be resubmitted and may be incorporated by reference.

baseRequirements.title: Investigational plan contents
baseRequirements.need: The investigational plan must include, in order, the purpose, protocol, risk analysis, device description, monitoring procedures, labeling, consent materials, IRB information, other institutions, and additional records and reports.

quote.text:
The investigational plan shall in-
clude, in the following order:
(a) Purpose. The name and intended
use of the device and the objectives and
duration of the investigation.
(b) Protocol. A written protocol de-
scribing the methodology to be used
and an analysis of the protocol dem-
onstrating that the investigation is
scientifically sound.

baseRequirements.topic: the contents and ordering of an investigational plan for a medical device study
baseRequirements.complies: The plan lists sections in the required sequence, starting with a purpose section giving the device name, intended use, objectives and duration, followed by a written protocol describing the methodology and an analysis showing the investigation is scientifically sound, then risk analysis, device description, monitoring procedures, labeling, consent materials, IRB information, other institutions, and additional records and reports.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The plan omits one or more required sections, presents them out of the required order, or gives a purpose section without the device name, intended use, objectives and duration, or a protocol without methodology and a scientific soundness analysis.
baseRequirements.hint: Present the plan with all ten sections in the stated order, beginning with purpose (device name, intended use, objectives, duration) and protocol (methodology plus soundness analysis).

baseRequirements.title: Report of prior investigations
baseRequirements.need: The report of prior investigations must include reports of all prior clinical, animal, and laboratory testing of the device and be comprehensive and adequate to justify the proposed investigation.

quote.text:
(a) General. The report of prior inves-
tigations shall include reports of all
prior clinical, animal, and laboratory
testing of the device and shall be com-
prehensive and adequate to justify the
proposed investigation.

baseRequirements.topic: the report of prior clinical, animal and laboratory testing used to justify a device investigation
baseRequirements.complies: The report includes reports of all prior clinical, animal and laboratory testing of the device and states that the information is comprehensive and adequate to justify the proposed investigation.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The report leaves out prior clinical, animal or laboratory testing, or presents only selected favorable results without covering all prior testing, so the proposed investigation is not justified.
baseRequirements.hint: Include reports of every prior clinical, animal and laboratory test of the device and explain how together they justify the proposed investigation.

baseRequirements.title: Bibliography and adverse information
baseRequirements.need: The report must include a bibliography of all relevant publications whether adverse or supportive, copies of all published and unpublished adverse information, and copies of other significant publications if requested by an IRB or FDA.

quote.text:
(1) A bibliography of all publications,
whether adverse or supportive, that are
relevant to an evaluation of the safety
or effectiveness of the device, copies of
all published and unpublished adverse
information, and, if requested by an
IRB or FDA, copies of other significant
publications.

baseRequirements.topic: the bibliography and adverse information in a report of prior investigations
baseRequirements.complies: The report contains a bibliography of all publications relevant to safety or effectiveness whether adverse or supportive, copies of all published and unpublished adverse information, and copies of other significant publications when an IRB or FDA requests them.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The report lists only supportive publications, omits adverse information, or fails to supply copies of other significant publications after an IRB or FDA request.
baseRequirements.hint: List every relevant publication whether adverse or supportive, attach copies of all adverse information published or not, and add other significant publications when an IRB or FDA asks.

baseRequirements.title: Good laboratory practice statement
baseRequirements.need: If nonclinical laboratory study information is provided, the report must include a statement that all such studies complied with part 58 good laboratory practice regulations, or a brief statement of the reason for noncompliance.

quote.text:
(3) If information on nonclinical lab-
oratory studies is provided, a state-
ment that all such studies have been
conducted in compliance with applica-
ble requirements in the good labora-
tory practice regulations in part 58, or
if any such study was not conducted in
compliance with such regulations, a
brief statement of the reason for the
noncompliance. Failure or inability to
comply with this requirement does not
justify failure to provide information
on a relevant nonclinical test study.

baseRequirements.topic: nonclinical laboratory studies included in a report of prior investigations
baseRequirements.complies: Where nonclinical laboratory study information is provided, the report states that all such studies were conducted in compliance with the part 58 good laboratory practice regulations, or gives a brief statement of the reason any study did not comply.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The report provides nonclinical laboratory study information without any good laboratory practice compliance statement, or notes noncompliance without giving a brief reason, or withholds a relevant nonclinical study because it did not comply.
baseRequirements.hint: For any nonclinical laboratory study information, state part 58 compliance or briefly give the reason for noncompliance, and still include the study.

baseRequirements.title: Human subjects compliance statement
baseRequirements.need: If U.S. clinical investigation data are provided, the report must include a statement that each investigation complied with part 50, part 56, and this part, or a brief statement of the reason for noncompliance, and for foreign data must address § 812.28 requirements.

quote.text:
(4)(i) If data from clinical investiga-
tions conducted in the United States
are provided, a statement that each in-
vestigation was conducted in compli-
ance with applicable requirements in
the protection of human subjects regu-
lations in part 50 of this chapter, the
institutional review boards regulations
in part 56 of this chapter, or was not
subject to the regulations under § 56.104
or § 56.105, and the investigational de-
vice exemptions regulations in this
part, or if any such investigation was
not conducted in compliance with
those regulations, a brief statement of
the reason for the noncompliance.

baseRequirements.topic: human subjects protection compliance statements for clinical investigation data in a report of prior investigations
baseRequirements.complies: For U.S. clinical investigation data, the report states that each investigation complied with part 50, part 56 and the investigational device exemptions regulations, or was exempt under § 56.104 or § 56.105, or gives a brief statement of the reason for noncompliance; foreign data are addressed under § 812.28.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The report includes U.S. clinical investigation data with no statement about part 50, part 56 and this part compliance or exemption, or notes noncompliance without a brief reason, or includes foreign data without addressing § 812.28.
baseRequirements.hint: For each U.S. clinical investigation, state compliance with parts 50 and 56 and this part, or the exemption or the brief reason for noncompliance, and handle foreign data under § 812.28.

baseRequirements.title: Acceptance of foreign data
baseRequirements.need: FDA will accept information on a clinical investigation conducted outside the United States to support an IDE or device marketing submission if the investigation is well-designed and well-conducted and the GCP statement, supporting information, and validation conditions are met.

quote.text:
FDA will accept informa-
tion on a clinical investigation con-
ducted outside the United States to
support an IDE or a device marketing
application or submission if the inves-
tigation is well-designed and well-con-
ducted and the following conditions are
met:
(1) A statement is provided that the
investigation was conducted in accord-
ance with good clinical practice (GCP).

baseRequirements.topic: clinical investigations conducted outside the United States offered to support an IDE or device marketing submission
baseRequirements.complies: The submission describes the foreign investigation as well-designed and well-conducted and includes a statement that it was conducted in accordance with good clinical practice, along with the supporting information and validation conditions required by § 812.28.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The submission relies on a foreign investigation without a good clinical practice statement, without showing the investigation was well-designed and well-conducted, or without the supporting information and validation conditions.
baseRequirements.hint: For foreign clinical data, show the investigation was well-designed and well-conducted and include a good clinical practice statement plus the § 812.28 supporting information and validation conditions.

baseRequirements.title: Supporting information submission
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor or applicant must submit the supporting information in § 812.28(b) for a significant risk device investigation, and for other investigations must submit specified paragraphs and make the remaining information available for agency review upon request.

quote.text:

baseRequirements.topic: submitting supporting information for a device investigation, including foreign clinical data, to FDA
baseRequirements.complies: The submission states that for a significant risk device investigation the full supporting information in § 812.28(b) is included, and for other investigations the specified paragraphs are submitted with the remaining information kept available for agency review on request.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The submission omits the supporting information for a significant risk device investigation, or says no supporting information was prepared and nothing is available for agency review on request.
baseRequirements.hint: State which type of investigation it is and confirm the § 812.28(b) information is submitted in full for significant risk studies or the specified paragraphs for others, with the rest available on request.

baseRequirements.title: GCP supporting information
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor or applicant submitting foreign clinical data must provide a description of actions taken to ensure the research conformed to GCP, including investigator names, qualifications, facility descriptions, protocol summary, device comparison, valid scientific evidence discussion, IEC information, consent and incentive descriptions, monitoring, and training.

baseRequirements.topic: foreign clinical investigations used to support an IDE or device marketing submission
baseRequirements.complies: The submission describes the specific actions the sponsor or applicant took so the foreign research conformed to GCP, such as monitoring visits, site training and protocol oversight.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The submission includes foreign clinical data but gives no description of actions taken to ensure GCP compliance, or states that no steps were taken to check GCP conformance.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe concretely what was done to make sure the foreign investigation followed GCP, not just that it did.

baseRequirements.title: IEC records retention
baseRequirements.need: The sponsor or applicant must maintain records supporting the statement that the IEC meets the definition in § 812.3(t), including records describing the qualifications of IEC members, and make these records available for agency review upon request.

records describing the qualifications of
IEC members, and make these records
available for agency review upon re-
quest;

baseRequirements.topic: the ethics committee (IEC) that reviewed a foreign clinical investigation
baseRequirements.complies: The submission names the IEC and its address, states that it meets the § 812.3(t) definition, and says records of member qualifications are kept and will be given to the agency on request.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The submission names an IEC but keeps no records supporting that it meets the § 812.3(t) definition, has no member qualification records, or says such records will not be provided to the agency.
baseRequirements.hint: Give the IEC name and address, state it meets § 812.3(t), and confirm member qualification records are kept and available to the agency on request.

baseRequirements.title: Investigator GCP commitments
baseRequirements.need: The sponsor or applicant must maintain any signed written commitments by investigators to comply with GCP and the protocol and make them available for agency review upon request.

baseRequirements.topic: training of investigators and their written commitments to follow GCP and the protocol in a foreign clinical investigation
baseRequirements.complies: The submission describes how investigators were trained on GCP and the protocol, states whether signed written commitments were obtained, and says any signed commitments are kept and available to the agency on request.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The submission gives no description of investigator training, does not say whether written commitments were obtained, or says signed commitments were not kept or cannot be produced for the agency.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe the investigator training, state whether signed written commitments were obtained, and confirm any signed commitments are retained and available on request.

baseRequirements.title: Waiver request contents
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor or applicant may ask FDA to waive requirements under § 812.28(a)(1) and (b), and the waiver request must contain an explanation why compliance is unnecessary or cannot be achieved, a description of an alternative, or other justifying information.

quote.text:
(c) Waivers. (1) A sponsor or applicant

requirements under paragraphs (a)(1)
and (b) of this section. A waiver re-
quest may be submitted in an IDE or in

IDE, in a device marketing application
or submission (an application under
section 515 or 520(m) of the Federal

section 510(k) of the Federal Food,

ment; or

baseRequirements.topic: asking FDA to waive the GCP and supporting information requirements for foreign clinical data
baseRequirements.complies: The waiver request explains why compliance is unnecessary or cannot be achieved, or describes an alternative that meets the requirement's purpose, or gives other information justifying the waiver.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The waiver request asks for the waiver without any explanation, alternative or other justification, or simply asserts that the requirements should not apply.
baseRequirements.hint: Include at least one of the three: why compliance is unnecessary or impossible, an alternative that meets the purpose, or other justifying information.

baseRequirements.title: Foreign data record retention
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor or applicant must retain the records required by § 812.28 for a foreign clinical investigation for 2 years after termination or completion of the IDE, or for 2 years after an agency decision on a marketing submission.

quote.text:

baseRequirements.topic: keeping records of a foreign clinical investigation after it ends or after an FDA decision
baseRequirements.complies: The submission states that records for the foreign investigation are kept for 2 years after the IDE is terminated or completed, or for 2 years after the agency decision on the marketing submission.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The submission says records will be destroyed sooner, kept only until the study ends, or gives a retention period shorter than 2 years after termination, completion or agency decision.
baseRequirements.hint: State the 2 year retention period tied to IDE termination or completion, or to the agency decision on the marketing submission.

baseRequirements.title: Prior approval for changes
baseRequirements.need: Except for specified exceptions, a sponsor must obtain approval of a supplemental application under § 812.30(a) and IRB approval when appropriate before implementing a change to an investigational plan, and must submit a separate IDE for an exception to informed consent.

quote.text:
(a) Changes in investigational plan—(1)

Changes requiring prior approval. Except
as described in paragraphs (a)(2)

through (a)(4) of this section, a sponsor
must obtain approval of a supple-
mental application under § 812.30(a),
and IRB approval when appropriate
(see §§ 56.110 and 56.111 of this chapter),
prior to implementing a change to an
investigational plan. If a sponsor in-
tends to conduct an investigation that
involves an exception to informed con-
sent under § 50.24 of this chapter, the
sponsor shall submit a separate inves-
tigational device exemption (IDE) ap-
plication in accordance with § 812.20(a).

baseRequirements.topic: changing the plan of an investigational device study before it is carried out
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor states that before any change to the investigational plan is implemented, it obtains approval of a supplemental application under § 812.30(a) and IRB approval where required, and that any exception to informed consent is filed as a separate IDE application.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The sponsor says it will start using a modified investigational plan right away and file the supplemental application later, or that it will run an exception to informed consent without submitting a separate IDE.
baseRequirements.hint: State that no change to the investigational plan is implemented until the supplemental application and any needed IRB approval are in place, and that an informed consent exception gets its own IDE.

baseRequirements.title: Emergency deviation reporting
baseRequirements.need: A deviation from the investigational plan to protect the life or physical well-being of a subject in an emergency does not require prior FDA approval but must be reported to FDA within 5 working days after the sponsor learns of it.

quote.text:
(2) Changes effected for emergency use.

The requirements of paragraph (a)(1) of
this section regarding FDA approval of
a supplement do not apply in the case
of a deviation from the investigational
plan to protect the life or physical
well-being of a subject in an emer-
gency. Such deviation shall be reported
to FDA within 5-working days after the
sponsor learns of it (see § 812.150(a)(4)).

baseRequirements.topic: deviating from an investigational plan to protect a subject in an emergency
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor describes a deviation made to protect the life or physical well-being of a subject in an emergency, notes that no prior FDA approval was sought, and states it reported the deviation to FDA within 5 working days after learning of it.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The sponsor treats an emergency deviation as needing prior FDA approval before acting, or makes the deviation and never reports it, or reports it weeks or months after learning of it.
baseRequirements.hint: Say the emergency deviation was made without prior FDA approval and was reported to FDA within 5 working days of the sponsor learning of it.

baseRequirements.title: Changes with 5-day notice
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor may make developmental changes or clinical protocol changes without prior approval if the criteria are met based on credible information and the sponsor provides notice to FDA within 5 working days of making the changes.

quote.text:
(3) Changes effected with notice to FDA
within 5 days. A sponsor may make cer-
tain changes without prior approval of
a supplemental application under para-
graph (a)(1) of this section if the spon-
sor determines that these changes
meet the criteria described in para-
graphs (a)(3)(i) and (a)(3)(ii) of this sec-
tion, on the basis of credible informa-
tion defined in paragraph (a)(3)(iii) of
this section, and the sponsor provides
notice to FDA within 5-working days of
making these changes.

baseRequirements.topic: making certain device or clinical protocol changes without prior FDA approval and giving FDA notice
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor states that the change met the criteria in (a)(3)(i) and (a)(3)(ii) based on credible information as defined in (a)(3)(iii), was made without prior approval, and that notice was given to FDA within 5 working days of making the change.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The sponsor makes the change without prior approval but gives no notice to FDA, gives notice later than 5 working days, or does not state any credible information basis for deciding the criteria were met.
baseRequirements.hint: State that the change met the (a)(3)(i) and (a)(3)(ii) criteria on credible information and that FDA was notified within 5 working days of making it.

baseRequirements.title: Notice of IDE change contents
baseRequirements.need: A notice of IDE change must be identified as such and include, for device changes, a summary of relevant information, a description of the change, and risk analysis and testing statements, or for protocol changes, a description, impact assessment, and credible information summary.

quote.text:

meeting the criteria in paragraphs

that are supported by credible informa-

prior FDA approval if the sponsor sub-
mits a notice of the change to the IDE
not later than 5-working days after
making the change. Changes to devices
are deemed to occur on the date the de-
vice, manufactured incorporating the
design or manufacturing change, is dis-

Such notices shall be identified as a

baseRequirements.topic: submitting a notice of IDE change to FDA after a device or protocol change
baseRequirements.complies: The submission is labeled a notice of IDE change and is sent to the IDE no later than 5 working days after the change, with a summary of relevant information, a description of the change, and risk analysis and testing statements for a device change, or a description, impact assessment, and credible information summary for a protocol change.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The submission is not identified as a notice of IDE change, is sent more than 5 working days after the change, or omits the description, risk analysis and testing statements, or credible information summary.
baseRequirements.hint: Label the submission a notice of IDE change, send it within 5 working days of the change, and include the device or protocol content items the rule lists.

baseRequirements.title: Minor changes in annual report
baseRequirements.need: Minor changes to the purpose of the study, risk analysis, monitoring procedures, labeling, informed consent materials, and IRB information that do not affect data validity, scientific soundness, or subject rights must be reported in the annual progress report under § 812.150(b)(5).

quote.text:
(4) Changes submitted in annual report.

The requirements of paragraph (a)(1) of
this section do not apply to minor
changes to the purpose of the study,
risk analysis, monitoring procedures,
labeling, informed consent materials,
and IRB information that do not affect:
(i) The validity of the data or infor-
mation resulting from the completion
of the approved protocol, or the rela-
tionship of likely patient risk to ben-
efit relied upon to approve the pro-
tocol;
(ii) The scientific soundness of the
investigational plan; or
(iii) The rights, safety, or welfare of
the human subjects involved in the in-
vestigation. Such changes shall be re-
ported in the annual progress report
for the IDE, under § 812.150(b)(5).

baseRequirements.topic: minor changes to a device study that are reported in the annual progress report
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor lists minor changes to the study purpose, risk analysis, monitoring procedures, labeling, informed consent materials, or IRB information, states that these do not affect data validity, the risk-benefit relationship, scientific soundness, or subject rights, safety, and welfare, and reports them in the annual progress report under § 812.150(b)(5).
baseRequirements.conflicts: The sponsor makes changes to the study purpose, risk analysis, monitoring, labeling, consent materials, or IRB information that alter data validity, scientific soundness, or subject rights and welfare, or makes minor changes and never reports them in the annual progress report.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe the changes as minor, say they do not affect data validity, risk-benefit, scientific soundness, or subject rights and welfare, and state they appear in the annual progress report.

baseRequirements.title: IRB approval for new facilities
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must submit to FDA a certification of any IRB approval of an investigation or part not included in the IDE application, and may not begin a part of an investigation at a facility until the IRB has approved, FDA has received the certification, and FDA has approved the supplemental application.

quote.text:

sponsor shall submit to FDA a certifi-
cation of any IRB approval of an inves-
tigation or a part of an investigation
not included in the IDE application. If
the investigation is otherwise un-
changed, the supplemental application

formation required by § 812.20(b) and (c)
and a description of any modifications
in the investigational plan required by
the IRB as a condition of approval. A
certification of IRB approval need not
be included in the initial submission of
the supplemental application, and such
certification is not a precondition for
agency consideration of the applica-

begin a part of an investigation at a fa-
cility until the IRB has approved the
investigation, FDA has received the
certification of IRB approval, and FDA,
under § 812.30(a), has approved the sup-
plemental application relating to that
part of the investigation (see
§ 56.103(a)).

baseRequirements.topic: adding a new facility or part of an investigation covered by IRB approval
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor submits to FDA a certification of the IRB approval for the part of the investigation not in the IDE application, updates the § 812.20(b) and (c) information with any IRB-required plan modifications, and states that work at the facility did not begin until the IRB approved, FDA received the certification, and FDA approved the supplemental application.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The sponsor begins the new part of the investigation at the facility before the IRB approved, before FDA received the certification, or before FDA approved the supplemental application, or never sends FDA the certification of IRB approval.
baseRequirements.hint: State that the IRB certification was sent to FDA and that no work at the facility started until IRB approval, FDA receipt of the certification, and FDA approval of the supplement were all in place.

baseRequirements.title: When investigation may begin
baseRequirements.need: An investigation may not begin until 30 days after FDA receives the application for a device other than a banned device unless FDA notifies the sponsor it may not begin, or until FDA approves an IDE by order.

quote.text:
(a) Approval or disapproval. FDA will
notify the sponsor in writing of the
date it receives an application. FDA
may approve an investigation as pro-

or disapprove it. An investigation may
not begin until:

the application at the address in § 812.19
for the investigation of a device other
than a banned device, unless FDA noti-
fies the sponsor that the investigation
may not begin; or
(2) FDA approves, by order, an IDE
for the investigation.

baseRequirements.topic: starting an investigation of a medical device under an investigational device exemption application
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the investigation starts only after 30 days have passed since FDA received the application (for a device that is not banned) and FDA has not told the sponsor it may not begin, or after FDA has approved the IDE by order.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the sponsor began the investigation immediately after submitting the application, or before 30 days passed, or after FDA notified the sponsor that the investigation may not begin, or without an FDA approval order.
baseRequirements.hint: State that the investigation begins only 30 days after FDA receives the application with no FDA stop notice, or after FDA approves the IDE by order.

baseRequirements.title: Grounds for disapproval
baseRequirements.need: FDA may disapprove or withdraw approval of an application for failure to comply with requirements, untrue statements or omitted material information, failure to respond to information requests, unacceptable risk-benefit or consent, or unreasonable investigation conditions.

quote.text:
(b) Grounds for disapproval or with-
drawal. FDA may disapprove or with-
draw approval of an application if FDA
finds that:

with any requirement of this part or

proval imposed by an IRB or FDA.
(2) The application or a report con-
tains an untrue statement of a mate-
rial fact, or omits material informa-
tion required by this part.

baseRequirements.topic: FDA disapproving or withdrawing approval of an investigational device exemption application
baseRequirements.complies: The text says FDA may disapprove or withdraw approval when the sponsor failed to comply with a requirement or condition of approval, or when the application or a report contains an untrue statement of a material fact or omits required material information.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says FDA cannot disapprove or withdraw approval for noncompliance, untrue statements, or omitted material information, or claims such problems have no effect on the application.
baseRequirements.hint: List the grounds FDA may use to disapprove or withdraw approval, including noncompliance, untrue material statements, and omitted material information.

baseRequirements.title: Notice of disapproval
baseRequirements.need: If FDA disapproves an application or proposes to withdraw approval, FDA will notify the sponsor in writing with a complete statement of reasons and an opportunity to request a hearing under part 16.

quote.text:
(c) Notice of disapproval or withdrawal.

If FDA disapproves an application or
proposes to withdraw approval of an
application, FDA will notify the spon-
sor in writing.
(1) A disapproval order will contain a
complete statement of the reasons for
disapproval and a statement that the
sponsor has an opportunity to request

baseRequirements.topic: FDA notice to a sponsor when an application is disapproved or approval is proposed to be withdrawn
baseRequirements.complies: The text says FDA notifies the sponsor in writing, and a disapproval order contains a complete statement of the reasons and a statement that the sponsor may request a hearing under part 16.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says FDA disapproves or withdraws approval without written notice, gives no reasons, or denies the sponsor any opportunity to request a hearing.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe written notice with a complete statement of reasons and the sponsor's opportunity to request a hearing under part 16.

baseRequirements.title: IRB and FDA approval required
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must not begin an investigation or part of an investigation until an IRB and FDA have both approved the application or supplemental application relating to it.

quote.text:
A sponsor shall not begin an inves-
tigation or part of an investigation
until an IRB and FDA have both ap-
proved the application or supplemental
application relating to the investiga-
tion or part of an investigation.

baseRequirements.topic: beginning an investigation of a medical device under an investigational device exemption
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the sponsor starts no part of the investigation until both an IRB and FDA have approved the application or supplemental application for it.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the sponsor began the investigation with only IRB approval, with only FDA approval, or before either approval was obtained.
baseRequirements.hint: State that both IRB and FDA approval of the application or supplement are in place before any part of the investigation begins.

baseRequirements.title: Monitoring exception from informed consent
baseRequirements.need: The sponsor must monitor the progress of all investigations involving an exception from informed consent under § 50.24 and promptly submit to the IDE file and the docket copies of public disclosure information received from the IRB, identified by IDE number.

baseRequirements.topic: sponsor monitoring of investigations using an exception from informed consent and handling of IRB public disclosure information
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the sponsor monitors the progress of all such investigations and, on receiving the IRB's public disclosure information, promptly submits copies to the IDE file and to the named docket, identified by the IDE number.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the sponsor does not monitor these investigations, or receives the IRB public disclosure information but does not send copies to the IDE file and docket, or sends them without the IDE number.
baseRequirements.hint: Say the sponsor monitors these investigations and promptly files the IRB public disclosure copies with the IDE file and the docket, marked with the IDE number.

baseRequirements.title: Reporting IRB non-approval
baseRequirements.need: The sponsor must monitor such investigations to determine when an IRB cannot approve the research and promptly provide that information in writing to FDA, investigators asked to participate, and other IRBs asked to review the investigation.
