baseRequirements.topic: sponsor handling of an IRB determination that it cannot approve research using an exception from informed consent
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the sponsor monitors the investigations, and when an IRB cannot approve the research for failing the § 50.24(a) criteria or other ethical concerns, promptly provides that information in writing to FDA, to investigators asked to participate, and to other IRBs asked to review it.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the sponsor learns an IRB cannot approve the research but does not inform FDA, does not tell investigators asked to participate, or does not tell other IRBs asked to review the investigation.
baseRequirements.hint: State that the sponsor monitors for IRB non-approval and promptly writes to FDA, participating investigators, and other reviewing IRBs.

baseRequirements.title: IRB compliance with part 56
baseRequirements.need: An IRB reviewing and approving investigations under this part must comply with part 56 in all respects, including composition, duties, and functions.

quote.text:
An IRB reviewing and approving in-
vestigations under this part shall com-
ply with the requirements of part 56 in
all respects, including its composition,
duties, and functions.

baseRequirements.topic: institutional review board (IRB) review and approval of investigations of medical devices
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that an IRB that reviews and approves investigations under this part follows part 56 in all respects, including how the board is composed and what duties and functions it carries out.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the IRB reviewing these investigations does not follow part 56, or that its composition, duties or functions are handled differently from part 56.
baseRequirements.hint: State that any IRB reviewing and approving these investigations meets part 56 fully, covering composition, duties and functions.

baseRequirements.title: IRB authority over investigations
baseRequirements.need: An IRB must review and has authority to approve, require modifications to secure approval, or disapprove all investigations covered by this part.

quote.text:
(a) An IRB shall review and have au-
thority to approve, require modifica-
tions in (to secure approval), or dis-
approve all investigations covered by
this part.

baseRequirements.topic: IRB review and decisions on investigations of medical devices
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that the IRB reviews every investigation covered by this part and has authority to approve it, to require modifications to secure approval, or to disapprove it.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the IRB cannot disapprove an investigation, cannot require changes before approval, or that some covered investigations are not reviewed by the IRB at all.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe the IRB as reviewing all covered investigations with authority to approve, require modifications to secure approval, or disapprove.

baseRequirements.title: Application when no IRB exists
baseRequirements.need: If no IRB exists or FDA finds an IRB's review inadequate, a sponsor may submit an application to FDA.

quote.text:
(b) If no IRB exists or if FDA finds
that an IRB’s review is inadequate, a
sponsor may submit an application to
FDA.

baseRequirements.topic: submitting an application to FDA when no IRB exists or IRB review is found inadequate
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that if no IRB exists, or if FDA finds an IRB's review inadequate, the sponsor may submit an application to FDA.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says a sponsor has no option to apply to FDA when no IRB exists or when FDA finds the IRB review inadequate, or that the investigation simply cannot proceed in that situation.
baseRequirements.hint: Note that a sponsor may submit an application to FDA when no IRB exists or when FDA finds the IRB's review inadequate.

baseRequirements.title: IRB continuing review
baseRequirements.need: The IRB must conduct its continuing review of an investigation in accordance with part 56.

quote.text:
The IRB shall conduct its continuing
review of an investigation in accord-
ance with part 56.

baseRequirements.topic: continuing review of investigations by an IRB
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that the IRB conducts its continuing review of an investigation in accordance with part 56.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the IRB's continuing review is not done under part 56, or that continuing review is skipped or handled by some other process.
baseRequirements.hint: State that the IRB's continuing review of an investigation follows part 56.

baseRequirements.title: Significant risk device determination
baseRequirements.need: If an IRB determines that an investigation presented under § 812.2(b)(1)(ii) involves a significant risk device, it must notify the investigator and, where appropriate, the sponsor, and the sponsor may not begin the investigation except as provided in § 812.30(a).

quote.text:
If an IRB determines that an inves-
tigation, presented for approval under
§ 812.2(b)(1)(ii), involves a significant
risk device, it shall so notify the inves-
tigator and, where appropriate, the
sponsor. A sponsor may not begin the
investigation except as provided in
§ 812.30(a).

baseRequirements.topic: IRB findings of significant risk device in investigations presented under § 812.2(b)(1)(ii)
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that when the IRB determines an investigation presented under § 812.2(b)(1)(ii) involves a significant risk device, it notifies the investigator and, where appropriate, the sponsor, and that the sponsor may not begin the investigation except as provided in § 812.30(a).
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the IRB keeps a significant risk device finding to itself without notifying the investigator or sponsor, or that the sponsor may begin the investigation without regard to § 812.30(a).
baseRequirements.hint: Say the IRB notifies the investigator and, where appropriate, the sponsor of a significant risk device finding, and that the sponsor may not begin except as § 812.30(a) provides.

baseRequirements.title: Treatment IDE criteria
baseRequirements.need: FDA shall consider use of an investigational device under a treatment IDE if the device is intended to treat or diagnose a serious or immediately life-threatening disease, no comparable alternative is available, the device is under investigation or trials are completed, and the sponsor is actively pursuing marketing approval with due diligence.

quote.text:
(b) Criteria. FDA shall consider the
use of an investigational device under a
treatment IDE if:
(1) The device is intended to treat or
diagnose a serious or immediately life-
threatening disease or condition;
(2) There is no comparable or satis-
factory alternative device or other
therapy available to treat or diagnose
that stage of the disease or condition
in the intended patient population;
(3) The device is under investigation
in a controlled clinical trial for the
same use under an approved IDE, or
such clinical trials have been com-
pleted; and
(4) The sponsor of the investigation is
actively pursuing marketing approval/
clearance of the investigational device
with due diligence.

baseRequirements.topic: treatment IDE for an investigational device
baseRequirements.complies: The text states FDA will consider a treatment IDE when the device is intended to treat or diagnose a serious or immediately life-threatening disease or condition, no comparable or satisfactory alternative is available for that stage in the intended patient population, the device is under investigation in a controlled clinical trial for the same use under an approved IDE or such trials are completed, and the sponsor is actively pursuing marketing approval or clearance with due diligence.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text claims FDA will consider a treatment IDE where the device treats a minor condition, a comparable alternative exists, no controlled trial is under way or completed, or the sponsor is not actively pursuing marketing approval with due diligence.
baseRequirements.hint: List all four criteria: serious or immediately life-threatening disease, no comparable or satisfactory alternative, controlled trial under an approved IDE or completed trials, and active pursuit of marketing approval with due diligence.

baseRequirements.title: Treatment IDE application contents
baseRequirements.need: A treatment IDE application must include, in order, the sponsor's contact information, intended use and patient selection criteria, rationale, evaluation measures, monitoring procedures, labeling, safety and effectiveness information, commitment statement, investigator agreement example, and sale price statement.

quote.text:
(c) Applications for treatment use. (1) A
treatment IDE application shall in-
clude, in the following order:
(i) The name, address, and telephone
number of the sponsor of the treatment
IDE;
(ii) The intended use of the device,
the criteria for patient selection, and a
written protocol describing the treat-
ment use;
(iii) An explanation of the rationale
for use of the device, including, as ap-
propriate, either a list of the available
regimens that ordinarily should be
tried before using the investigational
device or an explanation of why the use
of the investigational device is pref-
erable to the use of available marketed
treatments;

baseRequirements.topic: treatment IDE applications for investigational device treatment use
baseRequirements.complies: The application lists, in the required order, the sponsor's name, address and telephone number, then the intended use, patient selection criteria and written treatment protocol, then the rationale for use including available regimens to try first or why the investigational device is preferable.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The application omits the sponsor's contact information, leaves out patient selection criteria or the written protocol, gives no rationale or prior regimens, or presents the required items out of order.
baseRequirements.hint: Present every required item in the exact order listed in the rule, starting with the sponsor's name, address and telephone number.

baseRequirements.title: Treatment use investigator duties
baseRequirements.need: A licensed practitioner who receives an investigational device for treatment use under a treatment IDE is an investigator under the IDE and is responsible for meeting all applicable investigator responsibilities under this part and parts 50 and 56.

quote.text:
(2) A licensed practitioner who re-
ceives an investigational device for
treatment use under a treatment IDE
is an ‘‘investigator’’ under the IDE and
is responsible for meeting all applica-
ble investigator responsibilities under
this part and parts 50 and 56 of this
chapter.

baseRequirements.topic: licensed practitioners receiving investigational devices for treatment use under a treatment IDE
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that a licensed practitioner receiving the device for treatment use is an investigator under the IDE and must meet all applicable investigator responsibilities under this part and parts 50 and 56.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the licensed practitioner has no investigator duties, or that only some responsibilities under this part or parts 50 and 56 apply to that practitioner.
baseRequirements.hint: State that the licensed practitioner is an investigator and is responsible for all applicable investigator duties under this part and parts 50 and 56.

baseRequirements.title: Treatment use start
baseRequirements.need: Treatment use may begin 30 days after FDA receives the treatment IDE submission at the address in § 812.19, unless FDA notifies the sponsor in writing earlier that the treatment use may or may not begin.

quote.text:
(d) FDA action on treatment IDE appli-
cations—(1) Approval of treatment IDE’s.

Treatment use may begin 30 days after
FDA receives the treatment IDE sub-
mission at the address specified in
§ 812.19, unless FDA notifies the sponsor
in writing earlier than the 30 days that
the treatment use may or may not
begin. FDA may approve the treatment
use as proposed or approve it with
modifications.

baseRequirements.topic: starting treatment use of an investigational device after a treatment IDE submission
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that treatment use may begin 30 days after FDA receives the treatment IDE submission at the § 812.19 address, unless FDA notifies the sponsor in writing earlier that use may or may not begin.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text claims treatment use may start immediately on submission, or on a different timeline, or ignores FDA's earlier written notice allowing or barring use.
baseRequirements.hint: Say treatment use may begin 30 days after FDA receives the submission at the § 812.19 address unless FDA gives earlier written notice.

baseRequirements.title: Treatment IDE disapproval grounds
baseRequirements.need: FDA may disapprove or withdraw approval of a treatment IDE if the criteria are not met, required information is missing, grounds in § 812.30(b)(1) through (b)(5) apply, or evidence of safety and effectiveness is insufficient.

quote.text:
(2) Disapproval or withdrawal of ap-
proval of treatment IDE’s. FDA may dis-
approve or withdraw approval of a
treatment IDE if:
(i) The criteria specified in § 812.36(b)
are not met or the treatment IDE does
not contain the information required
in § 812.36(c);
(ii) FDA determines that any of the
grounds for disapproval or withdrawal
of approval listed in § 812.30(b)(1)
through (b)(5) apply;
(iii) The device is intended for a seri-
ous disease or condition and there is
insufficient evidence of safety and ef-
fectiveness to support such use;

baseRequirements.topic: FDA disapproval or withdrawal of approval of a treatment IDE
baseRequirements.complies: The text states FDA may disapprove or withdraw approval if the § 812.36(b) criteria are not met, required § 812.36(c) information is missing, grounds in § 812.30(b)(1) through (b)(5) apply, or evidence of safety and effectiveness is insufficient for a serious disease or condition.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text claims FDA can never disapprove or withdraw approval once submitted, or lists grounds that omit the missing information, the § 812.30(b) grounds, or insufficient safety and effectiveness evidence.
baseRequirements.hint: List each ground for disapproval or withdrawal exactly as the rule gives them, including missing required information and insufficient safety and effectiveness evidence.

baseRequirements.title: Criteria for treatment use
baseRequirements.need: A treatment IDE may be approved only if the criteria in § 812.36(d)(2), including the conditions on the device's safety and the state of the controlled investigation, are met.

quote.text:
(A) May be effective for its intended
use in its intended population; or
(B) Would not expose the patients to
whom the device is to be administered
to an unreasonable and significant ad-
ditional risk of illness or injury;

baseRequirements.topic: criteria for approving a treatment IDE
baseRequirements.complies: The text states a treatment IDE may be approved only if the device may be effective for its intended use in its intended population or would not expose patients to an unreasonable and significant additional risk of illness or injury.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text claims approval is available without meeting the criteria, or asserts the device may be used even though it would expose patients to an unreasonable and significant additional risk.
baseRequirements.hint: State that approval depends on meeting the criteria, including that the device may be effective in its intended population or adds no unreasonable and significant risk.

baseRequirements.title: Notice of disapproval or withdrawal
baseRequirements.need: If FDA disapproves or proposes to withdraw approval of a treatment IDE, FDA follows the procedures in § 812.30(c).

quote.text:
(3) Notice of disapproval or withdrawal.

If FDA disapproves or proposes to with-
draw approval of a treatment IDE,
FDA will follow the procedures set
forth in § 812.30(c).

baseRequirements.topic: FDA notice when a treatment IDE is disapproved or approval is withdrawn
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that if FDA disapproves or proposes to withdraw approval of a treatment IDE, FDA will follow the procedures in § 812.30(c).
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says FDA may disapprove or withdraw approval without following the § 812.30(c) procedures, or describes a different procedure.
baseRequirements.hint: State that FDA follows the § 812.30(c) procedures for disapproval or proposed withdrawal of a treatment IDE.

baseRequirements.title: Treatment use safeguards
baseRequirements.need: Treatment use of an investigational device is conditioned on the sponsor and investigators complying with the safeguards of the IDE process and the regulations governing informed consent (part 50) and IRBs (part 56).

quote.text:
(e) Safeguards. Treatment use of an
investigational device is conditioned
upon the sponsor and investigators
complying with the safeguards of the
IDE process and the regulations gov-
erning informed consent (part 50 of this
chapter) and institutional review
boards (part 56 of this chapter).

baseRequirements.topic: treatment use of an investigational device outside a clinical trial
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that treatment use is allowed only when the sponsor and investigators follow the safeguards of the IDE process and the rules on informed consent (part 50) and institutional review boards (part 56).
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says treatment use can go ahead without following IDE safeguards, or without informed consent under part 50 or IRB review under part 56.
baseRequirements.hint: Say that treatment use depends on the sponsor and investigators meeting IDE safeguards plus part 50 informed consent and part 56 IRB rules.

baseRequirements.title: General sponsor responsibilities
baseRequirements.need: Sponsors must select qualified investigators and give them the information needed to conduct the investigation properly, ensure proper monitoring, ensure IRB review and approval are obtained, submit an IDE application to FDA, and ensure IRB and FDA are promptly informed of significant new information.

quote.text:
Sponsors are responsible for selecting
qualified investigators and providing
them with the information they need
to conduct the investigation properly,
ensuring proper monitoring of the in-
vestigation, ensuring that IRB review
and approval are obtained, submitting
an IDE application to FDA, and ensur-
ing that any reviewing IRB and FDA
are promptly informed of significant
new information about an investiga-
tion.

baseRequirements.topic: sponsor duties in an investigational device investigation
baseRequirements.complies: The text lists the sponsor as responsible for choosing qualified investigators, giving them the information needed to run the investigation properly, ensuring proper monitoring, ensuring IRB review and approval are obtained, submitting an IDE application to FDA, and promptly informing the reviewing IRB and FDA of significant new information.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the sponsor does not need to monitor the investigation, does not need IRB approval, need not file an IDE application with FDA, or need not tell the IRB and FDA about significant new information.
baseRequirements.hint: List each sponsor duty: selecting qualified investigators, supplying needed information, monitoring, obtaining IRB approval, submitting the IDE application, and promptly reporting significant new information to the IRB and FDA.

baseRequirements.title: Selecting qualified investigators
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must select investigators qualified by training and experience to investigate the device.

quote.text:
(a) Selecting investigators. A sponsor
shall select investigators qualified by
training and experience to investigate
the device.

baseRequirements.topic: choosing investigators for an investigational device study
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the sponsor selects investigators whose training and experience qualify them to investigate the device.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the sponsor may pick investigators without regard to their training or experience, or assigns the study to people who lack the relevant qualifications.
baseRequirements.hint: State that the sponsor selects investigators qualified by training and experience to investigate the device.

baseRequirements.title: Shipping devices to qualified investigators
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must ship investigational devices only to qualified investigators participating in the investigation.

quote.text:
(b) Control of device. A sponsor shall
ship investigational devices only to
qualified investigators participating in
the investigation.

baseRequirements.topic: shipping investigational devices to investigators
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the sponsor ships investigational devices only to qualified investigators who are taking part in the investigation.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says devices are sent to unqualified people, to sites not in the investigation, or to anyone who asks.
baseRequirements.hint: State that investigational devices are shipped only to qualified investigators participating in the investigation.

baseRequirements.title: Signed investigator agreements
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must obtain from each participating investigator a signed agreement containing the investigator's curriculum vitae, relevant experience, explanation of any terminated research, commitment statements, and sufficient accurate financial disclosure information.

quote.text:
(c) Obtaining agreements. A sponsor
shall obtain from each participating
investigator a signed agreement that
includes:
(1) The investigator’s curriculum
vitae.
(2) Where applicable, a statement of
the investigator’s relevant experience,
including the dates, location, extent,
and type of experience.

baseRequirements.topic: signed agreements obtained from investigators in an investigational device study
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the sponsor obtains a signed agreement from each participating investigator that includes the investigator's curriculum vitae, a statement of relevant experience with dates, location, extent and type where applicable, an explanation of any terminated research, commitment statements, and accurate financial disclosure information.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says investigators are enrolled without a signed agreement, or the agreement omits the curriculum vitae, relevant experience, explanation of terminated research, commitments, or financial disclosure information.
baseRequirements.hint: State that each participating investigator signs an agreement containing a curriculum vitae, relevant experience, any terminated research explanation, commitments, and accurate financial disclosure information.

baseRequirements.title: Financial disclosure commitment
baseRequirements.need: The sponsor must obtain the investigator's commitment to promptly update financial disclosure information if relevant changes occur during the investigation and for 1 year after completion, and this information must be submitted in any marketing application but not in the IDE application.

quote.text:
The sponsor shall obtain a commit-
ment from the clinical investigator to
promptly update this information if
any relevant changes occur during the
course of the investigation and for 1
year following completion of the study.
This information shall not be sub-
mitted in an investigational device ex-
emption application, but shall be sub-
mitted in any marketing application
involving the device.

baseRequirements.topic: investigator financial disclosure information in an investigational device study
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the sponsor obtains the investigator's commitment to promptly update financial disclosure information if relevant changes occur during the investigation and for 1 year after completion, and that this information goes in any marketing application but not in the IDE application.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says investigators need not update financial disclosure information, that updates stop at study completion, or that the information is filed in the IDE application or left out of the marketing application.
baseRequirements.hint: State that the investigator commits to prompt updates during the study and for 1 year after completion, with the information submitted in the marketing application and not in the IDE application.

baseRequirements.title: Selecting qualified monitors
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must select monitors qualified by training and experience to monitor the investigational study in accordance with this part and other applicable FDA regulations.

quote.text:
(d) Selecting monitors. A sponsor shall
select monitors qualified by training
and experience to monitor the inves-
tigational study in accordance with
this part and other applicable FDA reg-
ulations.

baseRequirements.topic: choosing and assigning people to monitor an investigational device study on behalf of the sponsor
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor names the monitors and states their training and prior experience monitoring device studies, and ties that background to the applicable FDA regulations the monitoring follows.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The sponsor assigns monitoring to staff with no stated training or experience, or says monitors were picked without regard to qualifications or regulatory requirements.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe each monitor's training and experience and how it fits monitoring the study under this part and other FDA regulations.

baseRequirements.title: Securing investigator compliance
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor who discovers an investigator is not complying with the signed agreement, investigational plan, this part, other FDA regulations, or conditions of approval must promptly secure compliance or discontinue shipments and terminate the investigator, and require return or disposal of the device unless that would jeopardize a subject.

quote.text:
(a) Securing compliance. A sponsor
who discovers that an investigator is
not complying with the signed agree-
ment, the investigational plan, the re-
quirements of this part or other appli-
cable FDA regulations, or any condi-
tions of approval imposed by the re-
viewing IRB or FDA shall promptly ei-
ther secure compliance, or discontinue
shipments of the device to the investi-
gator and terminate the investigator’s
participation in the investigation.

baseRequirements.topic: a sponsor handling an investigator who is not following the study agreement, plan or regulations
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor states that on learning of noncompliance it promptly acts to bring the investigator back into compliance, or stops shipping the device, ends the investigator's participation, and arranges return or disposal of the device unless that would harm a subject.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The sponsor says it continued shipments and kept the noncomplying investigator enrolled with no corrective action, or ignored the noncompliance.
baseRequirements.hint: State that noncompliance triggers prompt correction or shipment stop plus termination and device return or disposal, with the subject-safety exception.

baseRequirements.title: Unanticipated adverse device effects
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must immediately evaluate any unanticipated adverse device effect and, if it presents an unreasonable risk to subjects, terminate all affected investigations not later than 5 working days after the determination and not later than 15 working days after first receiving notice of the effect.

quote.text:
(b) Unanticipated adverse device effects.

(1) A sponsor shall immediately con-
duct an evaluation of any unantici-
pated adverse device effect.
(2) A sponsor who determines that an
unanticipated adverse device effect
presents an unreasonable risk to sub-
jects shall terminate all investigations
or parts of investigations presenting
that risk as soon as possible.

baseRequirements.topic: unexpected harmful effects of an investigational device and the sponsor's response
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor says it immediately evaluates any unanticipated adverse device effect and, when it finds an unreasonable risk, terminates the affected investigations within 5 working days of that determination and no later than 15 working days after first notice.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The sponsor waits or takes no action after learning of an unanticipated adverse device effect, or keeps the risky investigations running past the stated deadlines.
baseRequirements.hint: Say the effect is evaluated immediately and that an unreasonable-risk finding ends affected studies within 5 working days of the decision and 15 working days of first notice.

baseRequirements.title: Resuming terminated studies
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor may not resume a terminated investigation of a significant risk device without IRB and FDA approval, and for a non-significant risk device without IRB approval and, if terminated under paragraph (b)(2), FDA approval.

quote.text:
(c) Resumption of terminated studies. If
the device is a significant risk device,
a sponsor may not resume a termi-
nated investigation without IRB and
FDA approval. If the device is not a
significant risk device, a sponsor may
not resume a terminated investigation
without IRB approval and, if the inves-
tigation was terminated under para-
graph (b)(2) of this section, FDA ap-
proval.

baseRequirements.topic: restarting an investigational device study that was terminated
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor states that a terminated significant risk device study resumes only with IRB and FDA approval, and a non-significant risk study resumes only with IRB approval plus FDA approval when it was terminated for unreasonable risk.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The sponsor restarts a terminated investigation with only one approval or none, or resumes a significant risk study without both IRB and FDA approval.
baseRequirements.hint: List the approvals needed before resuming: IRB and FDA for significant risk devices, IRB plus FDA (if terminated for risk) for non-significant risk devices.

baseRequirements.title: General investigator responsibilities
baseRequirements.need: An investigator is responsible for conducting the investigation according to the signed agreement, investigational plan, and applicable FDA regulations, protecting subjects' rights, safety, and welfare, controlling devices under investigation, and ensuring informed consent under part 50.

quote.text:
An investigator is responsible for en-
suring that an investigation is con-
ducted according to the signed agree-
ment, the investigational plan and ap-
plicable FDA regulations, for pro-
tecting the rights, safety, and welfare
of subjects under the investigator’s
care, and for the control of devices
under investigation. An investigator
also is responsible for ensuring that in-
formed consent is obtained in accord-
ance with part 50 of this chapter.

baseRequirements.topic: an investigator's duties in running an investigational device study and caring for subjects
baseRequirements.complies: The investigator states responsibility for following the signed agreement, investigational plan and FDA regulations, for protecting subjects' rights, safety and welfare, for controlling the devices, and for obtaining informed consent under part 50.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The investigator says the plan or agreement need not be followed, that subject safety or device control is someone else's job, or that consent is handled outside part 50.
baseRequirements.hint: Cover all four duties: following the agreement, plan and regulations; protecting subjects; controlling devices; and consent under part 50.

baseRequirements.title: Awaiting IRB and FDA approval
baseRequirements.need: An investigator may determine whether potential subjects would be interested but must not request written informed consent or allow any subject to participate before obtaining IRB and FDA approval.

quote.text:
(a) Awaiting approval. An investigator
may determine whether potential sub-
jects would be interested in partici-
pating in an investigation, but shall
not request the written informed con-
sent of any subject to participate, and
shall not allow any subject to partici-
pate before obtaining IRB and FDA ap-
proval.

baseRequirements.topic: contacting or enrolling subjects before an investigational device study is approved
baseRequirements.complies: The investigator says it may ask potential subjects about interest but will not seek written informed consent or let anyone participate until IRB and FDA approval are in hand.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The investigator says it collected signed consent forms or enrolled subjects before IRB and FDA approval.
baseRequirements.hint: State that only expressions of interest happen before approval, and that written consent and participation wait for IRB and FDA approval.

baseRequirements.title: Investigator compliance
baseRequirements.need: An investigator must conduct an investigation in accordance with the signed agreement with the sponsor, the investigational plan, this part, other applicable FDA regulations, and any conditions of approval imposed by an IRB or FDA.

quote.text:
(b) Compliance. An investigator shall
conduct an investigation in accordance
with the signed agreement with the
sponsor, the investigational plan, this
part and other applicable FDA regula-
tions, and any conditions of approval
imposed by an IRB or FDA.

baseRequirements.topic: how an investigator runs a clinical investigation of a medical device
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the investigator follows the signed sponsor agreement, the investigational plan, FDA device rules, and any conditions of approval set by an IRB or FDA, and describes steps showing each is followed.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the investigator departs from the signed sponsor agreement or the investigational plan, ignores FDA device regulations, or skips conditions of approval imposed by an IRB or FDA.
baseRequirements.hint: State that the investigator conducts the study per the signed sponsor agreement, the investigational plan, FDA regulations, and any IRB or FDA approval conditions.

baseRequirements.title: Supervising device use
baseRequirements.need: An investigator must permit an investigational device to be used only with subjects under the investigator's supervision and must not supply the device to any person not authorized under this part to receive it.

quote.text:
(c) Supervising device use. An investi-
gator shall permit an investigational
device to be used only with subjects
under the investigator’s supervision.
An investigator shall not supply an in-
vestigational device to any person not
authorized under this part to receive
it.

baseRequirements.topic: use and supply of an investigational medical device
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the device is used only with subjects under the investigator's supervision and is given only to persons authorized under the device rules to receive it.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the device is used with people not under the investigator's supervision, or that the device is handed out to unauthorized persons such as unlisted staff or outside parties.
baseRequirements.hint: Say the device is used only with subjects under the investigator's supervision and supplied only to persons authorized under the rules.

baseRequirements.title: Investigator financial disclosure
baseRequirements.need: A clinical investigator must disclose to the sponsor sufficient accurate financial information for complete and accurate certification or disclosure statements under part 54 and promptly update it during the investigation and for 1 year after completion.

quote.text:
(d) Financial disclosure. A clinical in-
vestigator shall disclose to the sponsor
sufficient accurate financial informa-
tion to allow the applicant to submit
complete and accurate certification or
disclosure statements required under
part 54 of this chapter. The investi-
gator shall promptly update this infor-
mation if any relevant changes occur
during the course of the investigation
and for 1 year following completion of
the study.

baseRequirements.topic: financial information a clinical investigator discloses to the sponsor
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the investigator gives the sponsor accurate financial information that lets the sponsor file complete and accurate part 54 certification or disclosure statements, and updates it promptly during the study and for 1 year after completion.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the investigator withholds financial information, gives inaccurate or incomplete figures, or fails to update changes during the study or in the year after it ends.
baseRequirements.hint: State that the investigator discloses accurate financial information for part 54 statements and promptly updates it during the study and for 1 year after completion.

baseRequirements.title: Disposing of device
baseRequirements.need: Upon completion or termination of the investigation or the investigator's part of it, or at the sponsor's request, an investigator must return remaining device supply to the sponsor or dispose of it as the sponsor directs.

quote.text:
(e) Disposing of device. Upon comple-
tion or termination of a clinical inves-
tigation or the investigator’s part of an
investigation, or at the sponsor’s re-
quest, an investigator shall return to
the sponsor any remaining supply of
the device or otherwise dispose of the
device as the sponsor directs.

baseRequirements.topic: remaining supply of an investigational device at the end of an investigation
baseRequirements.complies: The text says that when the investigation or the investigator's part ends, or when the sponsor asks, the investigator returns remaining device supply to the sponsor or disposes of it as the sponsor directs.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the investigator keeps, sells, gives away, or discards leftover devices without returning them to the sponsor or following the sponsor's directions.
baseRequirements.hint: Say leftover devices are returned to the sponsor or disposed of as the sponsor directs when the study or the investigator's part ends or on sponsor request.

baseRequirements.title: Notice of disqualification proceeding
baseRequirements.need: If FDA has information indicating repeated or deliberate noncompliance or false information, the Center will give the investigator written notice and an opportunity to explain in writing or at an informal conference, and if the explanation is not accepted, an opportunity for a regulatory hearing under part 16.

quote.text:
(a) If FDA has information indicating
that an investigator (including a spon-
sor-investigator) has repeatedly or de-
liberately failed to comply with the re-
quirements of this part, part 50, or part
56 of this chapter, or has repeatedly or
deliberately submitted to FDA or to
the sponsor false information in any
required report, the Center for Devices
and Radiological Health, the Center for
Biologics Evaluation and Research, or
the Center for Drug Evaluation and Re-
search will furnish the investigator
written notice of the matter com-
plained of and offer the investigator an
opportunity to explain the matter in
writing, or, at the option of the inves-
tigator, in an informal conference.

baseRequirements.topic: FDA notice to an investigator about possible disqualification for repeated or deliberate noncompliance or false information
baseRequirements.complies: The text says FDA's Center sends the investigator written notice of the matter, offers a chance to explain in writing or at an informal conference, and, if the explanation is not accepted, offers a regulatory hearing under part 16.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the investigator is disqualified without written notice, without any chance to explain in writing or at an informal conference, or without a part 16 hearing when the explanation is rejected.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe written notice of the complaint, a chance to explain in writing or at an informal conference, and a part 16 hearing if the explanation is not accepted.

baseRequirements.title: Notification of ineligibility
baseRequirements.need: If the Commissioner determines repeated or deliberate noncompliance or false information, the Commissioner will notify the investigator, sponsors, and reviewing IRBs that the investigator is not eligible to receive test articles and to conduct clinical investigations supporting FDA applications.

quote.text:
(b) After evaluating all available in-
formation, including any explanation
presented by the investigator, if the
Commissioner determines that the in-
vestigator has repeatedly or delib-
erately failed to comply with the re-
quirements of this part, part 50, or part
56 of this chapter, or has repeatedly or
deliberately submitted to FDA or to
the sponsor false information in any
required report, the Commissioner will
notify the investigator, the sponsor of
any investigation in which the investi-
gator has been named as a participant,
and the reviewing investigational re-
view boards (IRBs) that the investi-
gator is not eligible to receive test ar-
ticles under this part.

baseRequirements.topic: FDA determination that an investigator is ineligible to receive test articles and conduct clinical investigations
baseRequirements.complies: The text says that after weighing all information including the investigator's explanation, if the Commissioner finds repeated or deliberate noncompliance or false information, the Commissioner notifies the investigator, the sponsors of studies naming the investigator, and the reviewing IRBs that the investigator is not eligible to receive test articles.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the investigator is declared ineligible without the Commissioner's determination, or that sponsors or reviewing IRBs are never told of the ineligibility.
baseRequirements.hint: State that on the Commissioner's determination of repeated or deliberate noncompliance or false information, the investigator, sponsors, and reviewing IRBs are notified of ineligibility to receive test articles.

baseRequirements.title: Examination of unreliable data
baseRequirements.need: Each application or submission to FDA containing data reported by an ineligible investigator is subject to examination to determine whether the investigator submitted unreliable data essential to the investigation, clearance or approval, or continued marketing.

quote.text:
(c) Each application or submission to
FDA under the provisions of this chap-
ter containing data reported by an in-
vestigator who has been determined to
be ineligible to receive FDA-regulated
test articles is subject to examination
to determine whether the investigator
has submitted unreliable data that are
essential to the continuation of an in-
vestigation or essential to the clear-
ance or approval of a marketing appli-
cation, or essential to the continued
marketing of an FDA-regulated prod-
uct.

baseRequirements.topic: FDA applications or submissions that include data from an investigator found ineligible to receive FDA-regulated test articles
baseRequirements.complies: The submission states that data from the ineligible investigator are flagged and that FDA will examine them to decide whether they are unreliable and essential to the investigation, clearance, approval or continued marketing.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The submission treats data from an ineligible investigator as valid without any examination, or claims such data need not be reviewed because the investigator was only later found ineligible.
baseRequirements.hint: Say that any FDA submission containing data from an ineligible investigator will be examined to decide if that data are unreliable and essential to the investigation, clearance, approval or continued marketing.

baseRequirements.title: Termination for unreliable data
baseRequirements.need: If remaining data are inadequate to support continuing the investigation, the Commissioner notifies the sponsor, who may have a part 16 hearing, and if a danger to public health exists the Commissioner must terminate the IDE immediately and notify the sponsor and reviewing IRBs.

quote.text:
(d) If the Commissioner determines,
after the unreliable data submitted by
the investigator are eliminated from
consideration, that the data remaining
are inadequate to support a conclusion
that it is reasonably safe to continue
the investigation, the Commissioner
will notify the sponsor, who shall have
an opportunity for a regulatory hear-
ing under part 16 of this chapter. If a
danger to the public health exists, how-
ever, the Commissioner shall termi-
nate the investigational device exemp-
tion (IDE) immediately and notify the
sponsor and the reviewing IRBs of the
termination.

baseRequirements.topic: FDA action on an investigation when data from an ineligible investigator are removed and the remaining data are inadequate
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the Commissioner notifies the sponsor, the sponsor may request a part 16 regulatory hearing, and if a danger to public health exists the IDE is terminated immediately with notice to the sponsor and reviewing IRBs.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the investigation continues unchanged after unreliable data are removed, or that the sponsor has no hearing opportunity, or that a dangerous IDE stays in effect while notice is delayed.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe the sequence: Commissioner finds remaining data inadequate, notifies sponsor, sponsor may have a part 16 hearing, and immediate termination with notice to sponsor and IRBs if public health is endangered.

baseRequirements.title: Rescinding clearance or approval
baseRequirements.need: If the Commissioner determines that continued clearance or approval of the product cannot be justified after unreliable data are eliminated, the Commissioner will rescind clearance or withdraw approval under the applicable statutes.

quote.text:
(e) If the Commissioner determines,
after the unreliable data submitted by
the investigator are eliminated from
consideration, that the continued
clearance or approval of the product
for which the data were submitted can-
not be justified, the Commissioner will
proceed to rescind clearance or with-
draw approval of the product in accord-
ance with the applicable provisions of
the relevant statutes.

baseRequirements.topic: continued clearance or approval of an FDA-regulated product after unreliable data from an ineligible investigator are set aside
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that if continued clearance or approval cannot be justified once the unreliable data are eliminated, the Commissioner will rescind clearance or withdraw approval under the relevant statutes.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the product keeps its clearance or approval regardless of unreliable data, or that no rescission or withdrawal step exists when the remaining data cannot justify continued marketing.
baseRequirements.hint: State that when unreliable data are eliminated and continued clearance or approval cannot be justified, the Commissioner rescinds clearance or withdraws approval under the applicable statutes.

baseRequirements.title: Reinstatement of investigator
baseRequirements.need: An investigator determined ineligible may be reinstated when the Commissioner determines the investigator has presented adequate assurances of future compliance with this chapter.

quote.text:
(f) An investigator who has been de-
termined to be ineligible under para-
graph (b) of this section may be rein-
stated as eligible when the Commis-
sioner determines that the investigator
has presented adequate assurances that
the investigator will employ all test
articles, and will conduct any clinical
investigation that supports an applica-
tion for a research or marketing per-
mit for products regulated by FDA,
solely in compliance with the applica-
ble provisions of this chapter.

baseRequirements.topic: reinstatement of an investigator previously determined ineligible to receive FDA-regulated test articles
baseRequirements.complies: The text says an ineligible investigator may be reinstated when the Commissioner determines the investigator has given adequate assurances of using test articles and conducting clinical investigations solely in compliance with the chapter.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says ineligibility is permanent with no reinstatement path, or that reinstatement happens automatically without any assurances of future compliance.
baseRequirements.hint: Explain that an ineligible investigator can be reinstated only when the Commissioner finds adequate assurances that future test article use and clinical investigations will comply with the chapter.

baseRequirements.title: Investigational device label contents
baseRequirements.need: An investigational device or its immediate package must bear a label with the manufacturer's name and place of business, quantity of contents if appropriate, the caution statement, and labeling describing all relevant contraindications, hazards, adverse effects, interfering substances or devices, warnings, and precautions.

quote.text:
(a) Contents. An investigational de-
vice or its immediate package shall
bear a label with the following infor-
mation: the name and place of business
of the manufacturer, packer, or dis-
tributor (in accordance with § 801.1),
the quantity of contents, if appro-
priate, and the following statement:
‘‘CAUTION—Investigational device.
Limited by Federal (or United States)
law to investigational use.’’ The label
or other labeling shall describe all rel-
evant contraindications, hazards, ad-
verse effects, interfering substances or
devices, warnings, and precautions.

baseRequirements.topic: labeling of an investigational device and its immediate package
baseRequirements.complies: The label shows the manufacturer, packer or distributor name and place of business, the quantity of contents if appropriate, the statement CAUTION Investigational device. Limited by Federal (or United States) law to investigational use, and labeling lists relevant contraindications, hazards, adverse effects, interfering substances or devices, warnings and precautions.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The label omits the manufacturer name or place of business, lacks the CAUTION investigational use statement, or fails to describe contraindications, hazards, adverse effects, interfering substances or devices, warnings and precautions.
baseRequirements.hint: List every required label element: manufacturer or packer or distributor name and place of business, quantity of contents if appropriate, the CAUTION investigational use statement, and all relevant contraindications, hazards, adverse effects, interfering substances or devices, warnings and precautions.

baseRequirements.title: Prohibited labeling statements
baseRequirements.need: Investigational device labeling must not bear any false or misleading statement and must not represent that the device is safe or effective for the purposes being investigated.

quote.text:
(b) Prohibitions. The labeling of an in-
vestigational device shall not bear any
statement that is false or misleading in
any particular and shall not represent
that the device is safe or effective for
the purposes for which it is being in-
vestigated.

baseRequirements.topic: claims made in the labeling of an investigational device
baseRequirements.complies: The labeling avoids any false or misleading statement and does not claim the device is safe or effective for the purposes under investigation.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The labeling claims the device is safe or effective for the investigated purpose, or makes a false or misleading statement about the device.
baseRequirements.hint: Keep labeling free of false or misleading statements and never state that the investigational device is safe or effective for the purposes being studied.

baseRequirements.title: Animal research labeling
baseRequirements.need: An investigational device shipped solely for research on or with laboratory animals must bear the statement: ''CAUTION—Device for investigational use in laboratory animals or other tests that do not involve human subjects.''

quote.text:
(c) Animal research. An investiga-
tional device shipped solely for re-
search on or with laboratory animals
shall bear on its label the following
statement: ‘‘CAUTION—Device for in-
vestigational use in laboratory animals
or other tests that do not involve
human subjects.’’

baseRequirements.topic: labeling of investigational devices shipped for research on or with laboratory animals
baseRequirements.complies: The device label carries the statement 'CAUTION—Device for investigational use in laboratory animals or other tests that do not involve human subjects.'
baseRequirements.conflicts: The label omits the caution statement, or the device is described as shipped for animal research without any investigational-use caution on its label.
baseRequirements.hint: Put the exact caution statement on the label of any device shipped solely for animal research.

baseRequirements.title: No promotion before approval
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor, investigator, or person acting on their behalf must not promote or test market an investigational device until after FDA has approved the device for commercial distribution.

quote.text:
A sponsor, investigator, or any per-
son acting for or on behalf of a sponsor
or investigator shall not:
(a) Promote or test market an inves-
tigational device, until after FDA has
approved the device for commercial
distribution.

baseRequirements.topic: promotion and test marketing of an investigational device before FDA approval
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that no promotion or test marketing occurs until after FDA has approved the device for commercial distribution.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text describes advertising, sales pitches, or test marketing of the investigational device before FDA approval for commercial distribution.
baseRequirements.hint: Say that all promotion and test marketing waits until FDA approves the device for commercial distribution.

baseRequirements.title: No excessive charging
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor, investigator, or person acting on their behalf must not commercialize an investigational device by charging subjects or investigators a price larger than necessary to recover costs of manufacture, research, development, and handling.

quote.text:
(b) Commercialize an investigational
device by charging the subjects or in-
vestigators for a device a price larger
than that necessary to recover costs of
manufacture, research, development,
and handling.

baseRequirements.topic: pricing charged to subjects or investigators for an investigational device
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that subjects or investigators are charged only a price that recovers costs of manufacture, research, development, and handling.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text describes charging subjects or investigators a price above cost recovery, or describes making a profit from the investigational device.
baseRequirements.hint: State that any charge to subjects or investigators is limited to recovering manufacture, research, development, and handling costs.

baseRequirements.title: No undue prolongation
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor, investigator, or person acting on their behalf must not unduly prolong an investigation, and must promptly terminate the investigation if data indicate premarket approval cannot be justified for a class III device or a class II device will not comply with a performance standard.

quote.text:
(c) Unduly prolong an investigation.
If data developed by the investigation
indicate in the case of a class III device
that premarket approval cannot be jus-
tified or in the case of a class II device
that it will not comply with an appli-
cable performance standard or an
amendment to that standard, the spon-
sor shall promptly terminate the inves-
tigation.

baseRequirements.topic: duration and termination of an investigation of an investigational device
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that the investigation is ended promptly when data show premarket approval cannot be justified for a class III device or that a class II device will not comply with a performance standard.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text describes keeping the investigation running despite data showing approval cannot be justified or a performance standard will not be met, or describes delaying termination.
baseRequirements.hint: Say the investigation is terminated promptly once data show approval cannot be justified or a performance standard will not be met.

baseRequirements.title: No safety or effectiveness claims
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor, investigator, or person acting on their behalf must not represent that an investigational device is safe or effective for the purposes for which it is being investigated.

quote.text:
(d) Represent that an investigational
device is safe or effective for the pur-
poses for which it is being investigated.

baseRequirements.topic: claims about the safety or effectiveness of an investigational device
baseRequirements.complies: The text describes the device as investigational and makes no statement that it is safe or effective for the purposes under investigation.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text claims or implies the investigational device is safe or effective for the purposes being investigated.
baseRequirements.hint: Avoid any statement that the investigational device is safe or effective for the purposes under study.

baseRequirements.title: Status report contents
baseRequirements.need: A person submitting status reports under a cease distribution and notification order or mandatory recall order must include the number of devices returned or corrected by each contact, effectiveness checks, and estimated completion timeframes.

quote.text:
(4) The number of devices returned or
corrected by each health professional,
device user facility, consignee, or indi-
vidual contacted, and the quantity of
products accounted for;
(5) The number and results of effec-
tiveness checks that have been made;
and
(6) Estimated timeframes for comple-
tion of the requirements of the cease
distribution and notification order or
mandatory recall order.

baseRequirements.topic: status reports under a cease distribution and notification order or mandatory recall order
baseRequirements.complies: The status report gives the number of devices returned or corrected by each health professional, device user facility, consignee, or individual contacted, the quantity of products accounted for, the number and results of effectiveness checks, and estimated timeframes for completing the order.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The status report leaves out returned or corrected device counts per contact, omits effectiveness checks or their results, or gives no estimated completion timeframes.
baseRequirements.hint: Include per-contact returned or corrected counts, products accounted for, effectiveness check numbers and results, and estimated completion timeframes.

baseRequirements.title: Discontinuing status reports
baseRequirements.need: The person named in a cease distribution and notification order or recall order may stop submitting status reports only when the agency terminates the order under § 810.17.

quote.text:
(c) The person named in the cease
distribution and notification order or
recall order may discontinue the sub-
mission of status reports when the
agency terminates the order in accord-
ance with § 810.17.

baseRequirements.topic: submitting status reports under a cease distribution and notification order or a recall order
baseRequirements.complies: The named person states that status reports will keep being submitted until the agency terminates the order under § 810.17, and only then stops.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The named person says they will stop sending status reports on their own schedule, or once they believe they have complied, without waiting for the agency to terminate the order.
baseRequirements.hint: Say status reports continue until FDA terminates the order under § 810.17, and that stopping is tied to that termination.

baseRequirements.title: Requesting order termination
baseRequirements.need: A person seeking termination of a cease distribution and notification order or mandatory recall order must submit a written request to FDA certifying full compliance, include the most current status report, and describe the disposition of the recalled device.

quote.text:
(a) The person named in a cease dis-
tribution and notification order issued
under § 810.10 or a mandatory recall
order issued under § 810.13 may request
termination of the order by submitting
a written request to FDA. The person
submitting a request shall certify that
he or she has complied in full with all
of the requirements of the order and
shall include a copy of the most cur-
rent status report submitted to the
agency under § 810.16. A request for ter-
mination of a recall order shall include
a description of the disposition of the
recalled device.

baseRequirements.topic: asking FDA to terminate a cease distribution and notification order or a mandatory recall order
baseRequirements.complies: The named person describes sending FDA a written request that certifies full compliance with all order requirements, attaches the most current status report, and for a recall order describes the disposition of the recalled device.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The named person asks for termination by phone or without certifying full compliance, omits the most current status report, or leaves out the disposition of the recalled device for a recall order.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe a written request to FDA that certifies full compliance, includes the most current status report, and for a recall order describes the disposition of the recalled device.

baseRequirements.title: FDA termination notification
baseRequirements.need: FDA will provide written notification when a request for termination of a cease distribution and notification order or mandatory recall order is granted or denied, responding within 30 working days of receipt.

quote.text:
(c) FDA will provide written notifica-
tion to the person named in the order
when a request for termination of a
cease distribution and notification
order or a mandatory recall order has
been granted or denied. FDA will re-
spond to a written request for termi-
nation of a cease distribution and noti-
fication or recall order within 30 work-
ing days of its receipt.

baseRequirements.topic: FDA's response to a request to terminate a cease distribution and notification order or a mandatory recall order
baseRequirements.complies: The text says FDA will send written notification of whether the termination request is granted or denied, and will respond within 30 working days of receiving the request.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says FDA may grant or deny a termination request without written notice, or that FDA has no set deadline for responding.
baseRequirements.hint: State that FDA notifies the named person in writing of a grant or denial and responds within 30 working days of receipt.

baseRequirements.title: Existence of IDE confidential
baseRequirements.need: FDA will not disclose the existence of an IDE unless it has already been publicly disclosed or acknowledged, until FDA approves a premarket approval application for the device or a notice of completion of a product development protocol becomes effective.

quote.text:
(a) Existence of IDE. FDA will not dis-
close the existence of an IDE unless its
existence has previously been publicly
disclosed or acknowledged, until FDA
approves an application for premarket
approval of the device subject to the
IDE; or a notice of completion of a
product development protocol for the
device has become effective.

baseRequirements.topic: public disclosure of the existence of an investigational device exemption (IDE)
baseRequirements.complies: The text says FDA will not disclose that an IDE exists unless it was already publicly disclosed or acknowledged, and that this holds until FDA approves a premarket approval application for the device or a notice of completion of a product development protocol becomes effective.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says FDA will confirm or reveal the existence of an IDE on request before any public disclosure and before premarket approval or an effective PDP completion notice.
baseRequirements.hint: Say FDA keeps the existence of an IDE undisclosed unless already public, until premarket approval or an effective PDP completion notice.

baseRequirements.title: Summary for banned device IDE
baseRequirements.need: FDA will make publicly available, on request, a detailed summary of safety and effectiveness information that was the basis for an order approving, disapproving, or withdrawing approval of an IDE for a banned device, including adverse health effects.

quote.text:
(b) Availability of summaries or data.

(1) FDA will make publicly available,
upon request, a detailed summary of
information concerning the safety and
effectiveness of the device that was the
basis for an order approving, dis-
approving, or withdrawing approval of
an application for an IDE for a banned
device. The summary shall include in-
formation on any adverse effect on
health caused by the device.

baseRequirements.topic: public access to safety and effectiveness summaries for an IDE of a banned device
baseRequirements.complies: The text says FDA will make publicly available, on request, a detailed summary of the safety and effectiveness information behind an order approving, disapproving, or withdrawing approval of an IDE for a banned device, including any adverse health effects caused by the device.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says no summary of the safety and effectiveness basis for such an order is released, or that a released summary leaves out adverse health effects.
baseRequirements.hint: State that FDA gives a detailed safety and effectiveness summary on request for a banned device IDE order, including adverse health effects.

baseRequirements.title: Data not disclosed before approval
baseRequirements.need: If a device is banned or the IDE's existence has been publicly disclosed, data in the file is not available for public disclosure before premarket approval or the effective date of a PDP completion notice, except as the section provides.

quote.text:
(2) If a device is a banned device or if
the existence of an IDE has been pub-
licly disclosed or acknowledged, data
or information contained in the file is
not available for public disclosure be-
fore approval of an application for pre-
market approval or the effective date
of a notice of completion of a product
development protocol except as pro-
vided in this section.

baseRequirements.topic: public disclosure of data in an IDE file for a banned device or a publicly disclosed IDE
baseRequirements.complies: The text says that for a banned device or an IDE whose existence has been publicly disclosed or acknowledged, file data is not available for public disclosure before premarket approval or the effective date of a PDP completion notice, except as the section provides.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says file data for a banned device or a publicly disclosed IDE is released to the public before premarket approval or an effective PDP completion notice.
baseRequirements.hint: Say file data stays non-public before premarket approval or an effective PDP completion notice, except as the section allows.

baseRequirements.title: Undisclosed IDE file data
baseRequirements.need: If the existence of an IDE file has not been publicly disclosed or acknowledged, no data or information in the file is available for public disclosure except as provided in paragraphs (b)(1) and (c).

quote.text:
(3) If the existence of an IDE file has
not been publicly disclosed or acknowl-
edged, no data or information in the
file are available for public disclosure
except as provided in paragraphs (b)(1)
and (c) of this section.

baseRequirements.topic: public disclosure of data and information in an investigational device exemption (IDE) file
baseRequirements.complies: The text says that while the existence of the IDE file has not been publicly disclosed or acknowledged, no data or information in the file is released to the public, except as allowed under paragraphs (b)(1) and (c).
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text releases or offers to release data or information from an IDE file whose existence has not been publicly disclosed or acknowledged, without limiting release to paragraphs (b)(1) and (c).
baseRequirements.hint: State that data in an undisclosed IDE file stays non-public and is only released under paragraphs (b)(1) and (c).

baseRequirements.title: Disclosure of adverse effect reports
baseRequirements.need: Upon request or on its own initiative, FDA shall disclose to an individual on whom an investigational device has been used a copy of a report of adverse device effects relating to that use.

quote.text:
(c) Reports of adverse effects. Upon re-
quest or on its own initiative, FDA
shall disclose to an individual on whom
an investigational device has been used
a copy of a report of adverse device ef-
fects relating to that use.

baseRequirements.topic: disclosure of adverse device effect reports to people on whom an investigational device was used
baseRequirements.complies: The text says FDA will give an individual on whom an investigational device was used a copy of the adverse device effect report relating to that use, either when the individual requests it or on FDA's own initiative.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says adverse device effect reports are never shared with the individual who was used on, or that such a person must sue or use another route to obtain the report.
baseRequirements.hint: Say FDA discloses the adverse effect report for that use to the individual on request or on its own initiative.

baseRequirements.title: Other disclosure rules
baseRequirements.need: Except as otherwise provided in § 812.38, the availability for public disclosure of data and information in an IDE file is handled in accordance with § 814.9.

quote.text:
(d) Other rules. Except as otherwise
provided in this section, the avail-
ability for public disclosure of data and
information in an IDE file shall be han-
dled in accordance with § 814.9.

baseRequirements.topic: public availability of data and information in an IDE file
baseRequirements.complies: The text says that, apart from the exceptions in § 812.38, public disclosure of data and information in an IDE file follows § 814.9.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text sets out its own separate disclosure scheme for IDE file data, or says § 814.9 does not apply to IDE files.
baseRequirements.hint: Point to § 814.9 as the governing rule for public disclosure of IDE file data except where § 812.38 says otherwise.

baseRequirements.title: Subject case history records
baseRequirements.need: Investigator records must include each subject's case history and exposure to the device, including consent documents, relevant observations and adverse device effects, and the date and time of each device use.

quote.text:
(3) Records of each subject’s case his-
tory and exposure to the device. Case
histories include the case report forms
and supporting data including, for ex-
ample, signed and dated consent forms
and medical records including, for ex-
ample, progress notes of the physician,
the individual’s hospital chart(s), and
the nurses’ notes.

baseRequirements.topic: investigator records of each subject's case history and exposure to the device
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the investigator keeps each subject's case history and device exposure records, including signed and dated consent forms, medical records such as physician progress notes, hospital charts and nurses' notes, relevant observations, adverse device effects, and the date and time of each device use.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the investigator keeps no case histories, omits consent forms or medical records, or does not record when the device was used or what adverse effects occurred.
baseRequirements.hint: List the subject case history records the investigator must keep, including consent forms, medical records, adverse effects and the date and time of each device use.

baseRequirements.title: Sponsor records
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must maintain accurate, complete, and current records of correspondence, shipment and disposition, signed investigator agreements with financial disclosure, non-significant risk device records, adverse device effects and complaints, and other records FDA requires.

quote.text:
(b) Sponsor records. A sponsor shall
maintain the following accurate, com-
plete, and current records relating to
an investigation:
(1) All correspondence with another
sponsor, a monitor, an investigator, an
IRB, or FDA, including required re-
ports.

baseRequirements.topic: sponsor records for an investigation of an investigational device
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the sponsor keeps accurate, complete and current records of correspondence with other sponsors, monitors, investigators, IRBs and FDA, plus shipment and disposition records, signed investigator agreements with financial disclosure, non-significant risk device records, adverse device effects and complaints, and other FDA-required records.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the sponsor keeps no correspondence records, discards shipment or disposition records, has no signed investigator agreements or financial disclosure, or does not track adverse device effects and complaints.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe the sponsor's records as accurate, complete and current, and name the categories: correspondence, shipment and disposition, signed investigator agreements with financial disclosure, non-significant risk records, adverse effects and complaints.

baseRequirements.title: Non-significant risk device records
baseRequirements.need: For each investigation of a non-significant risk device under § 812.2(b)(1), the sponsor must keep consolidated records of the device name and intended use, why it is not significant risk, investigator and IRB names and addresses, the extent of part 820 compliance, and other FDA-required information.

quote.text:
(4) For each investigation subject to
§ 812.2(b)(1) of a device other than a sig-
nificant risk device, the records de-
scribed in paragraph (b)(5) of this sec-
tion and the following records, consoli-
dated in one location and available for
FDA inspection and copying:
(i) The name and intended use of the
device and the objectives of the inves-
tigation;
(ii) A brief explanation of why the de-
vice is not a significant risk

baseRequirements.topic: sponsor records for investigations of non-significant risk devices
baseRequirements.complies: The text says that for each non-significant risk device investigation under § 812.2(b)(1), the sponsor keeps consolidated records in one location available for FDA inspection and copying, covering the device name and intended use, the investigation objectives, a brief explanation of why the device is not significant risk, investigator and IRB names and addresses, and the extent of part 820 compliance.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says non-significant risk device records are scattered, missing the explanation of why the device is not significant risk, or not available for FDA inspection and copying.
baseRequirements.hint: Say the sponsor consolidates the listed non-significant risk records in one location and makes them available for FDA inspection and copying.

baseRequirements.title: IRB records
baseRequirements.need: An IRB must maintain records in accordance with part 56.

quote.text:
(c) IRB records. An IRB shall main-
tain records in accordance with part 56
of this chapter.

baseRequirements.topic: record keeping by an institutional review board overseeing a device study
baseRequirements.complies: The IRB keeps written records of its reviews, decisions and correspondence, and files them following the record keeping procedures of part 56.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The IRB says it keeps no records of its reviews, or keeps only informal notes with no procedure for what is kept and how long it is held.
baseRequirements.hint: State that the IRB maintains its records in line with part 56 of the chapter.

baseRequirements.title: Record retention period
baseRequirements.need: An investigator or sponsor must maintain the required records during the investigation and for 2 years after the later of the date the investigation is terminated or completed or the date the records are no longer needed to support a premarket submission.

quote.text:
(d) Retention period. An investigator
or sponsor shall maintain the records
required by this subpart during the in-
vestigation and for a period of 2 years

after the latter of the following two

of completion of a product develop-
ment protocol, a humanitarian device
