notification submission, or a request
for De Novo classification.

baseRequirements.topic: how long study records are kept by an investigator or sponsor of a device investigation
baseRequirements.complies: Records are kept throughout the investigation and for 2 years after the later of the date the investigation is terminated or completed or the date the records are no longer needed to support a premarket submission.
baseRequirements.conflicts: Records are destroyed as soon as the investigation ends, or are kept for a fixed short period such as 6 months regardless of whether they are still needed for a premarket submission.
baseRequirements.hint: Name both trigger dates and say records are held for 2 years after whichever comes later.

baseRequirements.title: Transfer of records custody
baseRequirements.need: An investigator or sponsor may transfer custody of records to another person who accepts responsibility under this part, and must notify FDA of the transfer not later than 10 working days after it occurs.

quote.text:
(e) Records custody. An investigator
or sponsor may withdraw from the re-
sponsibility to maintain records for the
period required in paragraph (d) of this
section and transfer custody of the
records to any other person who will
accept responsibility for them under
this part, including the requirements
of § 812.145. Notice of a transfer shall be
given to FDA not later than 10 working
days after transfer occurs.

baseRequirements.topic: handing over custody of study records to another person
baseRequirements.complies: Custody is transferred to another person who accepts responsibility under this part, and FDA is notified of the transfer within 10 working days.
baseRequirements.conflicts: Records are handed to another party with no one accepting responsibility under this part, or the transfer happens with no notice to FDA or notice sent months later.
baseRequirements.hint: Say the receiving person accepts responsibility under this part and that FDA is notified no later than 10 working days after the transfer.

baseRequirements.title: Entry and inspection
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor or investigator with authority to grant access must permit authorized FDA employees, at reasonable times and in a reasonable manner, to enter and inspect any establishment where devices are held or records of device use are kept.

quote.text:
(a) Entry and inspection. A sponsor or
an investigator who has authority to
grant access shall permit authorized
FDA employees, at reasonable times
and in a reasonable manner, to enter
and inspect any establishment where
devices are held (including any estab-
lishment where devices are manufac-
tured, processed, packed, installed,
used, or implanted or where records of
results from use of devices are kept).

baseRequirements.topic: FDA employees entering and inspecting places where study devices are held or device use records are kept
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor or investigator lets authorized FDA employees enter and inspect those establishments at reasonable times and in a reasonable manner.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The sponsor or investigator refuses entry to FDA inspectors, or admits them only on conditions such as prior written approval or a warrant that the rule does not require.
baseRequirements.hint: State that authorized FDA employees are allowed to enter and inspect such establishments at reasonable times and in a reasonable manner.

baseRequirements.title: Records inspection
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor, IRB, or investigator, or anyone acting on their behalf, must permit authorized FDA employees, at reasonable times and in a reasonable manner, to inspect and copy all records relating to an investigation.

quote.text:
(b) Records inspection. A sponsor, IRB,
or investigator, or any other person
acting on behalf of such a person with
respect to an investigation, shall per-
mit authorized FDA employees, at rea-
sonable times and in a reasonable man-
ner, to inspect and copy all records re-
lating to an investigation.

baseRequirements.topic: FDA inspection and copying of records relating to a device investigation
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor, IRB, investigator and anyone acting for them allow authorized FDA employees to inspect and copy all records relating to the investigation at reasonable times and in a reasonable manner.
baseRequirements.conflicts: Records relating to the investigation are withheld from FDA inspectors, or copying is refused, or access is granted only to selected files.
baseRequirements.hint: Say that all records relating to the investigation may be inspected and copied by authorized FDA employees at reasonable times and in a reasonable manner.

baseRequirements.title: Inspection of subject-identifying records
baseRequirements.need: An investigator must permit authorized FDA employees to inspect and copy records that identify subjects upon notice that FDA suspects inadequate informed consent or missing, incomplete, inaccurate, false, or misleading required reports.

quote.text:
(c) Records identifying subjects. An in-
vestigator shall permit authorized FDA
employees to inspect and copy records
that identify subjects, upon notice that
FDA has reason to suspect that ade-
quate informed consent was not ob-
tained, or that reports required to be
submitted by the investigator to the
sponsor or IRB have not been sub-
mitted or are incomplete, inaccurate,
false, or misleading.

baseRequirements.topic: FDA access to records that identify study subjects
baseRequirements.complies: On notice that FDA suspects informed consent was not adequately obtained or that required reports were missing, incomplete, inaccurate, false or misleading, the investigator lets authorized FDA employees inspect and copy subject-identifying records.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The investigator refuses to show subject-identifying records after such a notice, or says such records will never be released to FDA under any circumstances.
baseRequirements.hint: State that subject-identifying records are opened to authorized FDA employees for inspection and copying once FDA gives notice of such a suspicion.

baseRequirements.title: Investigator reports
baseRequirements.need: An investigator must prepare and submit complete, accurate, and timely reports on unanticipated adverse device effects, withdrawal of IRB approval, progress, emergency deviations, informed consent exceptions, a final report, and other information on request.

quote.text:
(a) Investigator reports. An investi-
gator shall prepare and submit the fol-
lowing complete, accurate, and timely
reports:
(1) Unanticipated adverse device effects.

An investigator shall submit to the
sponsor and to the reviewing IRB a re-
port of any unanticipated adverse de-
vice effect occurring during an inves-
tigation as soon as possible, but in no
event later than 10 working days after
the investigator first learns of the ef-
fect.

baseRequirements.topic: an investigator reporting on a medical device clinical investigation
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the investigator writes and sends reports on unanticipated adverse device effects, IRB approval withdrawal, progress, emergency deviations, informed consent exceptions, a final report and other requested information, and that the adverse effect report goes to the sponsor and reviewing IRB as soon as possible and no later than 10 working days after first learning of it.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the investigator waits weeks or months before reporting an unanticipated adverse device effect, reports it only to the sponsor and not the IRB, or leaves out required reports such as progress, deviations, consent exceptions or the final report.
baseRequirements.hint: State that each required report is complete, accurate and timely, and that unanticipated adverse device effects reach the sponsor and reviewing IRB within 10 working days of first learning of them.

baseRequirements.title: Reporting IRB approval withdrawal
baseRequirements.need: An investigator must report to the sponsor, within 5 working days, a withdrawal of approval by the reviewing IRB of the investigator's part of an investigation.

quote.text:
(2) Withdrawal of IRB approval. An in-
vestigator shall report to the sponsor,
within 5 working days, a withdrawal of
approval by the reviewing IRB of the
investigator’s part of an investigation.

baseRequirements.topic: an investigator reporting that an IRB has withdrawn approval of the investigator's part of a device investigation
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the investigator reports the IRB's withdrawal of approval of the investigator's part of the investigation to the sponsor within 5 working days.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the investigator delays telling the sponsor about the IRB approval withdrawal beyond 5 working days, or reports it only to the IRB or to others and not to the sponsor.
baseRequirements.hint: Say the investigator notifies the sponsor of the IRB approval withdrawal within 5 working days.

baseRequirements.title: Investigator progress reports
baseRequirements.need: An investigator must submit progress reports on the investigation to the sponsor, the monitor, and the reviewing IRB at regular intervals, but no less often than yearly.

quote.text:
(3) Progress. An investigator shall
submit progress reports on the inves-
tigation to the sponsor, the monitor,
and the reviewing IRB at regular inter-
vals, but in no event less often than
yearly.

baseRequirements.topic: an investigator sending progress reports on a device investigation
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the investigator submits progress reports at regular intervals, at least once a year, to the sponsor, the monitor and the reviewing IRB.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says progress reports go only to the sponsor, are sent less often than yearly, or are not sent at all.
baseRequirements.hint: State that progress reports go to the sponsor, monitor and reviewing IRB at regular intervals and no less often than yearly.

baseRequirements.title: Reporting emergency deviations
baseRequirements.need: An investigator must notify the sponsor and reviewing IRB of any emergency deviation from the investigational plan as soon as possible and no later than 5 working days after the emergency; otherwise prior sponsor approval and, if it may affect scientific soundness or subject rights, FDA and IRB approval are required.

quote.text:
(4) Deviations from the investigational
plan. An investigator shall notify the
sponsor and the reviewing IRB (see
§ 56.108(a) (3) and (4)) of any deviation
from the investigational plan to pro-
tect the life or physical well-being of a
subject in an emergency. Such notice
shall be given as soon as possible, but
in no event later than 5 working days
after the emergency occurred.

baseRequirements.topic: an investigator handling a deviation from the investigational plan made in an emergency to protect a subject
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the investigator notifies the sponsor and the reviewing IRB of the emergency deviation as soon as possible and no later than 5 working days after the emergency, and that any other deviation is made only with prior sponsor approval and, where it may affect scientific soundness or subject rights, FDA and IRB approval.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the investigator makes deviations without telling the sponsor or IRB, or reports an emergency deviation later than 5 working days after the emergency.
baseRequirements.hint: Say emergency deviations are reported to the sponsor and reviewing IRB as soon as possible and within 5 working days, and that other deviations need prior approvals.

baseRequirements.title: Reporting use without informed consent
baseRequirements.need: If an investigator uses a device without obtaining informed consent, the investigator must report the use to the sponsor and the reviewing IRB within 5 working days after the use occurs.

quote.text:
(5) Informed consent. If an investi-
gator uses a device without obtaining
informed consent, the investigator
shall report such use to the sponsor
and the reviewing IRB within 5 work-
ing days after the use occurs.

baseRequirements.topic: an investigator using a device on a subject without obtaining informed consent
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the investigator reports the use of the device without informed consent to the sponsor and the reviewing IRB within 5 working days after the use occurs.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the investigator does not report the consent-free device use, or reports it later than 5 working days after it occurred, or tells only one of the sponsor and the reviewing IRB.
baseRequirements.hint: State that any device use without informed consent is reported to both the sponsor and the reviewing IRB within 5 working days.

baseRequirements.title: Investigator final report
baseRequirements.need: An investigator must submit a final report to the sponsor and the reviewing IRB within 3 months after termination or completion of the investigation or the investigator's part of it.

quote.text:
(6) Final report. An investigator shall,
within 3 months after termination or
completion of the investigation or the
investigator’s part of the investigation,
submit a final report to the sponsor
and the reviewing IRB.

baseRequirements.topic: an investigator closing out a device investigation with a final report
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the investigator submits a final report to the sponsor and the reviewing IRB within 3 months after the investigation or the investigator's part of it is terminated or completed.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says no final report is sent, it goes only to the sponsor, or it is submitted more than 3 months after termination or completion.
baseRequirements.hint: Say the final report goes to the sponsor and reviewing IRB within 3 months of termination or completion.

baseRequirements.title: Sponsor reports
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must prepare and submit complete, accurate, and timely reports on unanticipated adverse device effects, IRB and FDA approval withdrawals, investigator lists, progress, recall and device disposition, final reports, informed consent exceptions, significant risk determinations, and other information on request.

quote.text:
(b) Sponsor reports. A sponsor shall
prepare and submit the following com-
plete, accurate, and timely reports:
(1) Unanticipated adverse device effects.

A sponsor who conducts an evaluation
of an unanticipated adverse device ef-
fect under § 812.46(b) shall report the re-
sults of such evaluation to FDA and to
all reviewing IRB’s and participating
investigators within 10 working days
after the sponsor first receives notice
of the effect.

baseRequirements.topic: sponsor reporting of unanticipated adverse device effects and other required study information to FDA, IRBs and investigators
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor writes and sends complete, accurate reports of unanticipated adverse device effects to FDA, all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators within 10 working days of first learning of the effect, and keeps other required reports on schedule.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The sponsor waits weeks or months before telling FDA and IRBs about an unanticipated adverse device effect, leaves out details, or never reports it at all.
baseRequirements.hint: State that each unanticipated adverse device effect is reported to FDA, every reviewing IRB and participating investigators within 10 working days of first notice, with complete and accurate content.

baseRequirements.title: Reporting IRB approval withdrawal
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must notify FDA and all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators of any withdrawal of approval of an investigation or part of it by a reviewing IRB within 5 working days after receiving the withdrawal.

quote.text:
(2) Withdrawal of IRB approval. A
sponsor shall notify FDA and all re-
viewing IRB’s and participating inves-
tigators of any withdrawal of approval
of an investigation or a part of an in-
vestigation by a reviewing IRB within
5 working days after receipt of the
withdrawal of approval.

baseRequirements.topic: withdrawal of IRB approval of an investigation
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor notifies FDA, all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators of the IRB approval withdrawal within 5 working days of receiving it.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The sponsor learns an IRB has withdrawn approval and tells only the study staff, or notifies FDA and investigators later than 5 working days after receiving the withdrawal.
baseRequirements.hint: Say the sponsor tells FDA, all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators of any IRB approval withdrawal within 5 working days of receiving it.

baseRequirements.title: Reporting FDA approval withdrawal
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must notify all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators of any withdrawal of FDA approval of the investigation within 5 working days after receiving notice of the withdrawal.

quote.text:
(3) Withdrawal of FDA approval. A
sponsor shall notify all reviewing IRB’s
and participating investigators of any
withdrawal of FDA approval of the in-
vestigation, and shall do so within 5
working days after receipt of notice of
the withdrawal of approval.

baseRequirements.topic: withdrawal of FDA approval of an investigation
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor notifies all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators of the FDA approval withdrawal within 5 working days of receiving notice of it.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The sponsor receives notice that FDA withdrew approval and delays notifying IRBs and investigators beyond 5 working days, or notifies no one.
baseRequirements.hint: Say the sponsor notifies all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators of any FDA approval withdrawal within 5 working days of receiving notice.

baseRequirements.title: Current investigator list
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must submit to FDA, at 6-month intervals, a current list of names and addresses of all investigators participating in the investigation, with the first list due 6 months after FDA approval.

quote.text:
(4) Current investigator list. A sponsor
shall submit to FDA, at 6-month inter-
vals, a current list of the names and
addresses of all investigators partici-
pating in the investigation. The spon-
sor shall submit the first such list 6
months after FDA approval.

baseRequirements.topic: submission of the list of participating investigators to FDA
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor sends FDA a current list of the names and addresses of all participating investigators every 6 months, with the first list sent 6 months after FDA approval.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The sponsor never sends FDA an investigator list, sends it only once, or sends it at intervals other than every 6 months starting 6 months after approval.
baseRequirements.hint: State that a current list of names and addresses of all participating investigators goes to FDA every 6 months, the first one 6 months after FDA approval.

baseRequirements.title: Sponsor progress reports
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must submit progress reports to all reviewing IRBs at least yearly and, for a significant risk device, also to FDA; a treatment IDE sponsor must submit semi-annual reports to IRBs and FDA and annual reports under this section.

quote.text:
(5) Progress reports. At regular inter-
vals, and at least yearly, a sponsor
shall submit progress reports to all re-
viewing IRB’s. In the case of a signifi-
cant risk device, a sponsor shall also
submit progress reports to FDA. A
sponsor of a treatment IDE shall sub-
mit semi-annual progress reports to all
reviewing IRB’s and FDA in accordance
with § 812.36(f) and annual reports in ac-
cordance with this section.

baseRequirements.topic: progress reports on an investigation sent to IRBs and FDA
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor sends progress reports to all reviewing IRBs at least once a year, also sends them to FDA for a significant risk device, and a treatment IDE sponsor sends semi-annual reports to IRBs and FDA plus annual reports.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The sponsor sends progress reports less than yearly, skips FDA for a significant risk device, or a treatment IDE sponsor files no semi-annual reports.
baseRequirements.hint: Say progress reports go to all reviewing IRBs at least yearly, to FDA as well for a significant risk device, and that a treatment IDE sponsor files semi-annual and annual reports.

baseRequirements.title: Recall and device disposition notice
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must notify FDA and all reviewing IRBs of any request that an investigator return, repair, or otherwise dispose of device units within 30 working days after the request and state why the request was made.

quote.text:
(6) Recall and device disposition. A
sponsor shall notify FDA and all re-
viewing IRB’s of any request that an
investigator return, repair, or other-
wise dispose of any units of a device.
Such notice shall occur within 30 work-
ing days after the request is made and
shall state why the request was made.

baseRequirements.topic: requests that an investigator return, repair or dispose of device units
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor notifies FDA and all reviewing IRBs within 30 working days of asking an investigator to return, repair or otherwise dispose of device units, and the notice states why the request was made.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The sponsor asks an investigator to return or dispose of devices but does not tell FDA or the IRBs, tells them more than 30 working days later, or gives no reason for the request.
baseRequirements.hint: State that any request to return, repair or dispose of device units is reported to FDA and all reviewing IRBs within 30 working days, with the reason for the request included.

baseRequirements.title: Sponsor final report
baseRequirements.need: For a significant risk device, the sponsor must notify FDA within 30 working days of completion or termination and submit a final report to FDA, all reviewing IRBs, and participating investigators within 6 months; for a non-significant risk device, a final report goes to all reviewing IRBs within 6 months.

quote.text:
(7) Final report. In the case of a sig-
nificant risk device, the sponsor shall
notify FDA within 30 working days of
the completion or termination of the
investigation and shall submit a final
report to FDA and all reviewing the
IRB’s and participating investigators
within 6 months after completion or
termination. In the case of a device
that is not a significant risk device,
the sponsor shall submit a final report
to all reviewing IRB’s within 6 months
after termination or completion.

baseRequirements.topic: closing out a device clinical investigation and sending final reports to FDA, IRBs and investigators
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the sponsor notified FDA within 30 working days of completion or termination of a significant risk device investigation and sent a final report to FDA, all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators within 6 months; for a non-significant risk device it says a final report went to all reviewing IRBs within 6 months.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says no final report is sent, or that reports go only to the sponsor's own files, or that notification to FDA comes months after completion, or that a non-significant risk device final report is sent to FDA instead of to the reviewing IRBs.
baseRequirements.hint: State who receives the final report and the deadline: FDA plus reviewing IRBs plus investigators within 6 months for significant risk devices, with FDA notification within 30 working days, and reviewing IRBs only within 6 months for non-significant risk devices.

baseRequirements.title: Reporting use without informed consent
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must submit to FDA a copy of any investigator report of use of a device without obtaining informed consent within 5 working days of receiving notice of the use.

quote.text:
(8) Informed consent. A sponsor shall
submit to FDA a copy of any report by
an investigator under paragraph (a)(5)
of this section of use of a device with-
out obtaining informed consent, within
5 working days of receipt of notice of
such use.

baseRequirements.topic: a sponsor passing to FDA an investigator's report of device use without informed consent
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the sponsor received notice that a device was used without informed consent and submitted a copy of the investigator's report to FDA within 5 working days of that notice.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the sponsor learned of a use without informed consent but did not send the investigator's report to FDA, or sent it weeks or months later, or sent it only to the IRB.
baseRequirements.hint: Say the sponsor forwarded a copy of the investigator's report of the consent-free use to FDA within 5 working days of receiving notice.

baseRequirements.title: Reporting significant risk determination
baseRequirements.need: If an IRB determines a device is a significant risk device and the sponsor had proposed it was not, the sponsor must submit a report of the IRB's determination to FDA within 5 working days after first learning of it.

quote.text:
(9) Significant risk device determina-
tions. If an IRB determines that a de-
vice is a significant risk device, and
the sponsor had proposed that the IRB
consider the device not to be a signifi-
cant risk device, the sponsor shall sub-
mit to FDA a report of the IRB’s deter-
mination within 5 working days after
the sponsor first learns of the IRB’s de-
termination.

baseRequirements.topic: an IRB deciding a device is significant risk after the sponsor proposed it was not
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the IRB determined the device was a significant risk device although the sponsor had proposed it was not, and the sponsor submitted a report of that determination to FDA within 5 working days of first learning of it.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the sponsor learned the IRB had overruled its non-significant risk proposal but did not report the determination to FDA, or reported it later than 5 working days, or reported it only to the IRB.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe the sponsor sending FDA a report of the IRB's significant risk determination within 5 working days of first learning of it.

baseRequirements.title: Information on request
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must, upon request by a reviewing IRB or FDA, provide accurate, complete, and current information about any aspect of the investigation.

quote.text:
(10) Other. A sponsor shall, upon re-
quest by a reviewing IRB or FDA, pro-
vide accurate, complete, and current
information about any aspect of the in-
vestigation.

baseRequirements.topic: a sponsor answering requests from a reviewing IRB or FDA about a device investigation
baseRequirements.complies: The text says that when a reviewing IRB or FDA asked about an aspect of the investigation, the sponsor provided information that was accurate, complete and current.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the sponsor refused or ignored an IRB or FDA request for information, or supplied outdated, partial or inaccurate information about the investigation.
baseRequirements.hint: Show the sponsor responding to an IRB or FDA request with information that is accurate, complete and current.

baseRequirements.title: Unanticipated adverse effect reports
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor who conducts an evaluation of an unanticipated adverse device effect must report the results to FDA and to all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators within 10 working days after first receiving notice of the effect, and submit additional reports as FDA requests.

quote.text:
A sponsor who conducts an evaluation

investigators within 10 working days

of the effect. Thereafter the sponsor

baseRequirements.topic: evaluating and reporting an unanticipated adverse device effect
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the sponsor evaluated an unanticipated adverse device effect and reported the results to FDA, all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators within 10 working days of first receiving notice, and sent further reports as FDA requested.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the sponsor received notice of an unanticipated adverse device effect but reported the evaluation results late, only to some parties, or not at all, or ignored FDA requests for additional reports.
baseRequirements.hint: State that the evaluation results went to FDA, all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators within 10 working days of first notice, with additional reports as FDA asks.

baseRequirements.title: IRB approval withdrawal notice
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must notify FDA and all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators of any withdrawal of approval of an investigation or part of an investigation by a reviewing IRB within 5 working days after receipt of the withdrawal.

quote.text:
Withdrawal of IRB approval. A

of an investigation or a part of an in-
vestigation by a reviewing IRB within
5 working days after receipt of the
withdrawal of approval.

baseRequirements.topic: a reviewing IRB withdrawing approval of a device investigation
baseRequirements.complies: The text says a reviewing IRB withdrew approval of the investigation or part of it and the sponsor notified FDA, all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators within 5 working days of receiving the withdrawal.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the sponsor received an IRB withdrawal of approval but did not notify FDA or the other parties, or notified them later than 5 working days, or told only the IRB.
baseRequirements.hint: Say the sponsor notified FDA, all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators within 5 working days after receiving the withdrawal of approval.

baseRequirements.title: FDA approval withdrawal notice
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must notify all reviewing IRBs and participating investigators of any withdrawal of FDA approval of the investigation within 5 working days after receipt of notice of the withdrawal.

quote.text:
Withdrawal of FDA approval. A

baseRequirements.topic: withdrawal of FDA approval of an investigation and telling the study sites about it
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor states that when it receives notice that FDA approval of the investigation is withdrawn, it notifies all reviewing IRBs and all participating investigators within 5 working days of receiving that notice.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The sponsor says it will inform IRBs and investigators of an FDA approval withdrawal only at the next scheduled meeting, or says it will notify FDA but not the IRBs and investigators, or gives no time limit or a limit longer than 5 working days.
baseRequirements.hint: State that every reviewing IRB and every participating investigator is told of an FDA approval withdrawal within 5 working days after the sponsor receives the notice.

baseRequirements.title: Current investigator list
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must submit to FDA, at 6-month intervals, a current list of the names and addresses of all investigators participating in the investigation, with the first list submitted 6 months after FDA approval.

vals, a current list of the names and

pating in the investigation. The spon-
sor shall submit the first such list 6
months after FDA approval.

baseRequirements.topic: periodic reporting to FDA of who is conducting the investigation
baseRequirements.complies: The sponsor states it sends FDA a current list of the names and addresses of all participating investigators every 6 months, with the first list sent 6 months after FDA approval.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The sponsor says it will send the investigator list only once, or only when investigators change, or at intervals other than 6 months, or says it will keep the list internally without sending it to FDA.
baseRequirements.hint: State that a current list of all investigators' names and addresses goes to FDA every 6 months, starting 6 months after FDA approval.

baseRequirements.title: Progress reports
baseRequirements.need: A sponsor must submit progress reports to all reviewing IRBs at regular intervals and at least yearly, to FDA as well for a significant risk device, and semi-annual progress reports to all reviewing IRBs and FDA for a treatment IDE.

quote.text:
Progress reports. At regular inter-
