ciate must comply with the applicable
standards, implementation specifica-
tions, and requirements of this subpart
with respect to electronic protected
health information of a covered entity.

baseRequirements.topic: application of the HIPAA security standards to electronic health information
baseRequirements.complies: The entity states that it applies the security subpart's standards, implementation specifications and requirements to all electronic protected health information it handles as a covered entity or business associate.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The entity says the security subpart does not apply to its electronic protected health information, or applies only some of its standards and implementation specifications.
baseRequirements.hint: Say plainly that the security subpart's standards, implementation specifications and requirements apply to the electronic protected health information involved.

baseRequirements.title: General security requirements
baseRequirements.need: Covered entities and business associates must ensure confidentiality, integrity and availability of electronic protected health information, protect against anticipated threats and impermissible uses or disclosures, and ensure workforce compliance.

quote.text:
(a) General requirements. Covered enti-
ties and business associates must do
the following:
(1) Ensure the confidentiality, integ-
rity, and availability of all electronic
protected health information the cov-
ered entity or business associate cre-
ates, receives, maintains, or transmits.
(2) Protect against any reasonably
anticipated threats or hazards to the
security or integrity of such informa-
tion.

baseRequirements.topic: protecting the confidentiality, integrity and availability of electronic health information
baseRequirements.complies: The entity states that it keeps electronic protected health information confidential, unaltered and available when needed, guards against reasonably anticipated threats and hazards, and requires its workforce to follow these protections.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The entity leaves electronic protected health information open to unauthorized viewing or change, has no safeguards against anticipated threats, or does not require workforce members to follow security rules.
baseRequirements.hint: Cover all three goals (confidentiality, integrity, availability), protection against anticipated threats, and workforce compliance.

baseRequirements.title: Choosing security measures
baseRequirements.need: Covered entities and business associates may use any security measures that reasonably and appropriately implement the standards, but must consider size, complexity, capabilities, technical infrastructure, costs, and the probability and criticality of risks.

quote.text:
(1) Covered
entities and business associates may
use any security measures that allow
the covered entity or business asso-
ciate to reasonably and appropriately
implement the standards and imple-
mentation specifications as specified in
this subpart.
(2) In deciding which security meas-
ures to use, a covered entity or busi-
ness associate must take into account
the following factors:

baseRequirements.topic: selecting security measures for electronic health information
baseRequirements.complies: The entity says it may choose any security measures that reasonably and appropriately implement the standards, and that its choice weighs its size, complexity, capabilities, technical infrastructure, costs, and the probability and criticality of risks.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The entity picks security measures without regard to whether they implement the standards, or decides on measures without considering its size, complexity, capabilities, infrastructure, costs, or the likelihood and seriousness of risks.
baseRequirements.hint: State that any measures may be used if they reasonably and appropriately implement the standards, and list the factors weighed: size, complexity, capabilities, infrastructure, cost, and risk probability and criticality.

baseRequirements.title: Required and addressable specifications
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must implement required implementation specifications, and for addressable ones must assess reasonableness, implement them if appropriate, or document why not and implement an equivalent alternative.

quote.text:
(2) When a standard adopted in
§ 164.308, § 164.310, § 164.312, § 164.314, or
§ 164.316 includes required implementa-
tion specifications, a covered entity or
business associate must implement the
implementation specifications.

baseRequirements.topic: implementing required and addressable security implementation specifications
baseRequirements.complies: The entity states that it implements every required implementation specification, and for addressable ones it assesses whether each is reasonable and appropriate, implements it when it is, or documents why not and puts an equivalent alternative in place.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The entity skips required implementation specifications, or ignores addressable ones without assessing them, documenting the reason, or adopting an equivalent alternative.
baseRequirements.hint: Say required specifications are always implemented, and addressable ones are either implemented or documented as not reasonable and appropriate with an equivalent alternative in place.

baseRequirements.title: Maintaining security measures
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must review and modify its security measures as needed and update the documentation of those measures under § 164.316(b)(2)(iii).

quote.text:
A covered entity or
business associate must review and
modify the security measures imple-
mented under this subpart as needed to
continue provision of reasonable and
appropriate protection of electronic
protected health information, and up-
date documentation of such security
measures in accordance with
§ 164.316(b)(2)(iii).

baseRequirements.topic: reviewing and updating an organization's security measures and the written documentation of those measures for protecting electronic health information
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that security measures are reviewed on a set schedule and after changes, modified when gaps are found, and that the written documentation of those measures is updated to match each change.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says security measures were set once at launch and never revisited, or that changes were made to safeguards but the written documentation was left as it was.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe a recurring review of security measures, changes made when needed, and the matching update of the written documentation.

baseRequirements.title: Security management process
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must conduct a risk analysis, implement risk management, apply sanctions for noncompliance, and regularly review information system activity records.

quote.text:
(A) Risk analysis (Required). Conduct
an accurate and thorough assessment
of the potential risks and
vulnerabilities to the confidentiality,
integrity, and availability of electronic
protected health information held by
the covered entity or business asso-
ciate.
(B) Risk management (Required). Im-
plement security measures sufficient
to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a
reasonable and appropriate level to
comply with § 164.306(a).

baseRequirements.topic: assessing and managing risks to the confidentiality, integrity and availability of electronic health information, and reviewing system activity
baseRequirements.complies: The text describes a documented risk analysis of threats and vulnerabilities to electronic health information, security measures chosen to reduce those risks to a reasonable and appropriate level, sanctions applied to workforce members who break the rules, and regular review of information system activity records.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says no risk analysis was ever done, that identified risks were left unaddressed, that staff who violate policy face no consequences, or that system activity logs are never reviewed.
baseRequirements.hint: Cover four things: a thorough risk analysis, measures that reduce the identified risks, sanctions for noncompliance, and regular review of system activity records.

baseRequirements.title: Assigned security responsibility
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must identify the security official responsible for developing and implementing the policies and procedures required by the security subpart.

quote.text:
Standard: Assigned security respon-
sibility. Identify the security official
who is responsible for the development
and implementation of the policies and
procedures required by this subpart for
the covered entity or business asso-
ciate.

baseRequirements.topic: naming the person in charge of an organization's health information security policies and procedures
baseRequirements.complies: The text names a specific security official, by role or name, who is responsible for developing and implementing the security policies and procedures.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says no one has been assigned security responsibility, that security duties are shared informally with no named owner, or that the responsible person is unnamed and undefined.
baseRequirements.hint: Identify a named security official and state that this person develops and implements the security policies and procedures.

baseRequirements.title: Workforce security
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must implement policies and procedures ensuring appropriate workforce access to electronic protected health information and preventing access by those not authorized.

quote.text:
(i) Standard: Workforce security. Im-
plement policies and procedures to en-
sure that all members of its workforce
have appropriate access to electronic
protected health information, as pro-
vided under paragraph (a)(4) of this sec-
tion, and to prevent those workforce
members who do not have access under
paragraph (a)(4) of this section from
obtaining access to electronic pro-
tected health information.

baseRequirements.topic: controlling which workforce members can get at electronic health information
baseRequirements.complies: The text describes written policies and procedures that give each workforce member the access their job requires and block access for workforce members who are not authorized.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says any employee can look at any patient record, that access is granted without regard to job role, or that there are no procedures to stop unauthorized staff from getting access.
baseRequirements.hint: State that policies and procedures grant access based on job role and prevent unauthorized workforce members from obtaining access.

baseRequirements.title: Information access management
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must implement policies and procedures for authorizing access to electronic protected health information consistent with subpart E, and a clearinghouse within a larger organization must protect its information from unauthorized access.

quote.text:
(i) Standard: Information access
management. Implement policies and
procedures for authorizing access to
electronic protected health informa-
tion that are consistent with the appli-
cable requirements of subpart E of this
part.
(ii) Implementation specifications:

(A) Isolating health care clearinghouse
functions (Required). If a health care
clearinghouse is part of a larger orga-
nization, the clearinghouse must im-
plement policies and procedures that
protect the electronic protected health
information of the clearinghouse from
unauthorized access by the larger orga-
nization.

baseRequirements.topic: authorizing access to electronic health information, including protecting a clearinghouse's information inside a larger organization
baseRequirements.complies: The text describes policies and procedures for authorizing access to electronic health information that follow the applicable subpart E requirements, and, where a clearinghouse sits inside a larger organization, measures that keep the larger organization from reaching the clearinghouse's information without authorization.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says access is granted with no authorization procedures, that authorization rules ignore subpart E, or that the parent organization can freely read the clearinghouse's health information.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe authorization policies consistent with subpart E and, if a clearinghouse is inside a larger organization, the steps that block the larger organization's unauthorized access.

baseRequirements.title: Security awareness and training
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must implement a security awareness and training program for all workforce members, including management.

quote.text:
(i) Standard: Security awareness and
training. Implement a security aware-
ness and training program for all mem-
bers of its workforce (including man-
agement).

baseRequirements.topic: security awareness and training for an organization's workforce
baseRequirements.complies: The text describes a security awareness and training program that reaches every workforce member, management included, and says how often it runs.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says training is offered only to some staff, that management is exempt, or that no security awareness or training program exists.
baseRequirements.hint: State that a security awareness and training program covers all workforce members, including management.

baseRequirements.title: Security incident procedures
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must implement policies and procedures to identify, respond to, mitigate and document security incidents and their outcomes.

quote.text:
(i) Standard: Security incident proce-
dures. Implement policies and proce-
dures to address security incidents.
(ii) Implementation specification: Re-
sponse and reporting (Required). Identify
and respond to suspected or known se-
curity incidents; mitigate, to the ex-
tent practicable, harmful effects of se-
curity incidents that are known to the
covered entity or business associate;
and document security incidents and
their outcomes.

baseRequirements.topic: handling of security incidents involving electronic health information
baseRequirements.complies: The text describes written procedures for spotting suspected or known security incidents, a defined way to respond and report them, steps taken to reduce their harmful effects where feasible, and records kept of each incident and how it was resolved.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says incidents are handled informally with no written procedure, that suspected breaches are not tracked or reported, that nothing is done to reduce harm after an incident, or that incidents and their outcomes are never documented.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe written steps for identifying, responding to, mitigating and documenting security incidents and their outcomes.

baseRequirements.title: Contingency plan
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must establish and implement contingency policies and procedures, including a data backup plan, disaster recovery plan and emergency mode operation plan.

quote.text:
(i) Standard: Contingency plan. Es-
tablish (and implement as needed) poli-
cies and procedures for responding to
an emergency or other occurrence (for
example, fire, vandalism, system fail-
ure, and natural disaster) that damages
systems that contain electronic pro-
tected health information.

baseRequirements.topic: planning for emergencies and disasters that damage systems holding electronic health information
baseRequirements.complies: The text describes written contingency policies and procedures covering a data backup plan, a disaster recovery plan and an emergency mode operation plan for events such as fire, vandalism, system failure or natural disaster.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says there is no backup plan, no disaster recovery plan or no emergency mode operation plan, or that no procedures exist for responding when systems holding electronic health information are damaged.
baseRequirements.hint: State that written contingency procedures exist and name the data backup, disaster recovery and emergency mode operation plans.

baseRequirements.title: Periodic security evaluation
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must perform a periodic technical and nontechnical evaluation of how its security policies and procedures meet the requirements of the security subpart.

quote.text:
Standard: Evaluation. Perform a
periodic technical and nontechnical
evaluation, based initially upon the
standards implemented under this rule
and, subsequently, in response to envi-
ronmental or operational changes af-
fecting the security of electronic pro-
tected health information, that estab-
lishes the extent to which a covered en-
tity’s or business associate’s security
policies and procedures meet the re-
quirements of this subpart.

baseRequirements.topic: periodic review of security policies and procedures for electronic health information
baseRequirements.complies: The text describes a scheduled technical and nontechnical evaluation of security policies and procedures against the security rule requirements, repeated periodically and rerun when environmental or operational changes affect security.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says security policies and procedures are never evaluated, that only a one-time review was done with no repeat, or that no review is triggered when operations or the environment change.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe a periodic technical and nontechnical evaluation, repeated after environmental or operational changes, of how the policies meet the security rule.

baseRequirements.title: Business associate assurances
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity may let a business associate handle electronic protected health information only with satisfactory assurances under § 164.314(a), and a business associate must obtain the same assurances from subcontractors, documented in a written contract.

quote.text:
(1) Business associate contracts and
other arrangements. A covered entity
may permit a business associate to cre-
ate, receive, maintain, or transmit
electronic protected health informa-
tion on the covered entity’s behalf only
if the covered entity obtains satisfac-
tory assurances, in accordance with
§ 164.314(a), that the business associate
will appropriately safeguard the infor-
mation.

baseRequirements.topic: letting business associates and subcontractors handle electronic health information
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that a business associate may handle electronic health information only after satisfactory written assurances of safeguarding under § 164.314(a), and that subcontractors must give the same written assurances in a contract.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says business associates or subcontractors can access electronic health information with no written contract, or that assurances of safeguarding are not required or not documented.
baseRequirements.hint: Say that written satisfactory assurances under § 164.314(a) are obtained from business associates and passed down to subcontractors before any handling of the information.

baseRequirements.title: Facility access controls
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must implement policies and procedures limiting physical access to its electronic information systems and facilities while allowing properly authorized access.

quote.text:
(a)(1) Standard: Facility access con-
trols. Implement policies and proce-
dures to limit physical access to its
electronic information systems and the
facility or facilities in which they are
housed, while ensuring that properly
authorized access is allowed.

baseRequirements.topic: physical access to facilities and systems holding electronic health information
baseRequirements.complies: The text describes written policies and procedures that limit physical entry to the systems and the buildings housing them, while allowing entry to people who are properly authorized.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says anyone can walk into the facility or reach the systems without restriction, or that authorized staff are blocked from access they should have.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe written procedures that restrict physical entry to the systems and their facilities while permitting properly authorized access.

baseRequirements.title: Workstation use
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must implement policies and procedures specifying the proper functions, manner of performance and physical surroundings of workstations that can access electronic protected health information.

quote.text:
Standard: Workstation use. Imple-
ment policies and procedures that
specify the proper functions to be per-
formed, the manner in which those
functions are to be performed, and the
physical attributes of the surroundings
of a specific workstation or class of
workstation that can access electronic
protected health information.

baseRequirements.topic: use and surroundings of workstations that access electronic health information
baseRequirements.complies: The text describes written policies and procedures stating which functions may be performed at workstations that access electronic health information, how those functions are carried out, and the physical attributes of their surroundings.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says nothing is specified about what workstations may be used for, how they are used, or where they are placed, or that any workstation anywhere may access the information with no rules.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe written rules naming the allowed functions, the manner of performing them and the physical surroundings for workstations that access electronic health information.

baseRequirements.title: Workstation security
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must implement physical safeguards for all workstations that access electronic protected health information to restrict access to authorized users.

quote.text:
Standard: Workstation security. Im-
plement physical safeguards for all
workstations that access electronic
protected health information, to re-
strict access to authorized users.

baseRequirements.topic: physical protection of computers and workstations used to access patients' electronic health information
baseRequirements.complies: The text says each workstation that reaches electronic protected health information sits in a locked room or is secured with a cable lock, and only staff on the authorized list may use those workstations.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says workstations holding electronic protected health information are left unlocked in public areas, or that anyone walking by may sit down and use them.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe the physical barriers and user limits that keep each workstation reaching electronic protected health information usable only by authorized users.

baseRequirements.title: Device and media controls
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must govern receipt, removal and movement of hardware and electronic media containing electronic protected health information, including disposal and media re-use procedures.

quote.text:
(1) Standard: Device and media con-
trols. Implement policies and proce-
dures that govern the receipt and re-
moval of hardware and electronic
media that contain electronic pro-
tected health information into and out
of a facility, and the movement of
these items within the facility.

baseRequirements.topic: tracking and controlling hardware and electronic media that hold patients' electronic health information as they come in, move around and leave a facility
baseRequirements.complies: The text says a log records each device or medium containing electronic protected health information when it arrives, when it moves between rooms, and when it leaves, and that disposal and re-use steps are written down and followed.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says laptops, drives or disks holding electronic protected health information are moved or taken out with no record, or are thrown away or handed to another user without wiping the data.
baseRequirements.hint: Write down the steps staff follow to log receipt, internal movement, removal, disposal and re-use of hardware and media holding electronic protected health information.

baseRequirements.title: Access control
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must implement technical access controls allowing access only to persons or software programs with access rights, assign unique user identifiers, and establish emergency access procedures.

quote.text:
(a)(1) Standard: Access control. Imple-
ment technical policies and procedures
for electronic information systems
that maintain electronic protected
health information to allow access
only to those persons or software pro-
grams that have been granted access
rights as specified in § 164.308(a)(4).

baseRequirements.topic: technical limits on who and what may reach patients' electronic health information in computer systems
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the system checks each user's granted rights before letting them in, gives every person their own unique user name, and spells out how staff get in during an emergency.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says staff share one login, or that anyone who reaches the network can open any electronic protected health information, or that no emergency access steps exist.
baseRequirements.hint: State that access is limited to people and programs holding granted rights, that each user has a unique identifier, and that emergency access steps are written down.

baseRequirements.title: Audit controls
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must implement hardware, software or procedural mechanisms that record and examine activity in information systems containing or using electronic protected health information.

quote.text:
Standard: Audit controls. Imple-
ment hardware, software, and/or proce-
dural mechanisms that record and ex-
amine activity in information systems
that contain or use electronic pro-
tected health information.

baseRequirements.topic: recording and reviewing activity in computer systems that hold or use patients' electronic health information
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the system keeps logs of who opened, changed or sent electronic protected health information, and that someone reviews those logs on a set schedule.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says activity logging is turned off, or that no one ever looks at the records of who touched electronic protected health information.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe the hardware, software or paper steps that record system activity and the routine for examining those records.

baseRequirements.title: Data integrity
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must implement policies and procedures to protect electronic protected health information from improper alteration or destruction.

quote.text:
(1) Standard: Integrity. Implement
policies and procedures to protect elec-
tronic protected health information
from improper alteration or destruc-
tion.

baseRequirements.topic: keeping patients' electronic health information from being wrongly changed or wiped out
baseRequirements.complies: The text says written steps require checks that data matches its source, limit who may edit records, and keep backups so lost or altered electronic protected health information can be restored.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says any user may overwrite or delete electronic protected health information, or that no backups or edit checks exist.
baseRequirements.hint: Set out the policies and procedures that stop electronic protected health information from being altered or destroyed by mistake or on purpose.

baseRequirements.title: Person or entity authentication
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must implement procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to electronic protected health information is the one claimed.

quote.text:
Standard: Person or entity authen-
tication. Implement procedures to
verify that a person or entity seeking
access to electronic protected health
information is the one claimed.

baseRequirements.topic: proving that a person or system asking for patients' electronic health information is really who they claim to be
baseRequirements.complies: The text says users prove their identity with a password, token or badge check before the system lets them reach electronic protected health information, and outside systems must present a credential.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the system takes a user's word for who they are, or lets someone in with only a name typed on a screen and no check.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe the steps that verify the identity of every person or system before it is allowed to reach electronic protected health information.

baseRequirements.title: Transmission security
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must implement technical security measures guarding against unauthorized access to electronic protected health information transmitted over a network.

quote.text:
(1) Standard: Transmission security.

Implement technical security measures
to guard against unauthorized access
to electronic protected health informa-
tion that is being transmitted over an
electronic communications network.

baseRequirements.topic: sending electronic protected health information over a network
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that ePHI sent over a network is encrypted and that access is restricted to authorized parties, with technical safeguards such as encryption or secure channels in place for all transmissions.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says ePHI is emailed or transferred over open networks without encryption, or that anyone on the network can reach the transmitted data.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe the technical measures (for example encryption or secure transmission channels) that block unauthorized access to ePHI while it travels over a network.

baseRequirements.title: Business associate contract terms
baseRequirements.need: The business associate contract must require the business associate to comply with the security subpart, ensure subcontractors agree to comply, and report any security incident, including breaches, to the covered entity.

quote.text:
(i) Business associate contracts.

The contract must provide that the
business associate will—
(A) Comply with the applicable re-
quirements of this subpart;
(B) In accordance with § 164.308(b)(2),
ensure that any subcontractors that
create, receive, maintain, or transmit
electronic protected health informa-
tion on behalf of the business associate
agree to comply with the applicable re-
quirements of this subpart by entering
into a contract or other arrangement
that complies with this section; and
(C) Report to the covered entity any
security incident of which it becomes
aware, including breaches of unsecured
protected health information as re-
quired by § 164.410.

baseRequirements.topic: contracts between a covered entity and a business associate
baseRequirements.complies: The text states the contract requires the business associate to follow the security subpart, to make its subcontractors agree to the same requirements through a contract, and to report any security incident, including breaches, to the covered entity.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the contract is silent on security duties, lets subcontractors handle ePHI without any agreement, or excuses the business associate from reporting incidents or breaches.
baseRequirements.hint: List the three contract terms: business associate complies with the security subpart, subcontractors sign compliant agreements, and all security incidents including breaches are reported to the covered entity.

baseRequirements.title: Security policies and procedures
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must implement reasonable and appropriate policies and procedures to comply with the security subpart, and any changes must be documented and implemented accordingly.

quote.text:
Standard: Policies and procedures.

Implement reasonable and appropriate
policies and procedures to comply with
the standards, implementation speci-
fications, or other requirements of this
subpart, taking into account those fac-
tors specified in § 164.306(b)(2)(i), (ii),
(iii), and (iv).

baseRequirements.topic: written security policies and procedures of a covered entity or business associate
baseRequirements.complies: The text states the organization has written policies and procedures for meeting the security subpart, chosen after weighing its size, complexity, capabilities and costs, and that changes to them are documented and put into effect.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the organization has no security policies, relies only on unwritten practice, or changes its procedures without recording or implementing the change.
baseRequirements.hint: State that written policies and procedures exist for each security requirement, reflect the organization's size and resources, and that any revision is documented and carried out.

baseRequirements.title: Security documentation
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity or business associate must maintain written policies, procedures and records of required actions, retain them 6 years, make them available to responsible persons, and update them as needed.

quote.text:
(1) Standard: Documentation. (i)
Maintain the policies and procedures
implemented to comply with this sub-
part in written (which may be elec-
tronic) form; and
(ii) If an action, activity or assess-
ment is required by this subpart to be
documented, maintain a written (which
may be electronic) record of the action,
activity, or assessment.

baseRequirements.topic: keeping written security policies, procedures and records
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that written or electronic policies, procedures and records of required security actions are kept for six years, are available to the people responsible for them, and are updated when needed.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says security records are not kept in writing, are discarded before six years, are withheld from responsible staff, or are never revised.
baseRequirements.hint: Say that policies, procedures and records of required actions are kept in written or electronic form for six years, available to responsible persons, and updated as needed.

baseRequirements.title: Security compliance dates
baseRequirements.need: Health plans, small health plans, health care clearinghouses and covered health care providers must comply with the security subpart by the applicable dates no later than April 20, 2005 or April 20, 2006 for small health plans.

quote.text:
(a) Health plan. (1) A health plan that
is not a small health plan must comply
with the applicable requirements of
this subpart no later than April 20,
2005.
(2) A small health plan must comply
with the applicable requirements of
this subpart no later than April 20,
2006.

baseRequirements.topic: deadlines for covered entities to meet the security rule
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that health plans other than small health plans, clearinghouses and covered health care providers complied by April 20, 2005, and small health plans by April 20, 2006.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says a covered entity set its own later compliance date, or claims the security subpart did not apply until well after April 2005 or April 2006.
baseRequirements.hint: Name the entity type and its date: April 20, 2005 for most covered entities, April 20, 2006 for small health plans.

baseRequirements.title: Breach subpart applicability
baseRequirements.need: The breach notification requirements apply to breaches of protected health information occurring on or after September 23, 2009.

quote.text:
The requirements of this subpart
shall apply with respect to breaches of
protected health information occurring
on or after September 23, 2009.

baseRequirements.topic: breach notification for protected health information
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that the breach notification requirements cover breaches of protected health information that occurred on or after September 23, 2009.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says breaches before September 23, 2009 fall under the breach notification rules, or that breaches on or after that date are outside them.
baseRequirements.hint: State that the breach notification requirements apply to breaches occurring on or after September 23, 2009.

baseRequirements.title: Breach presumption and risk assessment
baseRequirements.need: An impermissible acquisition, access, use or disclosure is presumed to be a breach unless the entity demonstrates a low probability of compromise based on a risk assessment of the specified factors.

quote.text:
(2) Except as provided in paragraph
(1) of this definition, an acquisition, ac-
cess, use, or disclosure of protected
health information in a manner not
permitted under subpart E is presumed
to be a breach unless the covered enti-
ty or business associate, as applicable,
demonstrates that there is a low prob-
ability that the protected health infor-
mation has been compromised based on
a risk assessment of at least the fol-
lowing factors:

baseRequirements.topic: a health data incident where protected health information was accessed, used or disclosed without permission
baseRequirements.complies: The text treats the incident as a breach by default and only sets it aside after a documented risk assessment of the specified factors shows a low probability that the information was compromised.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says an unauthorized access or disclosure is not a breach without any risk assessment, or declares it harmless based on general assurances rather than an assessment of the specified factors.
baseRequirements.hint: State that any impermissible access, use or disclosure is presumed a breach unless a documented risk assessment of the specified factors shows a low probability of compromise.

baseRequirements.title: Notice to affected individuals
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity must notify each individual whose unsecured protected health information was or is reasonably believed to have been accessed, acquired, used or disclosed as a result of a breach, with discovery measured by knowledge or reasonable diligence.

quote.text:
(1) General rule. A cov-
ered entity shall, following the dis-
covery of a breach of unsecured pro-
tected health information, notify each
individual whose unsecured protected
health information has been, or is rea-
sonably believed by the covered entity
to have been, accessed, acquired, used,
or disclosed as a result of such breach.

baseRequirements.topic: notifying people after a breach of their unsecured health information
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the entity will notify every individual whose unsecured protected health information was or is reasonably believed to have been accessed, acquired, used or disclosed because of the breach.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says only some affected individuals will be told, or that no one will be notified, or limits notice to people whose data is proven to have been misused.
baseRequirements.hint: Commit to notifying each individual whose unsecured health information was or is reasonably believed to have been involved in the breach.

baseRequirements.title: Timeliness of individual notice
baseRequirements.need: Except for law enforcement delay, a covered entity must notify individuals without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery of the breach.

quote.text:
Implementation specification: Time-
liness of notification. Except as provided
in § 164.412, a covered entity shall pro-
vide the notification required by para-
graph (a) of this section without unrea-
sonable delay and in no case later than
60 calendar days after discovery of a
breach.

baseRequirements.topic: how quickly people are told about a breach of their health information
baseRequirements.complies: The text says individuals will be notified without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after the breach is discovered, with any law enforcement delay noted.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text sets a longer deadline than 60 days, says notice will wait until the investigation is fully finished, or gives no timing at all.
baseRequirements.hint: State that notice goes out without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery, except for law enforcement delay.

baseRequirements.title: Content of breach notice
baseRequirements.need: The individual notice must describe what happened and when, the types of information involved, steps individuals should take, what the entity is doing, and contact procedures, and must be written in plain language.

quote.text:
(1) Elements. The
notification required by paragraph (a)
of this section shall include, to the ex-
tent possible:
(A) A brief description of what hap-
pened, including the date of the breach
and the date of the discovery of the
breach, if known;
(B) A description of the types of un-
secured protected health information
that were involved in the breach (such
as whether full name, social security
number, date of birth, home address,
account number, diagnosis, disability
code, or other types of information
were involved);

baseRequirements.topic: what a breach notification letter to individuals says
baseRequirements.complies: The notice describes what happened with the breach date and discovery date, lists the types of unsecured health information involved, tells people what steps to take, what the entity is doing, and how to make contact, all in plain language.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The notice omits what happened or the dates, does not say which types of information were involved, gives no steps for individuals or contact details, or is written in dense legal jargon.
baseRequirements.hint: Include in plain language: what happened and when, the types of information involved, steps individuals should take, what the entity is doing, and contact procedures.

baseRequirements.title: Methods of individual notice
baseRequirements.need: Notice must be given by first-class mail or agreed electronic mail, to next of kin if the individual is deceased, and by substitute notice where contact information is insufficient or out of date.

quote.text:
(1) Written notice. (i) Written notifica-
tion by first-class mail to the indi-
vidual at the last known address of the
individual or, if the individual agrees
to electronic notice and such agree-
ment has not been withdrawn, by elec-
tronic mail. The notification may be
provided in one or more mailings as in-
formation is available.

baseRequirements.topic: how breach notices are delivered to individuals
baseRequirements.complies: The text says notice is sent by first-class mail to the last known address or by email where the individual agreed to electronic notice, with substitute notice used when contact details are insufficient or out of date.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says notice is posted only on a website, sent by text message without agreement, or skipped entirely when an address is missing.
baseRequirements.hint: Send notice by first-class mail or agreed email, to next of kin if the person is deceased, and use substitute notice when contact information is insufficient or out of date.

baseRequirements.title: Notice to media
baseRequirements.need: For a breach involving more than 500 residents of a State or jurisdiction, a covered entity must notify prominent media outlets without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery, with content meeting § 164.404(c).

quote.text:
(a) Standard. For a breach of unse-
cured protected health information in-
volving more than 500 residents of a
State or jurisdiction, a covered entity
shall, following the discovery of the
breach as provided in § 164.404(a)(2), no-
tify prominent media outlets serving
the State or jurisdiction.

baseRequirements.topic: telling the news media about a health data breach affecting many people in a state
baseRequirements.complies: The text says that when a breach involves more than 500 residents of a State or jurisdiction, prominent media outlets serving that area are notified without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery, with the same content as the individual notice.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says media will not be contacted, or that outlets are told only after a longer delay, or that the media statement leaves out the required content.
baseRequirements.hint: State that for a breach affecting more than 500 residents of a State or jurisdiction, prominent media outlets there are notified without unreasonable delay and within 60 days, with the required content.

baseRequirements.title: Business associate breach notice
baseRequirements.need: A business associate must notify the covered entity of a breach without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery, identifying affected individuals and providing information the covered entity must include in its notice.

quote.text:
(a) Standard—(1) General rule. A busi-
ness associate shall, following the dis-
covery of a breach of unsecured pro-
tected health information, notify the
covered entity of such breach.

baseRequirements.topic: reporting a breach of unsecured protected health information by a business associate to the covered entity
baseRequirements.complies: The business associate notifies the covered entity of the breach without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 days after discovery, names the affected individuals, and supplies the details the covered entity needs for its own notice.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The business associate waits more than 60 days after discovery before telling the covered entity, or reports the breach without identifying who was affected or without the information the covered entity must include in its notice.
baseRequirements.hint: State that the business associate tells the covered entity within 60 days of discovery and passes along the affected individuals and the details the covered entity's notice needs.

baseRequirements.title: Law enforcement delay
baseRequirements.need: If a law enforcement official states that notification would impede an investigation or harm national security, the entity must delay as specified in writing, or document an oral statement and delay no longer than 30 days.

quote.text:
(a) If the statement is in writing and
specifies the time for which a delay is
required, delay such notification, no-
tice, or posting for the time period
specified by the official; or
(b) If the statement is made orally,
document the statement, including the
identity of the official making the
statement, and delay the notification,
notice, or posting temporarily and no
longer than 30 days from the date of
the oral statement, unless a written
statement as described in paragraph (a)
of this section is submitted during that
time.

baseRequirements.topic: delaying breach notification at the request of a law enforcement official
baseRequirements.complies: When a law enforcement official gives a written statement specifying a delay period, notification is held for exactly that period; when the statement is oral, the entity writes down the statement and the official's identity and delays no longer than 30 days from the oral statement.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The entity delays notification indefinitely on a verbal request, or delays without recording the official's identity and the statement, or holds notification beyond 30 days after an oral statement with no written statement submitted in that time.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe holding notification only for the written period specified, or for at most 30 days after a documented oral statement.

baseRequirements.title: Administrative requirements and burden of proof
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity must comply with the administrative requirements of § 164.530(b), (d), (e), (g), (h), (i) and (j), and bears the burden of proving that notifications were made or that no breach occurred.

quote.text:
(a) Administrative requirements. A cov-
ered entity is required to comply with
the administrative requirements of
§ 164.530(b), (d), (e), (g), (h), (i), and (j)
with respect to the requirements of
this subpart.
(b) Burden of proof. In the event of a
use or disclosure in violation of sub-
part E, the covered entity or business
associate, as applicable, shall have the
burden of demonstrating that all noti-
fications were made as required by this
subpart or that the use or disclosure
did not constitute a breach, as defined
at § 164.402.

baseRequirements.topic: administrative duties and proof of breach notifications by covered entities and business associates
baseRequirements.complies: The covered entity follows the administrative requirements of § 164.530(b), (d), (e), (g), (h), (i) and (j) for this subpart, and keeps records that show all required notifications were made or that the use or disclosure was not a breach.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The covered entity skips the listed administrative requirements, or cannot show any records proving notifications were sent or that no breach occurred when a use or disclosure in violation of subpart E happens.
baseRequirements.hint: Say the covered entity meets the listed § 164.530 administrative requirements and keeps records that can prove notifications were made or that no breach occurred.

baseRequirements.title: Document personnel designations
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity must document the personnel designations required by § 164.530(a)(1) as required by § 164.530(j).

quote.text:
A covered entity
must document the personnel designa-
tions in paragraph (a)(1) of this section
as required by paragraph (j) of this sec-
tion.

baseRequirements.topic: recording the designation of privacy and contact personnel by a covered entity
baseRequirements.complies: The covered entity writes down and keeps the personnel designations required by § 164.530(a)(1) in the manner § 164.530(j) requires.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The covered entity names a privacy official or contact person but never puts the designation in writing or keeps no record of it as § 164.530(j) requires.
baseRequirements.hint: State that the personnel designations are documented and retained following § 164.530(j).

baseRequirements.title: Workforce training
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity must train all members of its workforce on the policies and procedures for protected health information required by this subpart and subpart D, as necessary and appropriate for their functions.

quote.text:
A covered
entity must train all members of its
workforce on the policies and proce-
dures with respect to protected health
information required by this subpart
and subpart D of this part, as necessary
and appropriate for the members of the
workforce to carry out their functions
within the covered entity.

baseRequirements.topic: training a covered entity's workforce on protected health information policies and procedures
baseRequirements.complies: The covered entity trains every workforce member on the protected health information policies and procedures required by this subpart and subpart D, matched to what each member's job involves.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The covered entity trains only some staff, or gives no training on the required protected health information policies and procedures, or gives training that does not fit what members do in their roles.
baseRequirements.hint: Say all workforce members are trained on the required policies and procedures in a way that fits their functions.

baseRequirements.title: Training timing and records
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity must train each workforce member by the compliance date, each new member within a reasonable time after joining, and each member whose functions are affected by a material policy change within a reasonable time after the change, and must document that the training was provided.

quote.text:
A covered entity must pro-
vide training that meets the require-
ments of paragraph (b)(1) of this sec-
tion, as follows:
(A) To each member of the covered
entity’s workforce by no later than the
compliance date for the covered entity;
(B) Thereafter, to each new member
of the workforce within a reasonable
period of time after the person joins
the covered entity’s workforce; and
(C) To each member of the covered
entity’s workforce whose functions are
affected by a material change in the
policies or procedures required by this
subpart or subpart D of this part, with-
in a reasonable period of time after the
material change becomes effective in
accordance with paragraph (i) of this
section.

baseRequirements.topic: timing of workforce privacy training and records of that training
baseRequirements.complies: The covered entity trains each workforce member by the compliance date, each new member within a reasonable time after joining, and each member affected by a material policy change within a reasonable time after the change, and documents that the training was given.
baseRequirements.conflicts: New members go untrained for a long period after joining, members affected by a material policy change are not retrained, or the covered entity keeps no record showing the training was provided.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe training by the compliance date, soon after new members join and after material policy changes, with records kept for each session.

baseRequirements.title: Privacy safeguards
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity must have appropriate administrative, technical, and physical safeguards to protect the privacy of protected health information and must reasonably safeguard it from intentional or unintentional violations and limit incidental uses or disclosures.

quote.text:
A covered
entity must have in place appropriate
administrative, technical, and physical
safeguards to protect the privacy of
protected health information.
(2)(i) Implementation specification:
Safeguards. A covered entity must rea-
sonably safeguard protected health in-
formation from any intentional or un-
intentional use or disclosure that is in
violation of the standards, implemen-
tation specifications or other require-
ments of this subpart.

baseRequirements.topic: protecting the privacy of patients' health information through administrative, technical and physical safeguards
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that the organization has written administrative, technical and physical safeguards for health information, such as role-based access, locked storage, staff training, and steps to prevent accidental or deliberate misuse or disclosure.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says health information is left unsecured, that staff share one login, that paper records sit in open areas, or that the organization takes no steps to prevent accidental or deliberate disclosures.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe the specific administrative, technical and physical safeguards in place and how they prevent both intentional and unintentional privacy violations.

baseRequirements.title: Complaint process
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity must provide a process for individuals to complain about its privacy policies and procedures or its compliance with them or with this subpart and subpart D, and must document all complaints received and their disposition.

quote.text:
A covered entity must pro-
vide a process for individuals to make
complaints concerning the covered en-
tity’s policies and procedures required
by this subpart and subpart D of this
part or its compliance with such poli-
cies and procedures or the require-
ments of this subpart or subpart D of
this part.
(2) Implementation specification: Docu-
mentation of complaints. As required by
paragraph (j) of this section, a covered
entity must document all complaints
received, and their disposition, if any.

baseRequirements.topic: a process for patients to complain about privacy policies, procedures or compliance
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that individuals can file privacy complaints through a named contact or channel, and that every complaint received and how it was resolved is written down.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says there is no way for individuals to complain about privacy practices, or that complaints are handled informally and never recorded or tracked.
baseRequirements.hint: Name the complaint channel and state that all complaints received and their disposition are documented.

baseRequirements.title: Sanctions for noncompliance
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity must have and apply appropriate sanctions against workforce members who fail to comply with its privacy policies and procedures or the requirements of this subpart or subpart D, and must document the sanctions applied.

quote.text:
A covered
entity must have and apply appro-
priate sanctions against members of its
workforce who fail to comply with the
privacy policies and procedures of the
covered entity or the requirements of
this subpart or subpart D of this part.
This standard does not apply to a mem-
ber of the covered entity’s workforce
with respect to actions that are cov-
ered by and that meet the conditions of
§ 164.502(j) or paragraph (g)(2) of this
section.

baseRequirements.topic: sanctions against workforce members who break privacy policies or requirements
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that the organization has defined sanctions, such as warnings, retraining or termination, that are applied to staff who violate privacy policies, and that each sanction applied is documented.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says staff who break privacy rules face no consequences, that discipline is left to individual managers with no policy, or that sanctions are never recorded.
baseRequirements.hint: List the sanctions that apply to noncompliant workforce members and state that each applied sanction is documented.

baseRequirements.title: Mitigation of harm
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity must mitigate, to the extent practicable, any known harmful effect of a use or disclosure of protected health information in violation of its policies and procedures or this subpart by the covered entity or its business associate.

quote.text:
A covered en-
tity must mitigate, to the extent prac-
ticable, any harmful effect that is
known to the covered entity of a use or
disclosure of protected health informa-
tion in violation of its policies and pro-
cedures or the requirements of this
subpart by the covered entity or its
business associate.

baseRequirements.topic: reducing harm from a privacy violation involving health information
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that when a harmful use or disclosure of health information is discovered, the organization takes steps to lessen the harm, such as notifying affected people, retrieving records, or correcting the record.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the organization does nothing after learning of a harmful disclosure, or that it waits and takes no action to reduce the harm caused.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe the steps taken to reduce known harm after a violating use or disclosure, including by a business associate.

baseRequirements.title: No waiver of rights
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity may not require individuals to waive their rights under § 160.306, this subpart, or subpart D as a condition of treatment, payment, enrollment in a health plan, or eligibility for benefits.

quote.text:
A cov-
ered entity may not require individuals
to waive their rights under § 160.306 of
this subchapter, this subpart, or sub-
part D of this part, as a condition of
the provision of treatment, payment,
enrollment in a health plan, or eligi-
bility for benefits.

baseRequirements.topic: conditions placed on patients receiving treatment, payment, health plan enrollment or benefits
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that individuals are never asked to give up their privacy rights in order to get treatment, payment, plan enrollment or benefits.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says patients must sign away privacy rights, or agree not to file complaints, as a condition of receiving care, payment, enrollment or benefits.
baseRequirements.hint: State plainly that no one is required to waive privacy rights to obtain treatment, payment, enrollment or benefits.

baseRequirements.title: Policies and procedures
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity must implement reasonably designed written policies and procedures for protected health information that comply with the standards, implementation specifications, and other requirements of this subpart and subpart D.

quote.text:
A covered entity must implement poli-
cies and procedures with respect to
protected health information that are
designed to comply with the standards,
implementation specifications, or
other requirements of this subpart and
subpart D of this part. The policies and
procedures must be reasonably de-
signed, taking into account the size
and the type of activities that relate to
protected health information under-
taken by a covered entity, to ensure
such compliance.

baseRequirements.topic: written privacy policies and procedures for health information
baseRequirements.complies: The text states that the organization has written policies and procedures for health information that are designed to meet the applicable privacy standards and are scaled to its size and activities.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the organization has no written privacy policies, or that its policies are generic and not designed to meet the privacy standards or fit its size and activities.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe the written policies and procedures and explain how they are designed to comply with the privacy standards given the organization's size and activities.

baseRequirements.title: Changing policies and procedures
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity must change its policies and procedures as necessary to comply with changes in the law, may apply notice-related changes to information created or received before the notice revision only if it reserved that right in the notice, and may make other changes at any time if documented and implemented as required.

quote.text:
A covered entity must
change its policies and procedures as
necessary and appropriate to comply
with changes in the law, including the
standards, requirements, and imple-
mentation specifications of this sub-
part or subpart D of this part.
(ii) When a covered entity changes a
privacy practice that is stated in the
notice described in § 164.520, and makes
corresponding changes to its policies
and procedures, it may make the
changes effective for protected health
information that it created or received
prior to the effective date of the notice
revision, if the covered entity has, in
accordance with § 164.520(b)(1)(v)(C), in-
cluded in the notice a statement re-
serving its right to make such a change
in its privacy practices; or
(iii) A covered entity may make any
other changes to policies and proce-
dures at any time, provided that the
changes are documented and imple-
mented in accordance with paragraph
(i)(5) of this section.

baseRequirements.topic: updating a health organization's privacy policies and procedures when laws or stated privacy practices change
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the organization revises its policies and procedures whenever the law changes, and that it applies notice-related changes to information created or received before the notice revision only because the notice reserved that right; other changes are made at any time and are documented and implemented.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the organization keeps its old policies after the law changes, or applies a notice-related change to earlier information without having reserved that right in the notice, or makes changes without documenting and implementing them.
baseRequirements.hint: State that policies are revised when the law changes, that retroactive notice changes rely on a reserved right in the notice, and that all other changes are documented and implemented.

baseRequirements.title: Changes in law
baseRequirements.need: When a change in law requires a policy or procedure change, a covered entity must promptly document and implement the revised policy or procedure and promptly revise the notice if its content is materially affected.

quote.text:
Whenever there is a
change in law that necessitates a
change to the covered entity’s policies
or procedures, the covered entity must
promptly document and implement the
revised policy or procedure. If the
change in law materially affects the
content of the notice required by
§ 164.520, the covered entity must
promptly make the appropriate revi-
sions to the notice in accordance with
§ 164.520(b)(3).

baseRequirements.topic: responding to a change in law that requires updating a health organization's privacy policies or notice
baseRequirements.complies: The text says that when a change in law requires it, the organization promptly documents and implements the revised policy or procedure and promptly revises the notice if the law materially affects the notice's content.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the organization waits or delays after a legal change, leaves the old policy in place, or does not update the notice even though the law materially affects its content.
baseRequirements.hint: Say the revised policy is documented and implemented promptly after the legal change, and the notice is revised promptly if its content is materially affected.

baseRequirements.title: Changes to stated privacy practices
baseRequirements.need: To implement a change to a privacy practice stated in the notice, a covered entity must ensure the revised policy complies with this subpart, document it, and revise and make available the notice, and may not implement the change before the revised notice's effective date; without a reserved right it is bound by the stated practices for information created or received while the notice is in effect unless the change meets the specifications and applies only to information created or received after the notice's effective date.

quote.text:
To implement a change as
provided by paragraph (i)(2)(ii) of this
section, a covered entity must:
(A) Ensure that the policy or proce-
dure, as revised to reflect a change in
the covered entity’s privacy practice as
stated in its notice, complies with the
standards, requirements, and imple-
mentation specifications of this sub-
part;
(B) Document the policy or proce-
dure, as revised, as required by para-
graph (j) of this section; and
(C) Revise the notice as required by
§ 164.520(b)(3) to state the changed prac-
tice and make the revised notice avail-
able as required by § 164.520(c). The cov-
ered entity may not implement a
change to a policy or procedure prior
to the effective date of the revised no-
tice.

baseRequirements.topic: changing a privacy practice that is stated in a health organization's notice
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the revised policy complies with the applicable standards, is documented, and the notice is revised and made available, and that the change is not implemented before the revised notice's effective date.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the organization puts a stated-practice change into effect before the revised notice's effective date, skips revising or distributing the notice, or does not document the revised policy.
baseRequirements.hint: Describe revising the policy to comply, documenting it, revising and making available the notice, and waiting until the revised notice's effective date to implement the change.

baseRequirements.title: Changes to other policies
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity may change a policy or procedure that does not materially affect the notice content at any time, provided the revised policy complies with this subpart and is documented before its effective date.

quote.text:
A
covered entity may change, at any
time, a policy or procedure that does
not materially affect the content of the
notice required by § 164.520, provided
that:
(i) The policy or procedure, as re-
vised, complies with the standards, re-
quirements, and implementation speci-
fications of this subpart; and
(ii) Prior to the effective date of the
change, the policy or procedure, as re-
vised, is documented as required by
paragraph (j) of this section.

baseRequirements.topic: changing a health organization's privacy policy or procedure that does not affect the notice content
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the organization may change such a policy at any time, that the revised policy complies with the applicable standards, and that it is documented before the change's effective date.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says the organization changes a policy without documenting it, or documents it only after the change takes effect, or adopts a revised policy that does not comply with the standards.
baseRequirements.hint: State that the change is allowed at any time, that the revised policy complies with the standards, and that it is documented before its effective date.

baseRequirements.title: Documentation duties
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity must maintain its policies and procedures in written or electronic form, maintain required writings or electronic copies, maintain a written or electronic record of required actions, activities, or designations, and maintain documentation sufficient to meet its burden of proof under § 164.414(b).

quote.text:
A cov-
ered entity must:
(i) Maintain the policies and proce-
dures provided for in paragraph (i) of
this section in written or electronic
form;
(ii) If a communication is required by
this subpart to be in writing, maintain
such writing, or an electronic copy, as
documentation; and
(iii) If an action, activity, or designa-
tion is required by this subpart to be
documented, maintain a written or
electronic record of such action, activ-
ity, or designation.

baseRequirements.topic: keeping records of a health organization's privacy policies, written communications and required actions
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the organization keeps its policies and procedures in written or electronic form, keeps any required written communication or an electronic copy, and keeps a written or electronic record of each required action, activity or designation.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says policies exist only verbally, that required written communications are not kept, or that required actions, activities or designations are not recorded.
baseRequirements.hint: Say policies and procedures are kept in written or electronic form and that required writings and records of actions, activities and designations are maintained.

baseRequirements.title: Six-year retention
baseRequirements.need: A covered entity must retain the required documentation for six years from the date of its creation or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later.

quote.text:
A covered entity must re-
tain the documentation required by
paragraph (j)(1) of this section for six
years from the date of its creation or
the date when it last was in effect,
whichever is later.

baseRequirements.topic: how long a health organization keeps its privacy documentation
baseRequirements.complies: The text says the organization retains required documentation for six years from the date it was created or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later.
baseRequirements.conflicts: The text says documentation is destroyed sooner than six years, or is kept only from the date it was created even when it stayed in effect longer, or is discarded once replaced.
baseRequirements.hint: State a six-year retention period counted from creation or last in effect, whichever is later.

baseRequirements.title: Group health plan limits
baseRequirements.need: A group health plan providing benefits solely through an insurance contract or HMO and not creating or receiving protected health information except summary health information or enrollment information is not subject to the personnel, training, safeguards, complaints, sanctions, mitigation, and policies standards, and is subject to the documentation standard only for plan documents amended under § 164.504(f).

quote.text:
A
group health plan is not subject to the
standards or implementation specifica-
tions in paragraphs (a) through (f) and
(i) of this section, to the extent that:
(i) The group health plan provides
health benefits solely through an in-
surance contract with a health insur-
ance issuer or an HMO; and
(ii) The group health plan does not
create or receive protected health in-
formation, except for:
(A) Summary health information as
defined in § 164.504(a); or
(B) Information on whether the indi-
vidual is participating in the group
health plan, or is enrolled in or has
disenrolled from a health insurance
issuer or HMO offered by the plan.

baseRequirements.topic: group health plans that provide benefits only through an insurance contract or HMO and handle limited health information
baseRequirements.complies: The plan states it offers health benefits solely through an insurance contract with a health insurance issuer or an HMO, and that it creates or receives no protected health information other than summary health information or enrollment and participation information. It states it is exempt from the personnel, training, safeguards, complaints, sanctions, mitigation and policies standards, and keeps documentation only for plan documents amended under § 164.504(f).
baseRequirements.conflicts: The plan says it provides benefits through self-insurance or directly administers claims, or it says it creates or receives protected health information beyond summary health information and enrollment information. It claims the exemptions apply while also describing personnel, training, safeguards, complaints, sanctions, mitigation or policy activities it performs for the plan.
baseRequirements.hint: State that benefits are provided solely through an insurance contract or HMO, that only summary health information and enrollment or participation information are created or received, and list exactly which standards the plan is exempt from and which documentation it keeps.
